_meta: Externally-researched circuit-optimization techniques injected into Aristotle prompts by gen_prompts.py. Techniques are candidate ideas from the ZK literature — the Clean challenge is R1CS with cost = allocations + constraints, so some lookup/GKR/sumcheck tricks may NOT map; Aristotle must verify applicability before use. Refreshed periodically via web research.
_common: MECHANICAL POST-PASS over the finished constraint system (arkworks r1cs-optimizer passes): (a) DEAD VARIABLE ELIMINATION — drop every allocated witness never read by a surviving constraint; (b) CONSTRAINT DEDUPLICATION — identical rank-1 rows collapse to one; (c) CONSTANT FOLDING; (d) LINEAR SUBSTITUTION — a variable defined by an affine constraint is inlined into its uses and both it and its defining row disappear. Cost here is allocations+constraints, so each pass pays twice; run this sweep at the END of any rewrite, since hand-golfing reliably leaves orphaned witnesses behind.

GAUSSIAN-ELIMINATION DISTILLING (Albert et al., CAV 2022, 'Distilling Constraints in Zero-Knowledge Protocols', implemented in circom): run Gaussian elimination over the NON-LINEAR constraint set to DEDUCE previously implicit LINEAR constraints, then use those to substitute away variables and delete rows — strictly stronger than plain linear substitution, because it finds linear facts implied only by the quadratic rows. Reported up to 16.33% of constraints removed from circomlib circuits that had ALREADY been hand-simplified — assume a hand-golfed circuit still hides redundancy, and re-run this after every rewrite. HOW TO ACTUALLY RUN IT (circom --O2 mechanics, docs.circom.io/circom-language/circom-insight/simplification): collect the MAXIMAL CLUSTERS of linear constraints that share signals and solve each cluster in one go with a lazy Gauss-Jordan pass, rather than substituting one row at a time; then iterate to FIXPOINT — after substitution some constraints that were non-linear BECOME linear, so repeat rounds until no eliminable linear constraint remains. SCOPING RULE: only a constraint containing at least one PRIVATE signal may be eliminated; interface inputs/outputs are fixed by the challenge and can never be substituted away. IN CLEAN THIS IS CONCRETE: any value you `witness` that is an AFFINE function of values already in scope is pure waste — affine combinations are free Expressions here, so inline it and delete its assertEq. That removes 1 allocation AND 1 constraint, i.e. 2 units of score per elimination. Do this sweep LAST, after the circuit shape is final, and re-prove the affected theorems.

CLEAN STRUCTURING IDIOM (zksecurity, 'Verifying Poseidon in Clean'): wrap each repeated block in its OWN FormalCircuit and drive it with Circuit.foldl instead of unfolding every iteration inline — unfolding makes the elaborated term enormous and elaboration 'slow and brittle', which is the usual reason an aggressive rewrite cannot close its proofs and ends up returning `sorry`. Applies directly to all five challenges: 64 SHA-256 rounds, 24 Keccak rounds, the 17 RSA squarings/multiplies, the per-bit scalar-mul ladder. Conversely keep CHEAP AFFINE work (round constants, linear/matrix layers) INLINE — factoring it into its own circuit obscures the proof without lowering cost. localLength must account for EVERY intermediate witness, so count per-iteration allocations exactly (Poseidon reference: 6 per partial round vs 8 per full round) — that count IS half the score.

NAMED DEAD END — THE GNARK EMULATED-ARITHMETIC SPEEDUPS DO NOT APPLY HERE (checked against ivokub's writeup and the gnark std/algebra approach). All three of their constraint-count wins for non-native multiplication need a prover-verifier CHALLENGE that this cost model does not give you: (a) checking p_y(Z) = p_k(Z)*p_q(Z) by evaluating at random points instead of decomposing limbs — needs Fiat-Shamir randomness; (b) the log-derivative trick F'(Z)/F(Z) = S'(Z)/S(Z) — needs r = Commit({s_i},{e_i}); (c) augmented Groth16 with Pedersen commitments on witness limbs used as the challenge — needs a modified verifier. zkGolf checks a PLAIN R1CS with no commitment or Fiat-Shamir machinery, so none of it is available: you must still pay for the limb carries and range checks. If a paper's speedup rests on a random challenge, a commitment, a lookup argument, GKR or sum-check, it is out of scope here no matter how large the quoted saving.

COMPARISON AGAINST A CONSTANT — WHAT IS AND IS NOT NEW HERE (correcting an earlier note of mine). The weighted-accumulation comparator of Mathematics 13(24):3959 IS circomlib's existing CompConstant: bit PAIRS each contributing a compile-time weight in one quadratic row, with the accumulator sign read off by Num2Bits(135), so its 262 = 127 + 135. Its 759 baseline is a lexicographic comparator, and crucially IT TAKES THE 254 BITS AS INPUT — so it is a comparison optimisation, not a range check, and it is still linear in k. Do not expect a 65% cut on a range check from it. THE GENUINELY USEFUL TRICK FOR x < X WITH X A CONSTANT is Khovratovich's: change only the TOP weight, x = (X - 2^(n-1))*a_(n-1) + sum_(i<=n-2) a_i*2^i, plus n booleanity rows — the two branches overlap and cover exactly [0, X). Exhaustively verified for X = 2..300 and for 1000,1023,1024,1025,4095,5000. Measured at 254 bits: 254 rows and score 507, against Num2Bits(254) + CompConstant(X) at 515 rows and score 1028 — A CLEAN 2x, and circomlib has no such gadget. RELATED: for a plain k-bit range check, DO NOT ALLOCATE THE TOP BIT — define it as the free linear combination (x - sum_(i<k-1) 2^i b_i)/2^(k-1) and apply booleanity to that form, giving k rows + k-1 allocations = 2k-1. circom --O2 does this automatically; arkworks does not and pays 509 instead of 507.

THE SINGLE-ROW NON-VANISHING-MULTIPLIER TRICK (Verified-zkEVM/clean#395) — the general recipe behind the Keccak record, and it transfers to ANY small boolean function, including SHA-256's Ch/Maj/Xor3 (the record's own file notes it was 'ported from Solution.SHA256.Xor3'). Encode the output z in ONE rank-1 row of the shape L1 - (z + L2)*M = 0 where L1, L2, M are AFFINE in the boolean inputs and M is provably NON-ZERO everywhere on the boolean cube. Then the row is linear in z, so z is UNIQUELY pinned — and it inherits booleanity, so NO separate z(z-1)=0 row is needed. Two worked instances: 3-input XOR, (6a + 6b - 24c) - (z + 2a + 2b + 7c)*(a + b - 4c + 1) = 0, multiplier takes only +-1,+-2,+-3 for p > 3; chi = a XOR ((NOT b) AND c), (4a + 2b) - (z + 3a - b - c)*(4a + b + c - 3) = 0, multiplier again +-1,+-2,+-3. Each costs 1 allocation + 1 constraint per bit, HALF the cost of chaining two-input gadgets and with the booleanity row eliminated. To apply it to a new function: pick M affine and nonzero on the cube, then solve for L1, L2 so the row reproduces the truth table; verify M never vanishes (that is what makes z unique).

THE R1CS-NATIVE GATE LIBRARY IS NOT {AND, XOR} — IT IS 192 OF THE 256 THREE-INPUT FUNCTIONS (computed here by exhaustive SMT, cvc5 QF_FF over the circom prime; harness validated on the known XOR3 row). A function f(a,b,c) of boolean inputs is 'native' if it admits ONE rank-1 row L1 - (z + L2)*M = 0 with L1,L2,M affine in a,b,c and M non-vanishing on the cube: z is then uniquely pinned AND inherits booleanity, so the whole gate costs 1 allocation + 1 constraint with NO separate z(z-1)=0 row. FULL CLASSIFICATION: 192 of 256 are native, 64 are not. Every function of GF(2) ANF degree <= 2 is native (all 128 of them). Of the 128 degree-3 functions exactly 64 are native. NATIVE: XOR3, XNOR3, OR3, Maj(a,b,c), Ch(a,b,c), and chi = a XOR ((NOT b) AND c). NOT NATIVE: AND3 = abc, and 63 other degree-3 functions. NOTE THE INVERSION: the 3-input AND — the canonical 'one gate' of the multiplicative-complexity world — CANNOT be done in one row, while XOR3 and chi can. CONSEQUENCE, AND THIS IS THE POINT: a netlist minimised for AND-count under the free-XOR assumption (Bristol Fashion, Boyar-Peralta XAG synthesis, anything from the garbled-circuit or MPC literature) is optimal for a DIFFERENT basis and is NOT optimal here. Do not port such a circuit gate-for-gate. Re-synthesise the algorithm over the native library: cost = the number of MATERIALISED non-affine values, where each materialised value may be ANY of the 192 native functions of three already-materialised bits, and every affine combination in between is free. TO DERIVE THE ROW for a native f: pick an affine M that never vanishes on the cube, then solve the 8 linear equations (f(x) + L2(x))*M(x) = L1(x) for the coefficients of L1 and L2 — with M fixed the system is LINEAR, so this is a small exact solve, not a search. *** CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S EXAMPLE LIST: OR3 IS NOT NATIVE. Nativeness is invariant under input AND output complementation, and OR3 = 1 - AND3(1-a,1-b,1-c), so OR3 is native iff AND3 is — and AND3 is not (verified computationally: OR3 = 0xfe, native = False). The count of 192, the degree classification, and every other example in this entry are correct; only the OR3 example was wrong. ***

TENSOR RANK IS THE ROW LOWER BOUND FOR ANYTHING BILINEAR — the single most transferable structural idea. A rank-1 row is EXACTLY one product of two linear forms, and outputs are free linear combinations of row results, so THE MINIMUM NUMBER OF ROWS TO COMPUTE A BILINEAR MAP IS ITS BILINEAR COMPLEXITY (tensor rank). Consequences that are immediately usable: an m-limb by m-limb polynomial product is 2m-1 rows, not m^2, by checking (sum x_i c^i)(sum y_i c^i) = (sum z_i c^i) at the HARD-CODED constants c = 1..2m-1 — both sides are affine in the witnesses because the c^i are constants, there is NO randomness (two degree-(2m-2) polynomials agreeing at 2m-1 points are identical), and 2m-1 is OPTIMAL by Winograd's classical rank result, not merely good; verified in session for m = 2,3,4,8,16 (m=8 gives 15 rows against 64, m=16 gives 31 against 256). A 2x2 matrix product is 7 rows (Strassen), and 7 is a proven lower bound. The whole tensor-rank lower-bound literature — substitution method, Blaser, Winograd — therefore transfers verbatim as R1CS row lower bounds. Reach for this FIRST whenever outputs are bilinear in two groups of inputs.

THE MONOMIAL BASIS IS FREE ONLY FOR CONSTANT DATA — CORRECTING MY OWN ENTRY, WHICH WOULD HAVE SENT A JOB INTO A REGRESSION. The claim 'allocate the 2^k - k - 1 monomials of degree >= 2 in the bits and EVERY output is then a FREE linear combination' is CORRECT when the outputs are functions of the k boolean inputs alone, because each monomial x constant is affine and so is the sum. IT IS FALSE FOR VARIABLE DATA. My extension — 'MultiMux3 over n-wide data costs 1 + 6n against 4 by the monomial basis FOR ANY n' — does not hold in this harness: out = sum_e ind_e * c_e has ONE PRODUCT PER TABLE ENTRY, so r1csProducts >= 2 and the expression CANNOT APPEAR IN ANY ASSERT AT ALL (see the one-product-per-row entry). For a 2^k-entry VARIABLE table the mux TREE at 2^k - 1 rows per output cell is the right shape and beats the monomial basis — measured on the secp256k1 variable-base VarLookup: tree 135 for 9 cells against 11 + 9*15 = 146 for the monomial basis. VarLookup IS ALREADY OPTIMAL; do not send a job to 'apply the monomial basis' there. WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS STILL STRONG: the monomial basis is correct and cheap for CONSTANT tables (the fixed-base top window uses it at 11/11 for 16 entries with all 8 output limbs free) and for pure boolean-function blocks. The proved one-hot minimum of 2^w - w - 1 multiplications is unaffected — that is about BUILDING the one-hot, not about contracting a table against it.

PRIOR ART FOR THE SINGLE-ROW TRICK — THE NOVELTY CLAIM SURVIVES, BUT ONLY IN ITS SHARPENED FORM, AND IT HAS A LINEAGE. SPLIT THE CLAIM IN TWO. (1) 'One rank-1 row computes a boolean function and its output is boolean for free' is NOT novel — it is universal and deliberate since 2016 whenever the output is isolated in C and the function has degree <= 2: AND a*b = c; NOR (1-a)(1-b) = c; AND-NOT a(1-b) = c; XOR2 2a*b = a+b-c; Ch (f-g)*e = ch-g; select b(y-x) = y-z; conditional equality a*(b-c) = 0. It is named in the APIs (arkworks new_witness_without_booleanity_check, gnark MarkBoolean) and the Zcash spec says of XOR2 'This automatically boolean-constrains c'. (2) 'Put the output inside a MULTIPLICAND, over a VARIABLE affine multiplier that is a unit on the boolean cube, reaching DEGREE-3 functions with booleanity still free' — no prior art was found for this after an exhaustive sweep. THE HONEST ANTECEDENTS TO CITE: Daira Hopwood's Zcon0 Circuit Optimisation handout (2018, ZcashFoundation/zcon0-workshop-notes, cited by the ZKProof Community Reference as [Hop18]) lists 'merge to do two things at once — merging with boolean constraints in constant comparisons' AND separately the inversion principle with exactly the right side condition ('q*b = a if the inverse exists... what if a = b = 0? then q is unconstrained') — but never composes them, and his n-ary AND still pays a separate booleanity row. Zcash Protocol Spec A.3.2.1 (non-normative) says of unpacking 'it is possible to eliminate it by merging it into the boolean constraint of one of the output bits... we do not use it for the Sapling circuit', and A.3.2.2's constant range check actually deploys it ('the constraints corresponding to zero bits of c are in place of boolean constraints on bits of a_i', Theorem A.3.1). THE STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT: in both Zcash cases the output is recovered by dividing by a CONSTANT (2^-j) and appears in BOTH multiplicands; our form divides by a VARIABLE affine form and keeps the output in ONE multiplicand — that is what buys the extra degree. Closest 2-row analogue: Pinocchio's is-zero, X*M - Y = 0 and (1-Y)*X = 0, where booleanity of Y is IMPLIED by the pair and Y sits inside a multiplicand (arkworks independently exploited this: CHANGELOG 'saved 1 constraint in FpVar::{is_eq, is_neq} by removing the unnecessary booleanity check'). SHARPEST NEGATIVE DATAPOINT: Zcash A.3.2.2's n-ary AND puts the output in a multiplicand across 3 rows and STILL pays an explicit (1-b)b = 0 — precisely where the trick would have applied.

THE ABSENCE OF PRIOR ART HERE IS EVIDENCE, NOT AN ARCHIVE GAP — searched and empty, so do not re-run this survey. XOR3 costs 2 CONSTRAINTS PER BIT in libsnark, bellman, circomlib, bkomuves, arkworks AND gnark: every serious implementation from 2014 to 2025. libsnark's majority_gadget even emits a PURE BOOLEANITY ROW alongside its carry-save row — it must, since x=y=z=0, r=-1/2 satisfies the carry-save row alone. Came up empty: ZKProof Community Reference v0.3 (there is NO academic R1CS gadget cookbook), zkdocs (no R1CS section at all), 0xPARC learn / zk-bug-tracker, docs.circom.io, MoonMath, Vitalik's QAP posts, CirC and Bounded-Verification-for-FF-Blasting (emits w'(w'-1) as a SEPARATE assertion), Distilling Constraints (CAV'22 — explicitly notes 'circuits using bitwise operations leave small room for optimization', and did NOT find circomlib's XOR3 redundancy), Picus/QED2/Coda/AC4/Ecne/Plonkify, the SM3 ZK-circuit paper (Sensors 22(16):5951 — peer-reviewed bit-oriented hash minimization, uses a 2-constraint XOR3 and keeps booleanity separate), ethresear.ch, zkresear.ch, community.zkproof.org, StackExchange. GitHub global code search: '"implies booleanity" OR "booleanity is implied"' -> 0 results; 'xor3 "single constraint" r1cs' -> 0. NO NAME EXISTS for it: 'constraint fusion' is taken (ZKML rounding-merge), 'constraint packing' means batching LINEAR equalities (Zcash A.3.7 BLAKE2s, 7 checks/row), and 'implicit/folded/free booleanity' has zero usage. ONE RESIDUAL GAP, stated honestly: ePrint 2022/462 (Ambrona et al., PlonK arithmetization) is Cloudflare-403 to every tool here; its implementation paper Clap (arXiv:2405.12115) says 'augmented with the information of which variable is boolean [our inlining] can reach one constraint' — but that is about INPUT booleanity as an optimizer hypothesis for 2-input XOR in a degree-2 PlonKish gate, not output-booleanity folding in a rank-1 row. Low risk, not closed.

COMPARISON AND INTERVAL CHECKING AGAINST CONSTANTS IS SOLVED EXACTLY — Haner & Soeken, 'The multiplicative complexity of interval checking', arXiv:2201.10200. RE-VERIFIED HERE BY BRUTE FORCE, not quoted. THEOREM: for an n-bit x and constants a < b < 2^n, with j_a, j_b the TRAILING-ZERO counts of a and b, MC([a <= x < b]) = n - min(j_a, j_b) - 1 when j_a != j_b, and n - j_a - 2 when j_a == j_b. COROLLARY: a one-sided [a <= x] with a = 2^j * k (k odd) costs exactly n - j - 1. THE SURPRISE, AND THE ACTIONABLE PART: A TWO-SIDED INTERVAL CHECK NEVER COSTS MORE THAN A SINGLE COMPARISON, and is one gate CHEAPER when the two bounds have the same number of trailing zeros — so anywhere the circuit currently pays for `lo <= x` AND `x < hi` separately, it is paying about double. THE CONSTRUCTION IS TRIVIAL: for odd a, [a <= x] is the AND/OR chain x_1 o_1 (x_2 o_2 (... (x_{n-1} o_{n-1} x_n))) taken MSB-FIRST, with o_i = AND if bit i of a is 1 and OR if it is 0 — nothing else, no borrow chain, no subtraction. For even a = 2^j k, just DROP THE LOW j BITS OF x and compare the remaining n-j bits against k; those j gates are free. OPTIMALITY IS PROVED, so stop searching: the degree bound MC >= deg(f) - 1 matches the construction exactly. VERIFIED HERE: the chain computes [a <= x] with 0 mismatches over all odd a and all x for n <= 10; the even-constant reduction likewise 0 mismatches; and the Theorem-1 cost equals deg-1 in all 174250 (a,b,n) cases for n = 2..9. SCOPE, HONESTLY: this is an AND-GATE result, so it is DIRECTLY the score for the GF(2) challenges (score = 2 x AND count). In the NATIVE R1CS challenges it does NOT beat what we already have — a chain of n-1 single-row AND/OR gates costs 2(n-1) = 510 for n = 256, against Khovratovich's measured 507 and the Bezout floor of 2k-1 — so do not spend a native slot reimplementing it. Use it for (a) the GF(2) challenges, (b) any place a two-sided bound is currently paid as two comparisons, and (c) the trailing-zero discount, which is free wherever a bound is a multiple of a power of two.

AUTOMATED LOWER BOUNDS FOR BILINEAR COMPLEXITY — a TOOL for the tensor-rank entry above, not just a theorem. arXiv:2603.07280 (2026), 'Automated Lower Bounds for Bilinear Complexity over Finite Fields': encodes the bilinear-rank question as a constraint system and derives lower bounds automatically for ARBITRARY bilinear maps at moderate sizes. Headline: the bound for 3x3x3 matrix multiplication over F_2 was raised to 20, improving a value that had stood since 2003. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: tensor rank IS the minimum number of rank-1 rows for a bilinear map, so this is a way to COMPUTE the row floor for one of our sub-problems instead of guessing at it — point it at a candidate gadget (a limb-product block, a small field multiplication, a chi-layer slice) and it tells you whether the current row count is already optimal. Use it as a STOPPING RULE: it proves when to abandon a direction, it does not produce a construction. Caveat: feasible only at moderate dimension, and no released code is identified in the paper, so budget implementation effort before committing a slot to it.

LAMBDA-PACKED TWIN-INSTANCE GADGETS — HALF A ROW PER BIT, BELOW THE SINGLE-ROW 'FLOOR'. The single-row non-vanishing-multiplier form gives 1 allocation + 1 constraint per output bit and looks like the floor. IT IS NOT, WHENEVER YOU NEED THE SAME FUNCTION TWICE. A 32-bit value occupies 32 of BN254's 254 bits, so pack TWO instances into ONE witness at a base lambda = 2^40 — z[j] = f(instance A)[j] + lambda*f(instance B)[j] — and pin both with ONE rank-1 row. MEASURED IN THE SHA-256 RECORD: packed Ch is 32 allocations + 32 constraints for BOTH rounds' Ch words (64 Ch bits), and packed Maj likewise: 0.5 alloc + 0.5 constr PER BIT, against 1+1 for the single-row form. THE Ch ROW, which pins z outright because the row reduces to 8*(z - honest) = 0 modulo the four input-booleanity relations and 8 is a unit: (-3e + 2f + 4g + 2*lambda*u)*(e - 2f + 4g - 2*lambda*u) + (3e + (8*lambda+4)f - 8g + 4*lambda^2*u - 8z) = 0. PREREQUISITE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN CONSTRAINT: the two instances must SHARE most of their inputs so the row stays affine in a small input set. SHA-256 supplies this for free by pairing ADJACENT ROUNDS — Ch_{t+1}(new_e, e, f) reuses e and f, Maj_{t+1}(new_a, a, b) reuses a and b. The packed word is then consumed ADDITIVELY downstream, which splits the two lambda-slots apart at no cost. SAVING measured at 128 score per round pair = 4096 per 512-bit block. LOOK FOR THIS ANYWHERE a gadget is instantiated twice on overlapping inputs — it is not SHA-256-specific.

THE OUT-OF-RANGE DECOY ROOT — USE A TWO-ROOT ROW AND LET A DOWNSTREAM RANGE CHECK DISAMBIGUATE FOR FREE. A row (z - r1)*(z - r2) = 0 is one constraint but does NOT pin z: it admits two solutions, which is normally why the single-row non-vanishing-multiplier form is preferred. THE TRICK IS TO MAKE THE WRONG SOLUTION ARITHMETICALLY UNREACHABLE INSTEAD OF EXCLUDING IT WITH A SECOND ROW. Choose r1, r2 so that on every boolean input assignment exactly one root is the honest value and the other is displaced by a huge power of two Omega; the consuming addition already lives in a bounded window and rejects the decoy at zero extra cost. MEASURED (packed Maj of two SHA-256 rounds, 32 allocations + 32 constraints for 64 Maj bits), with lambda = 2^40 and Omega = 2^80: (z - ((1+lambda)a + Omega*(a-b))) * (z - (c + lambda*u + Omega*(1-a-b))) = 0. When a = b the first factor is the honest maj(a,b,c) + lambda*maj(u,a,b) and Omega*(a-b) vanishes; when a != b the second factor is honest and Omega*(1-a-b) vanishes. Either way the decoy is Omega away and a 35-bit-slot packed addition cannot absorb 2^80. WHERE THE COST GOES: nothing extra in rows, but the SOUNDNESS PROOF MOVES INTO THE ADDER — you must prove its operands are bounded. WHEN TO REACH FOR IT: any boolean function outside the 192 single-row-native ones, or any packed pair with no non-vanishing affine multiplier. The two-root form ALWAYS exists (interpolate through the two branch values) and is always one row.

A VALUE CONSUMED ONLY AS A FIELD SUM MUST NEVER BE BIT-DECOMPOSED — AUDIT EVERY MATERIALISED WORD FOR THIS. Bits cost 32 allocations + 32 booleanity constraints per word. Ask of each word: does ANY consumer read an INDIVIDUAL BIT (a rotation, a shift, a boolean gate)? If every consumer reads only its numeric value, keep it as an affine Expression and never witness it. THREE MEASURED INSTANCES IN THE SHA-256 RECORD, all free: (1) THE LAST TWO SCHEDULE WORDS w62, w63 — terminal, because a schedule step reads w[i-2] and w[i-15] so nothing later reads their bits, and rounds 62/63 consume them inside their own mod-2^32 reduction; since (X + w_raw) mod 2^32 = (X + w_raw mod 2^32) mod 2^32 the UNREDUCED 34-bit sum is handed over directly, 58/58 instead of 91/92, saving 134 score per block. (2) W0 OF EVERY BLOCK — only ever read as w_{i-16}, i.e. purely additive, so it is an affine combination of the raw message bytes with the out-of-range bytes gated one row each: 16 rows, 0 allocations, and it deletes 112 low-bit allocations. (3) THE FINAL PADDING-ONLY BLOCK, whose content is fixed by the message length, has its ENTIRE 64-word schedule as an affine function of 8 length flags — the schedule term vanishes from its cost definition altogether. GENERAL RULE: bits are an interface requirement of rotation and boolean gates, NOT of arithmetic.

ONE-HOT SELECTION FROM A WITNESSED FIELD INDEX COSTS n-2 ROWS VIA BINOMIAL MOMENTS — NO BIT DECOMPOSITION, NO EQUALITY TREE. To prove a length-n flag vector F is the indicator of a witnessed index L (variable-length padding, data-dependent branches, selecting among n precomputed constants), do NOT decompose L or emit n equality gadgets. The moments M_d = sum_k F[k]*C(k,d) are FREE affine combinations because the binomials are compile-time constants. Assert PASCAL'S RECURRENCE for d = 1..n-2: (L - d)*M_d - (d+1)*M_{d+1} = 0. Together with M_0 = sum F = 1 and M_1 = sum k*F[k] = L this forces M_d = C(L,d) for every d, which forces F to be one-hot at L. MEASURED at n = 256: 254 rank-1 rows, and THE TWO NORMALISATION EQUATIONS COST ZERO because only 254 of the 256 flags are witnessed and the last two are DEFINED to make them hold identically: tailHigh := L - sum_{j<254} j*F[j] - 254*(1 - sum_{j<254} F[j]), then tailLow := (1 - sum F[j]) - tailHigh. TOTAL 508 score for a 256-way one-hot pinned to a field element, against roughly 8 + 256 + 256 for decompose-then-compare. The flags are then reusable as FREE affine selectors everywhere downstream. NOTE how this relates to the proved 2^w - w - 1 one-hot lower bound: that bound is for building a one-hot from w BOOLEAN BITS; this is the different and cheaper problem of pinning a one-hot to a FIELD ELEMENT.

GATED BOOLEANITY — ONE ROW DOES BOOLEANITY AND CONDITIONAL ZEROING. When a witness bit must be boolean IF a region is active and ZERO otherwise, do not emit b*(b-1) = 0 plus a separate masking row. Emit b*(b - active) = 0 with `active` an affine boolean: at active = 1 it is exactly booleanity, at active = 0 it forces b = 0. MEASURED in a 255-byte variable-length padding check: covers all 7 witnessed low bits of every byte at 7 rows per byte with no masking rows, and it is what makes 'every byte past the message length is zero' free. Costs nothing, saves one row per gated bit. GENERALISES to any conditionally-present witness.

ADDING A COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT MAKES THE LOW BITS OF THE RESULT AFFINE — CHARGE 32 MINUS THE CONSTANT'S 2-ADIC STRUCTURE. In z = b + C mod 2^32 with C a constant there is no carry into bit 0, so z[0] = b[0] XOR C[0], which is affine (1 - b[0] when C is odd). If C = 2 mod 4 the low TWO bits are affine; if C = 4 mod 8, the low three. Witness only the remaining high bits and start the affine carry chain there. MEASURED: an odd-constant 32-bit adder is 31 allocations / 31 constraints, a C = 2 mod 4 adder is 30/30, a C = 4 mod 8 adder is 29/29, against 32/32 for the general two-operand adder. APPLIED TO SHA-256's BLOCK-0 CHAINING ADD against the IV: H1, H6, H7 odd give 31 each; H2 = 0x3c6ef372 and H3 = 0xa54ff53a are 2 mod 4 giving 30 each; H5 = 0x9b05688c is 4 mod 8 giving 29 — 182 instead of 192, a free 20 score. ALSO APPLIES to every round-constant add and to length-encoding words. Check the 2-adic valuation of EVERY constant addend in the circuit.

THE RANGE CHECK IS THE OUTPUT ENCODING — BYTE SERIALISATION OF A FIELD ELEMENT SHOULD COST ZERO. Any emulated field value that must be proved canonical (x < p) is ALREADY bit-decomposed. If the interface wants that value as bytes, build each byte as the affine combination sum_{j<8} b_{8t+j}*2^j OF THE VERY BITS THE RANGE CHECK ALLOCATED — affine combinations are free, so serialisation costs nothing. MEASURED: a standalone ToBytes for one 256-bit coordinate is 256 allocations / 260 constraints; folding it into the validator makes it 0/0, saving 1032 score for a two-coordinate point output. In the secp256k1 record the dedicated ToBytes and PointOutput gadgets survive only as proof-side specs and never enter the operation chain. GENERALISES TO EVERY MULTI-CONSUMER BIT VECTOR: whenever two passes over the same value both need its bits — range check, comparison, serialisation, bit-selection, a boolean gate — allocate the bits ONCE and make every other consumer an affine function of them. Audit the circuit for any value that is decomposed twice.

FIELD SUBTRACTION SHOULD COST EXACTLY ZERO ROWS — CARRY AN UNREDUCED BIASED REPRESENTATION AND PARAMETERISE THE MODMUL TO ACCEPT IT. Do not reduce a - b before feeding it to the next multiplication. Represent it limbwise as a[k] + borrow[k] - b[k] where borrow is a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT limb vector encoding 2p (for secp256k1: borrow[0] = 2^65 - 2^33 - 1954, borrow[k>0] = 2^65 - 2), chosen so every limb stays non-negative and below 3*2^64 with total value below 3p. That expression is AFFINE, hence free. Then instantiate the modmul certificate with input bounds Ca, Cb <= 4*2^64 — THE FOLDED CERTIFICATE'S COST IS INVARIANT IN THOSE BOUNDS (still 184/186); only the carry-width proof obligation moves. MEASURED: every x2-x1, y2-y1, x1-x3, 2y and beta*x difference in the affine chord/tangent/double formulas becomes 0/0, where a SubMod that materialises a canonical difference costs 285/294. The secp256k1 record contains ZERO explicit subtraction gadgets in its fused double-add. COMPOSES WITH sum-of-products: the same slack lets a fused r = a*b - s1 - s2 mod p put s1 and s2 straight into the certificate target unreduced, so a multiply-subtract-two costs the SAME as a plain multiply.

KEEP A VALUE AS A (2m-1)-CELL POLYNOMIAL IF IT IS ONLY EVER CONSUMED AS THE TARGET OF ANOTHER MODULAR CERTIFICATE — MUX AT THE POLYNOMIAL LEVEL, NOT THE FIELD LEVEL. Worked example, a Weierstrass slope that must divide by either x2-x1 (chord) or 2y (tangent), with numerator either y2-y1 or 3x^2. NAIVE: reduce x^2, scale by 3, mux against dy, then run a division certificate — TWO reductions. INSTEAD: compute Pxx = interpolatedMul(x,x) as a RAW 7-cell convolution (7 allocations / 7 constraints, never reduced), mux the 7-cell vector 3*Pxx against the zero-padded dy (7 more rows, one per cell), and hand the resulting POLYNOMIAL directly to a single certificate lambda*den = target (mod p). The square never becomes a field element. MEASURED: fused select-and-divide is 476/481 — IsZeroFeSum 2/2, three 4-limb muxes, interpolatedMul 7/7, a 7-cell mux 7/7, 4 result witnesses, canonical validator 260/267, one folded certificate 184/186 — against 999/1008 for reduce-then-divide. 1050 SCORE SAVED PER SLOPE, and there are two slopes per scalar-mul iteration. GENERAL RULE: selection, scaling by small constants, and addition all work at the polynomial level for one row per cell, and only the final certificate pays for a reduction.

STATE A SUB-CIRCUIT'S SPEC AS A CONGRUENCE, NOT A CANONICAL VALUE — THIS CAN MAKE A WHOLE GADGET FREE. A 256-bit scalar supplied as bits does NOT need a witnessed canonical remainder mod the group order: packing the bits into 4x64-bit limbs is a pure affine recombination (limb_k = sum_t bit*2^t) and the value it denotes is already in the right congruence class. The secp256k1 record's ScalarReduce is literally `pure (packBits input.bits)` with a proved cost of ZERO, and its Spec is stated modulo the group order rather than as an equality. AVOIDED: a witnessed remainder plus quotient with Normalize on both plus a LessThan is about 980 allocations / 989 constraints. THE PRECONDITION IS THE WHOLE TRICK — state the Spec as value % n = scalar % n and then CHECK THAT EVERY CONSUMER ONLY NEEDS THE CONGRUENCE CLASS. AUDIT EVERY Normalize AND LessThan IN A DESIGN AGAINST THIS QUESTION before assuming canonicality is required; each one that turns out to be unnecessary is worth hundreds of rows.

FOR A LARGE CONSTANT TABLE, NEVER MATERIALISE THE ONE-HOT — FACTOR IT AND PAY PER OUTPUT WIRE. The 2^w - w - 1 one-hot minimum is real but it is the WRONG COST MODEL above about w = 6: at w = 11 a flat one-hot is 2036 multiplications. Instead split w = wi + wo, build the two smaller one-hots independently (2^wi - wi - 1 and 2^wo - wo - 1 multiplications), and DO NOT tensor them into a flat vector. The 2^w-entry lookup for output wire L becomes sel_L = inner(L, 2^wo - 1) + sum_{q < 2^wo - 1} outer_q * (inner(L,q) - inner(L, 2^wo - 1)), where inner(L,q) = sum_{a < 2^wi} innerHot[a] * T[2^wi*q + a] is a FREE affine combination of the inner one-hot cells with compile-time coefficients. TOTAL = (2^wi - wi - 1) + (2^wo - wo - 1) + N*(2^wo - 1) multiplications for N output wires, against 2^w - w - 1 for the flat build. MEASURED IN THE 68797 FIXED-BASE RECORD: w = 11 magnitude bits, wi = 7, wo = 4, N = 12 output wires (4 x-limbs, 4 (p-y)-limbs, 4 delta-limbs) gives 130 + 11 + 180 = 321 multiplications, plus 11 sign XNORs and 4 final y wires = 336/336 per window; 21 windows = 14112 score. Against 2036 for the flat one-hot in ONE window. SWEEP wo: at N = 12, w = 11 the optimum is wo = 4 (wo = 3 gives 335, wo = 5 gives 455). THE COROLLARY THAT DECIDES WINDOW WIDTH: the marginal cost of a wider window is (2^wi growth) + N*(2^wo - 1), NOT 2^w — which is why w = 12 and w = 13 are affordable at all. USE THE FLAT MONOMIAL BASIS ONLY WHEN 2^w IS SMALL RELATIVE TO N: the same record uses it for its 4-bit top window at 11 = 2^4 - 4 - 1 monomials with all 8 output limbs free, total 11/11.

TESTING 'THESE INPUT BITS EQUAL THIS CONSTANT' COSTS ZERO ALLOCATIONS. Given boolean bits b_0..b_255 and a compile-time constant k, the MISMATCH COUNT sum_i (if bit_i(k) then 1 - b_i else b_i) is a PURELY AFFINE expression, lies in [0, 256] so it cannot wrap in the native field, and is zero exactly when the bits encode k. It costs NOTHING — no witness, no row. Only the zero TEST costs anything, and two of them can share: EitherZero materialises the product a*b and runs ONE IsZeroField for 3/3, one row cheaper than two independent zero tests plus an addition. MEASURED: the fixed-base record screens FOUR exceptional scalars (0, the group order n, 2^253-2, and an odd doubling scalar) with two EitherZero calls and two 8-wide affine muxes — 22 allocations + 22 constraints = 44 score, 0.06% of the circuit, for the ENTIRE exceptional-case handling of a whole scalar multiplication. GENERAL RULE: any predicate that is an affine function of the input bits and cannot wrap is free — push all constant-comparison logic into that form before reaching for a comparator gadget.

SHARING ONE REDUCTION ACROSS SEVERAL PRODUCTS IS LEGAL; MERGING TWO INDEPENDENT CONGRUENCES INTO ONE ROW IS NOT. Conflating these will make a job refuse a legal optimisation, so state the line precisely. ILLEGAL: taking two independent equations E1 = 0 mod p and E2 = 0 mod p and asserting E1 + z*E2 = 0 for a witnessed or prover-chosen z — that is a Schwartz-Zippel argument and needs a verifier CHALLENGE, which this cost model does not provide. LEGAL, AND WORTH A GREAT DEAL: ONE integer identity whose target happens to contain an unreduced linear combination of several convolutions. Both secp256k1 records do exactly this — a squared term and a difference muxed together at the POLYNOMIAL level and closed by a single folded certificate, and two products carried under one quotient and one carry chain. THE TEST TO APPLY: is there a SINGLE quotient q and a SINGLE carry chain certifying a SINGLE equation over the integers? Then it is sound no matter how many products the target contains.

DEFERRED-Y ACCUMULATORS: THE INVARIANT, THE TWO PRODUCTION PRECEDENTS, AND THE SIDE CONDITION THAT DECIDES WHETHER IT IS LEGAL. The invariant is Eisentraeger-Lauter-Montgomery READ BACKWARDS. ELM solves 2P+Q = (P+Q)+P for lam2 given a known y1; in a circuit `compute` is replaced by `constrain`, so you may instead solve the SAME identity for y_A given witnessed lam1, lam2: 2*y_A = (lam1 + lam2)*(x_A - x_R) with x_R = lam1^2 - x_A - x_P. Verbatim from halo2_gadgets/src/ecc/chip/mul/incomplete.rs: '/// Derives the expression Y_A = (lambda_1 + lambda_2) * (x_a - x_r);' and from the halo2 book: 'y_A,3^witnessed is assigned to a cell. This is unlike previous y_A,i's, which were implicitly derived from lambda_1,i, lambda_2,i, x_A,i, x_T, but never actually assigned.' Only x_A is carried row to row; the chaining works because y_A,i comes from row i's slopes and y_A,i-1 from row i+1's — an ADJACENT-ROW substitution. Sinsemilla strengthens it to eliminate the ADDEND's y too and blends the boundary with a selector rather than duplicating the gate. SECOND PRECEDENT: Aztec barretenberg stdlib/primitives/biggroup carries `struct chain_add_accumulator { Fq x1_prev, y1_prev, lambda_prev, x3_prev; }` with acc.y = lambda_prev*(x1_prev - x) - y1_prev, materialising once in chain_add_end. ITS ENABLING PRIMITIVE IS THE FUSED NON-NATIVE GADGET Fq::msub_div(a, b, d, c) = -(sum a_i b_i + sum c_j)/d — WITHOUT AN ANALOGUE THE SUBSTITUTION RELOCATES THE MULTIPLICATION RATHER THAN ELIMINATING IT, which plausibly explains the negatives. CLEAN NEGATIVES, DO NOT RE-SEARCH: arkworks r1cs-std (double_and_add_unchecked cites ELM03 but is DEAD CODE never reached from scalar_mul_le), gnark sw_emulated and sw_bls12377/24315 ('// omit y2 computation' is one-step ELM only), noir_bigcurve (witnesses lambda as a hint then discards it and range-checks a full y3 every step), Noir stdlib, o1js — NONE carries a y-free accumulator across iterations. ELM 2003 sec 3.1 and Ciet-Joye-Lauter-Montgomery 2006 chain it only to depth 2 and both note the chain BREAKS AT A DOUBLING because lam = 3x^2/2y needs y explicitly; no paper chains a deferred y across a doubling. Lopez-Dahab (x, lam) is BINARY FIELD ONLY. THE ONE SIDE CONDITION THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING: the invariant is an EQUATION DEFINING y, so it defines y only when its coefficient (x_A - x_R) is NONZERO. Where that fails the accumulator's y goes UNCONSTRAINED — a SOUNDNESS hole, not merely a completeness one, and distinct from the ordinary incomplete-addition side condition. Halo2 discharges it with an INDEX-LEVEL argument (Halo paper Thm 3: two points with distinct nonzero indices in -(q-1)/2 .. (q-1)/2 have different x), run as an integer shadow loop; for Pallas it fails at i = 252 so the last 3 iterations use COMPLETE addition. BEFORE PORTING THIS ANYWHERE, CHECK THAT (i) no lookup entry can be the identity, and (ii) you can run the analogous index argument — which needs all bases FIXED and PUBLIC with bounded integer indices. If any base is WITNESSED BY THE PROVER the argument collapses and the technique is UNSOUND. Also budget for degree: substituting y_A raises halo2's gates to degree 4-5, which is free in PlonKish and NOT free in R1CS.

MULTIPLICATIVE-COMPLEXITY LOWER BOUNDS: WHAT IS ACTUALLY KNOWN, AND THE UNIT ERROR THAT MAKES IT LOOK BETTER THAN IT IS. NO SUPERLINEAR MC LOWER BOUND IS KNOWN FOR ANY EXPLICIT FUNCTION, and the barrier is structural: MC(f) <= C_{B2}(f) always, so any superlinear explicit MC bound SUBSUMES the superlinear general-circuit-size problem — one of complexity theory's flagship open questions. Boyar-Find (arXiv:1407.6169) verbatim: 'there is no value of n where a concrete (n,1)-function has been exhibited with a proof that more than n - 1 AND gates are necessary'. Kojevnikov-Kulikov (CiE 2010) verbatim: 'Even a function with multiplicative complexity at least n is not known.' THE STATE OF THE ART: single-output (n,1) is n - 1 (Schnorr's DEGREE BOUND, MC >= deg - 1, AAECC 1988/89 — and note Boyar-Find's footnote that 'despite the name, this is not the same as Strassen's degree bound'); symmetric non-linear (n,1) is floor(n/2); multi-output (n,n) is 2n - 3 (Boyar-Find Thm 5) and that is now EXACTLY TIGHT via Haner arXiv:2307.07424; restricted to quadratic/SigmaPiSigma circuits only, > 2.32n. Random functions need ~2^(n/2) by counting (Boyar-Peralta-Pochuev, TCS 235(1), 2000). MC(Hamming weight) = n - H(n) exactly (Boyar-Peralta TCS 2008). The ONLY explicit single-output function ever proved to beat n-1 is a 6-variable one at MC = 6 (Calik-Turan-Peralta), found by exhaustive search at one fixed n, not an asymptotic family. THE UNIT ERROR TO AVOID: the famous 2n, 2.5n, 3n and 3.1n bounds are NOT multiplicative complexity — they count EVERY gate over the full binary basis B2. Stockmeyer 1977 (2.5n), Find-Golovnev-Hirsch-Kulikov FOCS 2016 ((3 + 1/86)n) and Li-Yang STOC 2022 (3.1n) are all B2 circuit complexity. There is no 2n / 2.5n / 3n MC lower bound. The one genuine crossover runs the other way: Kojevnikov-Kulikov derive a 7n/3 B2-circuit bound FROM the MC degree bound.

THE DIRECT-SUM QUESTION FOR BOOLEAN MULTIPLICATIVE COMPLEXITY IS APPARENTLY UNSTUDIED — WHICH MATTERS WHENEVER A ROUND IS MANY DISJOINT S-BOXES. 'Is MC(f1 (+) f2) = MC(f1) + MC(f2) for disjoint variable sets' appears never to have been stated as a conjecture, an open problem, or a theorem: an arXiv full-metadata query for 'multiplicative complexity' AND 'direct sum' returns ZERO results, and greps of Boyar-Find, Calik-Turan-Peralta and Sonmez Turan's BFA 2023 survey find no hits for 'direct sum', 'composition', 'additive' or 'amortiz'. Only the trivial subadditive bound MC(S_k o ... o S_1) <= sum MC(S_i) is used, always constructively. SHITOV DOES NOT TRANSFER: his counterexamples to Strassen's direct sum conjecture (Acta Mathematica 222(2), 2019) are about TENSOR RANK over infinite fields — a full-text grep finds ZERO hits for 'Boolean', 'GF(2)' or 'F2' — and tensor rank (bilinear algorithms) is not Boolean MC (arbitrary circuits), while direct sum (disjoint inputs) is not composition (sequential rounds). WHERE AN ADDITIVITY PROOF WOULD LIVE: Mirwald & Schnorr, 'The multiplicative complexity of quadratic Boolean forms', TCS 102(2):307-328, 1992, reportedly characterises computational independence of two quadratic forms, i.e. exactly when L(f1, f2) = L(f1) + L(f2). chi is quadratic, so a 320-fold direct-sum argument would go there. UNVERIFIED — ScienceDirect 403s every fetch. IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: for OUR GF(2) challenges this open question is MOOT, because the harness restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A, B affine and every output affine in (x, w), and in THAT model the dimension argument gives additivity outright. The open question bites only for general Boolean circuits.

THE BEZOUT ROW FLOOR NEEDS A DIMENSION HALF, AND WITH IT IT IS EXACT: A GADGET PINNING A VALUE TO A FINITE SET OF SIZE 2^k COSTS 2k, OR 2k-1 MARGINALLY. The row-only form we have been quoting ('r rank-1 rows accept at most 2^r values by Bezout') proves r >= k and says nothing about allocations, so it does not actually establish the 2k-1 figure. The complete statement uses Heintz's Bezout inequality: for f_1..f_r of degree <= 2 in A^N, the sum of the degrees of the irreducible components of V(f_1..f_r) is at most 2^min(r,N). If the accepted set of a designated affine form is finite of size S, then S <= (number of components) <= 2^min(r,N), so BOTH r >= log2 S AND N >= log2 S. Allocations + rows >= 2*log2 S. When the value being pinned is already allocated for another reason, N counts it and the marginal charge is (k-1) allocations + k rows = 2k-1. THREE COROLLARIES THAT CLOSE STANDING QUESTIONS. (a) Accepting a SUPERSET never helps: a finite acceptor of size 2^(k+s) costs >= 2(k+s), and completeness forces size >= 2^k, so loosening a bound strictly costs more. (b) Higher-radix digit decompositions TIE EXACTLY rather than 'at best': composing quadratics w1 = z^2+az, w2 = w1^2+b, ..., w_{k-1}(w_{k-1}-c) = 0 realises any degree-2^k root set in k-1 allocations + k rows, the same 2k-1 as booleanity, and this includes the popular x(x-1)(x-2)(x-3) = 0 trick (1 allocation + 2 rows for 2 bits). (c) THE F_p ESCAPE HATCH IS REAL BUT USELESS FOR RANGES. Bezout is a statement over the algebraic closure, so an F_p-specific gadget can restrict F_p-points without cutting dimension — this is exactly the z1^2 = d*z2^2 phenomenon that broke an earlier claim of ours. Checked here: the natural family is multiplicative, y^d = z restricting z to a coset of index d, and it costs about 2*log2(d) — EXACTLY 2 per bit again — and produces a coset, not an interval. So no F_p trick beats 2 per bit and none of them certifies integer smallness. USE THIS AS A STOPPING RULE, AND NOTE ITS SCOPE: it bounds a GADGET whose accepted set is finite. It says nothing about a circuit as a whole, where the accepted set is parameterised by the inputs and the floor is 2*log2(number of accepted input tuples) — typically orders of magnitude below what any known construction achieves. *** QUALIFIED — THIS IS PROVED ONLY FOR GADGETS WITH A FINITE ACCEPTOR, AND THE RANGE CHECK'S OWN ACCEPTOR NEED NOT BE FINITE. I have been quoting '2 per bit, PROVED OPTIMAL' throughout, and the hypothesis was never checked. Normalize32's designated object CANNOT be a single field element, because 2^256 > r ~ 2^254 so [0, 2^256) does not inject into F_r; the designated object is the 8-LIMB TUPLE, so the acceptor is a set A in F_r^8 containing S^8 with S = [0, 2^32). IN A^1 EVERY PROPER SUBVARIETY IS FINITE AND BEZOUT BITES AUTOMATICALLY; IN A^8 IT DOES NOT. If A is positive-dimensional, Heintz-Bezout gives only deg A <= 2^rows, and the minimum degree of any variety containing the grid S^8 is |S| = 2^32 by Schwartz-Zippel — which yields rows >= 32, NOT 256. TWO COUNTING FACTS NARROW BUT DO NOT CLOSE IT: by Lang-Weil a positive-dimensional component over F_r has at least r^d - O(D^2 r^(d-1/2)) points, so for d >= 2 that is 2^508 against a safe box of at most 2^280 and only d = 1 survives — AND IT SURVIVES ONLY BECAUSE 2^256 > r, so if BN254's r were at least 2^258 the escape would be closed by pigeonhole and THE WHOLE HOLE IS TWO BITS OF FIELD MARGIN. For an irreducible curve, Bombieri's character-sum bound forces D^2 >~ 2^127, i.e. D >= 2^63.5 and rows >= 63. SO THE HONEST FLOOR FOR A 256-BIT JOINT ACCEPTOR IS ABOUT 127 SCORE, NOT 512, a 4x gap, worth about 119,000 nominal across the variable-base tree. DO NOT FUND A SEARCH: the object required is an absolutely irreducible curve over F_r of degree at least 2^63 in A^8 containing the full base-2^32 digit grid and essentially none of its complement — an algebraic parameterisation of digit extraction — and a 63-row gadget produces degree at most 2^63, EXACTLY the Bombieri threshold with zero margin, which is the signature of a loose bound rather than an existence hint. THE REASON TO RECORD THIS IS THAT 'PROVED OPTIMAL' IS WHAT STOPS ANYONE LOOKING, AND AS STATED IT WAS FALSE. ***

THE RANGE CHECK IS THE FLOOR AND IT IS A BEZOUT FLOOR — SO OPTIMISE THE *NUMBER* OF MATERIALISED VALUES, NEVER THE ENCODING OF ONE. An R1CS row is rank-1, hence degree 2, so by Bezout the solution set of m rows projects onto any single coordinate in at most 2^m points; isolating the 2^k integers in [0, 2^k) therefore needs m >= k ROWS, and with the top-bit-free trick k rows + (k-1) allocations = 2k-1 score is EXACTLY optimal. Both secp256k1 records already sit on this floor (4 x 64 bits = 252 allocations + 256 constraints = 508). CONSEQUENCES: (a) no packing, no lambda-trick, no twin-instance trick can beat 1 constraint per bit for a RANGE check — unlike boolean functions, where packing does reach 0.5 rows per bit — so stop looking; (b) in any emulated-field circuit score ~= 2 * (total range-check bits), and total bits = 256 * (materialised elements) + per-certificate quotient and carry bits, which makes 'HOW MANY VALUES MUST EXIST' the only structural question; (c) production libraries all agree that only the LIMB bounds are a soundness requirement and full canonicality (x < p) is merely uniqueness — o1js splits Unreduced / AlmostReduced / Canonical and its AlmostReduced compares ONLY the top limb against the modulus; halo2-ecc's carry_mod explicitly does not constrain out < p; gnark separates Reduce from ReduceStrict. AUDIT EVERY CANONICALITY TAIL against 'does any consumer need uniqueness, or only the congruence class?' *** QUALIFIED — THIS IS PROVED ONLY FOR GADGETS WITH A FINITE ACCEPTOR, AND THE RANGE CHECK'S OWN ACCEPTOR NEED NOT BE FINITE. If A is positive-dimensional, Heintz-Bezout gives only deg A <= 2^rows, and the minimum degree of any variety containing the grid S^8 is |S| = 2^32 by Schwartz-Zippel — which yields rows >= 32, NOT 256.
