For an irreducible curve, Bombieri's character-sum bound forces D^2 >~ 2^127, i.e. D >= 2^63.5 and rows >= 63. SO THE HONEST FLOOR FOR A 256-BIT JOINT ACCEPTOR IS ABOUT 127 SCORE, NOT 512, a 4x gap, worth about 119,000 nominal across the variable-base tree. DO NOT FUND A SEARCH: the object required is an absolutely irreducible curve over F_r of degree at least 2^63 in A^8 containing the full base-2^32 digit grid and essentially none of its complement — an algebraic parameterisation of digit extraction — and a 63-row gadget produces degree at most 2^63, EXACTLY the Bombieri threshold with zero margin, which is the signature of a loose bound rather than an existence hint. THE REASON TO RECORD THIS IS THAT 'PROVED OPTIMAL' IS WHAT STOPS ANYONE LOOKING, AND AS STATED IT WAS FALSE. ***

BOUND-PROPAGATION RULES FROM PRODUCTION EMULATED-FIELD LIBRARIES, AS HARD NUMBERS TO CHECK YOUR OWN AGAINST. gnark std/math/emulated tracks an overflow parameter f per element: add f' = max(f0,f1) + 1; sub f' = max(f1+1, f0) + 1; mul f' = w + ceil(log2 nbResLimbs) + fa + fb; and it forces a reduce when w + f exceeds maxOverflow = FieldBitLen - 2 - w. At w = 64 on BN254 that is 188, so a plain product has f = 67 (131-bit limbs), a triple product f = 135 (199-bit limbs), and a QUADRUPLE product f = 203 > 188 — i.e. gnark's own analysis permits exactly TWO chained unreduced multiplications at 4x64. halo2-ecc asserts the same shape (num_limbs_log2_ceil + a.max_limb_bits + b.max_limb_bits <= NUM_BITS - 2); Barretenberg uses MAX_ADDITION_LOG = 10 (1024 free additions) and max unreduced value 2^((msb(M)-1)/2). NOTE THE TRAP THIS EXPOSES FOR A PSEUDO-MERSENNE FOLD: those libraries do not fold, so their limit is the RAW limb width, while a folded certificate must additionally survive multiplying a position by the fold constant AND packing a whole group into one native element — which is why a triple product fits gnark's rule at 4x64 but overflows a folded grouped-carry check there. ALSO WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE REACHES FOR CRT / 'CASTING OUT PRIMES': 2^256 * r_BN254 = 2^509.6 < p^2 = 2^512 for secp256k1, so a two-modulus CRT at t = 256 cannot certify even ONE raw product — this is exactly why Barretenberg uses 4 x 68-bit limbs — and post-fold the certified integer is only about 2^297, at which point the folded grouped-carry scheme (1 carry) already beats CRT (2 carries).

SHARPENING OF THE MASTER COST LAW: SPLIT M INTO CANONICALISED AND MERELY-RANGE-CHECKED ELEMENTS, BECAUSE THEY COST DIFFERENT AMOUNTS. The law score ~= 2*M*(256 + Wq + Wc) treats every materialised emulated element alike, but measured in the secp256k1 tree a materialised element that is only RANGE-CHECKED costs 252/256 (four ToBitsAffine 63 limb decompositions proving value < 2^256) while one that is additionally CANONICALISED costs 260/267 (the same plus the sparse-prime x < p tail: 3 IsZeroField + 2 prefix products + 3 quadratic assertions). The gap is exactly 8 allocations + 11 constraints = 19 score. So write M = M_normalized + M_canonical and charge the tail only to the second. THE DESIGN QUESTION THIS EXPOSES: canonicity is UNIQUENESS, not soundness — a value that is only ever consumed as an operand of another modular certificate never needs to be the canonical representative, and in an affine EC circuit that covers every witnessed SLOPE. Audit every canonicality assertion against 'does any consumer need uniqueness, or only the congruence class?' — in our variable-base circuit 136 of them did not.

HARNESS COST MODEL, READ FROM SOURCE AND COMPLETE — DO NOT RE-DERIVE. flatOperationCount is `.witness m -> <m,0>`, `.assert -> <0,1>`, `.lookup -> Count.zero`, `.interact -> Count.zero`; operationCount on `.subcircuit s` is nestedCount s.ops. THE FULL LIST OF OP-EMITTING PRIMITIVES (exhaustive, from the ExplicitCircuit instances): witnessVar/witnessField (.witness 1), witnessVars/witnessVector m (ONE .witness m op), ProvableType.witness (.witness (size M)), assertZero (.assert), lookup, Channel.emit/pull/push (.interact), and the subcircuit family. NOTHING ELSE EMITS AN OPERATION. FREE, EXACTLY: pure, map, every Expression built from +, -, multiplication by a CONSTANT and division by a nonzero constant, and — worth stating because it kills a whole family of received wisdom — ARBITRARY ROW DENSITY: A, B and C may each be sums of thousands of terms at zero cost, so every 'reduce the number of nonzero coefficients' technique from practical R1CS is worth EXACTLY ZERO here. LOOKUPS AND INTERACTIONS COST ZERO BUT ARE HARD-BANNED: flatOperationsIsR1CS maps them to False and isR1CS is a required theorem in all eight configs, including inside subcircuits. THE DECLARED COST IS AN EQUALITY — CostIs c K := forall n, operationCount = K, and circuitCost quantifies over ALL inputs — so nothing can be under- OR over-declared, and no circuit may have an input-dependent shape.

THE MASTER CONSTRAINT: AT MOST ONE PRODUCT PER ROW, CHECKED SYNTACTICALLY — EVERY GADGET TRICK IN THIS CORPUS IS A COROLLARY OF IT. r1csProducts on an `.add` node SUMS the two counts, and isR1CSRow demands the total be <= 1. THREE CONSEQUENCES THAT ARE LOAD-BEARING AND WERE NOT WRITTEN DOWN. (1) AN EXPRESSION CONTAINING TWO affine*affine PRODUCTS CANNOT APPEAR IN ANY ASSERT AT ALL — it is not 'two rows', it is REJECTED; an expression with J products costs J-1 extra materialisations, each itself a row. (2) THE CHECK IS SYNTACTIC, so a*b + a*c is REJECTED even though it is genuinely rank 1 — factor it by hand as a*(b+c). (3) `degree` is a structural over-approximation with no cancellation (degree (a*b) = degree a + degree b, degree (a+b) = max), so x + 0*y*z is NOT Affine. THE WHOLE LANGUAGE OF THIS HARNESS IS THEREFORE: affine forms are free and unbounded; exactly one product per row; every value that cannot be written that way costs 1 allocation + 1 row. Ask of every expression you build — how many products does it contain, and which single row is going to spend it?

A MUX COSTS NOTHING — CORRECTING THE 'Mux costs (size M, size M)' FIGURE I HAVE BEEN QUOTING. Clean's own Gadgets/Conditional.lean main emits ZERO OPERATIONS: it builds selector*(trueVars[i] - falseVars[i]) + falseVars[i] and returns it. The (size M, size M) figure is the cost of OUR OWN Solution/.../Mux.lean, which chooses to witness the result and emit one assertZero per cell — A DESIGN DECISION, NOT A HARNESS CHARGE. THE REAL RULE IS A DEGREE RULE. (a) If ifTrue - ifFalse has degree 0 — both constant, OR DIFFERING BY A COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT — the mux is AFFINE: free, unlimited reuse, never materialised. (b) Otherwise it carries EXACTLY ONE PRODUCT, so it is free IF AND ONLY IF it is the only product in the row that consumes it; if that row already has a product (an interpolatedMul cell, a modular certificate, a further mux level) it must be materialised at (1,1) per cell. AUDIT EVERY MATERIALISED MUX AGAINST (b) — and note the converse trap: a mux feeding the CHALLENGE OUTPUT must always be materialised, because AffineOutput is part of isR1CS.

ALLOCATIONS IS DEFINITIONALLY THE CIRCUIT'S localLength — A FREE HALF OF EVERY COST PROOF AND A FREE AUDIT. (operationCount ops).allocations = Operations.localLength ops holds by construction: witness contributes m to both, assert/lookup/interact contribute 0 to both, and for a subcircuit nestedCount s.ops = flatCount s.ops.toFlat whose allocations is s.localLength. The harness half-notices this — `Balanced c` is literally 'constraints = localLength'. CONSEQUENCES: (a) SCORE = elaborated.localLength + (number of asserts), so the ALLOCATION half of mainCost can be discharged from the ElaboratedCircuit field that `elaborate_circuit` already computes rather than by structural CostIs recursion; (b) any mismatch between a claimed allocation count and localLength is a BUG, checkable without touching the cost proof; (c) 'Balanced' in the canonical-challenge machinery is exactly the allocations == constraints condition, which is why canonical composition requires it.

computableWitness KILLS ProverHint AND ProverData OUTRIGHT — A WHOLE CLASS OF DESIGNS IS DEAD, CHECK BEFORE SPENDING A JOB ON IT. ProverEnvironment.AgreesBelow constrains ONLY `get`, but a ProverEnvironment also carries `data` and `hint`. Circuit.ComputableWitnesses quantifies over ALL env, env' agreeing below n and demands compute env = compute env'; the challenge hypothesis OnlyAccessedBelow is no help because Expression.eval reads only env.get. Take two environments identical in `get` but with different hints: AgreesBelow holds at every n, so the generator must agree ACROSS ALL HINTS AND ALL DATA. THEREFORE EVERY WITNESS GENERATOR MUST BE A TOTAL LEAN FUNCTION OF THE INPUT VARIABLES ALONE. ProverHint, GeneralFormalCircuit.WithHint, subcircuitWithHintAssertion and env.data are ALL UNUSABLE on all eight challenges — corroborated by every Interface.lean setting ProverSpec := True and ProverAssumptions := Assumptions, so nothing constrains a hint anyway. Any design of the form 'let the prover supply X as a hint' — a factorisation, a discrete log, a table index, an inverse — must instead COMPUTE X in Lean. COROLLARY ON BATCHING: witnessVector m emits ONE .witness m op whose generator must be computable from env BELOW its offset, i.e. NO INTRA-BATCH DEPENDENCIES; splitting into m separate witnessVar calls costs the identical m allocations and is strictly more permissive. There is never a cost reason to batch.

SUBCIRCUIT VERSUS INLINE: THE COST IS IDENTICAL, THE PROOF COST IS NOT — HERE IS THE RULE. CostIs.subcircuit proves the invocation costs EXACTLY the inner main's count, so the choice is purely proof and elaboration effort. WRAPPING BUYS: ConstraintsHold.Soundness uses forAllNoOffset, which for a subcircuit is `Assumptions -> Spec` and NEVER DESCENDS INTO THE SUBCIRCUIT'S ROWS. WRAPPING COSTS: both Assumptions and Spec of toSubcircuit are stated over `eval env input_var`, so every proof step carries an eval over the WHOLE routed ProvableType — routing a 16-wire ChainState instead of a 4-wire x is exactly why inlining won on stageC1/stageX. TWO FACTS THAT ARE FREE LEVERAGE. (1) PREFER FormalCircuit OVER FormalAssertion for anything producing a value: UsesLocalWitnessesCompleteness HANDS YOU the subcircuit's ProverSpec, which for a FormalCircuit is Assumptions -> Spec, so the parent's completeness gets the gadget's Spec FREE; for a FormalAssertion ProverSpec is True and ProverAssumptions is Assumptions AND Spec, so the parent must PROVE it. Same cost, strictly more work. (2) AffineOutput is required of `main` ONLY, never of subcircuits — a gadget may hand back a DEGREE-2 expression for free, and the check bites only where it lands in a row. PROVIDED COMBINATORS, EXHAUSTIVELY: pure, bind, map, witnessVector, witnessVar, witnessField, assertZero, subcircuit, assertion, forEach, mapFinRange, foldlRange. NOT PROVIDED: Circuit.foldl and Circuit.map. Circuit.foldl also demands a ConstantOutput autoparam that FAILS whenever the accumulator is a threaded affine expression — use foldlRange.

A CONSTRAINT WITHOUT AN ALLOCATION IS FREELY AVAILABLE ON SIX OF THE EIGHT CHALLENGES — SCOPE THE 'allocations >= constraints IS FORCED' RULE OR IT FORBIDS LEGAL CIRCUITS. assertZero over pre-existing variables is <0,1>: the AssertBytes BASELINE is 128 allocations / 144 constraints and our record is 112/128, so constraints strictly exceed allocations and this is legal. THE FORCING ARGUMENT APPLIES ONLY TO THE TWO isR1CS_Cidentity CHALLENGES (gf2-sha256, gf2-k12), where isCidentityRowAt pins one variable per ASSERT while witnesses leave the pin counter unchanged, so a row pinning a variable outside the circuit's own witness range is universally quantified in Completeness and only degenerate rows survive. DO NOT GENERALISE IT — doing so silently forbids terminal assertions, input booleanity and equality checks on the other six. TWO FURTHER CANONICAL-CHALLENGE FACTS, unrecorded: (a) since the pin counter advances only on asserts and the variable offset only on witnesses, witness and assert ops may be arbitrarily INTERLEAVED OR FULLY BATCHED provided the SEQUENCE of pinned variables is n, n+1, ...; (b) on ALL challenges a row may reference a variable allocated LATER in the same circuit, because UsesLocalWitnessesCompleteness covers main's entire operation list — THE CONSTRAINT GRAPH NEED NOT BE TOPOLOGICALLY ORDERED, only the witness-generation graph must be.

THE VERIFIER'S ENFORCEMENT IS THE AXIOM WHITELIST, AND THE TIMEOUT DEFENCE IS `irreducible`. The configs permit exactly propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice plus hCircomPrime (and Specs.Secp256k1.hPrime on the two EC instances); THE TWO GF(2) CHALLENGES PERMIT NO EXTRA AXIOM AT ALL. That is what bans native_decide (Lean.ofReduceBool), sorry (sorryAx) and any axiom we declare; enable_nanoda is false on all eight, so only Lean's own kernel checks. FOR THE TIMEOUT, COPY THE HARNESS'S OWN DEFENCE: CostR1CSCanonicalSpec marks its predicates irreducible and explains that whnf-normalising them at a concrete circuit 'actually runs the circuit do-block and materializes all ~48k operations as one term (minutes of elaboration, and unbounded in general)', while 'the kernel ignores reducibility attributes' so it can never make a proof easier to fake. PUT `attribute [local irreducible] isR1CSRow r1csProducts operationsIsR1CS flatOperationsIsR1CS` IN EVERY COST/R1CS FILE, and wrap every large named expression in a local irreducible def plus one Affine lemma. UNTESTED LEVER WORTH ONE EXPERIMENT: lakefile declares `lean_lib Solution` with a submodules glob and it is NOT the default target (only Challenge is), while the config names a single solution_module — so whether UNREACHABLE Solution files are elaborated by the verifier is UNKNOWN. Measured dead files by import-graph reachability from Solution/**/Main.lean: secp256k1-scalar-mul 53 of 165, secp256k1-fixed-base 53 of 165, sha256-hash 39 of 149, rsa 11 of 83, others 0 — about 32% of the elaboration surface on the three challenges most at risk, and WE HAVE ALREADY LOST A SUBMISSION TO A TIMEOUT. DECISIVE CHEAP TEST: submit an otherwise-identical artifact with a deliberately broken UNREACHABLE file; if it verifies, dead files are free, and if it fails, pruning them buys back a third of the budget.

THE MATERIALISATION LAW — THE SINGLE THEOREM BEHIND THE MASTER COST LAW, RANGE-BIT CONSERVATION AND THE GF(2) DIMENSION BOUND. Those are not three results: they are ONE theorem applied twice (Bezout) plus a genuinely different theorem (rank), and the unified statement is score >= 2 * SUM_{v in M} log2|range(v)|, where M is the set of MATERIALISED values (values affine in (1,x,w) on the honest assignment) and |M| >= dim_F span{[v]}. THEOREM R (RANK, PROVED, ANY FIELD, ALL SEVEN CHALLENGES): with Q = span{[y_j]} in Fun(X,F)/Aff(X), both allocations >= dim Q AND rows >= dim Q, hence score >= 2 dim Q. The ROW half needs NO finite-fiber hypothesis: soundness makes every output functional constant on the fiber V_x, so V_x sits in an affine subspace of codimension dim U where U is the span of output coefficient vectors; Krull's height theorem gives dim V_x >= T - r and completeness gives V_x nonempty, so r >= dim U >= dim Q. The premise 'outputs are affine in (1,x,w)' is in the TRUSTED surface of every challenge (AffineOutput, CostR1CS.lean:731 / CostR1CSCanonicalSpec.lean:74), so this applies to the native challenges too, not just GF(2). THEOREM B (HEINTZ-BEZOUT, PROVED, PER GADGET ONLY): a designated affine form with finite accepted set of size 2^k costs >= 2k (2k-1 marginally). R COUNTS THE VALUES, B PRICES EACH ONE. Instances: GF(2) k12, log2|range| = 1, |M| = 12x1600 -> 38400; native keccak/sha256 bits, log2|range| = 1, |M| = 1600/round -> 3200/round; emulated Fp element, log2|range| = 256 -> 512 per element (THE MASTER COST LAW); RSA reduction node, log2|range| = bits(q)+bits(r) = bits(P) -> 2*bits(P) (RANGE-BIT CONSERVATION). THE DECISION-RELEVANT CONSEQUENCE: Theorem B is a lower bound on a DESIGN (it presupposes the circuit materialises that value), never on the CHALLENGE. Only Theorem R bounds the problem, and it is capped at 2 x (output arity). Quote the master cost law and range-bit conservation as EXACT COST ACCOUNTINGS OF A CHOSEN ARCHITECTURE, never as floors on the challenge.

THE CEILING THEOREM — WHY NO REFINEMENT OF OUR LOWER-BOUND MACHINERY CAN EVER BE TIGHT, AND WHAT WOULD HAVE TO REPLACE IT. Let beta_R and beta_B be the best bounds obtainable from the rank and Bezout mechanisms. Then beta_R <= 2m + O(log2 deg f) where m = OUTPUT ARITY, and beta_B <= 2 log2|A| where |A| = size of the accepted public set. BOTH ARE FUNCTIONS OF INTERFACE SIZE ONLY; the records are width x depth. That, and nothing else, is the entire 12x-to-550x gap on every challenge. THREE CONSEQUENCES, ALL CHECKED. (1) The rank bound is VACUOUS for assertion circuits: RSA has Output = unit, so dim Q = 0 and there is NO non-trivial unconditional lower bound for it at all; same for both secp challenges, where the ceiling is 2 x 65 = 130 against records of 350148 and 54677. (2) THE DEGREE-FILTRATION REFINEMENT IS MUCH WEAKER THAN OUR CORPUS CLAIMS. The k12 entry's '1600 then ~58 then ~12 then ~6, caps at ~1680' assumes BOTH factors of a top-degree product are high-degree. ONE FACTOR MAY BE AFFINE, and there are n+1 = 1601 free affine generators, so C(1601,2) swamps 1600 and the recursion never bites. Filtration adds O(log2 deg), not O(sqrt m): corrected ceiling 1612 rows / 3224 score. The conclusion is unchanged and strengthened. (3) THE ONLY FIELD-SPECIFIC TOOL WITH NO GENERAL-CASE ANALOGUE IS CHEVALLEY-WARNING: if the honest fiber is a single Fp point then sum of degrees >= T, i.e. r >= T/2. Sharpening that to r >= c*T with c > 1/2 by exploiting RANK-ONE-ness (each row is a PRODUCT of two affine forms, not an arbitrary quadric) is the one lower-bound direction in reach; a proof of r >= T would make the Materialisation Law unconditional. DO NOT FUND depth-sensitive bounds: any technique proving score >> input+output size for an explicit f is a superlinear lower bound on rank-one verification complexity, which subsumes superlinear multiplicative complexity, which subsumes superlinear B2 circuit size.

*** SUPERSEDED IN PART — the cyclic/forward-reference mechanism this points at has since been MEASURED AT EXACTLY ZERO by exhaustive search, and the 'all three are one problem' identification is right as slogan but WRONG AS MECHANISM. Read the two cyclic-rows entries in _common before acting on anything below. *** RANK-ONE VERIFICATION COMPLEXITY — THE RIGHT MEASURE, ITS DEFINITION, AND WHY THE LITERATURE IS ABOUT A DIFFERENT ONE. In this cost model the prover supplies witnesses free and affine relations are free, so the question is not 'how hard is f to COMPUTE' but 'how few rank-one rows PIN a nondeterministically supplied answer'. Formally, for a relation R, RV_F(R) = min{T + r : exist q_1..q_r with q_i = A_i*B_i - C_i, A/B/C affine on F^(n+m+T), and pi(V(q_1..q_r)(F)) = R}. This is NOT multiplicative complexity, NOT arithmetic circuit size, NOT tensor rank: nondeterminism makes it a DEFINABILITY measure (minimal rank-one quadrics whose projected variety is the graph), not a computation measure. NO NAME EXISTS; the four nearest named objects and exactly how each fails: (a) SET-THEORETIC DEFINING EQUATIONS of a variety (Eisenbud-Evans: every algebraic set in A^N is cut out set-theoretically by N equations) has the right shape but no degree restriction, so it says nothing here; (b) EXTENSION VARIABLES IN ALGEBRAIC PROOF COMPLEXITY is the sharpest analogy and is a BARRIER not a tool — a witness pinned by one degree-2 row IS an extension axiom, and superlinear lower bounds against systems with extension variables (Extended Frege, Extended PC) are open for precisely our reason, that the adversary may define intermediates you did not anticipate; (c) VALIANT'S VNP is the closest class but is about the VALUE of a sum over Boolean witnesses, not about pinning; (d) PCP / LOCAL CHECKABILITY bounds query complexity and proof length, never row count. Also note RV_{F2}(f)/2 <= MC(f), so nondeterminism can only help and a superlinear RV bound is strictly harder than the already-open superlinear MC bound. UNEXPLOITED DEGREE OF FREEDOM FOUND IN THE HARNESS: isCidentityRowAt k e := exists affine A B, e = var k - A*B places NO restriction on which variables A and B reference, INCLUDING INDICES GREATER THAN k. So a GF(2) constraint system may be CYCLIC — row k may relate w_k to w_{k+5} — and completeness is unaffected because ComputableWitnesses orders only the GENERATOR, not the constraints. Our gf2-k12 do-not-try list closes 'A or B reference the PINNED variable' but not FORWARD references, and a cyclic system is exactly a system that need not materialise intermediates. No construction is known; the do-not-try list overstates its coverage.

THE DEAD-FILE QUESTION IS SETTLED EMPIRICALLY AND THE ANSWER IS 'UNREACHABLE MODULES ARE NEVER ELABORATED' — DO NOT SPEND A JOB PRUNING THEM. The earlier entry proposed submitting an artifact with a deliberately broken unreachable file as a decisive test. WE ALREADY RAN THAT EXPERIMENT BY ACCIDENT AND IT PASSED. Our verified RSA record (submission 141ea5fa-f4d3-43c4-aada-e68c291b675f, 321889, currently #1 on the leaderboard) SHIPPED TWO ORPHAN MODULES THAT CANNOT COMPILE: Score.lean asserts `allocations + constraints = 326297 := by decide` while Main.lean declares 160587 + 161302 = 321889, so that `decide` evaluates to False; and Optimality.lean imports Solution.<ns>.Optimality.Accounting/.Chain/.Attained/.LimbWidth/.CarryTables when no Optimality/ subdirectory exists at all (the tree is flat, 83 files). Both were left behind by the 326297 -> 321889 rewrite. tick.py uploads a FLAT glob of soldir/*.lean, so both files were unquestionably in the artifact. IT VERIFIED ANYWAY. CONCLUSION: despite lakefile.lean declaring `lean_lib Solution where globs := #[.submodules `Solution]`, the verifier elaborates only the import closure of the declared solution_module — the `Solution` lib is not the default target, only `Challenge` is. TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) The 'prune the 53-of-165 unreachable files to buy back a third of the elaboration budget' hypothesis is DEAD — there is no budget being spent on them, so timeouts must be attacked inside the REACHABLE closure (irreducible attributes, local defs, smaller decide terms). (2) Stale orphans are cosmetically bad but HARMLESS, so do not burn job slots or risk a rewrite fixing them: secp256k1-fixed-base's SelectHotLemmas.lean:479 and SelectSound.lean:59 still typed at `Var (fields 15)` where Select12.hot4 now takes `Var (fields 14)` are in this category. Keep the 'NEUTRALIZED DEAD EXPLORATORY MODULE' banner convention for tidiness, not for safety.

CORRECTION TO 'A MUX COSTS NOTHING' — SCOPE IT, OR IT WILL BREAK isR1CS. That entry is right that Clean's Gadgets/Conditional.lean main emits ZERO operations by building selector*(ifTrue - ifFalse) + ifFalse as an EXPRESSION. IT IS ONLY FREE IF NO DOWNSTREAM ROW NEEDS THAT VALUE TO BE AFFINE. That expression is DEGREE 2, and by the one-product-per-row constraint a row admits at most ONE product, checked syntactically. CONCRETE COUNTEREXAMPLE IN OUR OWN TREE: secp256k1-fixed-base's Mux.lean:19-31 deliberately re-implements the mux to MATERIALISE its output (ProvableType.witness + size-M assertZero rows, costed (size M, size M) at Cost.lean:334), and it HAS to — FinalAdd.lean:525-532 routes both 8/8 muxes into CheapIncompleteAdd and into Canonicalize, and CheapIncompleteAdd.isR1CS_main's signature literally demands (hAx : AffineW b.A.x). Replacing them with the free expression form would put two products on one row and be REJECTED. THE DECISION PROCEDURE: a mux is free iff every consumer of its output either (a) is itself an assertZero whose OTHER operands are all affine, so the mux's single product is that row's one permitted product, or (b) re-witnesses the value anyway. Otherwise the materialisation IS the cost of making it affine and it is not removable. AUDIT THE CONSUMERS BEFORE COSTING A MUX AT ZERO.

CYCLIC (FORWARD-REFERENCING) ROWS: THE HARNESS CLAIM IS TRUE, THE MECHANISM IS CONSTRUCTIBLE TODAY, AND IT BUYS EXACTLY ZERO — CLOSED BY AN EXHAUSTIVE EQUALITY OF TWO FAMILIES, NOT BY A FAILED SEARCH. SOURCE, VERIFIED: CostR1CSCanonicalSpec.lean:37-39 is `isCidentityRowAt (k) (e) := exists A B, Affine A and Affine B and e = var k - A*B` — A and B are arbitrary degree-<=1 expressions with NO index condition, so a row may reference witnesses allocated after its own pin; flatOperationsIsCid (same file 45-50) advances the pin counter only on .assert; Clean Circuit/Basic.lean:305 ComputableWitnesses restricts only witness GENERATORS, never constraint order. CONSTRUCTIBLE WITH ZERO NEW MACHINERY: the k12 record's own Round.lean already batch-allocates (witnessVector permutationBits) and only then emits rows (forEach ... assertZero (products[i] - chiProduct pre i)), so every row already has every witness of the batch in scope — pointing row i at products[j] with j > i is a one-token edit. THE DECISIVE REFORMULATION, which is what makes this an equality rather than a failed search: for a fixed row-set C the set R(C) of certifiable output functions is a LINEAR SUBSPACE of Fun(GF(2)^n, GF(2)) — if o1 and o2 are each constant on every fibre then so is o1+o2 — so a target of ANY output arity is r-realisable iff it lies in R(C) for some COMPLETE C, and CYCLIC BEATS ACYCLIC AT r ROWS IFF SOME R(C_cyclic) IS CONTAINED IN NO R(C_acyclic), where acyclic is exactly the multiplicative-complexity model. MEASURED, EXHAUSTIVE OVER THE FULL CANDIDATE SPACE, ZERO NOT-CONTAINED EVERYWHERE: n=3 r=1 (1024 candidates / 391 complete / 8 subspaces vs 8 acyclic); n=4 r=1 (4096/1303/36 vs 36); n=3 r=2 (16777216/2608285/51 vs 43); n=4 r=2 (268435456/22302253/2641 vs 2521); n=5 r=2 (4294967296/225461581/67581 vs 66341). Self-references (A or B naming the PINNED variable) AND forward references were both in the space. FREE UNPINNED WITNESSES ARE WORTH NOTHING — e = 1,2,3 give IDENTICAL subspace families. Independent z3 cross-check on a separate encoding: chi3 UNSAT at r=1 and r=2 and SAT at r=3, chi5 UNSAT at r=3 in both modes, AND5 SAT at r=4 = MC. THE ONE SCALE-FREE CONSEQUENCE: the r-certifiable class is closed under substituting constants for inputs, and ANF degree is detected by restriction, so the exhaustive finding that NO degree-4 function on 4 variables is 2-row certifiable (measured degree histograms: r=1 -> max degree 2, r=2 -> max degree 3, reconfirmed over all 67581 subspaces at n=5) gives deg f <= r+1 for r <= 2 IN ANY NUMBER OF VARIABLES — exactly Schnorr's DETERMINISTIC bound MC(f) >= deg(f) - 1. So the purest composition z = f(g(x)) with g = (x0x1, x2x3) and f = uv, i.e. AND4 with MC = 3, is NOT certifiable by 2 cyclic rows, exhausted over all 268435456 two-row systems. CONJECTURED for all r, with a partial proof: normalise row 1 to w1*B' = C' with B',C' free of w1 (over GF(2), w1(b + beta*w1) = c + gamma*w1 iff w1(b + beta + gamma) = c); if B' contains no witness the split B'=0 / B'=1 is an INPUT hyperplane and each half eliminates row 1, so f has degree <= r on each half and <= r+1 globally. THE GAP: when B' contains other witnesses the split is not an input predicate and the covering sets need not be affine. STILL OPEN AND WHAT IT COSTS: r >= 3 is TIMED OUT, NOT EMPTY — the r=3 degree probe died at 5400s, AND5@r=3 and AND6@r=4 at 3600s, chi5@r=4 at 1800s; the cheap close is an exhaustive C search at n=3 r=3, about 5 CPU-hours. Toy scale also cannot see the width x depth question at all: 2 rounds of a 3-bit permutation IS a 3-bit permutation and both models reach it at r=2. DO NOT SPEND JOB SLOTS ON CYCLIC GF(2) ROW SETS. Re-open ONLY on a refutation of deg <= r+1 at r >= 3, or an explicit row-set at any size whose R(C) is in no acyclic R(C') of the same row count. NOTE WHICH DIRECTION IS LIVE: cyclicity is an UPPER-BOUND tool, so only a CONSTRUCTION can close it — no lower bound can help, since our own ceiling theorem says no counting/rank/degree argument separates k12's 19200 from 1600, and no explicit n-variable function is known to have MC > n-1.

SCOPE CORRECTION — FORWARD REFERENCES ARE A NEW DEGREE OF FREEDOM ONLY IN THE TWO GF(2) CHALLENGES, AND THE FIVE R1CS CHALLENGES ALREADY HAVE A STRICTLY STRONGER NON-MATERIALISING PRIMITIVE. In model A the row predicate is `isR1CSRow e := match r1csProducts e with | some k => k <= 1 | none => False` (Challenge/Utils/CostR1CS.lean:79-82) — PURELY SYNTACTIC on the expression, it never mentions a variable index, and flatOperationsIsR1CS carries no counter. So (i) forward references were NEVER restricted there, and (ii) model A additionally admits rows with NO FRESH WITNESS AT ALL — a pure assertion A*B = C — which the C-identity form forbids, since every GF(2) row must introduce and pin a new variable. EVERY MODULAR-REDUCTION CERTIFICATE IN THE SECP AND RSA RECORDS IS A NON-MATERIALISING VERIFICATION OF EXACTLY THAT KIND — MulModEqFold is the purest example, asserting a*b = s1+s2 mod p with no remainder witnessed at all. So 'can a rank-one system verify a composition without materialising the intermediates' IS NOT AN UNEXPLOITED IDEA IN MODEL A; IT IS THE STANDARD TECHNIQUE, and the live lever there is range-bit accounting of the values that ARE witnessed, not cyclicity. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE 'SAME OPEN GAP' ENTRY: identifying (a) the RSA joint certificate, (b) the k12 non-affine round output and (c) the secp master cost law as ONE question is right as slogan and WRONG AS MECHANISM — (b) lives in a strictly weaker row model than (a) and (c). The GF(2) negative CLOSES (b) and closes the cyclic-row mechanism corpus-wide; it does NOT close (a) or (c). SECOND CORRECTION, TO (b)'s PHRASING: 'can a round's output be NOT affine in (x,w) while the next round's AND multiplicands are still affine forms' is close to a CATEGORY ERROR — in the C-identity model every multiplicand is an affine FORM in (x,w) by fiat, there is no syntactic slot for a non-affine intermediate, and the only content is how many pinned witnesses the affine span must contain, which is exactly the row count. That is WHY the exhaustive search found nothing: cyclicity adds no mechanism, it only widens which affine forms a row may multiply, and the R(C)-subspace test enumerates all of those.

'ASSERTION, NOT VALUE' DELETES TARGETS, NOT OPERANDS — THE SCOPE RULE, AND IT IS WHAT DECIDES WHETHER THE MECHANISM TRANSFERS. MulModEqFold is worth -531 per site because it deletes a materialised value that is only ever the TARGET of a certificate: nothing reads it, it merely has to satisfy an equation, so the folded certificate runs directly against the target expression and the witness disappears. IT CANNOT DELETE AN OPERAND. An operand of a non-native product must have LIMB-CERTIFIED DIGITS or its F_p convolution coefficients carry no integer meaning — verified by 200/200 forgeries at toy scale on the RSA tree. SO THE AUDIT QUESTION IS NOT 'does anything read this value' BUT 'does anything read it AS AN OPERAND OF A PRODUCT'. Worked example of each: on secp256k1 the curve-equation residue in PointValid and the terminal slope residue are TARGETS, and deleting them was worth -531 each; on RSA the 15 chain residues r_i are each read as the operand a of the NEXT squaring's convolution, so all 15 are irreducible, and the single target-only node (the terminal a^2*b = q*n + em) was ALREADY folded. A THIRD CATEGORY THAT LOOKS DELETABLE AND IS NOT: a value nobody reads whose RANGE CHECK IS ITSELF THE CERTIFICATE — the RSA quotients q_i are read by no one, but removing their range checks is a forgery, not a saving, because the dimension count (171 free unknowns against 37 group equations) is what pins the reduction. CLASSIFY EVERY CANDIDATE AS TARGET / OPERAND / CERTIFICATE-BY-RANGE BEFORE COSTING IT.

OFFSETTING ONLY ONE OPERAND OF A BILINEAR CONVOLUTION SAVES EXACTLY ZERO — PROVED, AND IT KILLS A WHOLE FAMILY OF 'BALANCE THE LIMBS' IDEAS. For a bilinear convolution with per-limb cap M and offsets a,b <= M/2, writing A = M - a and B = M - b, the balanced coefficient bound is A*B + a*B + A*b = M^2 - a*b. Minimised at a = b = M/2, giving exactly 0.75*M^2, i.e. a cap gain of log2(4/3) = 0.415 BITS — not the ~1.32 a naive 'halve both operands' reading suggests. Setting b = 0 gives M^2 - 0: THE CROSS TERM COSTS BACK PRECISELY WHAT THE ONE-SIDED BALANCING SAVES. CONSEQUENCES ALREADY BANKED: on RSA this cut the q*n cap lever from a claimed 1467 to a measured 218, and zeroed a claimed ~130 for balancing b in the final block, where a is genuinely balanced (a change of the certified quantity, no cross term) and b is exactly the one-sided case. The gain is FURTHER DILUTED wherever the carry width is log2(OFF_P + OFF_N) and only one side's OFF is touched. Before costing any limb-balancing idea, check whether BOTH operands can be offset; if only one can, the answer is zero without further work.

THE CONSUMER-FUNCTIONAL LAW — THE QUANTITATIVE FORM OF 'ASSERTION, NOT VALUE'. An emulated field element used only as a CERTIFICATE ADDEND has TWO coordinates, not four. The yes/no test asks whether a value is read at all; the sharp form is PER-COORDINATE and is a rank computation. A multi-cell value costs in proportion to its NUMBER OF CELLS in every gadget that builds it by selection (mux tree, one-hot contraction, table lookup, packed-borrow select), but each consumer reads only a set of LINEAR FUNCTIONALS of the cell vector. THE NUMBER OF CELLS THAT MUST BE PRODUCED IS dim span{all consumers' functionals}, NOT the arity of the ProvableType. PROVED FROM SOURCE for the folded certificate, the dominant consumer in both secp trees: GroupedFlex.main (fixed-base GroupedFlex.lean:195-205) emits exactly two kinds of row — carryLoop ... (G-2) 0, and one final assertZero (polyEvalExpr (Pc - Sc) (2^B)). With G = 3 at every call site the carryLoop runs ONE iteration, range-checking carryExpr 0, which reads positions posOf 0 .. posOf 0 + gf 0 - 1; with gfFold = 2 and posOfFold k = 2k that is positions {0,1} ONLY. Positions 2,3,4 appear in NO row but the single final polyEval row, which reads sum_k coeff_k 2^(64k). SO A TARGET/ADDEND VECTOR ENTERS THROUGH EXACTLY TWO INDEPENDENT FUNCTIONALS: T_lo = t_0 + 2^64 t_1 and T_hi = t_2 + 2^64 t_3. THE COMPLEMENTARY FACT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT UNIVERSAL: a value used as a MULTIPLICAND of interpolatedMul is read through 2m-1 EVALUATIONS of its limb polynomial at distinct constants, which is FULL RANK m — a multiplicand always needs all four limbs and this can never apply to one. RANK LEDGER, APPLY MECHANICALLY: convolution multiplicand -> 4; certificate addend under a one-carry group schedule -> 2; value only tested for zero or equality -> 1 (subject to the boundedness caveat in the costed-negatives entry); circuit output -> whatever the interface declares. AUDIT RULE: for every value produced by a SELECTOR, list its consumers, write down each consumer's functionals, and produce only a BASIS of their span.

'ASSERTION, NOT VALUE' AND ITS MULTIPLICAND DUAL ARE STRUCTURALLY VACUOUS IN COST MODEL B — DO NOT SWEEP gf2-sha256 OR gf2-k12 FOR EITHER; IT IS A CATEGORY ERROR. From the trusted surface, CostR1CSCanonicalSpec.lean:37-39 and 45-50: isCidentityRowAt k e := exists A B, Affine A and Affine B and e = var k - A*B, and flatOperationsIsCid advances the pin counter on EVERY assert and on no witness. Two consequences. (1) EVERY ROW MATERIALISES EXACTLY ONE VALUE BY FIAT: the C-side must be a bare variable var k, so there is no row that checks a certificate without introducing a value, and 'delete the materialisation and run the certificate against the target' has no syntactic slot to live in. Model A's non-materialising pure assertion A*B = C is FORBIDDEN here. (2) EVERY MULTIPLICAND IS ALREADY AN AFFINE FORM BY FIAT: A and B range over all degree-<=1 expressions, so 'a value consumed only as a multiplicand should be an affine form, not a witness' is already true of every multiplicand, and there is nothing to convert. The only remaining question in model B is HOW MANY rows, i.e. AND count. EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION THAT NEITHER TREE HAS A STRAY WITNESS: gf2-sha256's record declares allocations = 22215 AND constraints = 22215; gf2-k12 is 19200/19200. Allocations equal constraints to the unit in both, and since allocations >= constraints is forced there while any surplus allocation is an unpinned universally-quantified variable worth nothing, EQUALITY IS PROOF THAT NOT ONE VALUE IS MATERIALISED WITHOUT BEING PINNED AND CONSUMED. There is no dead-value sweep to run on either GF(2) slug, now or ever.

FIVE COSTED NEGATIVES AROUND THE PACKING / NON-MATERIALISATION FAMILY — ALL CHECKED, ALL EMPTY, WITH THE ARITHMETIC. (1) PACKED CONDITIONAL EQUALITY NEEDS A BOUND ON THE WITNESS SIDE AND THAT IS USUALLY THE WHOLE COST. The gadget s * (sum_i 2^((b+1)i) (u_i - v_i)) = 0 collapses k conditional equalities into ONE row (one product, zero allocations) and is sound when every residual is a signed integer below 2^b and (b+1)k < log2 p - 1. It fails wherever the pinned value is a FREE WITNESS: in sha256's SelectDigest the 8 digest words are witnessed and pinned by 5 groups x 8 rows = 8 alloc / 40 rows; packing 4 words per row would give 8/10 (-30) but the digest words carry no row-level bound, so a prover cancels 2^33*d_1 against d_0 and the pack is UNSOUND. Buying the bound costs 8 x 32 range-check bits. (2) MERGING TWO MODULAR CERTIFICATES UNDER ONE CARRY CHAIN SAVES NOTHING. Packing two integer identities E1 + 2^K E2 = 0 at disjoint bit ranges is sound (no challenge, so not Schwartz-Zippel) and worthless: each certified integer is ~2^300, the grouped carry exists precisely to cut a 300-bit identity into sub-p groups, and packing two just doubles the group count. CARRY BITS ARE PROPORTIONAL TO TOTAL IDENTITY WIDTH, WHICH IS INVARIANT. (3) THE MUX CANNOT BE PACKED BY ITS COMMON SELECTOR. sum_i B^i (w_i - b_i) = s * sum_i B^i (a_i - b_i) is genuinely ONE product once factored and would turn an m-cell mux from m alloc + m rows into m alloc + 1 row — but the w_i are free witnesses and the same unboundedness kills it. It becomes available exactly when the mux output is range-checked downstream for another reason; in both secp trees the mux-output limb bounds come from the SPEC (proof-side, free), never from rows. (4) sha256's Round0Block1Sparse is 32 alloc + 33 rows and the top-bit-free trick does NOT apply: dropping the top bit forces witnessing the wrap carry instead, 32/33 either way. (5) keccak's chi is at the dimension floor with its row already saturated, so there is no assertion-not-value site and no free product slot there.

LOWER BOUNDS STATED ONLY FOR 'QUADRATIC' OR SIGMA-PI-SIGMA CIRCUITS APPLY IN FULL FORCE TO COST MODEL B — THE USUAL CAVEAT IS NOT A CAVEAT FOR US. Much of the multiplicative-complexity literature proves bounds only for QUADRATIC CIRCUITS (every gate computes a function of degree <= 2) or SIGMA-PI-SIGMA form, and states this as a restriction that weakens the result relative to general circuits. OUR TWO GF(2) CHALLENGES ARE LITERALLY THAT CLASS: isCidentityRowAt k e := exists affine A B, e = var k - A*B makes every row a product of TWO AFFINE FORMS pinned to a fresh variable, which is exactly a quadratic / SigmaPiSigma gate. SO WHEN SCANNING THE LITERATURE FOR APPLICABLE BOUNDS, DO NOT DISCARD A RESULT BECAUSE IT IS 'ONLY' FOR QUADRATIC CIRCUITS — that is our model exactly, and such a result is STRICTLY MORE APPLICABLE here than a general-circuit bound would be elsewhere. WORKED EXAMPLE: Boyar et al., 'Multiplicative Complexity of Vector Valued Boolean Functions' (arXiv:1407.6169), Corollary 1 — 'any quadratic circuit computing an almost bent (n,n)-function has at least L(n,(n-1)/2) AND gates, and for sufficiently large n that exceeds 2.32n'. For a general circuit this would be a restricted statement; against model B it is a direct bound. The same reading applies to any ANF-degree or rank argument in that literature. NOTE THE CONVERSE, so this is not over-applied: cost model A (the five R1CS challenges) is NOT the quadratic-circuit class, because a row there may carry no fresh witness at all and the constraint system need not be a circuit in any order — see the forward-reference scope entry.

A NEW RECORD CAN SILENTLY LOSE GROUND THE PREVIOUS RECORD HELD — ALWAYS DIFF A RECORD AGAINST ITS PREDECESSOR FOR LOST ATOMS, NOT ONLY FOR GAINED ONES. THE MECHANISM: check_records reseeds projs/<slug>/Solution/ when a record moves, but jobs already in flight keep their OLD checkout ('running jobs left to finish'). A job that started before record N lands can therefore produce record N+1 that is BETTER OVERALL yet MISSING everything N added — and nothing in the loop notices, because the only test applied is 'does the total beat the leaderboard'. MEASURED INSTANCE, secp256k1-fixed-base: the 52256 record descends from the 52676 seed, not from the 52430 record that preceded it. Evidence, three independent atoms: implicitScreenedCost is 1640/1649 (the 52676 value; 52430 had 1634/1643), the three folded-quotient RangeCheck widths are 68/70/68 (the 52676 values; 52430 had shaved them to 67/69/67), and combCost 26280/26396 - 26070/26186 = 210/210 = exactly 21 x the selectCost delta 298/299 -> 288/289. So 52256 = 52676 - 420 and the 52430 record's -246 IS NOT IN IT. THE TWO ARE ORTHOGONAL AND STACK: re-applying the lost 246 to the current tree gives ABOUT 52010 for zero new ideas. GENERAL PRACTICE, now three variations on one theme: (a) when two jobs both beat the seed, diff their atoms — the loser's cheaper atoms are free score; (b) when a record lands, diff it against the PREVIOUS RECORD and re-apply any atom that got worse; (c) the cheap discriminator for whether two trees are the same work is the DECLARED allocations/constraints pair, never the tarball hash, which moves with comments and proof text. ALSO RE-CHECK ON THIS SLUG: hot4 in the 52256 tree takes `h : Var (fields 15)` where an earlier note recorded `fields 14` from two affinely-derived cells — determine whether that refinement was lost too before re-costing the one-hot item.

A FAILED VERIFICATION IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A TIMEOUT — CHECK THE DURATION AGAINST KNOWN SUCCESSES BEFORE BLAMING ELABORATION COST. Instance: sha256-hash submission bdc0ff37 claiming 145471 (-8) came back status=failed with score=None after 17.5 minutes, and the natural reading was the timeout that this corpus has previously lost a submission to. THE DURATIONS SAY OTHERWISE. Measured submitted_at -> verified_at on recent submissions: fixed-base 50825 VERIFIED in 19.2 min, secp256k1-scalar-mul 331777 VERIFIED in 12.7, 342300 VERIFIED in 12.5, rsa 321769 VERIFIED in 14.1, against the FAILED sha256 at 17.5. A SUCCESS RAN LONGER THAN THE FAILURE, so 17.5 min is nowhere near a cliff and verification duration carries NO timeout signal in the 12-20 minute band. The failure is therefore a genuine proof or soundness rejection, not an elaboration budget problem. NOTE WHAT THE API DOES AND DOES NOT GIVE: the submission record exposes status, score, allocations, constraints, description, submitted_at and verified_at, but NO failure reason and NO log — so diagnosing a rejection means re-deriving it locally from the submitted tree, BUT THE TREE IS *NOT* RETRIEVABLE FROM THE API — I ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE HERE AND IT IS WRONG. /api/submissions/<id>/download returns HTTP 409 {"detail": "Only verified submissions can be downloaded."} for BOTH failed and still-pending submissions; only a VERIFIED submission downloads (measured on all three states). SO A FAILED SUBMISSION'S TREE EXISTS IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE: the local out/<slug>/ directory the tick extracted it into — and the NEXT job on that slug overwrites it. If a failure is worth diagnosing, copy out/<slug>/ aside IMMEDIATELY on the failure notification; after the next tick it is gone for good. The description field of that submission listed several aggressive claims worth suspecting first when one does fail: 'affine carry chain: zero carry allocations', 'terminal schedule words left unreduced', and '7-of-8 bits per byte'.

INVERT THE CERTIFICATE TO MOVE THE AWKWARD OPERAND INTO THE TARGET POSITION. MEASURED -75 alloc / -77 constr PER SITE, AND IT GENERALISES TO EVERY CONSTANT MULTIPLIER IN EVERY CHALLENGE. Setting: you want r = c*a mod p with c a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT and a an INPUT, and you want to run the certificate in a cheaper limb view (base 2^32) than the one a arrives in (base 2^64). Naively you must re-limb a, which costs a Normalize. DON'T — certify the equation the other way round. c is invertible mod p, so r = c*a is EQUIVALENT to c^-1*r = a, and in that form the two multiplicands are (i) the freshly witnessed remainder r, whose 32-bit limbs come FOR FREE out of the bytes its canonicality check already allocates, and (ii) the compile-time constant c^-1 — while a appears ONLY AS THE CERTIFICATE TARGET, i.e. an affine addend, where its native 64-bit limbs are all that is needed. THIS IS THE CONSUMER-FUNCTIONAL LAW USED AS A DESIGN MOVE RATHER THAN AN AUDIT: targets are read as affine addends and are cheap in ANY limb view, multiplicands need full rank, so an inversion that swaps which value sits where can pay for itself outright. MEASURED IN THE 318534 secp256k1-scalar-mul RECORD as MulModBeta32 (the GLV endomorphism constant beta): 4 witnesses + ValidPBytes 260/265 + MulModFold32 101/103 = 365/368, against 440/443 for the base-2^64 MulModSub2 it replaces. PRECONDITION IS ONLY THAT c BE INVERTIBLE MOD p AND KNOWN AT COMPILE TIME — c^-1 is a numeral, so the inverted certificate costs exactly what the forward one would have. SWEEP FOR IT: any fixed multiplier (endomorphism constants, curve constants, Montgomery/Barrett factors, round constants) whose operand arrives in the wrong view is a candidate.

SHARED SELECTOR DECOMPOSITION — A MULTI-LIMB MUX MUST DECOMPOSE ITS SELECTOR ONCE, NOT ONCE PER LIMB. This is pure allocation+row saving with no lookup or randomness dependence, and it applies to EVERY windowed table select in every challenge we have. gnark's emulated MSM was re-deriving the selector bits inside each limb's mux: a 16-to-1 mux over a 6-limb value paid 24 REDUNDANT BOOLEAN ASSERTIONS. Decompose once, reuse the same bit wires across all limbs. Source Consensys/gnark PR #1704 (2026-02-09), https://github.com/Consensys/gnark/pull/1704, measured in R1CS at BLS12-381 G1.ScalarMul 291552 -> 279576 and BN254 ECMul 210369 -> 202669. AUDIT SHAPE: for every multi-component value selected by shared control bits, count how many times a booleanity row is emitted for the SAME bit. The answer should be once. READ THE CAVEAT BEFORE TRUSTING ANY GNARK NUMBER: gnark's headline emulated-arithmetic counts are NOT reachable in our model, because its Field.MulMod/Eval deferred check uses a Fiat-Shamir challenge from a prover commitment (in-circuit randomness) and its range checks are LogUp (lookups). What transfers is the CIRCUIT STRUCTURE, and only that. Treat every percentage below as evidence a lever exists, never as our predicted saving.

AUDIT FOR REPEATED BIT DECOMPOSITIONS OF THE SAME VALUE — EACH REDUNDANT ONE IS n ALLOCATIONS + n+1 ROWS. gnark found ToBitsCanonical calling ToBits several times on one element and fixed it by inlining the comparison and reusing the bits, then by memoising decompositions keyed on the element. Measured: triple ToBits on the same element 1920 -> 896 (-53%), ToBitsCanonical ~2880 -> 2378, multi-compare against three identical bounds 11145 -> 10119. Source PR #1707, https://github.com/Consensys/gnark/pull/1707. Companion PR #1699 (https://github.com/Consensys/gnark/pull/1699) tracks, PER LIMB, the widest bit-width already enforced and skips any NARROWER re-check — the same idea applied to range checks rather than decompositions. This is an audit, not an invention, but the -53% shows how large the leak gets when it is never looked for. SPECIAL-CASE THE NON-NATIVE ZERO/EQUALITY CHECK OUT OF THE GENERIC MULMOD PATH. To assert a == 0 mod p for a non-native a, do NOT route it through the batched weighted multiplication check; assert directly that a = q*p for a witnessed q, which gnark reports collapses to a single constraint. Source PR #1694, https://github.com/Consensys/gnark/pull/1694. GENERALISATION WORTH SWEEPING: every use of a general-purpose certificate where the operand is a CONSTANT, ZERO, or otherwise degenerate is a candidate for a hand-written special case — the generic gadget pays for generality nobody at that site is using. This is the same ledger error as sizing a quotient range check to its type instead of its call site.
