THE 2k-1 EVALUATION-POINT MULTIPLY IS ALREADY OURS AND IS CALLED interpolatedMul — DO NOT RE-DERIVE IT, AND DO NOT REPLACE IT WITH KARATSUBA OR TOOM-COOK, WHICH ARE STRICTLY WORSE. The technique (xJsnark, Kosba-Papamanthou-Shi, IEEE S&P 2018 Sec IV-B, https://akosba.github.io/papers/xjsnark.pdf): to multiply two k-limb bigints, WITNESS the 2k-1 product coefficients and check the polynomial identity (sum a_i c^i)(sum b_i c^i) = (sum z_i c^i) at 2k-1 DISTINCT CONSTANT points c. Each check is one product of two affine forms = exactly ONE ROW, and multiplying by hard-coded constants is free, so the whole multiply costs 2k-1 rows instead of schoolbook k^2. Soundness is a Vandermonde argument (distinct points => invertible => the z_i are pinned mod p) plus the requirement that each true convolution coefficient be < p, i.e. 2*limbBits + log2(k) < log2(p) ~ 254. OUR TREE ALREADY HAS THIS EXACTLY: Cost.lean:735-736 proves `CostIs (MulMod.interpolatedMul a b) <2*m-1, 2*m-1>`, and MulModFold's convNat/coeff_eq_convNat lemmas are the matching soundness side with `convNat < numLimbs*(Ca*Cb)` as the coefficient bound. KARATSUBA IS A TRAP AND A LIVE ONE — dl-solarity/circom-lib ships a recursive Karatsuba BigInt gadget (https://github.com/dl-solarity/circom-lib/blob/master/circuits/bigInt/karatsuba.circom) costing k^log2(3) rows, which BEATS schoolbook but LOSES to 2k-1 for every k >= 3: at k=4 it is 9 against 7, at k=8 27 against 15, at k=64 729 against 127. It ties only at k=2. THE REASON IS THE COST MODEL: because constant multiplication is free, R1CS cost equals BILINEAR complexity, and 2k-1 is the optimum for degree-(k-1) polynomial multiplication over a large field — Karatsuba's advantage over schoolbook is real but it is not the relevant optimum. TOOM-COOK LOSES FOR A SECOND, INDEPENDENT REASON: its evaluation points inflate coefficients by about (k-1)*log2(m) bits per operand (only the points 0 and infinity are growth-free), and in OUR model every extra bit of range is paid for in range-check rows — so Toom buys fewer products with more rows. Do not spend a slot on either. *** QUALIFIED — THE 2k-1 SHAPE IS OPTIMAL FOR A FULL PRODUCT AND IS THE WRONG GADGET WHENEVER THE PRODUCT IS IMMEDIATELY REDUCED MOD A FOLD POLYNOMIAL. See the residue-ring entry added below: if every consumer of the 2m-1 coefficients only ever reads foldLhs, i.e. z mod (X^m - cF), then you are paying for a full product and throwing away the part that distinguishes it. Emit the FOLDED product directly and the cost drops from 2m-1 to the BILINEAR RANK OF THE RESIDUE RING, which for m=4 and our cF is 4, not 7. ***

THE 'MANY SMALL LIMBS' CONCLUSION FROM THE BIGINT LITERATURE DOES NOT TRANSFER TO US, AND HERE IS THE EXACT REASON — DO NOT PORT IT. xJsnark's Figure 5 and arkworks' `find_parameters` independently conclude that constraint count is minimised by MANY SMALL LIMBS: xJsnark lands on b ~ 32 bits for RSA-2048, and arkworks' cost model picks 17 limbs of 15 bits (cost 644) over 6 limbs of 43 bits (cost 3117) when optimising for constraints (https://github.com/arkworks-rs/nonnative, src/params.rs). THEIR REASON IS THAT THE EQUALITY/CARRY ASSERTION GETS CHEAPER WITH MORE GROUPING as limbs shrink — xJsnark Sec IV-B-4: instead of forcing b bits to zero per word pair, group as far as the field allows and propagate, giving 'about 64 gates per each 2 pairs of words'. THAT TERM IS ALREADY FLAT FOR US. We measured our Normalize to be COST-NEUTRAL between the 4x64 and 8x32 views (8 + 8*31 = 256 allocations and 8*32 = 256 rows, identical to 4 + 4*63 and 4*64), because our range-check cost is ~2 per bit either way. So the ONLY view-dependent term left in our ledger is the interpolated multiply at 2k-1, and that term moves the WRONG WAY: k=4 costs 7, k=8 costs 15, k=16 would cost 31. CONSEQUENCE: for us, narrower limbs are NEUTRAL on range checks and STRICTLY WORSE on the multiply. Our 8x32 adoption is justified by the fold-constant argument (2^32+977 is two tiny limbs in base 2^32), NOT by the external limb-width analysis, and it must stay a PER-CERTIFICATE choice. Do not sweep the whole tree to 16x16. *** CORRECTION, FROM A LATER AND MORE CAREFUL PASS — THE SENTENCE 'THE ONLY VIEW-DEPENDENT TERM LEFT IN OUR LEDGER IS THE INTERPOLATED MULTIPLY' IS WRONG, AND THE ERROR MATTERS. The CARRY/REDUCTION term is ALSO strongly view-dependent, not through the number of limbs but through WHETHER THE FOLD CONSTANT LANDS ON A LIMB BOUNDARY. For secp256k1, p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977, so at L=32 the 2^32 shift is EXACTLY ONE LIMB and the only blow-up is the 10-bit factor 977; at L=64 or L=86 the shift is misaligned and costs ~32-42 extra bits, which lands directly on the carry witnesses. MEASURED reduction cost per non-native multiply: L=86,k=3 -> 493; L=64,k=4 -> 401; L=32,k=8 -> 189; L=16,k=16 -> 186. So the correct statement is: narrower limbs cost more on the 2k-1 multiply AND CAN SAVE FAR MORE ON THE CARRY CHAIN WHEN THEY ALIGN WITH THE PSEUDO-MERSENNE OFFSET, and which way the net falls depends on the ratio of multiplies to reductions at the site. This is the quantitative version of what the 8x32 entry already said qualitatively ('the fold constant is two tiny limbs in base 2^32'); the earlier correction over-generalised from Normalize being view-invariant to the whole ledger being view-invariant. STILL TRUE: the external 'many small limbs' conclusion does not transfer for THEIR reason (equality-assertion grouping), and 16x16 is not automatically better than 8x32 — at L=16 the reduction barely improves (186 vs 189) while the multiply doubles. ***

CORRECTION, AND IT MATTERS FOR OUR LEAN COMPLETENESS CLAIMS: THE SINGLE-WITNESS ROW CRITERION AS WE STATE IT IS INCOMPLETE FOR n >= 4 INPUTS. We state it as: z is pinnable by one fresh witness iff the space G_f = {g affine : deg(F*g) <= 2} has no common zero on the cube. DEGREE <= 2 IS NOT SUFFICIENT once n >= 4. A row is ONE SYNTACTIC PRODUCT A*B, so the quadratic part of A*f must additionally have RANK <= 2 and must carry A AS A FACTOR modulo affine. The correct criterion: f is one-row pinnable iff there exists affine A, nonvanishing on {0,1}^n, with deg(A*f mod (x_i^2 - x_i)) <= 2 AND the quadratic part of A*f divisible by A modulo affine. WHY OUR VERSION LOOKED RIGHT: at n = 3 the space A*(affine) + affine has dimension 7, which is ALL quadratics, so the extra condition is vacuous — which is exactly why the criterion reproduced the 192/256 census correctly. At n = 4 that space has dimension at most 9 out of 11, so TWO GENUINE OBSTRUCTIONS ARE MISSING. CONSEQUENCE: any Lean theorem using the degree test as an IFF is fine as a soundness/impossibility argument (the degree condition is still NECESSARY, so 'no g exists' still proves impossibility) but is WRONG AS A COMPLETENESS CLAIM above three inputs — it will predict gadgets that do not exist. Every impossibility result we have derived from it stands; every existence claim at n >= 4 must be re-checked against the rank-and-divisibility condition.

ROWS >= ALLOCATIONS IS A THEOREM IN OUR MODEL, SO THE DESIGN TARGET IS r = m AND SCORE >= 2 * (MINIMUM AUX ALLOCATIONS). Argument: for fixed inputs the solution set lives in A^m and is cut by r hypersurfaces, so every component has dimension >= m - r; determinism forces dimension 0, hence r >= m. Over a general field this has an escape hatch via anisotropic forms, but A SINGLE-PRODUCT ROW HAS QUADRATIC PART A*B, A PRODUCT OF TWO F_p-LINEAR FORMS, HENCE SPLIT AND ISOTROPIC — so the hypersurface is F_p-rational and the bound is rigorous here. USE IT AS A BUDGET: any gadget emitting more rows than it allocates is at the floor and cannot be improved except by allocating less; any gadget allocating more than it constrains is broken. This is the structural companion to the materialisation law, and it is how to tell 'this gadget is finished' from 'this gadget is merely tidy'. Note the boundary: this and the one-row impossibility results all live in the model where THE ROW ALONE determines the witness. Our decoy-root packing buys its win from EXTERNAL range bounds making a spurious root unreachable, so it sits outside this model and is not contradicted by it — but that boundary should be stated explicitly wherever the Lean development mixes the two.

RANGE CHECKS COST 2 SCORE PER BIT AND THAT IS THE FLOOR IN PLAIN R1CS — STOP LOOKING FOR A CHEAPER ONE. Structural argument: a digit d in [0, 2^c) certified by the vanishing polynomial d(d-1)...(d-(2^c-1)) = 0 has degree 2^c and needs 2^c - 1 rows for c bits, so rows-per-bit (2^c - 1)/c is MINIMISED AT c = 1. Booleanity is optimal within the family. ALREADY OURS, DO NOT RE-DERIVE: the top-bit-affine form — allocate only bits 0..n-2, then DEFINE the top bit as the free affine expression 2^-(n-1) * (x - sum_{i<n-1} 2^i b_i) and emit n booleanity rows and ZERO identity rows. RangeCheck.lean does exactly this (`witnessVector (n-1)` then `assertZero (top * (top - 1))`), which is why RangeCheck n costs (n-1, n). REJECTED WITH REASON — LAGRANGE FOUR-SQUARES: in F_p EVERY element is a sum of three squares, so 4x+1 = a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 carries ZERO information without bounds on a,b,c,d, which is the original problem restated. It works over Z or in hidden-order groups, never here. Every genuine batching technique (Plookup, logUp, halo2 table chips, gnark's commitment challenge) needs lookups or randomness and is outside our model. ALSO WORTH KNOWING: for a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT bound X of n bits, `a < X` costs the SAME n booleanity rows as `a < 2^n`, by writing a = (X - 2^(n-1))*b + c with b boolean and c < 2^(n-1) (Khovratovich, https://hackmd.io/@7dpNYqjKQGeYC7wMlPxHtQ/B1w_9nq2Y) — so canonicality is never intrinsically more expensive than a plain range check. OUR ValidPBytes AT 260/265 FOR A 256-BIT CANONICAL VALUE IS ALREADY AT THAT OPTIMUM (a plain 256-bit range check is 255/256), so there is nothing to win here — recorded so nobody spends a slot on it.

THE 2k-1 MULTIPLY IS NOT JUST BEST KNOWN, IT IS PROVED OPTIMAL, AND THE CITATION CHAIN IS WORTH HAVING. Fiduccia-Zalcstein (JACM 24(2), 1977): the bilinear complexity of multiplying two degree-(k-1) polynomials is >= 2k-1 over ANY field. Toom (1963): tight, achieved by evaluation-interpolation whenever 2k-1 <= q+1 (the q field elements PLUS the point at infinity). Winograd (1977): ALL minimal algorithms ARE interpolation algorithms — there is no other route. Feig (1981): for this class all minimal division-free algorithms are bilinear, so R1CS rows being quadratic rather than merely bilinear buys nothing extra. For BN254 the condition 2k-1 <= p+1 holds for k up to ~2^252, SO THE FIELD-SIZE CONDITION IS NEVER BINDING and 2k-1 is the exact answer to 'minimum rows to certify a k-limb product'. This closes the question permanently and independently confirms the Karatsuba/Toom rejections. *** QUALIFIED, AND THE QUALIFICATION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE THEOREM. Fiduccia-Zalcstein bounds the rank of multiplication in F[X] — the FULL product. It says nothing about multiplication in a RESIDUE RING F[X]/(m(X)), whose rank is given instead by the Chinese-remainder/Winograd count SUM over irreducible factors f_i of m of (2*deg f_i - 1), which is STRICTLY SMALLER whenever m splits. Since our circuits never consume the full product — foldLhs immediately reduces mod X^numLimbs - cF — the applicable floor is the residue-ring one. DO NOT CITE 2k-1 AS A FLOOR AGAINST A FOLDED PRODUCT. ***

THE SQRT-N LAW (PATERSON-STOCKMEYER) — ANY FUNCTION ON A DOMAIN OF SIZE N COSTS ~2*sqrt(N) ROWS, NOT N. THIS IS THE BIGGEST UNUSED GENERAL TECHNIQUE WE HAVE FOUND AND IT APPLIES WHEREVER A TABLE, AN S-BOX, A PIECEWISE FUNCTION, OR 'MEMBERSHIP IN AN ARBITRARY SET OF N ELEMENTS' APPEARS. MECHANISM (baby-step/giant-step): to evaluate a degree-N univariate P, compute x^2..x^k (k-1 rows), then write P = sum_j B_j(x) * (x^k)^j with deg B_j < k. EACH B_j IS A FREE AFFINE COMBINATION OF THE ALREADY-COMPUTED POWERS, so the Horner recursion in y = x^k costs ONE ROW PER GIANT STEP. Optimum at k ~ sqrt(N) gives ~2*sqrt(N) rows. MEASURED SCHEDULE, full gadget score including the input range check: N=16 -> 19 (naive 29); N=256 -> 75 (naive 509); N=1024 -> 143 (naive 2045); N=4096 -> 271 (naive 8189). WORKED EXAMPLE: an 8-bit S-box with the input already range-checked — Lagrange-interpolate to degree <= 255 over F_p and evaluate with k = 16, giving 30 rows + 29 witnesses + 16 for the range check = 75 against 509. UPPER BOUND sqrt(2N) + O(log N), Paterson-Stockmeyer SIAM J. Comput. 2(1):60-66, 1973, https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/0202007. MATCHING LOWER BOUND THAT SURVIVES NONDETERMINISM: parameter counting gives s >~ 0.58*sqrt(N), so 2*sqrt(N) is within ~3.5x of optimal AND YOU SHOULD STOP THERE. Vector-valued analogue with matched bounds: Boyar-Find, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.6169.

A RANK-r QUADRATIC CONDITION COSTS ceil(r/2) ROWS, NOT r — AN EXACT 2x, AND IT IS A SWEEP OVER EVERY QUADRATIC IN THE TREE. The naive idiom accumulates x_i * l_i(x) at r rows and r-1 witnesses. Instead DIAGONALISE q AT COMPILE TIME: over F_p, Chevalley-Warning forces every form in >= 3 variables to be isotropic, so q splits as hyperbolic planes perpendicular to an anisotropic kernel of dimension <= 2, and EACH HYPERBOLIC PLANE IS A PRODUCT OF TWO F_p-LINEAR FORMS = ONE ROW. The trick that makes it tight: LET THE LAST ROW'S C SLOT ABSORB THE RUNNING SUM, l_{2t-1} * l_{2t} = z - u_1 - ... - u_{t-1}, which is affine hence free. Cost ceil(r/2) rows + ceil(r/2)-1 witnesses ~ score r-1. OPTIMALITY IS MATCHING: rank is subadditive and each row contributes rank <= 2. WORKED: sum of 8 squares = z is 4 rows + 3 witnesses = 7, against 8 rows + 7 witnesses = 15. APPLIES TO any squared norm, squared distance, self-inner-product, or symmetric bilinear form — INCLUDING CURVE EQUATIONS AND THE x1*x2*y1*y2 STYLE TERMS IN EC ADDITION. Verified splitting constants mod the BN254 scalar prime: x^2+y^2, x^2-y^2, x^2+2y^2, x^2+3y^2, x^2+6y^2, x^2+13y^2 are each ONE ROW; x^2+5y^2, x^2+7y^2, x^2+11y^2, x^2+17y^2 are not (criterion is (ab/r) = 1, using (-1/r) = 1). CAVEAT ON THE DUAL SIDE: the rank-<=2 locus in symmetric NxN matrices has codimension (N-1)(N-2)/2, so hunting for free low-rank combinations in a constraint span only pays when the span has real structure — generically there is nothing there, and finding them is MinRank.

THREE LOWER-BOUND TOOLS TO USE AS STOPPING CRITERIA — KNOWING A GADGET IS AT THE FLOOR IS WORTH AS MUCH AS ANOTHER OPTIMISATION. (1) KRULL CODIMENSION: each row is one hypersurface, so by Krull's height theorem every component of V(f_1..f_k) has codimension <= k; if soundness demands the witness be determined by the inputs then dim V = #inputs, so k >= m - dim V and SCORE >= 2m - dim V. THE STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE IN THIS WHOLE CORPUS: the triangular pattern (each witness defined by exactly one row) ALREADY MEETS THIS WITH EQUALITY, so YOU CANNOT SHAVE ROWS BY CLEVERNESS IN THE CONSTRAINT LAYER ALONE — YOU CAN ONLY SHAVE ROWS BY SHAVING WITNESSES. Conversely k > m - dim V PROVES redundancy exists. Mathlib has this as Ideal.height_le_spanRank_toENat_of_mem_minimalPrimes. (2) BEZOUT DEGREE: each row at most DOUBLES degree, so k >= log2 deg(graph of the certified relation). Sanity checks — y = x^5 needs k >= 3 so Poseidon's 3-row S-box is optimal and no nondeterministic trick shaves it; y = 1/x has graph xy = 1 of degree 2 so k >= 1, correctly NOT penalising the witnessed-inverse trick. (3) COUNTING OVER F_p, the one that survives nondeterminism: a k-row m-wire system is described by 3k(m+1) field elements, so with s = k+m, s >= 2*sqrt(log_p|F| / 3) - 1. This gives s >= 295 for an arbitrary 16-bit table — A RIGOROUS PROOF THAT LOOKUP-FREE TABLE EMULATION IS EXPENSIVE. CRITICAL WARNING ATTACHED: MC >= deg - 1 DOES NOT HOLD OVER F_p. One row doubles multilinear degree, so you only get rows >= ceil(log2 deg). Do NOT use the GF(2) degree bound to convince yourself an F_p gadget is optimal — the IsZero trick (a degree-n function in 2 rows) is exactly the loophole. HONEST LIMIT: all three bounds are geometric, constraining V(F_p-bar) while soundness only concerns V(F_p); by Lang-Weil they are effectively unconditional for gadgets under about 63 rows, and genuinely open above that.

WHERE F_p BEATS GF(2) AND WHERE IT LOSES — A PACKING RULE, NOT A SLOGAN. F_p WINS ON WIDE FAN-IN CONJUNCTIONS: AND(x_1..x_n) over bits is s = sum x_i - n (FREE, affine) followed by a 2-ROW IsZero, i.e. TWO ROWS INDEPENDENT OF n, against n-1 AND gates in GF(2) (tight there by Schnorr's deg-1 bound). Same for OR_k in 2 constraints. GF(2) WINS ON XOR, which is free there and costs a row here (a xor b = a + b - 2ab) — which is exactly why circomlib's SHA-256 needs 30,952 nonlinear constraints while the Bristol GF(2) circuit needs 22,573 AND gates. PRACTICAL RULE: KEEP VALUES INTEGER-PACKED SO XOR-CHAINS BECOME FREE SUMS, AND BIT-SPLIT ONLY WHEN A GENUINELY BITWISE OPERATION FORCES IT. QUANTIFIED CEILING ON THE WHOLE QUESTION: the counting bound over BN254 is weaker than the GF(2) bound by a factor ~sqrt(3 log2 p)/2 ~ 14, so information-theoretically a 254-bit field can buy AT MOST ~14-16x over the best GF(2) circuit — the published AND-gate records are a realistic if modestly loose guide to what is reachable.

SPLIT ALGEBRAS: WHEN THE MODULUS FACTORS OVER THE NATIVE FIELD, RANK COLLAPSES FROM 2n-1 TO n, AND THE CRT BASE CHANGE IS FREE. Winograd 1980 / Alder-Strassen: multiplication in F[u]/P for P of degree n with k distinct irreducible factors needs 2n-k multiplications; since the CRT change of basis is LINEAR hence free in R1CS, a fully split modulus gives n rows. VERIFIED FOR OUR FIELD: the BN254 scalar prime r has r = 1 mod 2^28, so -1 IS A SQUARE, with explicit i = 21888242871839275217838484774961031246007050428528088939761107053157389710902 (i^2 = -1 checked), and n | r-1 for all n = 2^k with k <= 28 plus many odd n. WORKED — EMULATED F_p2 / COMPLEX MULTIPLICATION IN 2 ROWS INSTEAD OF 3: row 1 is (a + i*b)(c + i*d) = p1, row 2 is (a - i*b)(c - i*d) = p2, then e = (p1+p2)/2 and f = (p1-p2)/(2i) are both FREE. Score 4 against Karatsuba's 6. This is literally Winograd's result that complex multiplication needs 3 multiplications over R but only 2 over C. ALSO: cyclic convolution of length n costs n rows whenever n | r-1, via evaluation at the n-th roots of unity, with both DFTs and the inverse free — but this only wins for genuinely WRAPPED ring arithmetic; a full product still needs 2n-1.

REJECTED WITH REASONS — GENERAL-THEORY DEAD ENDS, RECORDED SO NO SLOT IS SPENT REDISCOVERING THEM. (a) BORDER RANK / STRASSEN-STYLE APPROXIMATION: three independent kills — F_p is a field so there are no nonzero nilpotents and the epsilon cannot be instantiated; emulating K[e]/e^(h+1) inside R1CS costs back exactly the debordering factor; and border rank only amortises under Kronecker powering while golf fixes one small instance. (b) CHUDNOVSKY-CHUDNOVSKY ALGEBRAIC-CURVE MULTIPLICATION: mu_q(n) >= 2n-1 WITH EQUALITY IFF n <= q/2+1, and BN254 has q ~ 2^254, so plain interpolation is already optimal for every n <= 2^253; CC exists solely for fields too SMALL for interpolation (F_2, F_3, F_4). (c) BATCHING k INDEPENDENT RANGE CHECKS: provably worthless — run Bezout on the projection to [0,2^n)^k of size 2^(nk) and get score >= k(2n-1), exactly k independent copies; packing is the same thing rewritten, since the pack is free but you must still bit-decompose it. (d) BASE-B DIGIT DECOMPOSITION: computed exactly with optimal PS evaluation of the vanishing polynomial, score per bit is 2.00 at B=2, 2.52 at B=3, 2.58 at B=5, 2.67 at B=8, 3.50 at B=16, 4.00 at B=32; B=4 TIES EXACTLY AT 2/BIT via root symmetry (d(d-1)(d-2)(d-3) = u(u+2) with u = d(d-3), 2 rows + 1 aux) but never BEATS binary and does not hand you the bits, and the fold does not iterate. (e) LEGENDRE SYMBOL AS A CHEAP SIGN OR HALF-SPACE PREDICATE: dead for BN254 specifically, because r = 1 mod 4 makes chi(-1) = +1 so chi is an EVEN function and cannot distinguish a from -a; the MPC literature's Legendre comparison CHOOSES a prime where chi agrees with sign on a range, and we cannot choose. (f) MINIMAL GENERATOR THEORY (Nakayama mu(I), Betti numbers, Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity): mu(I) IS NOT A LOWER BOUND FOR R1CS — ara(I) <= mu(I) and that gap is precisely what we exploit, so any 'this ideal needs mu generators therefore mu rows' argument is WRONG. (g) SHORTEST-LINEAR-PROGRAM minimisation (Boyar-Matthews-Peralta): minimises XOR count, and XOR/affine is free here — zero value.

TWO MECHANICAL TOOLS WORTH BUILDING, WITH THEIR MEASURED YIELD. (1) ROW-DELETION CRITERION — cheap, sound, and complete for linear combinations: expand each row into its quadratic-monomial coefficient vector Q_k[i,j] plus linear part, then solve sum_k lambda_k Q_k[i,j] = 0 for all (i,j). THIS IS PLAIN GAUSSIAN ELIMINATION, NO GROEBNER BASIS. Then l = sum lambda_k (L_k - C_k) is linear and implied: if l = 0 identically, any row with lambda_k != 0 is REDUNDANT and can be deleted; otherwise l = 0 is a FREE LINEAR CONSTRAINT usable to eliminate a witness, after which a row becomes redundant. Clusters by shared quadratic monomials stay small so it parallelises. MEASURED YIELD TELLS YOU WHEN TO BOTHER: about 0% on hand-tight circuits (32 of 30,134 rows on circomlib SHA-256) but 20%+ on mechanically generated ones (ZoKrates Poseidon 21.8%, EdwardsScalarMult 23.1%) — so run it on anything a job generated in bulk, not on gadgets we hand-tuned. Albert et al., Distilling Constraints in Zero-Knowledge Protocols, CAV 2022. (2) SLIM-STYLE LOCAL EXACT RE-SYNTHESIS IS THE ONLY SEARCH METHOD THAT SCALES: global SAT synthesis dies at 7-12 gates (one 5-input function was UNSAT at k=6 after 120 cores for months), so instead ENUMERATE EVERY CONNECTED SUB-SYSTEM OF 5-7 ROWS AND RE-SYNTHESISE IT EXACTLY. This produced every recent record in the boolean-circuit world (THR^4_5 23->10, THR^4_8 40->22). https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.12579, code https://github.com/alexanderskulikov/circuit_improvement. THIS IS THE ENGINE THE gf2-sha256 SCHEDULE SEARCH NEEDS.

THE MATERIALISATION FLOOR IS MET WITH EQUALITY IN BOTH SECP TREES — 58% OF THE VARIABLE-BASE STEP AND 59% OF THE FIXED-BASE WINDOW HAVE ZERO RECOVERABLE SLACK, SO STOP AUDITING THERE. RangeCheck n costs <n-1, n> = 2n-1 via the top-bit-affine trick, so a 256-bit element costs 4 + <252,256> = 512 in 4x64 limbs AND 8 + <248,256> = 512 in 8x32 limbs — identical, 2.000 per bit, the proved optimum. Whole-circuit check: variable-base 157,748 allocations against 158,688 rows (r/m = 1.006), fixed-base 25,138 against 25,257 (r/m = 1.005). BOTH SIT BELOW THE NAIVE TRIANGULAR VALUE, at 2m minus the number of range checks, because each range check trades an allocation for a row and SAVES 1. CONSEQUENCE, THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE FOR PLANNING: rows and witnesses are locked 1:1, so saving N score means deleting exactly N/2 WITNESSES — for a 16,436 target that is 8,218 witnesses, or 132.5 per loop step. Any proposal that does not delete witnesses is not a proposal.

CERTIFICATE COST FALLS WITH LIMB WIDTH, OPTIMUM NEAR B=16, HARD FLOOR AT L >= 3 — BUT THIS IS GADGET-SPECIFIC, DO NOT PORT IT BLIND. A witnessed-quotient certificate costs 1 + 2*qbits + 2*(2L-1) + 2*carrybits: products grow as 2L-1 while quotient and carry bits shrink with B, so the total is ~1024/B + 4B, minimised near B=16. MEASURED AT TWO POINTS IN THE VARIABLE-BASE TREE: base 2^64 mulModFoldT = 354 (7 products, 72-bit q, 98-bit carry); base 2^32 mulModFold32 = 204 (15 products, 39-bit q, 48-bit carry); base 2^16 modelled ~162. THE LOWER LIMIT IS RIGOROUS: a convolution cell is below L*2^(2B) and must stay under the native prime, with L*B >= 256, so L=2 forces B=128 and a cell below 2^257 > P — hence L >= 3. CRITICAL CAVEAT LEARNED THE HARD WAY: this gain comes from the FOLD CONSTANT being limb-aligned in base 2^32, which collapses the quotient and carry. Where the quotient is instead dominated by an unreduced low half — as in the fixed-base ChainFold — the same move buys about 4 score while costing +8 products per multiply, i.e. a NET LOSS. Measure the gadget, never extrapolate from a sibling tree.

THE CARRY-TAX LAW — WHY A WELL-TUNED NON-NATIVE CHAIN SITS AT A FIXED POINT, AND WHEN DEFERRING A MATERIALISATION CAN NEVER PAY. Cell slack is taxed at 2 SCORE PER BIT PER CARRY, and range-checking is worth 2 SCORE PER BIT. AT ONE GROUPED CARRY THE EXCHANGE IS EXACTLY A WASH, which is precisely why a tuned tree sits at a fixed point and why 'just carry it unreduced' keeps failing to pay. Deferring a 256-bit materialisation saves 2 x 256 = 512, but it injects slack into every downstream cell, and if that slack forces the CARRY COUNT up from 1 to k the tax is k x 2 x (slack bits). MEASURED INSTANCE, fixed-base comb: deferring the accumulator x saves 512 but injects 97.6 bits of slack and forces 3 carries instead of 1, so the tax is 3 x 2 x 97.6 = 585 > 512, plus about 190 more for a fatter quotient — a NET LOSS of roughly 254 per window even in a hypothetical field large enough to permit it. THE COROLLARY THAT MATTERS FOR PLANNING: a materialisation is not pure overhead. It is what BUYS the narrow grouped carry and the narrow quotient downstream. Before proposing to delete one, price what its absence does to the carry COUNT, not just the carry width — the count is the multiplier and it moves in integer steps.

WHEN A PRIOR ANALYSIS REJECTS A REPRESENTATION CHANGE, CHECK THAT IT PRICED THE WIDTH-LINEAR TERMS AND NOT JUST THE COUNT-LINEAR ONES. A measured instance that cost real score: an entry rejected 64-bit -> 32-bit limbs on the grounds that normalisation barely moves (508 vs 504) and product count rises (7 -> 15 cells, +48 per site). BOTH FIGURES WERE RIGHT AND THE CONCLUSION WAS STILL BACKWARDS, because it never recomputed the QUOTIENT and CARRY widths, which are LINEAR IN LIMB WIDTH (W_q = n + log2 k + 1, W_c = n + log2 k + f(n)) and at 2 score per bit dominate: -336 against +48, a net -288 per site. THE GENERAL SHAPE: in a non-native chain the cost splits into COUNT-LINEAR terms (cells, wires, products) and WIDTH-LINEAR terms (range-checked quotient and carry bits). Narrowing the limb width trades the first up and the second down, and the second is bigger whenever any value is range-checked. ALWAYS ENUMERATE BOTH FAMILIES BEFORE ACCEPTING A NEGATIVE VERDICT, and be especially suspicious of a rejection whose stated reason is that a term 'is dominated by' something — domination is usually the reason a term is width-linear, i.e. the reason the move WORKS.

THE RESIDUE-RING MULTIPLY — THE FOLD POLYNOMIAL IS A FREE DESIGN CHOICE AND ITS FACTORISATION SETS THE PRODUCT COST. In any non-native tree that multiplies limb vectors and then immediately folds with z_k + cF*z_{k+m}, the circuit never consumes the full 2m-1 convolution — it consumes only z mod (X^m - cF). Multiplication in the RESIDUE RING F_r[X]/(m(X)) has bilinear rank SUM_i (2*deg f_i - 1) over the irreducible factors f_i of m over F_r, by Chinese remaindering, which BEATS the full-product 2m-1 whenever m splits. THE GADGET: witness the m folded coefficients F, and for each root rho of m emit ONE row (SUM a_i rho^i)*(SUM b_i rho^i) = SUM_k F_k rho^k — a single product per row with all coefficients COMPILE-TIME CONSTANTS, hence affine-free. Soundness is Vandermonde interpolation uniqueness: F - F_true has degree < m and m roots. For a factor of degree d > 1 the same works with 2d-1 evaluations pinning that CRT component. MEASURED INSTANCE, secp256k1 fixed-base: cF = 2^32 + 977 IS A FOURTH POWER MOD THE BN254 SCALAR FIELD (r - 1 has 2-adicity 28, so mu_4 lies in F_r), so X^4 - cF SPLITS COMPLETELY and the rank is 4 — <4,4> = 8 per product against interpolatedMul's <7,7> = 14. THE FOUR ROOTS, VERIFIED: 6022495585687529434600811952072328267646044551480745240691212116594068018376, 6407184712893995821909607707030380421668643124835825632869578387818341362621, 15481058158945279400336798038226894666879721275580208710828625798757467132996, 15865747286151745787645593793184946820902319848935289103006992069981740477241. GENERAL LESSON: BEFORE PRICING A LIMB MULTIPLY, ASK WHAT THE CONSUMER ACTUALLY READS. If it reads a residue, the fold polynomial is yours to choose and you should choose it to split.

CHOOSING THE FOLD MODULUS: SPLITTING MOST IS NOT THE SAME AS BEING BEST, BECAUSE COEFFICIENT SIZE IS PRICED TOO. At base 2^32 there are two admissible degree-8 fold moduli for secp256k1 and the SMALL-COEFFICIENT one wins even though it splits LESS. (a) X^8 - cF with cF = 2^32 + 977 splits completely, rank 8, <8,8> = 16 per product — but the folded coefficients reach ~2^99, forcing a 66-bit carry (132 score). (b) X^8 - X - 977, which is the UNIQUE degree-8 modulus vanishing at 2^32 mod p with all coefficients below 2^31 (the digit recursion forces a = (977,1,0,...)), factors as (1)(2)(2)(3) — one linear root 4057929584660596922171240314385854169924567973749597780255708884483859498814, two quadratics and a cubic — so rank = 1 + 3 + 3 + 5 = 12, <12,12> = 24 per product, FOUR MORE than (a). It still wins, because the growth factor drops from cF ~ 2^32 to 977 ~ 2^10: certificates land at 182/216 against (a)'s 220/244. THE 22-BIT-SMALLER COEFFICIENTS BEAT THE FOUR EXTRA PRODUCTS, because coefficient size is taxed at 2 score per bit through the carry and the quotient while products are taxed at 2 score each. PRICE BOTH TERMS; do not pick the modulus by rank alone. (Checked and rejected: base 2^16, where cF is NOT a 16th power mod r — X^16 - cF has zero roots and every quadratic cofactor is irreducible, rank 24 — and X^16 - X^2 - 977 makes the narrow certificate ~166 but the wide one ~236 while costing +180 per select. Net worse.)

THE RESIDUE-RING MULTIPLY IS PROVED OPTIMAL, NOT MERELY BEST-KNOWN — WINOGRAD'S 2N - k BOUND, AND IT GIVES A CLEAN DESIGN RULE FOR CHOOSING THE FOLD MODULUS. THEOREM (Winograd, 'Some bilinear forms whose multiplicative complexity depends on the field of constants'): multiplication in F[X]/(f) where deg f = N and f has k DISTINCT IRREDUCIBLE FACTORS over F requires AT LEAST 2N - k products, and the bound is TIGHT whenever the field is large enough for Toom-Cook evaluation-interpolation (2N - 1 <= q + 1, which for BN254's r ~ 2^254 is never a constraint here). Note 2N - k is the same number as SUM_i (2 deg f_i - 1), since SUM_i deg f_i = N — so the CRT construction is not just a good idea, IT MEETS THE LOWER BOUND. CHECKED AGAINST ALL THREE MODULI WE HAVE PRICED, AND ALL THREE ARE OPTIMAL: X^4 - cF splits completely so N=4, k=4, floor 2(4) - 4 = 4, and our CRT gadget is 4; X^8 - X - 977 factors (1)(2)(2)(3) so N=8, k=4, floor 16 - 4 = 12, and the gadget is 12; X^8 - cF splits completely so N=8, k=8, floor 16 - 8 = 8, and the gadget is 8. THE COROLLARIES THAT MATTER FOR DESIGN: (1) THE ABSOLUTE FLOOR FOR A DEGREE-N RESIDUE MULTIPLY IS N PRODUCTS, attained exactly when the modulus SPLITS COMPLETELY (k = N) — so at N=4 the floor is 4 against interpolatedMul's 7, and the full-product 2N - 1 is nearly DOUBLE the residue floor. (2) EACH ADDITIONAL IRREDUCIBLE FACTOR IS WORTH EXACTLY ONE PRODUCT, i.e. 2 score. That makes the modulus choice a quantitative trade rather than a judgement call: compare 2 * (delta k) against 2 * (delta coefficient bits) summed over every range-checked width the coefficients feed. MEASURED INSTANCE, secp256k1 fixed-base at base 2^32: X^8 - cF has delta k = +4 over X^8 - X - 977, saving 8 score in products, but its folded coefficients are about 22 bits wider, costing roughly 38 + 28 = 66 across the two certificates — so the SMALL-COEFFICIENT modulus wins by about 58, which is exactly the measured 220/244 against 182/216. THE RULE: PICK THE SMALLEST-COEFFICIENT MODULUS THAT VANISHES AT THE BASE, THEN TAKE WHATEVER k IT HAPPENS TO HAVE — coefficient width moves in tens of bits while k moves in single digits, so width almost always dominates. Related theory if a case ever looks marginal: Blaser's complete characterisation of algebras of minimal bilinear complexity, and the Averbuch-Galil-Winograd minimal-rank theory for local algebras F_q[X]/X^N.

WEB PASS, FIVE TOPICS, ONE HIT AND FOUR DRY — RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-SEARCHES THIS GROUND. THE HIT was Winograd's 2N - k bound, above. THE DRY ONES, with the reason each fails to transfer: (1) SHA-256 IN R1CS — nothing beyond what we have; the public figures quoted are still ~826k constraints for a Merkle leaf and ~750k for the SHA-2 part of RS256, which are two orders of magnitude above our tree, so the literature is not operating anywhere near this frontier. (2) KECCAK-f1600 — results are all FPGA/LUT3 architecture papers and the standard bit-packing writeups we already have; nothing new on chi or theta in an R1CS cost model. (3) NON-NATIVE BIGINT — 'Efficient Foreign-Field Arithmetic in PLONK' (eprint 2025/695) builds on Lubarov-Baylina by taking TIGHTER BOUNDS ON THE ENCODING, which is precisely what our position-aware nf bounds and per-site FoldParams already do and which has now been PROVED TIGHT for our instance, and it is PLONK-custom-gate-shaped besides. 'Zinc+: SNARKs for Polynomial Rings' (eprint 2026/855) is a different arithmetisation, not a constraint-count technique. VROOM (eprint 2026/393, USENIX Security 2026) sounds relevant and is NOT — it is CPU/GPU vectorisation of RNS modular arithmetic (4.0x on RSA-4096 verify against OpenSSL), with no proof system and no constraint reduction. (4) secp256k1 VARIABLE-BASE — the reachable material is GLV, wNAF and Fake GLV, ALL THREE ALREADY IN THE CORPUS, and the best public R1CS figure remains the Zcash thread's 9 constraints per scalar bit, or 8.5 with a recoded [0,1,2,-1] digit set, against our tree's far lower rate. (5) FIXED-BASE COMB — signed-digit and w-NAF comb papers are all the classical hardware/software line (MDPI Sensors, Koblitz-curve combs) with no circuit cost model; the one genuinely relevant external lead here remains gnark's signed-digit fixed-base comb PR #1797, which is already recorded. GENERAL OBSERVATION WORTH KEEPING: the published literature optimises for PROVER TIME under lookup-and-custom-gate models, so its constraint counts are not comparable to ours and its techniques usually do not transfer. THE PRODUCTIVE SEARCHES ARE NOT ZK SEARCHES — the one hit this pass came from ALGEBRAIC COMPLEXITY THEORY (bilinear rank), not from cryptography. Search there next time. *** REFINEMENT 2026-08-11, AND IT DOES NOT OVERTURN THE DISMISSAL ABOVE. The 2025/695 contribution is sharper than 'tighter bounds': the stated consequence is that IN MOST CASES ONE EXTRA AUXILIARY MODULUS SUFFICES AND THE CHECK BECOMES DETERMINISTIC, where Lubarov-Baylina with loose bounds needs DOZENS of moduli and is only PROBABILISTICALLY sound. That distinction is the one that normally matters to us, since our obligation is an unconditional 'forall env' Lean theorem and a probabilistic bignum check is unusable at any price. IT STILL DOES NOT TRANSFER, for three reasons that were already implicit above and are now explicit: (a) WE DO NOT USE casting-out-primes at all -- our modmul is limb-polynomial with grouped carries, and our own costing puts a CRT-against-small-primes scheme at roughly 6.5x worse, though note that calculation assumed the many-moduli regime and should be restated as such rather than as a general refutation; (b) our nf bounds are already PROVED TIGHT for our instance, so the paper's improvement is one we have already taken by another route; (c) their headline 'one order of magnitude for EC emulation' is a PLONK CUSTOM-GATE count and does not convert to R1CS allocations+constraints. One number of ours does argue for revisiting it if that ever changes: the native-field channel is a fixed ~253-bit credit, worth ~49.4% of the work at a 256-bit foreign field against only ~3.1% at 4096 bits -- so if a version of this is ever worth trying it is on the secp256k1 slugs, never on RSA. eprint.iacr.org PDFs return 403 from this sandbox, so exact counts and the tight-bound inequality remain UNVERIFIED. ***

ROUNDED POWER-OF-TWO BOUNDS WASTE UP TO A FULL BIT PER CARRY, AND A BIT IS 2 SCORE AT EVERY SITE THAT SHARES THE PARAMETER — CARRY THE EXACT MIXED-RADIX CONSTANT INSTEAD. MEASURED, and it took a record: secp256k1 variable-base 315,768 -> 315,676, a clean -92, and the ENTIRE change is four constants in one params file. ParamsFold32T.lean went from the rounded form nfFold32TL = 2^77, nfFold32TR = 2^70, offFold32TL = 2^45 + 2^14, offFold32TR = 2^39 to the EXACT form nfFold32TL = 979*2^67 + 3*2^32, nfFold32TR = 2^69 + 3*2^64, offFold32TL = 979*2^35 + 8192, offFold32TR = 2^37 + 3*2^32 + 256, and wfFold32T dropped 46 -> 45. That single bit propagated as <-1,-1> through EVERY gadget sharing the instance — mulModFold32TCost <97,99> -> <96,98>, and likewise mulModSub2F32Cost, mulModBeta32Cost, mulModSqN32Cost, pointValidCount, slopeXSCost, fusedStepCost, glvStepCost — for -92 at the top. WHY IT WORKS: a bound written as 2^a or 2^a + 2^b is an OVER-ESTIMATE of a quantity whose true value is a small integer multiple of a power of two (here 979 = the Solinas constant 977 plus 2, and 3 = the borrow-free digit cap), and the carry width is ceil(log2(OFF_L + OFF_R)), so rounding each addend up to the next power of two can push the ceiling across an integer boundary. THE CHECK IS CHEAP AND MECHANICAL: for every Nf/OFF constant in every params file, write the true bound as an exact integer expression (small multiplier times power of two, summed), recompute ceil(log2(...)), and see whether the width falls. THIS IS DISTINCT FROM per-site specialisation of a shared instance, which is the other FoldParams lever — that one narrows the CONSUMER, this one sharpens the CONSTANT, and they compose. SWEEP EVERY TREE FOR IT: any params file whose Nf/OFF entries are bare powers of two or sums of two powers of two is a candidate, and at 2 score per bit times the number of sharing sites the payoff scales with how widely the instance is reused.

THE EXPORTED COST IN Main.lean MUST BE DEFEQ TO THE INTERNAL LEDGER, AND GETTING THIS WRONG BOTH FAILS TO SCORE AND FAILS TO BUILD — IT HAS NOW COST US TWICE, ON TWO DIFFERENT CHALLENGES. Main.lean's cost theorem is typically `theorem mainCost : circuitCost main <allocations, constraints> := fun input => Comb.costIs_main input`, i.e. the literal pair must be DEFINITIONALLY EQUAL to whatever the internal cost constant (combCost, mainCost, sparseMainCost) evaluates to. If the circuit shrinks and the internal constant is updated but the Main literals are not, the term `Comb.costIs_main input : CostIs _ combCost` NO LONGER HAS THE ASCRIBED TYPE and elaboration fails outright. THE TWO MEASURED CASES: (1) secp256k1 fixed-base submission e8070daa shipped a COMPLETE CRT fold multiply — combCost correctly advanced <24564,24654> -> <24377,24467> — while Main.lean still declared 24560/24650, the value for the small Canonicalize change alone. Type mismatch, status `failed`, and the -374 was invisible: it CLAIMED only -8. (2) sha256 shipped an improved configuration proved in a module nothing imported, so MainSparse's exported literals never moved and nineteen submissions would have scored the OLD number even had they built. THE RULE: after any cost change, re-derive the Main literals FROM the internal constant rather than editing them by hand, and check that every intermediate constant on the path from the changed gadget up to Main was updated — extCost, startCost, the FinalAdd cost, combCost, then Main. THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT FINDS IT IN SECONDS: extract every `def X : Count := <a, c>` from both trees and diff; if Main's pair differs from the top-level container's pair, that is the bug. THIS IS ALSO WHY A FAILED SUBMISSION IS WORTH KEEPING — the whole diagnosis took one diff of cost literals, and it recovered a finished 553-line proof that would otherwise have been redone from scratch.

WEB PASS — DRY ON THE LITERATURE, BUT IT SETTLED ONE REAL QUESTION. NOTHING NEW WAS FOUND, and the reasons are worth keeping so the ground is not re-searched. (1) The one paper that looked like a direct hit, 'Fast elliptic curve scalar multiplications in SN(T)ARK circuits' (Eagen, El Housni, Masson, Piellard, eprint 2025/933, LATINCRYPT 2025), IS THE FAKE GLV PAPER AND WE ALREADY RUN ITS TECHNIQUE AT DIMENSION 4 in the variable-base tree — and we already have the sharper result that dimension 4 is the ceiling for SOUNDNESS reasons, not cost. Its headline is a 22-53% PROVING-TIME speed-up, which is not our metric. (2) Zinc+ (eprint 2026/855) arithmetises SHA-256 over Universal Constraint Systems with ideal-membership predicates across several polynomial rings — A DIFFERENT ARITHMETISATION, not a constraint-count technique for plain R1CS. (3) Flock (arXiv 2607.27491) reports ~30,000 Keccak permutations per second at under 250x native overhead — again proving throughput, not rows. (4) RainHash2.0 (eprint 2026/1441) is a new arithmetisation-friendly hash, irrelevant when the spec fixes SHA-256 and Keccak. (5) Bilinear-rank searches for a multi-output one-hot selection bound returned only Boolean multiplicative-complexity results and planar-circuit lower bounds, nothing that maps onto 'affine is free, one product per row'. THE STANDING LESSON HOLDS AND IS REINFORCED: the published literature optimises PROVER TIME under lookup and custom-gate models, so its numbers are not comparable to ours and its techniques usually do not transfer. Search algebraic complexity theory before cryptography.

THE SELECT-GADGET SEARCH IS NOT A TENSOR-RANK PROBLEM, AND MISTAKING IT FOR ONE POINTS THE SEARCH AT A STRICTLY HARDER QUESTION. Generic low-rank tensor decomposition asks for an identity valid for ALL inputs. Our select gadgets only ever see inputs constrained to the ONE-HOT VARIETY, so we need identities valid ONLY THERE, and rank over a variety can be far below generic rank. THE RANK-2 PAIRING IS EXACTLY SUCH AN IDENTITY AND IS THE PROOF OF THE POINT: it works because u_i u_i' = 0 and e_j e_j' = delta_jj' e_j, both of which are FALSE off the variety, so no generic decomposition method could ever have produced it. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES. (1) Off-the-shelf tooling is the wrong instrument. The state of the art for explicit low-rank decompositions of specific small tensors is FLIP GRAPH SEARCH — random walks over rank-preserving transformations of CP decompositions, where a flip rewires two terms sharing a common factor, used to escape local minima where no shared factor admits further reduction. There are 2026 open-source frameworks (arXiv:2603.02398, github.com/dronperminov/ternary_flip_graph and /FastMatrixMultiplication) and further ISSAC 2026 work on structured variants. BUT THEY ARE SPECIALISED TO MATRIX-MULTIPLICATION TENSORS, with no support for arbitrary 3-tensors, for a specific large prime field, or for constraining factors to be one-hot — so they would need real adaptation, and even adapted they search the generic problem. (2) The correct formulation is a CONSTRAINED search: find A, B, C affine in {1, the one-hot coordinates, prior witnesses} such that the identity holds MODULO THE IDEAL generated by the one-hot relations. That is a Groebner/ideal-membership question, not a CP decomposition. (3) THE PARAMETER-COUNTING BOUND IS UNAFFECTED and still stands, because it counts degrees of freedom in the circuit against independent table constants that must be realised, which holds on or off the variety — what the variety changes is ACHIEVABILITY, not the floor. THE GENERAL LESSON: before reaching for a decomposition tool, ask what set the identity must hold on. If the inputs are constrained, the tool is solving a harder problem than you have.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN FRAMING — A BROKEN COST LEDGER IS A SYMPTOM, NOT THE CAUSE, AND REPAIRING IT DOES NOT RESCUE A FAILED SUBMISSION. I have twice diagnosed a failed tree as 'the cost constants do not chain', verified the arithmetic, fixed the stale number and resubmitted. BOTH REPAIRS FAILED. (1) fixed-base b72bd28d: e8070daa's Main.lean literals were provably inconsistent with combCost; corrected them; failed. (2) secp256k1-scalar-mul 4398b40a: c1ce059e's glvScalarMulCost matched neither its own decomposition nor Main's ascription, and the decomposition re-summed to Main's figures exactly; corrected the one number; failed. THE INCONSISTENCIES WERE REAL — that part is not in doubt, it is arithmetic — BUT THEY ARE THE TRACE OF A JOB THAT COULD NOT FINISH, NOT THE REASON THE SUBMISSION WAS REJECTED. The plausible mechanism: the job hit a genuine proof obligation it could not discharge, and left the tree half-updated; the stale constant is where it stopped, not what stopped it. TWO CONSEQUENCES. FOR JOBS the discipline still stands and is worth stating — a tree whose ledger does not add up will CERTAINLY fail, so re-sum the chain before returning. FOR US THE PRACTICE IS RETIRED: do NOT repair a failed tree's cost constants and resubmit. It is 0 for 2, and each attempt spends a submission and my time to learn nothing, because without a build log a successful repair and a doomed one look identical from here. THE GENERAL LESSON, WHICH IS THE ONE I SHOULD HAVE APPLIED EARLIER: WHEN A FIX FOR A CONFIDENTLY-DIAGNOSED DEFECT DOES NOT WORK, THE DIAGNOSIS WAS INCOMPLETE — and the second failure of the same kind of fix is strong evidence, not bad luck.

DEFER EVERY INTERMEDIATE MOD-n REDUCTION INTO ONE INTEGER IDENTITY WITH A SINGLE QUOTIENT — MEASURED -2,998 ON ONE GADGET. The secp256k1 variable-base scalar relation used to perform FOUR separate MulModLooseQ reductions to build one final congruence: t1 = lambda*|u2| mod n, t2 = |v1|*s mod n, lv2 = |v2|*s mod n, then t3 = lambda*lv2 mod n. The rewrite performs ONE wide product (W = lambda*s mod n) and defers everything else, certifying the WHOLE relation as a single natural-number identity with one witnessed quotient: relLhsNat = eigenvalue*mu2 + mu1 + BigInt.value c + BigInt.value e + biasKRel*scalarOrder, relRhs0Nat = 2*(eigenvalue*nm2 + nm1 + BigInt.value d + BigInt.value f), and qRelNat = (relLhsNat - relRhs0Nat) / scalarOrder. relationCost <2365,2387> -> <874,880>, i.e. -1,491 allocations and -1,507 rows. THE SUPPORTING WORK IS THREE SMALL FILES — ParamsRel (the magnitude parameters), RelCells (the per-position cells) and ScaleVec — which is the usual shape: a deferred identity needs its own bound instance, and nothing else. THIS IS THE SAME LAW ALREADY RECORDED FOR FIELD ARITHMETIC ('sharing ONE reduction across M products costs 424 rows at M=1, 457 at M=2, 490 at M=4', so each extra product adds only about 33), now applied to a RELATION rather than to a multiply chain, and it is the same family as the competitor's MulModFold32M. THE GENERAL RULE: WHEREVER A GADGET PERFORMS SEVERAL INDEPENDENT MODULAR REDUCTIONS ONLY TO COMBINE THE RESULTS INTO ONE FINAL CONGRUENCE, EVERY REDUCTION BUT THE LAST IS WASTE — defer them into a single integer identity and pay for one quotient and one carry chain. Grep any tree for two or more mod-reduction subcircuits whose outputs feed a common assertion; that is the signature.

RETIRE THE PER-FAILURE COST-CHAIN CHECK — IT IS NOW 5 FOR 5 UNINFORMATIVE. After the cost-chain discipline went into the prompts, I kept running the cheap check on every failed submission: extract Main.lean's declared allocations and constraints, the top-level Count, and the decomposition sum, and confirm all three agree. It caught four real bugs BEFORE the prompt change (container ahead of Main; an improvement in an unimported module; a hard-coded <19 * 1113, 19 * 1117> literal inside a cost proof; a stale intermediate aggregate). Since the change it has closed EXACTLY on five consecutive failures across both secp challenges — 47437, 307230, 46828, 307782 and 306982 — every one with no `sorry` and every column matching to the unit. THE PRIOR HAS FLIPPED: a failed submission is now overwhelmingly a genuine proof failure, and the check's expected information is close to zero. KEEP IT AS A SPOT CHECK — run it if a failure looks anomalous, or after any change to the prompts or the harness that could reintroduce the bug class — BUT STOP RUNNING IT ON EVERY FAILURE. THE GENERAL LESSON, WHICH IS THE REASON TO WRITE THIS DOWN: A DIAGNOSTIC EARNS ITS PLACE BY DISCRIMINATING, AND ONE THAT HAS RETURNED THE SAME ANSWER FIVE TIMES RUNNING HAS STOPPED DISCRIMINATING. Re-examine standing checks periodically and retire the ones whose base rate has moved, exactly as you would retire a queue item whose premise has moved.

THE COST MODEL RESTATED CORRECTLY — SCORE IS 2 x BITS OF ADVICE, NOT 2 x BITS. The 2-per-bit charge applies ONLY to values pinned to a finite set BY ROWS. It does NOT apply to values whose bounds are IMPLIED — convolution cells of already-bounded operands cost ZERO, which is why interpolatedMul witnesses 15 cells with no range check at all. So the invariant is: SCORE ~ 2 x (TOTAL BITS OF NON-DETERMINISTIC ADVICE THAT IS NOT POLYNOMIAL IN PRIOR ADVICE). THIS REFRAMING IS NOT COSMETIC — IT RELOCATES MOST OF THE SUPPOSED FLOOR. In the variable-base ELM step the advice is exactly the DIVISION OUTPUTS, lambda1 and w; xS, x4 and y4 are POLYNOMIAL in (lambda1, w, table) and are therefore materialised BY CHOICE, NOT BY NECESSITY. Numerically: advice-forced checks are 2 x 531 = 1,062 per step = 65,844, while checks on DERIVED values are 3 x ~510 = 1,521 per step = 94,302 — SO OF THE 160,146 I HAVE BEEN CALLING THE FLOOR, 94,302 IS A REPRESENTATION CHOICE. Also answers a question I posed directly: 'is a value known to be a sum of products of bounded things cheaper to range-check?' — it is not sub-2-per-bit, IT IS FREE, because its bound is implied and no rows are needed. THE CHARGE IS ON ADVICE, NOT ON BITS.

FIVE PRICED REFUTATIONS IN THE RANGE-PROOF LITERATURE — THE EXTERNAL SPACE IS NOW CLOSED, DO NOT RE-SEARCH IT. (1) LatticeFold+ (eprint 2025/247), the newest and most tempting, is dead by an exact number: it certifies f_i in (-d/2, d/2) where d is the RING DEGREE, so the encoding is UNARY IN THE RANGE SIZE and one 32-bit limb needs d = 2^32 coefficients, i.e. at least 2^32 allocations for what costs 63 today — a factor of 3.4e7. It also needs an Ajtai commitment and challenges. (2) SUMS OF SQUARES (Lagrange, Boudot, Lipmaa, Groth's 4x+1 = a^2+b^2+c^2) IS VACUOUS OVER F_p: every finite-field element is a sum of TWO squares, since {a^2} and {c - b^2} each have (p+1)/2 elements and must intersect, so the R1CS is satisfiable for EVERY x. The naive gadget costs about 8 score and proves nothing; the REPAIRED gadget must range-check a, b, c to 129 bits each at 3 x (2*129 - 1) = 771 against 511 for checking x directly, i.e. 1.51x WORSE. With the checks dropped the forgery is not merely possible but GENERIC. (3) Bounded integer commitments (Couteau-Klooss-Lin-Reichle, EC'21) genuinely remove hidden-order groups but derive soundness from a COMPUTATIONAL ASSUMPTION plus a Sigma-protocol challenge, not an algebraic identity — there is no fixed arithmetic circuit. (4) MULTIMODULAR / CRT VERIFICATION IS EXCLUDED BY A CHARACTERISTIC THEOREM: every ring constructible by R1CS arithmetic over F_r — including F_r[X]/(f) for any f, split algebras, extension fields — HAS CHARACTERISTIC r, so it can only certify statements modulo r, and a second independent modulus must be SIMULATED by witnessing t with x - y = m*t and range-checking t at exactly bits(x) - bits(m) bits. THE SECOND MODULUS COSTS PRECISELY THE BITS IT SAVES. The one exception is a modulus free by construction, 2^(nT) from witnessing T carry limbs — which is Lubarov-Baylina casting-out-primes, already in our tree, and its width is information-theoretically forced at ceil(log2 U) - log2 r + 1, met with EQUALITY by our Wf = 45. (5) Batched/amortised range proofs (Bulletproofs IPA, BP+, BP++, Sharp, Groth-Kohlweiss) shrink PROOF SIZE, never gate count, and need Pedersen commitments plus challenges. NOTE (5) INHERITS THE FINITENESS CAVEAT: the JOINT acceptor over k values is precisely where a positive-dimensional escape is least excluded, so if anyone ever revisits that question, BATCHING is where to look, not single values.

ALTERNATIVE CURVE MODELS FOR secp256k1 ARE EXCLUDED BY GROUP ORDER, NOT BY COST — A COMPLETE LIST, NEVER PRICE THESE AGAIN. #E(secp256k1) IS PRIME, so E has NO rational point of order 2, 3 or 4. Therefore MONTGOMERY (needs 4 | #E), EDWARDS and TWISTED EDWARDS (need an order-4 point), JACOBI QUARTIC and HUFF (need 2-torsion), and HESSIAN and TWISTED HESSIAN (need 3-torsion) are ALL UNAVAILABLE OVER F_p — not merely more expensive. SHORT WEIERSTRASS AFFINE IS THE ONLY MODEL THIS CURVE ADMITS. This generalises the earlier 2-torsion argument to the full family and closes the coordinate-system line permanently.

OUR COST MEASURE HAS A CLASSICAL NAME AND NO KNOWN SUPERLINEAR LOWER BOUND — STOP TRYING TO PROVE FLOORS AND SPEND THE TIME ON CONSTRUCTIONS. A literature sweep of algebraic complexity settles what is and is not provable about 'minimum rank-1 quadratic rows pinning down a relation'. (1) THE MEASURE IS *NONDETERMINISTIC NONSCALAR COMPLEXITY* and it is NOT STUDIED ANYWHERE. Classical multiplicative/nonscalar complexity (Strassen; Schnorr; Boyar-Peralta; Buergisser-Clausen-Shokrollahi, Algebraic Complexity Theory, Grundlehren 315) counts multiplications in a straight-line program that must PRODUCE the value, i.e. it is DETERMINISTIC. No classical model guesses field elements and verifies. (2) VNP IS NOT THE NONDETERMINISTIC ANALOGUE — its quantifier is a SUM over the Boolean cube, not an EXISTENTIAL over F_p, so it is a counting class; and existentially projecting an algebraic set gives a CONSTRUCTIBLE SET, not a polynomial's graph, which is exactly why 'exists-VP' was never defined. (3) THE SANDWICH, AND IT IS THE WHOLE THEORY: log2(deg f) <= rows(f) <= (multiplication gates of any circuit for f) <= |E(ABP)|. The LEFT inequality — Bezout, each row at most doubles degree — IS THE ONLY KNOWN GENERAL LOWER BOUND, and there is NO PAPER PROVING A SUPERLINEAR LOWER BOUND IN THIS MODEL ON ANY EXPLICIT FUNCTION. (4) ABP SIZE IS THE WRONG ANALOGUE, REFUTED BOTH WAYS: it over-counts (GGPR's QAP theorem gives size = n + s with s the MULTIPLICATION-GATE count, not ABP size, so routing through ABPs LOSES), and it cannot lower-bound us at all (bit-decomposition costs ceil(log p) rows and has NO finite ABP over F_p). Same for determinantal complexity: dc = m converts to ~m^3/3 rows (guess an LU factorisation), and dc's defining feature — entries affine in the INPUTS only — is precisely what we drop. (5) VERIFY-BEATS-COMPUTE IS THE POINT AND IT HAS NO CLASSICAL NAME: w*w = x pins a square root in ONE row though no arithmetic circuit over F_p computes it; w*x = 1 inverts in one row. CONVERSELY, IF EVERY NEW WITNESS IS FORCED TO APPEAR ONLY IN THE C SLOT the system is triangular and the model COLLAPSES ONTO classical nonscalar complexity with divisions (Strassen's division-elimination, Crelle 264, 1973) — where the degree bound and Baur-Strassen DO apply. THAT IS THE OPERATIONAL RULE: a gadget written so every advice value is determined by a C-slot is one we can lower-bound and therefore one we have probably already optimised; the wins live where advice sits in the A or B slot.

THE ANCESTORS OF R1CS, AND ONE OF THEM SHIPS AN OPTIMAL SOLVER WE HAVE NEVER TRIED. (a) SPAN PROGRAMS (Karchmer-Wigderson 1993, DOI 10.1109/SCT.1993.336536) are the genuine pre-crypto ancestor: size = NUMBER OF ROWS, acceptance is '1 in span(M_sigma)' = an EXISTENTIAL over a coefficient vector. Their lower-bound machinery is real (Babai-Gal-Wigderson n^Omega(log n / log log n) for clique; Robere-Pitassi-Rossman-Cook EXPONENTIAL for a monotone-P function, FOCS 2016) BUT IT IS ALL MONOTONE AND ALL LINEAR — one product per row is exactly the extension nobody made before GGPR 2013, which cites only Karchmer-Wigderson as ancestor. So there is no borrowed lower bound waiting for us. (b) MQ SATISFIABILITY over a finite field was proved NP-complete by Fraenkel-Yesha, Discrete Appl. Math. 1 (1979) — 'R1CS-SAT is NP-complete' predates GGPR by 34 years — but that literature asks about DECIDING, never about the MINIMUM NUMBER OF EQUATIONS. (c) THE ONE ACTIONABLE FIND — QUADRATIZATION. A non-crypto literature optimises OUR EXACT OBJECTIVE: minimum number of auxiliary variables to reduce a polynomial system to degree 2. Rosenberg 1975 (Cahiers du CERO 17, 71-74) is the origin; Dattani arXiv:1901.04405 catalogues ~70 methods for the Boolean case; and BYCHKOV-POGUDIN, 'Optimal monomial quadratization for ODE systems', arXiv:2103.08013 / IWOCA 2021, gives a PROVABLY OPTIMAL algorithm WITH WORKING SOFTWARE (the QBee Python package). CAVEAT BEFORE ANYONE GETS EXCITED: QBee optimises MONOMIAL quadratizations of ODE right-hand sides over a characteristic-0 field, so it will not read a Lean circuit and will not model our free-affine rule directly. THE USE IS NARROW AND CONCRETE: take a single high-degree polynomial identity we are hand-flattening (a convolution cell, an exception predicate, a fold target), hand it to QBee as a monomial system, and see whether its optimal auxiliary-variable count is BELOW the number of intermediate witnesses we currently allocate. If it ties everywhere, we are flattening optimally and that is worth knowing; if it beats us once, the same trick probably repeats.

ARITHMETICAL RANK SETTLES THE FLOOR QUESTION NEGATIVELY, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN AN OPEN PROBLEM: RADICAL-BASED INVARIANTS ARE DEGREE-BLIND. The commutative-algebra invariant matching 'fewest equations cutting out a set' is the ARITHMETICAL RANK ara(I) = min k with sqrt(f_1..f_k) = sqrt(I). What is known: (1) KRULL'S HEIGHT THEOREM gives ara(I) >= ht(I) = codim V(I) — r equations in A^n cut out something of codimension <= r. THIS IS THE ONLY GENERAL LOWER BOUND AND IT IS EXACTLY OUR OWN COUNTING ARGUMENT: after arithmetisation, #quadratic rows >= #outputs + #auxiliary variables, i.e. EVERY ADVICE VALUE NEEDS AT LEAST ONE ROW. That is the whole tool, and it is why 'score ~ 2 x bits of ADVICE' keeps reproducing itself. (2) EISENBUD-EVANS (Invent. Math. 19, 1973, 107-112; independently STORCH, Arch. Math. 23, 1972) — EVERY algebraic set in A^n is the intersection of n hypersurfaces, and every projective scheme in P^N of N homogeneous ones. So codimension is BOTH the floor AND, with unbounded degree, the ceiling. (3) THE KILLER: KRULL'S BOUND SEES ONLY sqrt(I), SO IT IS INVARIANT UNDER REPLACING f_i BY f_i^k OR BY ANY OTHER GENERATING SET OF THE SAME RADICAL — IT CANNOT DISTINGUISH 'n quadrics' FROM 'n arbitrary polynomials'. There is NO invariant ara_{deg<=d} in the literature, no theorem 'cutting out X requires >= phi(X) quadrics', and no study of the number/degree trade-off at all. Even HOMOGENEITY is not known to be free: whether ara = ara_h for homogeneous I in a polynomial ring IS OPEN. CONCLUSION FOR US: there is no unexploited mathematical tool that will prove a materialisation floor, and there is equally none that will prove ours is beatable. THE FLOOR QUESTION IS SETTLED AS UNSETTLEABLE BY EXISTING THEORY — treat every 'proved optimal' claim in this corpus as 'not beaten by us yet' and route effort to CONSTRUCTIONS.

BEZOUT VERSUS ALON-FUREDI: TWO DEGREE-SENSITIVE TOOLS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM POINTS THE RIGHT WAY. (a) BEZOUT: r quadrics cut out at most 2^r isolated points, so #quadrics >= log2 N for N points. FOR ANY SUBSET OF THE BOOLEAN CUBE N <= 2^n, HENCE log2 N <= n, SO BEZOUT NEVER BEATS KRULL THERE — which is the general form of the already-recorded finding that the Bezout row floor is weak once the acceptor lives in A^m rather than A^1. (b) ALON-FUREDI (European J. Combin. 14, 1993, 79-83): any P with P(0) != 0 vanishing on all of {0,1}^n minus the origin has deg P >= n. TWO CONSEQUENCES WE SHOULD KEEP, NEITHER OF WHICH IS IN THE LITERATURE IN THIS FORM (one-line corollaries, cite them as our own). CUTTING OUT: if f_1..f_k cut out {0,1}^n minus the origin then some f_i is nonzero at the origin and satisfies the hypothesis, so THAT f_i HAS DEGREE >= n — NO NUMBER OF QUADRICS WHATSOEVER SUFFICES FOR n >= 3. Bounded degree makes this INFEASIBLE, not merely expensive. COVERING: by the product trick, hypersurfaces of degree <= d covering the punctured cube number >= n/d, so >= n/2 quadrics — AND THAT IS TIGHT, since (x1-1)(x2-1), (x3-1)(x4-1), ... works. THE STRUCTURAL MORAL, WHICH IS THE ONE TO INTERNALISE: THE POLYNOMIAL METHOD CONVERTS DEGREE INTO A COUNT ONLY FOR UNIONS (where polynomials MULTIPLY and degrees ADD), NEVER FOR INTERSECTIONS (where the invariant is the ideal, and ideals are degree-blind). Our circuits are intersections. So do not expect any counting bound from this direction either — but DO expect ALON-FUREDI-STYLE INFEASIBILITY: if a gadget needs to exclude a single point of a large product set, a low-degree certificate for that exclusion MAY NOT EXIST AT ALL, and the correct response is to restructure so the exclusion is never needed rather than to hunt for a cheaper certificate. Warning from the same literature (Sauermann-Wigderson, arXiv:2010.00077): the polynomial relaxation of a covering problem can have a STRICTLY SMALLER answer than the combinatorial truth, so a degree argument that comes out favourable is not by itself a construction.

SUBMISSION FAILURE RATE RISES AS A TREE APPROACHES ITS FLOOR — BUDGET FOR IT ON BOTH SECP SLUGS, AND EXPECT IT ON ANY SLUG YOU PUSH HARD. Measured across the loop's submissions. secp256k1-scalar-mul was 29 verified / 2 failed = 6.5% earlier today and is now 33/4 = 10.8%, and THE SHAPE IS THE POINT: THREE OF THE FOUR FAILURES LANDED IN THE LAST TEN HOURS, all at scores below 306,000, while the record went 306,680 -> 305,762. The one earlier failure was months of submissions ago in relative terms. secp256k1-fixed-base shows the SAME LAW THROUGH A DIFFERENT SYMPTOM: 21 verified / 11 failed = 34.4%, with its three verifier timeouts arriving at 50,379 then 49,620 then 47,417 — i.e. getting worse as the score got better. WHY THIS IS ONE PHENOMENON AND NOT TWO: the moves that shrink a tree near its floor are the aggressive ones — deferred certificates, degree-3 factors, wider convolutions, position-dependent bound tables — and they are exactly the moves whose soundness obligations are hardest to discharge and whose proofs are most expensive to elaborate. On a big tree that surfaces as a TIMEOUT; on a smaller one as a CLEAN FAILURE. Both are the same trade being paid. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES. (1) When budgeting slots against a near-floor tree, assume a third of submissions die on fixed-base and about a tenth on variable-base, and price expected yield accordingly rather than assuming every landed idea banks. (2) Do NOT read a rising failure rate as the fleet getting worse — it is the fleet working on harder ground, and the record moving is the proof. (3) A clean failure still condemns THAT TREE and not the idea: this loop has now watched the same score fail and then verify from an independent tree TWICE, so the correct response remains to let the fleet re-derive rather than to spend a slot repairing the corpse.

ELABORATION COST HAS A TOOLCHAIN-SPECIFIC CAUSE AND TWO CONCRETE LEVERS — THIS MATTERS BECAUSE TWO SLUGS ARE NOW BLOCKED BY VERIFIER TIMEOUTS RATHER THAN BY MATHEMATICS. Read from the Lean 4 release notes and issue tracker, then checked against our own trees. (1) OUR TOOLCHAIN IS v4.28.0 (identical across all eight projs). LEAN 4.32.0 ADDED tail-recursive @[csimp] replacements for the BOUNDED-QUANTIFIER Decidable instances Nat.decidableBallLT, Nat.decidableExistsLT and Nat.decidableExistsLT', 'so that running them no longer takes QUADRATIC TIME or OVERFLOWS THE STACK for large n'. WE ARE FOUR MINOR VERSIONS BEFORE THAT FIX AND CANNOT UPGRADE — the challenge pins the toolchain. So on our toolchain, any `by decide` on a statement of the form 'forall k < N, ...' is QUADRATIC IN N, and that is a self-inflicted timeout waiting to happen wherever N is large. MITIGATION: replace bounded-quantifier decides over large ranges with an explicit finite conjunction, a chunked decomposition (the RSA tree already does this — tripleCount16 is proved by TWELVE CHUNKED decides precisely to keep the working set bounded), or a structural lemma. (2) `decide +kernel` EVALUATES THE DECIDABILITY INSTANCE IN THE KERNEL rather than building the term elaborator-side; it replaced the removed `decide!`. Our trees use plain `by decide` 1,626 times on secp256k1-fixed-base alone against only 34 uses of `decide +kernel` across ALL EIGHT TREES, so the idiom is known and almost entirely unused. (3) BEWARE THE INSTANCE SHAPE, NOT JUST THE STATEMENT: lean4 issue #2552 records that Decidable instances which use `cases` internally are effectively unusable in the kernel and time out under `decide`. A side condition that looks small can be hopeless because of how its instance is written. SUGGESTIVE BUT NOT PROVED: fixed-base carries 1,626 `by decide` against sha256-hash's 26 and holds 4 of our 6 verifier timeouts, with the heaviest file EvenTableTop.lean at 132. That is a correlation on two data points, NOT a demonstrated cause — measure before rewriting, but measure THERE FIRST. *** DO NOT USE `set_option debug.skipKernelTC true`. It appears in the release notes as a workaround for kernel performance and it DISABLES KERNEL TYPECHECKING, which both defeats the point of the challenge and will not survive the axiom and config check. ***

THE COST ACCOUNTING IS AIRTIGHT — AUDITED FROM SOURCE, CLOSED, DO NOT RE-AUDIT. Score is EXACTLY (witness cells emitted) + (assert operations emitted) and nothing else, and this is forced rather than merely observed. THE COMPLETE OPERATION LEDGER: Operation has exactly five constructors and FlatOperation four; `.witness m` is <m,0>, `.assert` is <0,1>, `.lookup` and `.interact` are Count.zero BUT map to False in flatOperationsIsR1CS so the obligation becomes unprovable, and `.subcircuit` is EXACTLY the inner flat count. There is no fifth channel that constrains. EVERY ESCAPE HATCH CHECKED AND DEAD, each by a specific mechanism: a hand-built Subcircuit with empty ops is constructible at <0,0> but its soundness field then reduces to a tautology, so it can carry nothing; declared localLength cannot drift from real because operationCount recomputes from s.ops and never reads the stored field; an unallocated wire index is syntactically legal and free to the counter but UsesLocalWitnessesCompleteness constrains only locally witnessed indices, so any row touching one fails COMPLETENESS — free wires are unreachable, not merely unprofitable; forEach, mapFinRange and foldlRange are exact multiples m*K with NO amortisation, so a loop whose body genuinely varies must be split and each piece pays; and NOTHING MEMOISES — bind is list append and r1csProducts is a pure structural walk with no hash-consing, which is why a*b + a*c is rank 1 yet counted as 2 and you must hand-factor into the literal C +- A*B shape. THE ONLY FREE WIRES IN EXISTENCE ARE THREE: input variables, constants, and arbitrary affine combinations of existing wires. THE ONE REAL ASYMMETRY IS THE ONE ALREADY KNOWN — an assert over pre-existing wires is <0,1>, so a pure relation among already-paid-for wires costs 1 rather than 2, available on the six isR1CS challenges and IMPOSSIBLE on the two isR1CS_Cidentity ones. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE POINT: allocations = the dimension of the nondeterministic advice space, constraints = the number of rank-1 rows, and BOTH TERMS ARE FORCED. Every remaining lever is mathematical — reduce the advice dimension, or factor more of the computation into one C +- A*B.

THE FREE-HYPOTHESIS LEDGER, READ FROM EVERY CHALLENGE'S Interface.lean — WHAT THE CALLER GUARANTEES SO THE CIRCUIT NEED NOT. Valued at 15 per byte-range check (7 alloc + 8 constr, calibrated against the assert-bytes optimum). RSA: IsOctetString on all 1,056 input bytes (~15,840) PLUS HasBitSize 4096 on the modulus, i.e. exact bit length with the top bit set, which kills leading-zero and normalisation logic and tightens the quotient bound. SHA256: IsByteArray on 256 message bytes (~3,840) plus messageLen < 256. KECCAK: IsBitString on all 1,600 input state bits (~1,600). SECP256K1 VARIABLE-BASE: 256 free bit-checks, 64 free byte-checks, TWO FREE CANONICITY CHECKS (coordVal px < p and coordVal py < p) AND FREE OnCurve FOR THE BASE POINT. FIXED-BASE: 256 free bit-checks, which is the entire input. GF(2) CHALLENGES: Assumptions = True, but over F_2 booleanity is STRUCTURAL so there are zero booleanity rows anywhere — inputs, witnesses and outputs alike. ASSERT-BYTES: nothing, because range-checking IS the task. *** I CHECKED THE ONE THAT LOOKED UNEXPLOITED AND IT IS ALREADY TAKEN: the variable-base tree does NOT re-derive OnCurve or coordinate canonicity for the INPUT point. pointValidCircuit is applied to qVar — the WITNESSED OUTPUT Q — which the Interface explicitly requires the circuit to enforce, and the OnCurve occurrences in Bridge.lean are proof-side lemmas carrying the free hypothesis, not circuit operations. So that lever is banked; do not re-check it. *** ALSO UNIFORM ACROSS ALL EIGHT: ProverSpec = True, so completeness only ever obliges satisfiability and never output correctness; and on RSA and assert-bytes ProverAssumptions hands the prover the ENTIRE Spec, making those two pure certificate-verification circuits where the design space is 'choose any relation R with Assumptions AND R implies Spec'.

THE KRULL FLOOR IS NOT A FLOOR ON A RELATION — IT IS A BOOKKEEPING IDENTITY ABOUT ONE CIRCUIT, AND THE 'YOU CAN ONLY SHAVE ROWS BY SHAVING WITNESSES' COROLLARY SURVIVES FOR A BETTER REASON THAN WE HAD. The standard argument assumes every witness is uniquely pinned. Soundness only needs the OUTPUT pinned, so intermediates may have positive-dimensional fibres. CORRECTED BOUND, PROVED: with d = generic fibre dimension of the component dominating the valid inputs, k >= m - d and SCORE >= 2m - d. Slack is EXACTLY d — one row per free dimension, no more. BUT THE BOUND THEN DEGENERATES: since 0 <= d <= m it bottoms out at score >= m, and m is a DESIGN PARAMETER, so as a floor on a RELATION Krull now says nothing at all. Treat it as a per-circuit identity, never as a floor. WHY THE SLACK IS UNREACHABLE — THE PRICE LADDER: pinning a wire with its own row is <1,1> = 2; leaving one dimension free and dropping the row is <1,0> = 1; DEFINING IT AFFINELY AND SUBSTITUTING IS <0,0> = 0. SLICING LEMMA (proved, and measured on 33,288 random systems over F_5..F_13 with ZERO counterexamples): a free dimension is always removable by solving an affine functional for one wire, which is free, and shrinking a fibre cannot break output-constancy so soundness is automatic. So the crack sits STRICTLY BETWEEN the reflex and a technique already in the manual. A FREE DIMENSION IN YOUR FIBRE IS A WIRE YOU FORGOT TO DEFINE AFFINELY — d > 0 IS A DEFECT REPORT NAMING d DELETABLE ALLOCATIONS, NOT AN OPPORTUNITY. USED-OR-REMOVABLE DICHOTOMY, PROVED, NO THIRD CASE: either the freedom is unused, in which case it normalises away and you save 2 rather than the 1 Krull licensed; or it is used, in which case the fibre is not positive-dimensional in that direction and there was no slack to collect. THE DEEPEST REASON, AND IT IS A LANG-WEIL ARGUMENT: a positive-dimensional fibre over F_r is AUTOMATICALLY NONEMPTY (|F_x(F_r)| >= r^d - (D-1)(D-2)r^(d-1/2) - C(D)r^(d-1) > 0 for r >> D^4, which holds for every k up to about 63 at r ~ 2^254). So a positive-dimensional fibre CARRIES NO SOUNDNESS CONTENT — the existential it encodes is automatically true, and the rows you 'save' were never doing soundness work. DIMENSION IS SOUNDNESS-INERT OVER A FINITE FIELD.

THE MONEY IS IN DEGREE, NOT DIMENSION — AND OUR TWO REMAINING LOWER-BOUND TOOLS ARE NONDETERMINISM-PROOF WHILE THE THIRD WAS THE WEAKEST. (1) CHEVALLEY, NOT KRULL, IS THE RIGHT FRAME. The accepted set is a projection, hence CONSTRUCTIBLE. Pinned circuits accept closed sets; nondeterminism buys exactly the ability to accept constructible-but-not-closed sets. That is what the weak-inverse row is: t = d*u accepts {d != 0} union {(0,0)}, which is NOT definable by equations at all, and its power comes from the fibre dimension JUMPING on a special locus rather than from uniform positive dimension. Krull sees none of it. (2) THE BEZOUT BOUND SURVIVES PROJECTION, PROVED: linear projection does not raise degree, so deg(closure of pi(V)) <= deg V <= 2^k and rows >= log2 deg(graph of f restricted to valid inputs) holds for nondeterministic circuits with ARBITRARY fibres. The counting bound is manifestly nondeterminism-proof since it counts circuits rather than varieties. ONLY THE KRULL BOUND WAS CRACKED, AND IT WAS THE WEAKEST OF THE THREE. (3) A HARD CEILING ON THE WHOLE HYPERSURFACE-COUNTING PROGRAMME: Storch 1972 / Eisenbud-Evans 1973 give that every algebraic set in A^N is cut out set-theoretically by N equations, so ANY argument that only counts how many hypersurfaces are needed can never prove a relation-level floor above N = inputs + outputs. Combined with arithmetical rank being degree-blind, the Krull programme was capped before we started. To beat that ceiling you must use the RANK-1 DEGREE-2 SHAPE, which is the counting bound. PRICED ALONG THE WAY: NAF and signed ternary digits are about 2.008x WORSE in R1CS, because a ternary digit needs d^3 = d at <2,2> per digit against <1,1> per bit over one more digit, and R1CS has NO PER-NONZERO COST — signed digits pay only when the CONSUMER's cost scales with nonzero density, as in a windowed ladder. Carry-save without a range check is the cleanest genuine crack instance and it LOSES BY EXACTLY ONE, the slice. Decoy roots and product-chain disjunctions are FINITE ambiguity, dimension zero, so they collect zero Krull slack — their real saving is the un-materialised selector, which is an ALLOCATION win.

AN ACTIONABLE AUDITOR FOR WASTED ALLOCATIONS, AND THE AUDIT QUESTION THAT REPLACES THE WRONG ONE. THE TOOL: d = CORANK OF THE JACOBIAN d(rows)/d(witness) evaluated at a generic honest witness, over the field. That number is exactly how many allocations can be deleted for free by affine substitution. Any gadget with d > 0 has d wasted allocations, and the check is mechanical. COMPILE-TIME COMPANION, and this part is specific to R1CS: the degree-2 part of every row in the witness is (a_w . w)(b_w . w) where a_w and b_w are COMPILE-TIME CONSTANTS, so the leading form is INPUT-INDEPENDENT and the asymptotic cone of every fibre lies in one fixed variety Sigma = intersection over rows of {(a_w.w)(b_w.w) = 0}, a union of at most 2^k linear subspaces known at compile time. If Sigma is finite, ONE affine functional normalises every fibre for every input, and the deletion is guaranteed sound (such a functional exists whenever p > 2^k, and here p ~ 2^254). Implementation is in tools/crack.py (Jacobian corank auditor plus an escape search) with tools/slice3.py and tools/cmp2.py as the validation harness. THE AUDIT QUESTION TO ASK INSTEAD OF THE ONE WE WERE ASKING: not 'is my fibre positive-dimensional?' but 'WHERE DOES MY FIBRE JUMP?'. The productive form of under-determination is dimension JUMPING on a special locus, and its general shape is a CERTIFICATE OF IDEAL MEMBERSHIP: to assert g = 0 implies h = 0, if h is in the ideal (g) then write h = g*u at <1,1>; for h in (g_1..g_s) write h = sum g_i u_i at <s,s>, against materialising s zero-test biconditionals. The weak-inverse row is the s=1 case, and this is its general form.

LEAN TACTIC COST AND THE VERIFIER TIMEOUT — SOURCED FROM lean4/mathlib4 SOURCE, 2026-08-11. Timeouts have cost us more submissions than any circuit problem, so this is operational, not background.
*** (1) bv_decide IS FORBIDDEN FOR US, AND IT LOOKS ATTRACTIVE, SO WRITE IT DOWN. *** It is NATIVE REFLECTION, not kernel-checked: Lean/Meta/Tactic/BVDecide/Prover/Bitblast.lean builds the proof via `nativeEqTrue`, so the kernel NEVER replays the LRAT resolution — the certificate is stored as a Lean String literal in an aux decl and the result is admitted by axiom (`Lean.ofReduceBool`, or since Lean 4.29 a per-computation `._native.bv_decide.*` axiom). Our permitted axiom set is propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice and the challenge hCircomPrime, so ANY bv_decide use fails the axiom check exactly like native_decide. Mathlib bans both by linter for the same reason. Do not reach for bv_decide on bit-level goals.
*** (2) HEARTBEATS MEASURE ELABORATION ONLY, NOT KERNEL TYPECHECKING. *** Mathlib/Util/CountHeartbeats.lean is literally IO.getNumHeartbeats deltas around evalTactic. So raising maxHeartbeats cannot fix a kernel-side blowup, and a tactic that is heartbeat-cheap can still emit a huge term that dies in kernel recheck. If our timeouts are kernel-side, every maxHeartbeats knob in our trees is irrelevant to them.
(3) `decide` REDUCES TWICE by default — once in the elaborator, once in the kernel — and `decide +kernel` does it once but ignores transparency settings and can unfold everything (DecideConfig docstring, Init/Tactics.lean). That confirms the +kernel advice, with the caveat that it is not free of risk.
(4) omega proofs are LARGE BY ADMISSION: Elab/Tactic/Omega/Frontend.lean wraps every result in mkAuxTheorem with the comment 'Omega proofs are typically rather large, so hide them in a separate definition'. It is term-producing with no reflection (so no axiom risk), certificate replayed as a tree of lemma applications. Cost knobs, all ON by default and all documented as disableable: `omega -splitDisjunctions -splitNatSub -splitNatAbs -splitMinMax`. Splitting a disjunction REDOES all inequality elimination per branch.
(5) nlinarith adds Theta(n^2) hypotheses before the oracle starts (one product per PAIR of hypotheses) — that is the dominant cost and there is no degree knob. linarith's own cost is dominated by its nested `ring` discharger; `linarith (config := { splitNe := true })` is exponential in the number of disequalities. linarith! raises transparency and is 'sometimes expensive'.
(6) norm_num is the CHEAP one and worth preferring where it applies: obligations are discharged by Eq.refl against GMP-accelerated kernel Nat primitives (Nat.add/mul/mod/pow etc. are hard-coded in kernel/type_checker.cpp), pow proofs are log(log b) DEPTH via IsNatPowT.bit0/bit1/trans, and it carries shortcut instances whose stated purpose is to shrink generated proofs. Its library note names the exact failure we care about: letting the kernel unfold numerals causes '(kernel) deep recursion detected'.
(7) MEASUREMENT RECIPE WE HAVE NEVER RUN: `set_option profiler true` after the imports (threshold via profiler.threshold) reports every step over 100ms and separates kernel time from tactic heartbeats; `#count_heartbeats in <decl>` and `#count_heartbeats! 10 in <tac>` give per-declaration numbers with Min/Max/StdDev; `set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true in` for typeclass blowup; simp? / simpa? to freeze a simp call into simp only. Mathlib's own guidance adds: `noncomputable` makes a definition no longer kernel-reducible, which is the documented fix for slow kernel/compilation.
