PROFILING THE VERIFIER TIMEOUT — MEASURED ON v4.28.0, 2026-08-11, AND IT CORRECTS ADVICE WE HAD BEEN INJECTING INTO EVERY PROMPT.
*** (1) `decide +kernel` WAS THE WRONG HEADROOM ADVICE AND MAY HAVE BEEN MAKING THINGS WORSE. *** maxHeartbeats bounds the ELABORATOR: exhausting it throws a deterministic error, i.e. a clean fast rejection. KERNEL type-checking is effectively NOT bounded by it — measured, a `decide +kernel` goal SUCCEEDED while burning 18.6 s of type checking under maxHeartbeats at a tenth of default, where the same file at 2000 heartbeats failed instantly in the elaborator. So every declaration moved kernel-side trades a clean rejection for an unbounded wall-clock burn, which is exactly the failure mode killing us. It is correct in ONE narrow case: bounded-quantifier decide over a large range, ~1.5x faster and at N=4000 it survives where plain `decide` aborts with SIGABRT. On small closed goals it measured ~25% WORSE (it creates an aux declaration for the kernel).
*** (2) IT WAS ALSO AIMED AT THE WRONG TREE. *** Tactic counts inside the actual import closure of Solution.SHA256.Main (156 of 189 files elaborate): norm_num 5,073 / omega 3,253 / simp only 2,063 / rfl 1,507 / bare simp 39 / decide 30 / decide +kernel 0. The advice came from fixed-base (1,659 `decide`) and does not transfer. 30 sites on the slug that keeps timing out.
(3) A FREE MAP OF THE HOT DECLARATIONS, NO BUILD NEEDED: our 253 `set_option maxHeartbeats ... in` annotations are a hand-labelled list of expensive declarations. 78 sit at >=20x default and 6 at 100x, and all six of those are `theorem soundness` in TailPairTight, TailPairWide, TailPairWidePack, SHA256RoundPair, SHA256RoundPairB1 and SHA256RoundPairW. Profile those first. Also: 4 of the 253 are UNSCOPED file-wide (MessageScheduleSparseSoundness, MessageScheduleSparseCompleteness, CostSparseD, R1CSSparseD) — those remove the brake from every declaration in the file and should be scoped.
(4) MEASURED LADDER, 2000 goals/file, baseline subtracted: closed `i < N` by decide / simp / `Nat.le_of_ble_eq_true rfl` all ~2.2 ms and indistinguishable; the same by omega 3.3-3.5 ms, ~1.5x WORSE; an open `j + k < N` by omega 10.2 ms, but factored into one helper lemma plus a closed side condition 3.6 ms — 2.8x faster. omega processes EVERY hypothesis, so its cost scales with context size rather than goal size, and splitNatSub/splitMinMax/splitDisjunctions are all ON by default.
(5a) ONE EXCLUSION THAT INVERTS THE RULE, APPLY IT BEFORE ANY MECHANICAL PASS: for PRIMALITY goals norm_num is much FASTER than decide, because Nat.minFacAux is well-founded recursive and hence irreducible since Lean 4.9.0, so decide cannot reduce it at all. Mathlib documents this explicitly. Do not include primality sites in a norm_num sweep.
(5) norm_num IS NEVER CHEAPER THAN simp ON THE SAME GOAL — it is simp plus extension dispatch at every subterm in both phases, loading the full Mathlib simp set. Ladder: norm_num -> `norm_num only [...]` -> `norm_num1` (does not call simp). Expect a real failure rate; sweep with per-site compile checks. Not replaceable by decide over R or Q.
(6) Elab.async is one line in lakefile leanOptions and worth up to 40% EITHER WAY — 40% faster with it OFF on an omega-heavy file, faster with it ON on a decide-heavy one. Measure, do not assume.
(7) Clean's `circuit_proof_start` (199 sites) runs a ~586-lemma circuit_norm simp set plus six `dsimp only ... at *` passes each wrapped in try/catch — FAILED ATTEMPTS STILL COST FULL ELABORATION TIME. That is the structural hot spot. Bulk-convert with `set_option tactic.simp.trace true` rather than hand-editing.
(8) SCORING vs SPEED, WORTH KNOWING: lean4export is a pure importModules + DAG dump — no elaboration, no whnf, no kernel calls. So the verifier's cost is essentially all `lake build`, and optimising for export size is NOT the same as optimising for the timeout.
(9) THE RECIPE, INSTALLED AT tools/profile_tree.sh AND NEVER YET RUN ON OUR TREES. By hand: `lake env lean -Dprofiler=true -Dprofiler.threshold=50 F.lean` for phase totals (prints 'type checking took' vs 'elaboration took'); `lake env lean -Dtrace.profiler=true -Dtrace.profiler.output=prof.json F.lean` for PER-DECLARATION attribution separating [Kernel] from [Elab.command], loadable in profiler.firefox.com; `-Ddebug.skipKernelTC=true` to decide which phase is biting (LOCAL DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, never submit); `-Ddiagnostics=true` to find simp lemmas tried and never applied. TWO GOTCHAS: trace.profiler.output SILENTLY DOES NOTHING when set via set_option inside a file — it must be -D on the command line; and Mathlib's command is `#count_heartbeats in <decl>` with the hash, the bare form is gone.
NOT AVAILABLE TO US AT v4.28.0, confirmed by measurement: cbv/decide_cbv and `simp +instances` are 4.29+, and the Nat.decidableBallLT fix is 4.32.

*** THE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT EVERY ONE OF OUR REJECTED DELETIONS, AND IT RUNS IN 0.02 SECONDS. MEASURED 0/20000 VERSUS 100/100 ON A FAITHFUL MODEL OF OUR OWN FAILURE MODE. *** Our recurring bad argument is 'this row holds identically in the wires once q is rewritten as an affine expression of allocated wires'. That is redundancy GIVEN the substitution. Our obligation is unconditional: for EVERY environment satisfying the REMAINING rows, the spec must hold. The two differ exactly as 'forall HONEST WITNESSES' differs from 'forall SOLUTIONS OF S minus r' — and here is the operational consequence, measured on a range-checked-quotient model of the exact shape we keep getting rejected on: SAMPLING HONEST WITNESSES REFUTED IT 0 TIMES IN 20,000. FREED-VARIABLE PERTURBATION REFUTED IT 100 TIMES IN 100. *** THE PERTURBATION TEST: *** take an honest witness; take the variables the DELETED row constrained and REASSIGN THEM FREELY; re-propagate through the REMAINING rows only; check the spec. In the measured instance it immediately produced q = 12589388...950995940, far past 2^16, with S minus r fully satisfied. cvc5 needed 45 s and timed out on the same refutation; this took 0.018 s. *** RUN THIS BEFORE WRITING A LINE OF LEAN ON ANY DELETION. *** If a deletion candidate does not survive perturbation, you have saved a submission. If it does, it is worth the SMT query below. And note the epistemic point, which is why this corpus has repeatedly felt certain and been wrong: honest-witness testing CONFIRMS the false claim every single time, so 'I tested it on real values and it held' is ZERO EVIDENCE for a deletion. This is a systematic bias, not a run of bad luck.

*** ROW-DELETION IS DECIDABLE AT OUR SCALE — 30 ms AT 33,792 ROWS — AND THE UNSAT CORE HANDS YOU THE LEMMA LIST YOUR LEAN PROOF MUST CITE. MEASURED HERE, NOT CITED. *** Row r is deletable from S iff Sol(S minus r) is contained in Sol(r), i.e. iff (S minus r) AND (NOT r) is UNSAT over F_p. That is a QF_FF query and cvc5 answers it. THREE THINGS MAKE IT PRACTICAL AND NONE IS THE DEFAULT. *** (1) LOCALIZE, AND IT IS SOUND TO DO SO. *** For ANY subset T of S minus r, if T AND (NOT r) is UNSAT then (S minus r) AND (NOT r) is UNSAT, because Sol(S minus r) is contained in Sol(T) is contained in Sol(r). So restrict to the CONE of rows sharing variables with r and an UNSAT answer is still an unconditional proof. MEASURED: full system 528 rows = 77.7 s; cone depth 2 (66 rows) = 0.030 s; and cone depth 2 out of a 33,792-ROW SYSTEM = STILL 0.030 s. Whole-system queries time out past ~4,000 rows even tuned, so localization is not an optimisation, it is the only route. Depth 2 sufficed in every case measured; escalate depth only on inconclusive. *** (2) --ff-solver=split, WHICH IS OFF BY DEFAULT AND WORTH 52x ON OUR EXACT SHAPE. *** Measured 77.7 s -> 1.5 s. This is CAV 2024 Split Groebner Bases (Ozdemir-Pailoor-Bassa-Ferles-Barrett-Dillig, cs.utexas.edu/~isil/ff-solver.pdf) and the paper names our pathology outright: a full Groebner basis goes EXPONENTIAL 'because of the combination of the bitsum sum 2^(i-1) X_i and the bit constraints X_i(1-X_i)=0'. That is every limb decomposition we write. Also enable --ff-bitsum and --ff-elim-disjunctive-bit. *** (3) --produce-unsat-cores, AND THIS IS THE ITEM THAT ANSWERS 'WHY DID SEVEN ATTEMPTS TAKE SEVEN ATTEMPTS'. *** Name every row with (! <row> :named row_1234). The unsat core is the MINIMAL SET OF RETAINED ROWS THAT FORCES r — i.e. exactly the facts the Lean proof must cite, computed BEFORE any Lean is written. Our fixed-base stageO2 deletion took seven attempts and succeeded only by discharging with a lemma ALREADY PRESENT IN THE TREE; the core names that lemma on attempt one. Maintain a row-name -> Lean-lemma-name map once and the citation list becomes mechanical. *** ONLY THE UNSAT DIRECTION IS USABLE. *** SAT (proving NON-redundancy) timed out at 528 rows and even at a 67-row cone — the asymmetry is structural (the CAV 2023 procedure's cheap phase is the Groebner refutation; model construction is where the 255-bit field bites). Use perturbation sampling for refutation, SMT for proof. AND NOTE: cvc5's QF_FF proof objects emit ':rule trust' for the field-theory step, so the core is a TRUSTWORTHY POINTER, NOT A CHECKABLE CERTIFICATE. The checkable certificate is the cofactors, next entry.

*** SHIP COFACTOR CERTIFICATES CLOSED BY `ring`, NOT TACTIC PROOFS — IT FIXES THE SOUNDNESS FAILURE AND THE ELABORATION FAILURE WITH ONE CHANGE. *** If the deleted row r can be written r = sum h_i f_i over the retained rows f_i (which the unsat core has just named for you), the Lean obligation is a POLYNOMIAL IDENTITY. Consequences, all of them ours: it is closed by `ring` — no simp set, no omega, no decide, no search, CONSTANT ELABORATION COST; and it is UNCONDITIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION, because the identity holds in F_p[X], so there is NO WAY to accidentally prove the conditional 'redundant given the substitution' statement that keeps getting us rejected. *** THE THEORY, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS OBJECTION DOES NOT BITE. *** Complete redundancy over F_p needs the field equations x^p - x, and p is about 2^254, so they cannot be written down — this is the central obstacle in the area and both cvc5 papers say so. But ideal membership WITHOUT field equations is the SOUND relaxation, and sound is all we need: if r = sum h_i f_i as a polynomial identity then r holds at every point of every extension, a fortiori on F_p. So do not chase completeness; the computable relaxation is already the right tool. *** ONE HARD IMPLEMENTATION TRAP, MEASURED. *** Naive multivariate division against a NON-Groebner generating set is ORDER-DEPENDENT AND INCOMPLETE. Same problem, sympy over GF(p): gens=(y,x) gives rem=0 and cofactors [1, x+y-1]; gens=(x,y) gives rem = y^2-y and cofactors [0,0] — SILENT FAILURE, no certificate, no error. USE SAGE'S f.lift(I), which computes a Groebner basis WITH THE TRANSFORMATION MATRIX and returns cofactors w.r.t. your ORIGINAL generators: complete and order-independent. The circuit-optimization skill already ships scripts/cofactors.sage doing exactly this lift. If only sympy is available, try several variable orders and treat a nonzero remainder as INCONCLUSIVE, never as a refutation. *** THE END-TO-END GATE, ALL FOUR STEPS MECHANICAL: *** perturbation sample (cheap refutation) -> local cone -> cvc5 --ff-solver=split --produce-unsat-cores (sound proof plus the citation list) -> lift the cored rows -> cofactors -> Lean `ring`.

*** UNDERCONSTRAINEDNESS TOOLS DECIDE A DIFFERENT AND STRICTLY WEAKER QUESTION THAN OURS — SCREEN WITH THEM, NEVER TRUST THEM, AND DO NOT SPEND A JOB EXPECTING ONE TO ANSWER 'IS THIS ROW REDUNDANT'. *** Picus/QED2 (Pailoor et al., PLDI 2023, github.com/Veridise/Picus) and Ecne (github.com/franklynwang/EcneProject) both decide UNIQUENESS/DETERMINISM — 'do any two satisfying assignments agreeing on inputs agree on v', by self-composition over two copies. THAT IS NOT REDUNDANCY AND IT IS NOT CORRECTNESS. Deleting a row can PRESERVE determinism while ENLARGING the accepted solution set: drop a range check on an input-side signal and every output is still a unique function of it, so PICUS ANSWERS 'SAFE' ON A CIRCUIT THAT HAS BECOME UNSOUND. That is the Dark Forest / ZkDrops bug class and it is OUR class. Both are sound-but-incomplete (Picus measured 70 percent solved, 114/163, 30 percent 'unknown'; Ecne's README states plainly that false 'just means Ecne is unable to prove that the constraints are sound'). WHAT THEY ARE GOOD FOR: both consume PLAIN .r1cs directly (Ecne wants .r1cs + .sym), and ECNE'S 'WITNESS VERIFICATION' MODE CHECKS UNIQUENESS OF AUXILIARY VARIABLES, not just outputs, which is a genuinely cheap non-SMT screen worth running on a submitted tree. CLEAN NEGATIVES, DO NOT RE-SURVEY: circomspect is 14 SYNTACTIC passes, no semantic reasoning, does not read R1CS; ZKAP (USENIX Sec 2024) is pattern-matching over a Circom dependence graph, does not read R1CS; Corset is the Linea constraint compiler and not an underconstraint detector at all; Coda (IEEE S&P 2024) is the closest analogue to our workflow (refinement types, residue discharged in Coq) but requires rewriting the circuit in its own DSL. *** NO TOOL TAKES AN R1CS FILE AND A ROW INDEX AND ANSWERS 'IS THIS ROW REDUNDANT'. YOU MUST POSE THE QUERY YOURSELF; it is about 30 lines of glue. ***

*** maxHeartbeats IS PER COMMAND, SO SPLITTING ONE GIANT THEOREM INTO N LEMMAS MULTIPLIES THE ELABORATION BUDGET BY N WITH ZERO PROOF CHANGES — THE CHEAPEST TIMEOUT FIX WE HAVE, AND IT IS SIX MECHANISMS AT ONCE. *** This bears directly on the measured fact that one fixed-base tree needed TEN submissions, nine of which timed out. (1) BUDGET: N declarations each get their own 200000 heartbeats. (2) PARALLELISM: Lean 4.19 PR #7084 parallelises the elaboration of THEOREM BODIES, and Elab.async — which defaults false in the option but IS OVERRIDDEN TO TRUE in cmdline and the language server, so lake build already has it — is per-DECLARATION. One giant theorem = ONE CORE; ten lemmas = ten cores. TWO THINGS SILENTLY KILL IT: putting theorems in a `mutual` block, and a theorem STATEMENT CONTAINING METAVARIABLES (the gate is a single non-mutual .theorem with no mvars in the type — so an `_` in a theorem's TYPE, not its proof, costs you the parallelism with no diagnostic). Note Mathlib's #count_heartbeats sets Elab.async false internally for determinism, so measured heartbeats and built wall-clock diverge. (3) instantiateMVars IS SUPERLINEAR IN PROOF SIZE (lean4#5610: it grows from 34 percent to 56 percent of elaboration as one proof grows), so two half-size proofs are strictly cheaper than one. (4) The kernel typechecks one enormous term at the end with peak memory proportional to term size and NO CHECKPOINT. (5) maxRecDepth 512 is hit by term DEPTH. (6) RETRY GRANULARITY: a failed lemma is re-attempted in isolation. Mathlib enforces a 1500-line file ceiling by linter; copy it. *** AND THE OFFICIAL SPEEDUP LOOP, WHOSE THIRD RULE IS THE ONE FOR US: *** leanprover-community.github.io/extras/speedup.html — for 'elaboration took <long>', 'look for `_`s in the declaration and REPLACE THEM BY THE CORRESPONDING EXPLICIT ARGUMENTS'. Mathlib PR #12412 got -65.8 percent instructions on one file and reports that WILDCARD REPLACEMENT ALONE WAS ~15 s of it. Our machine-generated circuit statements are exactly where unification-filled holes on large structured terms blow up.

*** FOUR ELABORATION KNOBS WITH SOURCED DEFAULTS, PLUS THE PROFILING INTERFACE WE HAVE BEEN QUOTING WRONG, PLUS FOUR THINGS THAT DO NOT EXIST — STOP CHASING THEM. *** (1) `simp` HAS zeta := true BY DEFAULT, WHICH SUBSTITUTES EVERY `let`. On machine-generated subcircuit terms that DUPLICATES HUGE SUBTERMS at every occurrence; `simp -zeta` is often a large win and costs nothing to try. Other Simp.Config defaults worth knowing: maxSteps 100000, maxDischargeDepth 2, decide false, index true (index:=false is a correctness escape hatch that DISABLES the discrimination-tree fast path). (2) `omega` RUNS +splitDisjunctions +splitNatSub +splitNatAbs +splitMinMax ALL ON BY DEFAULT, each a case split, and they compound multiplicatively; each x/k and x%k adds fresh variables. On circuit code use `omega -splitDisjunctions -splitMinMax -splitNatSub -splitNatAbs`, and MOVE TO Int SO TRUNCATED SUBTRACTION DISAPPEARS ENTIRELY. This matters at our scale: 3,253 omega calls in the SHA-256 import closure alone. (3) `set_option diagnostics true` (threshold 20) IS THE SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE COMMAND FOR OUR SITUATION and we have never run it. It reports UNFOLDED DECLARATIONS (your irreducible hit-list — the top entry is almost certainly the subcircuit to seal), unfolded instances, 'heuristic for solving f a =?= f b' (direct evidence of unification thrash), max synth pending failures, and 'kernel: unfolded declarations' (your decide cost). Also relevant: maxSynthPendingDepth defaults to 1 and MATHLIB SETS IT TO 3 PROJECT-WIDE; synthInstance.maxHeartbeats is 20000 PER TYPECLASS PROBLEM, not per command. (4) THE PROFILER INTERFACE CHANGED AND WE HAVE THE OLD ONE. `set_option profiler true` was DEPRECATED 2026-07-30 in favour of `set_option trace.profiler true` with `trace.profiler.useHeartbeats true` (deterministic — heartbeats are allocation counts, stable across machines and load) plus `trace.profiler.output` / `trace.profiler.serve` for a Firefox-Profiler flamegraph. THRESHOLD DEFAULTS TO 10 ms, NOT 100. These must go on the COMMAND LINE (-Dtrace.profiler=true), not in the file. *** DO NOT EXIST, VERIFIED, WE HAVE PROPOSED SEVERAL OF THESE: *** `lake exe pole` (removed from mathlib4; the longest-pole tool is now `lakeprof record` / `lakeprof report -p|-r`), `lake build --profile`, a LEAN_PROFILER env var, `#time` in current lean4, LEAN_NUM_THREADS, and debug.byAsTactic. AND ONE STRUCTURAL LEVER WE HAVE NOT USED: `irreducible_def foo := ...` generates foo_def : foo = 42 so you unfold DELIBERATELY via simp [foo_def] — exactly the right shape for a subcircuit, and Lean core does this to itself (4.9.0 PR #4061 marks WF-recursive functions @[irreducible] by default 'to prevent the expensive and often unfruitful unfolding'). Mathlib's own rule is that irreducible_def 'should be used only when there is a documented necessity from profiling' — we have that necessity.

*** THE PRECONDITIONING LITERATURE IS CLOSED: THE FAMOUS RESULT DOES NOT TRANSFER TO F_p AND IS THE WRONG COST MODEL ANYWAY, BUT PATERSON-STOCKMEYER SURVIVES INTACT — AND THAT IS THE ONE WE ACTUALLY USE. *** Sourced from Buergisser-Clausen-Shokrollahi 'Algebraic Complexity Theory' chapter previews, Knuth's own Stanford index to TAOCP vol. 2, and arXiv:1102.4772. *** (1) MOTZKIN/BELAGA/PAN/KNUTH-EVE 'floor(n/2)+2 MULTIPLICATIONS WITH PRECONDITIONING' IS DEAD HERE, TWICE OVER. *** BCS Theorem (5.1) HYPOTHESISES THE FIELD IN ITS STATEMENT: 'Let K be REAL OR ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED', and the proof splits into an algebraically-closed case and a separate real case. BCS also say the preconditioning phase 'might involve more complex tasks as FINDING ROOTS OF POLYNOMIALS'. Knuth-Eve is the concrete instance and it needs (a) complex root-finding of p, (b) a REAL-PART ORDERING to choose the shift t >= Re(r_2), and (c) the condition that p^o SPLIT OVER THE REALS. None of the three exists over F_p — there is no ordering and no 'half of the complex plane'. AND THE SECOND, INDEPENDENT REASON IT IS IRRELEVANT: BCS chapter 5 COUNTS ALL MULTIPLICATIONS INCLUDING SCALAR ONES ('multiplications with scalars in K are NOT free of charge'), which is the opposite of our model, where affine combinations and constant multiplications are FREE. So even if the field hypothesis held, the theorem would be optimising the wrong quantity. DO NOT SPEND A JOB ON PRECONDITIONED HORNER. *** (2) BUT PATERSON-STOCKMEYER IS FIELD-INDEPENDENT, AND THIS CONFIRMS THE SQRT-N LAW ENTRY IN THIS FILE RATHER THAN UNDERMINING IT. *** BCS state it as Prop. (9.1) and the proof is pure baby-step/giant-step: write f = sum_{i<q} f_i X^{pi} with deg f_i <= p-1, compute X^2..X^p with p-1 multiplications, 'then we have all the f_i FOR FREE at our disposal since we do not count multiplications with scalars in K', then Horner in X^p with q-1 more. NO FIELD HYPOTHESIS, NO PRECONDITIONING, NO ROOT-FINDING — every step is a rational rearrangement of the GIVEN coefficients. It goes through over F_p verbatim. DO NOT CONFLATE THE TWO RESULTS: different model (all multiplications vs nonscalar only), different mathematics, opposite verdicts here. *** (3) THE TRANSCENDENCE-DEGREE LOWER BOUND IS ANOTHER TOOL THAT DIES OVER F_p, AND BCS SAY SO THEMSELVES: *** 'if the coefficients of f are ALGEBRAIC OR EVEN RATIONAL, then the transcendence degree bounds are USELESS.' Every element of F_p is algebraic over the prime field, so chapter 5's whole lower-bound method has zero content for us. Their own replacement is the DEGREE BOUND (Strassen/Baur, chapter 8), and note chapter 8 defaults to 'k algebraically closed' with section 8.1 relaxing only to 'k infinite' — which is exactly why *** BCS HAVE A DEDICATED SECTION 8.6 'THE CASE OF A FINITE FIELD', p. 195. THAT IS THE PAGE TO READ AND IT WAS NOT OBTAINABLE; if institutional access ever appears, get it. *** *** (4) THE COUNTING BOUND, AND AN OPEN QUESTION STATED HONESTLY. *** BCS section 9.1 gives the parameter count: r nonscalar multiplications leave (r+1)^2 + 1 free parameters, so sweeping an (n+1)-dimensional space of polynomials forces r >~ sqrt(n). Over F_p-bar their conclusion ('the F_{r,nu} must be ALGEBRAICALLY DEPENDENT OVER THE PRIME FIELD') is VACUOUS, since everything is. A naive CARDINALITY count might still work — p^{(r+1)^2+1} >= p^{n+1} forces r >~ sqrt(n) for most f — BUT THIS IS UNSOURCED AND THE OBVIOUS HOLE IS THAT A STRAIGHT-LINE PROGRAM'S CONSTANTS NEED NOT LIE IN F_p. TREAT IT AS A CONJECTURE TO CHECK, NOT A RESULT, AND do not build a floor claim on it. *** (5) ONE FINITE-FIELD-SPECIFIC PAPER EXISTS AND IT DOES NOT APPLY TO US. *** Elia-Rosenthal-Schipani, arXiv:1102.4772, is the paper that notices the gap ('what is usually considered in the literature ... refers, SOMETIMES IMPLICITLY, to polynomials with coefficients taken from an INFINITE SET', and Horner optimality per Pan 1966 and Winograd 1967 'is proved ASSUMING THAT THE FIELD OF COEFFICIENTS IS INFINITE'). Their Frobenius-based algorithms give ~2 sqrt(n(p-1)) for f in F_p[x] evaluated at alpha in F_{p^m} with m > 1. WE ARE THE DEGENERATE CASE THEY EXCLUDE: they state that 'if both the coefficients and the evaluation point are in F_p, then the polynomial has degree at most p-1, and our methods cannot be applied'. Our evaluations are in F_p itself. CLOSED — do not re-search this.

WEB PASS 2026-08-14 — DRY ON TECHNIQUES, FIVE NEW ITEMS CLOSED WITH REASONS SO NOBODY RE-SEARCHES THEM. No new or better constraint-count technique surfaced for any of the five primitives; the standing lesson held again. THE NEWLY-EVALUATED ITEMS, none previously in this file: *** (1) THE 'MODULAR R1CS' FAMILY IS THE MOST TEMPTING DEAD END ON THE BOARD, BECAUSE ITS NAME DESCRIBES EXACTLY WHAT WE WANT. *** Zinc (eprint 2025/316, GWHD25) transforms the standard R1CS relation into modR1CS, whose instances carry INTEGER matrices plus explicit moduli and QUOTIENT VECTORS; Zinc+ (2026/855) generalises this to Universal Constraint Systems; Limber (2026/1635) builds low-overhead SNARKs for integers over any PCS. ALL THREE CHANGE THE CONSTRAINT SYSTEM ITSELF. Our challenge fixes plain R1CS over BN254 with score = allocations + constraints, and the relation is not ours to redefine — so their entire saving is unavailable by construction, not by cost. Read the name 'modular R1CS' as 'a different arithmetisation', every time. *** (2) MULTI-SCALAR MULTIPLICATION AND PIPPENGER ARE A CATEGORY ERROR HERE, TWICE. *** eprint 2026/966 ('A New Multiscalar Multiplication Method Resistant to Timing Attacks', a Pippenger bucket-method variant with a recoding that removes zero digits, claiming +25 percent) and eprint 2026/1316 (MSM on memory-constrained devices). FIRST, MSM AMORTISES ACROSS MANY SCALAR-POINT PAIRS AND WE HAVE ONE SCALAR — the bucket method has nothing to amortise over. SECOND, their metric is PROVER WALL-CLOCK, and 2026/966's specific goal, a UNIFORM digit stream with no zeros, is worth exactly zero to us: a circuit already pays the worst case at every position, so removing data-dependence buys no rows and the recoding's extra digits would COST rows. The corpus's standing rule covers this — any technique whose benefit is an average over inputs, or a data-dependence property, is worth zero here. *** (3) CALIBRATION THAT WILL BE QUOTED AT US AND IS NOT COMPARABLE: SPARTAN-ECDSA'S ~3,039 TO ~8,000 CONSTRAINTS FOR ECDSA VERIFICATION. *** That is on secq256k1, THE TWIN CURVE, chosen precisely so secp256k1 group arithmetic is NATIVE to the proving field. Our challenge is secp256k1 over BN254, i.e. fully non-native, which is the entire source of our cost. Same for the Zcash/Sapling figures already in this file (9 constraints per scalar bit, 8.5 with a recoded [0,1,2,-1] digit set, 750 constraints for a 3-bit-window fixed-base Edwards mul): ALL NATIVE-CURVE NUMBERS. Never benchmark our trees against them. *** (4) SHA-256 AND KECCAK REMAIN UNMOVED. *** SHA-256 multiplicative-complexity searches return only the Boyar-Peralta line already in this file plus the standing open problem that no explicit function on n variables is known with MC > n; Keccak theta returns the same SLP-over-GF(2) literature the theta-as-SLP lead already points at. The public R1CS figures quoted for these hashes remain two orders of magnitude above our trees, so the literature is still not operating at this frontier. *** (5) RSA e = 65537 IS 16 SQUARINGS PLUS ONE MULTIPLICATION IN EVERY SOURCE — CONFIRMING, NOT IMPROVING, THE 17-MODMUL FLOOR ALREADY RECORDED. *** No addition-chain result beats it, which is expected: 65537 = 2^16 + 1 is prime and its chain is optimal. Do not spend another pass here.

*** THE ONE-ROW BIT-EXTRACTION CRITERION — A COMPLETE, GENERAL TEST, USE IT BEFORE COSTING ANY PROPOSED ONE-ROW GADGET ON ANY CHALLENGE. *** A single row pins c = f iff f = O/R - A with A, R, O affine over already-pinned values and R a unit on the reachable set — equivalently iff *** f*R HAS DEGREE AT MOST 2 *** in the pinned coordinates. The specialisation worth memorising: ONE ROW PLUS ONE ALLOCATION EXTRACTS ONE BIT FROM A FREE-AFFINE FIELD ELEMENT IF AND ONLY IF THAT ELEMENT'S RANGE IS A SET OF AT MOST 4 VALUES. The reason is a degrees-of-freedom count, not a search: a Moebius map has 3 d.o.f. plus 2 for the additive affine part = 5 parameters, while matching a 2-valued non-affine pattern on n points imposes n conditions — so n = 4 is exactly break-even and n >= 5 is inconsistent. VERIFIED EXACTLY OVER Q: parity and top-bit of V in {0,1,2,3} YES with R = 2V-3; parity of V in {0..4} NO; parity of V in {0..5} NO; bit-2 of V in {0..5} NO; top bit of V in {0..7} NO. Consequence for GF(2)-linear work: every F_2-linear value in this cost model is produced by an XOR of at most 3 already-pinned values at 1 allocation + 1 row, and that is THE WHOLE GATE LIBRARY — which is why such a circuit's cost is exactly a shortest-linear-program count in the 3-input-XOR basis. *** AND A PRIMITIVE THIS CORPUS DID NOT HAVE: THE INVERSE OF AN AFFINE FORM COSTS 1 ALLOCATION + 1 ROW. *** h = 1/L is pinned by the single row (h)(L) = 1, sound whenever L is a unit on the reachable set. It is a legitimate NON-BOOLEAN helper that widens the gate library beyond the F_2-linear world: measured on Keccak's parity-5, h = 1/(S+delta) with S the free affine column sum makes parity(S) single-row pinnable at delta = -7/2, -10/3, -5/3, giving a 4-score route that TIES the two-XOR3 chain. It did not win there, but the primitive is cheap, general, and worth testing wherever a value's range is too wide for the <= 4 rule.

THE LOWER-BOUND AND GADGET LITERATURE IS EMPTY WHERE WE NEED IT, SEARCHED PROPERLY THIS TIME — TWO NEGATIVES THAT ARE EVIDENCE OF NOVELTY, NOT GAPS TO FILL. Searched via IACR ePrint full text, DBLP, Crossref, arXiv, Google Scholar and Sourcegraph code search. (1) NO R1CS LOWER-BOUND LITERATURE EXISTS. 'non-scalar complexity' returns ZERO DBLP hits; 'Ostrowski measure' returns five, all false positives (structural dynamics, stock-market entropy, amino-acid chirality). The classical terms are real — Strassen's 'Algebraic Complexity Theory' survey, Montana-Pardo's non-scalar model, Mirwald-Schnorr on boolean quadratic forms — but NOTHING applies them to boolean functions embedded in a large F_p, and searches for rank-1-constraint or dimension-theoretic lower bounds on constraint counts returned no results at all. Every hit for 'multiplicative complexity' plus 'R1CS' is a DESIGN paper minimising it (Arion, Griffin, Aly et al. TOSC 2020), never a lower bound. This corpus's Lemma-A-style arguments have no prior art to check against, so THEY MUST BE SELF-CHECKED WITH CONTROLS — do not assume a reviewer's eye exists. (2) NO MOEBIUS/RATIONAL DIGIT-EXTRACTION GADGET IS PUBLISHED. Searches for one-constraint bit extraction from a range-bounded field element found nothing; the only 'digit extraction' hits are the FHE sense (BGV/BFV bootstrapping). So the one-row bit-extraction criterion in this file — a row pins f iff f*R has degree <= 2, specialising to 'extractable in one row iff the range has at most 4 values' — is unpublished. That is a reason to TRUST OUR OWN EXACT COMPUTATIONS OVER RECALLED FOLKLORE on this point, and a reason to re-verify anything a job claims to remember about it. (3) ONE PAPER IS DIRECTLY ON POINT FOR WHY OUR WHOLE COST MODEL HURTS: Skatharoudis, 'The Small-Field Turn in Succinct Proofs', ePrint 2026/1371 — 'a bitwise operation in a prime field has no native counterpart at all', and 'hash-heavy computations that can be expressed in field-native S-boxes favor the prime fields, whereas bit-heavy computations pay range-check tolls that the binary fields avoid'. It is a systematisation, not a technique, and it explicitly tags which of its claims are peer-reviewed versus vendor/blog — worth reading once for framing, not for a lever.

*** BUILD BOTH ONE-HOTS AND EVERY PRODUCT ROW BUYS A RANK-2 MATRIX INSTEAD OF A RANK-1 ONE — A GENERAL FACTOR-OF-SQRT(2) ON ANY TABLE SELECTION, VERIFIED OVER THE BN254 SCALAR PRIME. *** Whenever a gadget selects m values from a 2^w-entry constant table, do NOT peel bits. Split w = t + j and materialise BOTH one-hot vectors, cost (2^t - t - 1) + (2^j - j - 1). Every affine form over the witness is then additive, alpha_a + gamma_c, and (alpha_a + gamma_c)(beta_a + delta_c) = alpha_a*beta_a + gamma_c*delta_c + (alpha (x) delta + beta (x) gamma). THE FIRST TERM IS A FUNCTION OF a ALONE AND THE SECOND OF c ALONE, so both are free affine combinations of the one-hots already built, and the row delivers the rank-2 matrix for nothing. Each target viewed as a 2^t x 2^j matrix then costs ceil(rank/2) rows rather than 2^j - 1. Asymptotically sqrt(2)*sqrt(m * 2^w) against the peel law's 2*sqrt(m * 2^w). The peel law is also the published constant (Boyar & Find, 'Multiplicative Complexity of Vector Valued Boolean Functions', TCS 2018, Thm 7, arXiv:1407.6169; Thm 6 lower bound sqrt(m*2^n) - 2n - m/2) — BUT DO NOT SAY THIS 'BEATS THE LITERATURE': that line measures MULTIPLICATIVE COMPLEXITY OVER GF(2), basis (AND, XOR, 1), and an R1CS row over F_p is strictly more powerful than a GF(2) AND gate, so undercutting it is expected rather than remarkable. The gain over peel IS real and bankable. THE COROLLARY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE CONSTANT: whenever a corpus entry says a gadget 'attains the one-hot/peel minimum and is therefore optimal', THAT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT ONE CONSTRUCTION FAMILY, NOT A FLOOR. Two fixed-base entries said exactly that about Select12 and both were wrong. Ask what the row is buying — rank-1 or rank-2 — before believing any attainment argument.

SOLVING A LARGE POLYNOMIAL SYSTEM OVER BN254 IS UNREACHABLE BY EVERY PUBLISHED ROUTE — SIX APPROACHES CLOSED WITH MARGINS, PLUS TWO TOOL TRAPS THAT WILL WASTE AN HOUR. Recorded because 'just solve for the parameters' keeps getting proposed whenever a counting bound sits below a construction. *** NO FAST GROEBNER ENGINE EVEN ACCEPTS OUR PRIME. *** msolve caps characteristic at < 2^31 (src/neogb/io.c), FGb at < 65521, Singular at <= 2^31. Only Magma and Maple can represent BN254 at all, and not on their fast paths. Scale for orientation: the largest published msolve benchmark is Katsura-14 — FIFTEEN VARIABLES, FIFTEEN DAYS; the largest system solved by anything (chordal elimination, Cifuentes-Parrilo) is 288 variables / 528 equations. A near-square system is the WORST case, because overdeterminedness is the only thing that collapses the degree of regularity. *** MEASURED, AND THE FAILURE MODE IS NOW CONFIRMED: msolve IS OOM-KILLED ON THE SMALLEST INSTANCE OF THE FAMILY. *** (w,m,M) = (4,1,2) is 16 equations and 29 essential unknowns, encoded as 61 quadratic variables — 1/900th of (11,7,106) in equation count. Four attempts, all producing ZERO BYTES (msolve writes -o only at the end, so an empty file means it aborted rather than finished): 402 s at 0 slices, 1024 s at 13 slices, one at 14 slices, and a definitive run that returned *** EXIT 137 — SIGKILL — AFTER 1366 s ON A 15 GB MACHINE. *** So MEMORY IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, NOT TIME, AND IT BINDS IMMEDIATELY. The sharp consequence: there is NO PARTIAL RESULT TO BE HAD AT ANY SIZE — not at w=8, not at w=5 — so do not propose 'try a smaller instance first' as a way in. Generic Groebner is not a tool for this problem at any scale. This is consistent with the published envelope (largest msolve benchmark: Katsura-14, FIFTEEN variables, FIFTEEN DAYS) even though our system is all-quadratic and highly structured. *** HENSEL / p-ADIC LIFTING IS BACKWARDS. *** Every version (Conrad Thm 3.3; Berthomieu-Lebreton ISSAC 2012, whose input is literally a straight-line program) takes a REGULAR ROOT MOD p AS ITS HYPOTHESIS and produces a Z_p or Q answer. PARI says it in the signature: padicappr(pol, a) — the mod-p root is an ARGUMENT. The F_p point is the input, not the output. F_p[[t]] deformation is the same theorem with (p) -> (t). *** HOMOTOPY AND RATIONAL RECONSTRUCTION ARE DEAD TWICE OVER. *** Breiding, a HomotopyContinuation.jl author, on whether Newton works p-adically: 'Unfortunately, the answer is negative. The p-adics are totally disconnected, making it impossible to even find any path between two points.' And F_p-points are NOT reductions of Q-points — Selmer's cubic has real and all p-adic points but no rational ones — so even exact rationals would not transfer. *** LANG-WEIL / CAFURE-MATERA IS VACUOUS AT OUR SIZES, AND THE BINDING EXPONENT IS p^(1/4), NOT p^(1/2). *** Their corollary needs q > max{2(r+1)*deg^2, 2*deg^4}, which for BN254 caps deg V at about 2^63. It stays usable up to CODIMENSION 9 — nine equations, not thousands. Geometric irreducibility is also a HYPOTHESIS, and checking it is strictly harder than the Groebner computation you invoked Lang-Weil to avoid. ONE FACT WORTH KEEPING: at dimension 0 degree buys nothing — the expected number of F_p-points on a random 0-dim slice is exactly 1, with P(>=1) -> 1 - 1/e ~ 63 percent, INDEPENDENT OF DEGREE (Diaconis-Fulman-Guralnick). *** PINNING KNOWN ROWS AND SOLVING THE TAIL FALSIFIES EXPERIMENTALLY. *** Exact Jacobian ranks over F_p show that pinning even ONE row generically drops the image below full dimension ((5,1,3) goes 32/32 -> 31/32 at one pinned row, 21/32 at two; (5,2,4) goes 64/64 -> 56 -> 46 -> 34). Pinning row k destroys 2(w+k) parameters, and the rows you would most want to pin are the LEAST generic ones. *** TWO msolve TRAPS. *** It SILENTLY MIS-PARSES x*x as x, returning a wrong answer with no warning — x^2 is required; verified, x*x-y, y-1 gives a degree-1 parametrisation where x^2-y, y-1 gives degree 2. And it caps characteristic below 2^31 with only a 'Warning:' on stderr plus exit code 1, which is easy to miss in a pipeline. *** THE STANDING LESSON. *** When a counting bound sits far below a construction, the gap is a CONSTRUCTIVE problem, not a solving problem. Dominance of the parameter map (which is cheap to check by Jacobian rank over F_p, and worth checking) tells you solutions EXIST; it gives you no way to find one. Spend the time on better algebraic identities — that is where the sqrt(2) selector win came from — not on solvers.
sha256-hash: CALIBRATION REBUILT FROM ACTUAL CIRCUIT GENERATION (every number below was measured by building the circuit and counting, not quoted). Per ONE 512-bit compression, plain R1CS, no lookups: jsnark 25656 with the constant IV and 25968 generic (variable chaining value) — verified by emitting the real .arith and applying CircuitReader's instruction-to-R1CS mapping; xJsnark claims 25538 (paper Table III, same jsnark->libsnark pipeline, credible but not independently re-measured); bellman 25840 BUT THAT IS A CONSTANT-IV FIRST-BLOCK ARTIFACT — a generic bellman block is 26192 (26166 nonlinear), because with a constant IV the first rounds' ch/maj/rotate-XORs fold away; libsnark 27280 (NOT the widely repeated 27904, which appears in no libsnark file, test or constant and is folklore), rising to 27792 if you count input booleanity, which libsnark deliberately omits (issue #37); arkworks crypto-primitives about 40880 per block, a naive port, not a target; gnark about 25.8k marginal but OUT OF SCOPE and irrelevant anyway, since std/math/uints is built on 2^8 x 2^8 lookup tables plus about 130k fixed table cost. WATCH THE CONVENTION: these differ by whether the 512 message bits' booleanity is counted (jsnark 25392 excluding vs 25968 as measured). Pin that down before claiming a win.

CORRECTION — ONE ROW PER BIT IS NOT THE FLOOR FOR Ch AND Maj; THE RECORD IS AT HALF A ROW PER BIT. I previously wrote that we were 'already at ONE row per Maj bit including booleanity' and used that to reject jsnark's cross-round Maj sharing (which gets 1.5 multiplications per Maj bit and is indeed a regression against 1). BOTH HALVES NEED UPDATING: the jsnark trick is still a regression, but our floor is now 0.5 alloc + 0.5 constr per bit via lambda-packed twin instances (see the _common entry). CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE-CLASSIFICATION WORK: the exhaustive SMT sweep that found 192 of 256 three-input functions to be single-row NATIVE answered the question for ONE instance of a function. The open and more valuable question is WHICH PAIRS OF NATIVE FUNCTIONS SHARING INPUTS ADMIT A SINGLE LAMBDA-PACKED ROW — that is where the remaining factor of two lives, and the sweep has not been run for it.
Majority(B,C,D) = (B&C) ^ (B&D) ^ (C&D): three ANDs + XOR-fold; Ch(E,F,G) = G ^ (E&(F^G)) uses ONE AND (E&(F^G)) instead of two.

Represent each 32-bit word's bits once and reuse; XOR / rotation / shift are FREE affine combinations of bit variables — never allocate constraints for them, only for the AND (booleanity + one rank-1 product).

CALIBRATION, CORRECTED AND MEASURED (the widely-quoted numbers are wrong in two places). bkomuves/hash-circuits' 26170 is labelled 'approximate' in its own README, appears nowhere else, and ships no benchmark harness; compiled here with circom 2.2.3 --O2 it is 26232 general / 26040 constant-IV (budget: rounds 64x294 + 264 = 19080, schedule 48x149 = 7152). libsnark's real figure is 27280 (sha256_gadget.tcc: `return 27280; /* hardcoded for now */`) — THE WIDELY-CITED 27904 IS FOLKLORE, traceable to no primary source. circomlib Sha256compression() = 30328 nonlinear (--O2; 30952 at --O0), Sha256(256) = 29412, Sha256(512) = 59313. bellman = 25840, a hard CI assertion at src/gadgets/sha256.rs:331, constant-IV, so it beats bkomuves' constant-IV 26040 by 200. THE PUBLISHED FRONTIER IS xJsnark's 25538 (Kosba et al., S&P 2018, Table III; Buffet 44999 / Geppetto 38556). ALL of these count NONLINEAR CONSTRAINTS ONLY, with no allocations, so none of them is directly comparable to our allocations+constraints score — and none of them threatens it. Verified-zkEVM/clean's own public Clean/Gadgets/SHA256/ (main branch, NOT PR #395) is about 40280: chained two-operand Add32 at 33 each, written for provability rather than cost. gnark, Noir and arkworks-via-lookups are OUT OF SCOPE (LogUp / plookup / BSB22 commitments).
Carry-save (3:2 compressor) addition to combine the 6-7 addends in the round function before a single final modular reduction, rather than chained 2-input adds.

CORRECTION — THE TOP-CARRY-BIT-AS-AFFINE-COMBINATION IS ALREADY APPLIED, AND IT GOES FURTHER THAN THE -1/-1 I CLAIMED. My earlier note said no implementation defines the top carry bit affinely and that doing so saves 1 allocation + 1 constraint per decomposition. The RECORD SOLUTION ALREADY DOES IT, in three places, and beats that figure: (a) CarrySumAdd32 witnesses ONLY the 32 output bits and makes EVERY carry — including the top — affine, via the recursion c_{n+1} = 2^-1*(a[n] + b[n] + c_n - z[n]); a full 32-bit modular add is 32 allocations + 32 constraints with ZERO carry allocations AND NO TIE ROW, because each carry's DEFINITION is the sum equation. The per-bit row is (c_next + a[i] + b[i] - 9c + 3)*(a[i] + b[i] + 6c - 4) + 12 = 0. (b) The fused round adders define their BOTTOM carry bit affinely and assert only its booleanity, which discharges two packed 32-bit reductions at once. (c) Every message byte witnesses 7 bits, not 8: hi = 128^-1*(byte - sum 2^t low[t]). THE RESIDUAL QUESTION, AND IT IS CLOSED: can a SECOND carry bit per fused adder also be made affine? No — one field identity solves for exactly one unknown, so all remaining carry bits must be witnessed. GENERAL RULE THAT SURVIVES: in any decomposition, allocate k-1 of the k bits and derive the last affinely; a k-bit range check costs 2k-1, not 2k.

Smart bitwidth adjustment (xJsnark): track a STATIC upper bound on every intermediate 32-bit word through the adds/XOR-folds and insert a bit-decomposition/normalization ONLY when that bound would overflow the native field — not after every operation. Reported ~3.2k constraints saved vs Geppetto and ~10k vs Buffet on SHA-256; each skipped decomposition removes 32 allocations + its booleanity constraints, so it pays double in this metric.

Global common-subexpression / multivariate-polynomial minimization across the 64 rounds (xJsnark, reported ~8.8k constraints on SHA-256): the message schedule and round function reuse the same sigma/XOR-fold subexpressions — allocate each distinct affine combination ONCE and share it everywhere rather than per-round.

If the framework exposes lookups: 'spread'/interleaved-bit tables (Barretenberg-style) turn XOR3 and Maj into table reads; only worth it if a lookup is cheaper than the ~1 constraint the arithmetic form already costs — verify against this R1CS cost model first.

Boyar-Peralta counter bound also applies to the NATIVE SHA-256 challenge's bit-level adders: MC of Hamming weight of n bits is exactly n - H(n), so multi-operand column addition wants optimal k:log(k) counters, not chained 3:2 compressors. Weigh against the field-arithmetic route here (a native field can add many 32-bit words in one linear combination and range-check once) — pick whichever costs fewer allocations+constraints, but do not assume chained full adders are optimal.

CORRECTION — 184 DECOMPOSITIONS PER BLOCK IS NOT THE FLOOR; THE RECORD DOES 180. My earlier note called 184 the 'settled' design (64x2 rounds + 48 schedule + 8 final) and said anything above it was free score. The record measures 180: 128 for the rounds (64x2, unchanged), **46** schedule words instead of 48, and **6** final chaining adds instead of 8. The two structural reasons are separate entries below — w62/w63 are never reduced or decomposed because nothing downstream reads their BITS, and the chaining adds for state words 0 and 4 are folded into round 63's own reduction. THE SHARING CLAUSES OF THE ORIGINAL NOTE ARE ALL CORRECT AND ARE HONOURED BY THE RECORD: d and h are never FRESHLY decomposed (they exist as bit vectors only because they are earlier a's and e's), b/c are previous a's, f/g previous e's, a's bits serve Sigma0 and Maj, e's bits serve Sigma1 and Ch, rotations are re-indexing. circomlib's 4-per-round remains the outlier. TREAT 180 AS THE NUMBER TO BEAT, and ask of every remaining decomposition whether ANY consumer reads an individual bit.

THE PREMISE THAT MODULAR REDUCTION DOMINATES THE NATIVE COST IS FALSE — BIT-LOGIC IS THE COST, AND MY EARLIER PROJECTION OF WHAT A GOLFED BLOCK COSTS WAS 17% PESSIMISTIC. Corrected against the record's own cost proofs, for one GENERIC 512-bit block: rounds 21062 (31 round-pairs at 658 plus a 664 tail pair), schedule 8627 (23 step-pairs at 365 plus two 58/58 last steps), final chaining adds 384 — TOTAL 30073 score per block. I had projected about 35.1k (25216 + 9360 + 520); all three sub-budgets are beaten, the rounds budget by 4154. Where the round cost actually sits, per PAIR of rounds (328 alloc / 330 constr): four upper sigmas 128, four 32-bit word decompositions 128 allocations + 128 booleanity, packed Ch 32/32, packed Maj 32/32, and the two fused adders 8 allocations + 10 constraints for FOUR 32-bit modular reductions. So the reductions are about 3% of a round pair and the bit-logic and decompositions are the rest. Block 0 (constant IV) is 29780 and the final padding-only block is 21442 because its whole schedule is affine.

BLOCK 0's CHAINING VALUE IS THE CONSTANT IV — this challenge hashes a MESSAGE, not a compression with a variable state, so every operation consuming the initial state in block 0 is against compile-time constants and is partially foldable. In the Boolean world that alone is worth -301 ANDs (Goldfeder's sha256Unpadded.txt = 22272 vs Bristol's general 22573; github.com/matteocam/sha256-circuit). In the native world it is the difference between bkomuves' 26232 and 26040. Make sure the first block is specialized and not calling the same generic compression circuit as blocks 1..n.

CLOSED — bellman's MultiEq IS ENTIRELY SUBSUMED, AS SUSPECTED. The open question was whether the framework charges for standalone affine equality (tie) rows, in which case bellman's trick of packing ~7 sum-equalities into one row by bit-offsetting them would pay. IT DOES NOT ARISE: the record has NO TIE ROWS ANYWHERE, because every carry is defined as the affine expression that the sum identity solves for, so the identity is discharged by asserting the carry's booleanity and never appears as a separate row. Do not spend a slot on MultiEq.

DO-NOT-TRY, AND IT IS A TEMPTING ONE: XOR-GATE / SHORTEST-LINEAR-PROGRAM MINIMIZATION BUYS EXACTLY ZERO HERE. There is a large and still-active literature on minimizing the number of 2-input XOR gates needed to evaluate an F2-LINEAR MAP — the Shortest Linear Program problem: Boyar-Peralta, Tan-Peyrin (TCHES'20) adding randomization and 3-input XOR gates, the 'Superior Boyar-Peralta' (SBP) depth-aware heuristic, 'Improved Heuristics for Low-Latency Implementations of Linear Layers', and eprint 2025/1493 which revisits BP and cuts the AES linear layer from 91 to 89 g-XOR. Keccak's theta (and rho/pi, and SHA-256's Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1) are exactly such linear maps, so this looks like the obvious attack on the biggest remaining slack. IT IS NOT, BECAUSE AN XOR GATE COSTS NOTHING IN EITHER OF OUR COST MODELS. In native R1CS an affine combination lives inside the A/B/C vectors of a row and is free. In the GF(2) challenges the harness restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A and B AFFINE, so an arbitrary XOR-combination is free inside a multiplicand. Halving the XOR count of theta changes the score by ZERO. WHAT THETA'S 2240 ROWS PER ROUND ACTUALLY PAY FOR IS *MATERIALIZATION*, NOT XOR COUNT: a value costs an allocation exactly when it must appear as a BARE WITNESS VARIABLE — because it is a circuit output, or because its consumer needs a variable rather than an affine form. THEREFORE THE ONLY QUESTION WORTH ASKING IS: for each currently-materialized intermediate, WHO CONSUMES IT, and can that consumer take an affine form instead? Every row saved comes from deleting a materialization, never from restructuring the XOR tree that feeds it.

LAMBDA-FUSED MULTI-OPERAND MODULAR ADDITION — TWO 32-BIT REDUCTIONS FOR 5 ALLOCATIONS AND 6 CONSTRAINTS, WITH NO TIE ROW. Do not emit one 'sum = value' equality per modular reduction. Pack TWO independent 6-operand mod-2^32 reductions into ONE field identity at base lambda = 2^40 (both sums are < 2^35 so the slots cannot collide over BN254), witness all but one of the carry bits, and DEFINE the remaining carry bit as the affine expression the identity solves for. Asserting only that this expression is boolean then discharges BOTH sum equations and its own range at once. MEASURED (the E-path adder across two SHA-256 rounds): witness 2 carry bits for round t and 3 for round t+1 = 5 allocations; 5 booleanity rows plus 1 row for the derived low carry = 6 constraints. The A-path adder (5 operands, 2 carry bits per round) is 3 allocations / 4 constraints. TOTAL 8 allocations + 10 constraints for FOUR 32-bit modular reductions in a round pair. THE DERIVED CARRY: lowCarry = 2^-32*(sum operands_t + z_packed + lambda*sum operands_{t+1} - out_t - lambda*(out_{t+1} + 2^32*carry_{t+1})) - 2*c_t[1] - 4*c_t[2], then assertZero(lowCarry*(lowCarry - 1)). Note the packed Ch/Maj word enters as a SINGLE expression and splits into the two lambda-slots automatically. Subtracting a state word is not32(d) + 1 — two's complement, affine, free.

FUSE THE FINAL CHAINING ADDITION INTO THE LAST ROUND'S OWN REDUCTION. The Merkle-Damgard feed-forward H[i] += state[i] is normally 8 separate 32-bit adds after the 64 rounds. TWO OF THEM ARE FREE: round 63 already computes new_e and new_a by a modular reduction, so add the chaining value INTO THAT SAME SUM and witness the result once. MEASURED: out4 := s4 + c + g + Sigma1' + Ch + K63 + w63 and out0 := out4 + s0 - s4 + Sigma0' + Maj - c + 2, each a single 32-bit decomposition inside the round-63 gadget, so only 6 of the 8 chaining adds survive as standalone adders. SAVES 2 decompositions = 64 score per block and takes the per-block decomposition count from 182 to 180. The extra operands widen the sum by one bit, absorbed by the existing carry witnesses. GENERALISES to any Merkle-Damgard hash: any last-round output word that coincides with a feed-forward target is free to fold.

PACK THE 2-INPUT-XOR LANES OF sigma0/sigma1 — 58 WITNESSES FOR 64 SIGMA LANES, NOT 64, AND NEVER MATERIALISE THE SIGMA WORDS. SHA-256's SCHEDULE sigmas contain a SHIFT, so their top lanes degenerate to 2-input XORs: sigma0 = rotr7 ^ rotr18 ^ shr3 is a genuine 3-input XOR only on lanes 0..28, and sigma1 = rotr17 ^ rotr19 ^ shr10 only on lanes 0..21. A 3-input lane needs its own witness (single-row form), but TWO 2-INPUT LANES FIT IN ONE WITNESS by difference of squares: with lambda = r^2, 2a - 2b + 2*lambda*(c+d) - 1 - (r*(c+d) - (1-a+b))*(r*(c+d) + (1-a+b)) = xor2(a,b) + lambda*xor2(c,d) — ONE rank-1 row, verified for lambda = 4, 2 and 1. MEASURED per schedule step: 29 + 22 three-input lanes, 6 packed pairs and 1 singleton = 58 allocations and 57 rows covering all 64 lanes, against 64 + 64 for two separate XOR3 words. The singleton lane is then DEFERRED and shared across two adjacent steps by one more lambda = 2^40 packed row, so a PAIR of schedule steps is 182 allocations / 183 constraints. The 58 field elements recombine into the schedule sum affinely and the sigma words are never built as 32-bit vectors at all. DOES NOT APPLY to the ROUND sigmas Sigma0/Sigma1 — those are pure rotations with no degenerate lanes, so they stay at 32/32.

DECOMPOSE ONLY 7 OF 8 BITS PER MESSAGE BYTE, AND PAIR THE 8TH-BIT CHECKS. The top bit of a byte that is already an input signal is AFFINE in the byte and its low bits: hi := 128^-1*(byte - sum_{t<7} 2^t*low[t]). Witness only 7. THEN pack the remaining high-bit range checks TWO BYTES AT A TIME by difference of squares: centre each as x := (byte - lowSum) - 64*active so that x is in {-64, 0, +64} and x^2 = 4096*active, then settle two bytes in one row: (x0 - 1024*x1)*(x0 + 1024*x1) - 4096*(active0 - 1048576*active1) = 0, where the 1024^2 = 2^20 weight keeps the slots from interfering because |x| <= 64. MEASURED over 239 checked bytes: 1673 allocations (239 x 7) and 1793 constraints, i.e. 7 allocations + 7.5 constraints per byte against a naive 8 + 9 — saves 2.5 score per input byte.

A FREE ASSUMPTION NOBODY HAS BANKED: messageLen < 256 IS ASSUMED, NOT ENFORCED. Challenge/Specs/SHA256.lean gives `Assumptions input len := IsByteArray input AND len < bufferLen` with bufferLen = 256 and len = input.messageLen.val. The byte-ness half is already exploited (it is what makes the 7-bits-per-byte decomposition complete), but the LENGTH BOUND IS NOT MENTIONED ANYWHERE IN THIS CORPUS — soundness only has to hold when it holds. AUDIT THE PADDING AND LENGTH PATH for any range check, bit decomposition or comparison on messageLen that exists ONLY to establish messageLen < 256; every such row is free score. NOTE WHAT THE ASSUMPTION DOES NOT GIVE: booleanity of the witnessed low bits is still needed (an adversary picks the bits), and the Spec's `if len <= bufferLen then output = sha256 (truncate input len) else False` still forces the digest words to be exact naturals, so the output decomposition stays.

*** EVIDENCE GAP, CONCLUSION UNCHANGED — this sweep's lambda list omitted the ONLY lambdas SHA-256 can actually use; see the lambda-list correction entry, which closes the realisable cases and upgrades the result from sampled to PROVED. *** CLOSED, NEGATIVE — THE LAMBDA-PACKING SWEEP FOR SIGMA0/SIGMA1 IS EMPTY, AND THE REASON IS THE ROTATION OFFSETS. Our own entries named this the highest-value unrun experiment (-128 per round pair, ~-17k overall). IT HAS NOW BEEN RUN AND IT IS EMPTY; the circuit stands at 145479 and the 256 per round pair spent on the four upper sigmas (Cost.lean:75-79) is NOT recoverable by packing. METHOD (exhaustive, PROVED complete): a row whose only witness is z is (p_z z + P0)(q_z z + Q0) = r_z z + R0 with P0,Q0,R0 affine in the already-materialised boolean inputs; expanding to A z^2 + B(x) z + C(x) = 0 and splitting on which of p_z,q_z vanish gives exactly THREE cases and no others — CASE 1 T in Aff*Aff+Aff (unique root; this is the PackedCh row); CASE 2 exists affine B non-vanishing on the cube and affine L with deg_ML(B*(T+L)) <= 1 (unique root; the Xor3 row); CASE 3 exists affine u,v and constant c with deg_ML(T^2 + T*(u+v+c) + u*v) <= 1 (TWO roots, needs the out-of-range decoy; the PackedMaj row). DECIDED NEGATIVE for lambda in {1,2,4,2^16,2^32,2^33,2^40,2^41,2^64,123456789,p-1,(p-1)/2,3^77}: Sigma-lane x Sigma-lane on the same word (1 shared bit), on different words (0 shared), Sigma x Maj and Sigma x Ch in all 9 argument alignments each, the alternative maj-lane materialisation (Sigma0 word = affine - 2*majword, so maj lanes may be materialised instead of xor lanes) in all the same configurations, Ch x Ch disjoint, 3-way and 4-way Ch chains, 3-way Maj, Ch+Ch+Sigma triples, and 3-way Sigma. ALL: NO SINGLE ROW. DO NOT RE-RUN THIS SWEEP.

THE PACKING CRITERION, AND WHY SHA-256 SUPPLIES IT EXACTLY ONCE. A pair of gadget instances packs into ONE witness and ONE row essentially iff they SHARE AT LEAST TWO OF THEIR THREE INPUTS: xor3|xor3 and xor3|xor2 both pack at 2 shared inputs (the first via the two-root form, the second via a UNIQUE-ROOT non-vanishing-multiplier row, coefficients extracted and brute-force verified) and both fail at 0 or 1 shared inputs. Symmetry-reduced exhaustive sweep over all 256x256 pairs: at 0 shared inputs only 25 of 361 orbits pack, ALL via Case 1 and ALL with both functions of DIAGONAL-CORRECTED RANK 1 (a quadratic in a SINGLE affine form — the XOR2/AND2/OR2 family, 38 of the 256 three-input functions; this is exactly the difference-of-squares schedule packing we already run, and it is the ONLY disjoint packing that exists). At 1 shared input 297 of 1300 orbits pack but NOT ONE involves XOR3, Maj or Ch. At 2 shared inputs packing is abundant — which is where Ch and Maj live. NOW THE SHA-256 FACT, MEASURED EXHAUSTIVELY OVER EVERY LANE PAIR IN THE WHOLE CIRCUIT: no two materialised bit-gadget lanes reading the same word share more than ONE input bit. The offsets at which gadgets read a word are a-word {0 (Maj), 2,13,22 (Sigma0)}, e-word {0 (Ch), 6,11,25 (Sigma1)}, w-word {7,18,3-shift (sigma0), 17,19,10-shift (sigma1)}, and within every cohabiting gadget pair the PAIRWISE DIFFERENCES ARE ALL DISTINCT MOD 32, so one lane offset can align at most one input. Ch and Maj get their two shared inputs from a different mechanism entirely — the STATE ROTATION (a,b,c)->(new_a,a,b) and (e,f,g)->(new_e,e,f), an OFFSET-ZERO alignment. SHA-256 aligns two inputs in exactly one place and we already bank it. GENERAL RULE FOR OTHER HASHES: before attempting a packing, compute the multiset of pairwise differences of the offsets at which every gadget reads a shared word; a REPEAT is necessary for a pairing to exist.

HOW TO RUN A ROW-EXISTENCE QUERY — THE NAIVE ENCODING DOES NOT TERMINATE. Existentially quantifying all row coefficients and asserting the 2^n completeness equations TIMES OUT in cvc5 1.3.4 even at n=3, on plain XOR3. USE THE STAGED FORM: the degree->=3 part of the constraint is a LINEAR system over F_p in the unknown affine multiplier (B for the unique-root form, S for the two-root form) — solve it exactly by Gaussian elimination, and hand only the residual small bilinear degree-2 system to cvc5. That decides n=6 in MILLISECONDS. Non-vanishing of B is exact and cheap: over F_p a subspace is never covered by <= 2^n proper hyperplanes, so a non-vanishing B exists iff no cube point annihilates the whole solution space. VALIDATE ANY SUCH HARNESS against four known-good rows before trusting it: XOR3 native, AND3 non-native, PackedCh = Case 1, PackedMaj = Case 3; and re-verify every POSITIVE by extracting explicit coefficients and brute-forcing the cube. THE 192-OF-256 NATIVE CLASSIFICATION IS CONFIRMED with the exact criterion — f is native iff there is an affine M non-vanishing on the cube and an affine L with the multilinear reduction of M*(f+L) affine; the failure mode of all 64 non-natives is always that EVERY admissible M vanishes at some cube point; all 128 functions of GF(2) ANF degree <= 2 are native and exactly 64 of the 128 degree-3 ones are; the 'z = product of two affines + affine' subfamily is 70 functions and is a STRICT SUBSET of the 192.

WHAT THE PACKING NEGATIVE DOES NOT CLOSE — WORD-LEVEL SIGMA MATERIALISATION IS STILL OPEN AND IS NOW THE TOP SIGMA LEVER. The sweep closes LANE-LEVEL packing only. The untouched question is whether a whole 32-bit Sigma0 word can be certified in fewer than 32 allocations + 32 rows by an identity that NEVER MENTIONS INDIVIDUAL LANES. The reduction to state: Sigma0(a) = rotr2(a) + rotr13(a) + rotr22(a) - 2*C, where the three rotations are FREE affine forms and C is the carry-save carry (majority) word — so the whole question is 'what does ONE carry word cost'. NOTHING IN THIS CORPUS FORBIDS < 64: Theorem R gives only >= 2 per materialised value, and Bezout on the full system is already discharged by the 32 booleanity rows of the input word, so neither floor binds. The evidence for 64 is EMPIRICAL ONLY — every implementation from 2014 to 2025 pays >= 1 row per XOR3 bit. SEPARATELY, DO NOT CHASE 'pack a Sigma lane together with a decomposition bit' (also nominally -128 per round pair): it fails not on algebra but on EXTRACTABILITY — the bits of new_a/new_e are consumed INDIVIDUALLY by the next round's Sigma/Ch/Maj rows and a packed witness does not expose its slots as affine forms. Sigma WORDS by contrast are consumed only additively, so for them the consumption side was never the obstacle; the algebra is.

SWEEP RESULT FOR 'ASSERTION, NOT VALUE' OUTSIDE THE CARRY-WORD QUESTION: THE BOUNDARY GADGETS ARE ALREADY AT OR BELOW WHAT THE PRINCIPLE CAN REACH. (a) CheckPad7Sparse is 0 allocations / 2063 constraints (CostSparse.lean:14) — already a pure assertion block over witnesses allocated at top level (MainSparseCandidate.main:152-156 allocates compactLow and lenFlagsLow and hands them down), which is the principle taken to its limit; its rows are gated booleanity b*(b - active) = 0 (Padding7.lean:95-97), one product each, so they cannot be packed with each other. (b) SelectDigest (SelectDigest.lean:88-97) ALREADY USES the assertion form rather than a mux — groupFlagSum g * (fromBitsExpr S[g][w] - digest[w]) = 0 — at 8 allocations / 40 constraints; the obvious packing to 8/10 is UNSOUND because the 8 digest words carry no row-level bound, and a 5-way mux would also cost 40 rows. (c) Round0Block1Sparse (Round0Block1.lean:220-227) is 32 alloc + 33 rows and the top-bit-free rule does not apply (dropping the top bit forces witnessing the wrap carry: 32/33 either way). (d) ONE GENUINELY UNEXPLOITED KNOWN RULE, worth a mechanical grep before the next adder job: the signature 'witnessVector n; boolVec n; assertZero (link)' is 2 score above the floor at every occurrence, because RangeCheck n is (n-1, n) on an expression. Round0Block1Sparse is the one instance checked and it is a false positive. NOTHING HERE TOUCHES THE MULTI-OPERAND CARRY-WORD QUESTION, which is where all the remaining headroom on this slug is.

CLOSED, NEGATIVE, PROVED — THE SIGMA CARRY WORD COSTS 64 AND THE SIGMAS ARE FINISHED. The word-level question was the last open lever: Sigma0(a) = rotr2+rotr13+rotr22 - 2*C (verified as an exact integer identity over 200000 random words), so everything reduced to 'what does ONE carry word cost'. IT COSTS 64 AND THAT IS NOW A THEOREM. C = sum_j 2^j*maj(a_{j+2},a_{j+13},a_{j+22}) is multilinear of degree EXACTLY 3 in the 32 input bits (128 monomials); an R1CS row is degree 2. (A) SINGLE PACKED WITNESS m = C: expanding (p*m+P0)(q*m+Q0) = r*m+R0 gives p*q*m^2 + B*m + (P0Q0-R0) = 0 with B affine. ML(C^2) has 400 DEGREE-6 MONOMIALS while ML(B*C) is degree <= 4 and P0Q0 is degree <= 2, so the two-root stage-1 solve is INFEASIBLE and p*q = 0 in every row; and the kernel of B -> [deg >= 3 part of ML(C*B)] over 33 columns and 3392 equations is EXACTLY {0}, so B = 0 in every row. Both coefficients vanish identically => NO ROW MENTIONS m => m is unconstrained => unsound, FOR ANY NUMBER OF ROWS. Identical for the xor materialisation and for Sigma1. (B) EVERY MULTI-LANE PACKING, ANY WEIGHTS, ANY ROW COUNT: two enumerated lemmas do the work — L1, the 928 4-sets {i} u T_j (i not in T_j) are pairwise distinct; L2, the 400 6-sets T_j u T_k (disjoint) are pairwise distinct; and there are ZERO four-lane subsets with a common bit or without a disjoint pair. So |J| >= 4 dies (L1 forces the multiplier constant, requiring degree <= 2; L2 leaves a degree-6 coefficient 8*c_j*c_k != 0). NOTE WHAT DID NOT BIND, EXACTLY AS PREDICTED: Theorem R gives only >= 2 and Theorem B is saturated by the input word's own 32 booleanity rows, so neither floor forbids < 64 — THE OBSTRUCTION IS THE DEGREE FILTRATION, and it is sharp. SCORE DELTA 0; record 145479 unchanged; the 256 per round pair at Cost.lean:76-79 is FINAL. Sigma0 = Xor3 of three rotations at UpperSigma0.lean:12-13, sigmaCost = <32,32> at Cost.lean:50, single-row lane at Xor3.lean:16-18. HONEST RESIDUAL, CONJECTURED NOT PROVED: schemes where one row is affine in TWO OR MORE witnesses simultaneously. The sketch is that matching the degree-6 coefficients (unique by L2) forces p_{t(j)}q_{t(k)} + p_{t(k)}q_{t(j)} = 0 on every disjoint lane pair, hence one whole factor witness-free, after which L1 forces the shared multiplier constant and the row degenerates — but that is not machine-checked.

CORRECTION TO THE LAMBDA SWEEP — ITS LAMBDA LIST OMITTED THE ONLY LAMBDAS SHA-256 CAN ACTUALLY USE, AND THE FIX IS A STRONGER NEGATIVE. The sweep decided lane packing for lambda in {1,2,4,2^16,2^32,2^33,2^40,2^41,2^64,123456789,p-1, (p-1)/2,3^77}. But a packed witness z = C_j + lambda*C_j' recombines AFFINELY into the 32-bit sigma value only when lambda = 2^(j'-j), and two Sigma lanes share a bit only at j'-j in {9,11,20} for Sigma0 (rotations 2,13,22) and {5,14,19} for Sigma1 (6,11,25) — NONE of which is in that list. The conclusion was right; the evidence did not cover the only realisable case. NOW DECIDED, exactly over F_p: all negative, and likewise Sigma-lane x Maj-word lane at lambda = 2^2,2^13,2^22 and Sigma-lane x Ch-word lane at 2^6,2^11,2^25. AND THE ALL-LAMBDA STATEMENT IS NOW PROVED, NOT SAMPLED: for a 1-shared-bit pair the ONLY affine multiplier admitting deg_ML(B*T) <= 2 is B = x_shared - 1/2, INDEPENDENT OF LAMBDA (symbolic nullspace over Q(lam), generic rank 5 of 6), and ML(B*T) then carries a degree-2 coefficient -1/2 (maj lanes) or 1 (xor3 lanes) on a pair DISJOINT from B's support, which no affine L can cancel because the degree-2 part of ML(B*L) lives only on pairs touching x_shared; the two-root case dies by Groebner saturation over Q[lam,t]/(lam*t-1) returning the unit ideal. Three-lane packings split into exactly two orbits — STAR (J = {i-2,i-13,i-22}, the three lanes reading bit a_i, i.e. the 'three rotations share one source word' idea) and TRIANGLE (pairwise-sharing, no common bit) — both dead. THE STRENGTHENING THAT MATTERS: in every negative case BOTH stage-1 tests fail, so the result is not 'no SINGLE row' but 'NO ROW OF ANY KIND constrains the packed witness', which also kills the multi-row escape of covering the cube with several multipliers B_i that each vanish somewhere.

THE VERTEX-STAR TRICK: AN AND WORD OF TWO ROTATIONS COSTS 2*(MIN VERTEX COVER), NOT 2*32 — MEASURED, AND IT LOSES ON SHA-256's SIGMAS, SO BANK IT ELSEWHERE. Decomposing the Sigma carry word as C = val(A&B) + val(A&D) + val(B&D) - 2*val(A&B&D) exposes a clean structure: the lanes form 32 TRIANGLES on Z_32, and the edge graph is the 6-regular circulant C_32(9,11,20) for Sigma0 and C_32(5,14,19) for Sigma1, 96 edges each. Every AND lane is a product of two variables, so ALL edges incident to one vertex c pack into ONE row z_c = a_c * (sum of weighted neighbours) — a star, arbitrary weights, ONE allocation and ONE constraint — and the z_c recombine affinely. Covering all 96 edges therefore costs 2*(minimum vertex cover): measured independence number 9 for C_32(9,11,20) -> VC 23 -> 46 score, and 8 for C_32(5,14,19) -> VC 24 -> 48, for ALL THREE AND words at once, against 64 lane-by-lane. THE ROUTE STILL LOSES HERE because the cubic word val(A&B&D) survives: both endpoints of an edge determine its triangle uniquely, so a row a_c*z_c' yields at most ONE on-target cubic monomial plus garbage, i.e. >= 64 more, total >= 110 against the record's 64. GENERAL RULE WORTH CARRYING TO OTHER CHALLENGES: wherever a circuit needs a bitwise AND (or any degree-2 lane function) of two rotations or shifts of ONE word, build the STAR COVER of the difference-circulant instead of paying per lane — the saving is 2*(n - alpha). It fails on SHA-256 only because SHA-256 never needs an AND word on its own, only inside a degree-3 XOR3.

RETRACTED BY EVENTS — THE 145471 DESIGN IS FINE AND IS NOW THE RECORD. I wrote here that a 145471 tree (72445 alloc / 73026 constr) had failed verification, that a second job was re-deriving a rejected design, and that a third attempt should not be allowed to burn a slot. THE SECOND ATTEMPT VERIFIED AND TOOK THE RECORD FROM tekkac's 145478. The reasoning was wrong in a specific and instructive way: I treated an identical COST LEDGER as identical WORK. It is not — we had already established, on the twin RSA submissions at 321769, that two trees can share a declared allocations/constraints pair and differ completely in source, since proof text and gadget formulation do not move the ledger. So the first 145471 and the second were two different implementations that happened to cost the same, and only one of them was provable. THE RULE THAT SURVIVES: a verification failure condemns THE TREE, NEVER THE SCORE. Do not blacklist a cost figure, and do not infer a systematic design fault from a repeat at the same total — check whether the trees actually differ, which on the API means comparing what you can reach, because a failed submission cannot be downloaded at all. WHAT REMAINS TRUE from the retracted entry: the failure was not a timeout (a fixed-base success ran 19.2 min against its 17.5), and a failed tree survives only in out/<slug>/ until the next job overwrites it.

tekkac's 145478 TREE MINED — NOTHING TO PORT, BUT TWO CHEAP NEGATIVES. We dominate on EVERY shared cost atom and our 145471 is better in BOTH components (72445/73026 against their 72449/73029), so there is no stacking here. They do have NINE author-unique files, which is the signal that normally justifies a look, and it is an ALTERNATIVE BLOCK-1 STRATEGY: CompressBlock1Mixed, ComputableCompressBlock1Mixed(+Structural), Round0PaddingCombined, Round0PaddingFoldBounds, Round0PaddingMixed, SHA256Rounds1Mixed. THE ONE REAL IDEA, worth exactly 1: CheckPad7SparseUnchecked at 0/2062 against the checked 0/2063, i.e. one redundant constraint dropped from the padding path. NOTE THE DISCRIMINATOR WORKED AS INTENDED: a non-empty author-unique file set correctly flagged this tree as worth opening, and opening it correctly returned a negative — that is the check earning its keep, not failing.

VERIFIED ONE-ROW GADGET SET (cvc5 QF_FF over the actual BN254 prime, all unsat) — USE THESE SHAPES AND DO NOT RE-DERIVE THEM. Each is one syntactic product, one fresh witness, and CRUCIALLY THE OUTPUT'S BOOLEANITY IS IMPLIED so no separate booleanity row is needed. With s = x+y+z: XOR3 is (2s-3)*(2o-s) = -s; MAJ3 is (2s-3)*(4o-s) = s; CH (o = e ? f : g) is e*(f-g) = o-g; KECCAK CHI (o = a xor (NOT b and c)) is (-3+2a-2b+2c)*(8o+5-10a-2b+2c) = -15+12a. Characteristic conditions: XOR3/MAJ3 need char != 2,3; chi needs char != 2,3,5; Ch needs nothing. The whole Lean obligation is a case split on the 8 cube points plus a unit-inverse argument showing the multiplier A never vanishes (2s-3 lies in {-3,-1,1,3}; chi's A lies in {-5,-3,-1,1}) — no range bounds, no field-size condition. CENSUS: EXACTLY 192 OF THE 256 THREE-INPUT BOOLEAN FUNCTIONS ARE ONE-ROW PINNABLE (75%), and the blocked 64 have a clean characterisation — f is blocked iff c_{123} != 0 AND (c_{23}, c_{13}, c_{12}) all lie in {0, -c_{123}}. The blocked set is the 8 point-indicators and their complements, AND3/OR3/NAND3/NOR3, and the weight-{1,3,5,7} functions with |c_{123}| = 1. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MESSAGE SCHEDULE: XOR4 and XOR5 are blocked, so the sigma rotations CANNOT be widened past three inputs in one row — see the keccak entry for the proof that this is not a search failure but an impossibility.

MEASURED r-VERSUS-m SURVEY OF THE 145470 SEED — THE WHOLE TREE IS AT THE STRUCTURAL FLOOR EXCEPT ONE BLOCK, AND THAT BLOCK IS THE PADDING CHECK. Using the rows >= allocations theorem (every row introduces at most one witness, so the triangular pattern r = m is the floor), I extracted every `def X : Count := <a, c>` in Solution/SHA256 and ranked by c - a. RESULT: checkPad7Cost is <0, 2167>, checkPad7SparseCost <0, 2063> and checkPad7SparseUncheckedCost <0, 2062> — ZERO ALLOCATIONS AND ~2062 ROWS — while the NEXT LARGEST GAP IN THE ENTIRE TREE IS 88 (compressBlock1SparseD at 14785/14873). Everything else — the compress blocks, both message schedules, all the per-lane gadgets — sits within 88 of r = m, i.e. essentially at the floor. So ~2062 rows, 1.4% of the 145470 total, live in a single pure-ASSERTION block that allocates nothing. THE CAVEAT THAT MUST BE STATED: the Krull bound is about rows needed to DETERMINE witnesses, and a pure assertion block determines none, so this is NOT a proof that 2062 is above ITS floor — it is the observation that this is the one place in the tree whose row count is not explained by witness-pinning, hence the only place a redundancy argument could bite. THE RIGHT TOOL IS THE ROW-DELETION CRITERION, and this is exactly its best case: expand each of the 2062 rows into its quadratic-monomial coefficient vector plus linear part, solve sum_k lambda_k Q_k[i,j] = 0 by plain Gaussian elimination, and either delete rows with lambda_k != 0 or harvest a free linear constraint. Measured yield elsewhere is ~0% on hand-tight circuits but 20%+ on mechanically generated ones — and a 2062-row all-assertion padding predicate is far more likely to be the latter. ALSO RECORDED SO NO SLOT IS WASTED: the one-row gadgets are ALREADY IN THIS TREE — ch32Cost, and32Cost and lowerSigma0Cost are all <32, 32>, i.e. one row and one allocation per bit — so do NOT port XOR3/Maj/Ch from the verified gadget set, they are landed.

*** SUPERSEDED — THE CAUSE WAS A HARNESS BUG IN OUR OWN LOOP, NOT THE MATHEMATICS, AND IT IS NOW FIXED. Nineteen consecutive sha256 submissions failed, and the reason was that tick.py extracted every job's tarball into a REUSED out/<slug> directory that was never cleaned, then submitted glob('*.lean') over it — i.e. THE UNION of the job's tree with every previous job's leftovers. MEASURED: the last sha256 job's own tarball held 203 .lean files, 246 were on disk and submitted, 43 were stale, and the union contained 119 DUPLICATE FULLY-QUALIFIED DECLARATIONS (for example Solution.SHA256.MessageScheduleSparse.circuit46 declared in both MessageScheduleSparse.lean and MessageScheduleSparseSoundness.lean), which is a hard Lean build error. THE LEFTOVER COUNT TRACKED THE FAILURE RATE EXACTLY ACROSS SLUGS: fixed-base carried 1 leftover and verifies routinely, scalar-mul carried 6 and verifies, sha256 carried 43 and never verified once. WORSE, THE IMPROVEMENT WAS NEVER REAL: parse_cost globbed every .lean and took the first `def allocations`, so it read 72207/72789 off a LEFTOVER CostSparseMain.lean rather than from the job's own tree — which is why eleven jobs 'independently converged' on exactly that ledger and why redirecting them changed nothing (the trees did change; the reported number did not). The last job's actual tarball declared 72445/73025 = 145,470, EQUAL TO THE RECORD, so the `score >= best` guard should have suppressed the submission entirely. FIXED: tick.py now wipes out/<slug> before extracting (preserving submitted-*.tar.gz), and parse_cost reads Main.lean and at most one level of re-export instead of globbing. Verified after the fix: sha256 now parses as 145,470. The contaminated salvage/sha256-hash (225 files) was reseeded from records/sha256-hash (201). THE HONEST REMAINING GAP: nineteen submissions tested the harness, NOT the mathematics, so nothing is yet known about whether the intended improvement's proofs close. *** ORIGINAL ENTRY, RETAINED FOR THE MEASUREMENTS: NINE FAILED ATTEMPTS IN ONE DAY ACROSS THREE DISTINCT LEDGERS, ZERO VERIFIED — THE OBSTACLE IS PROOF CLOSURE ON THIS SEED, NOT ONE BAD DESIGN. Measured from state_subs: seven submissions claimed EXACTLY 144999 at EXACTLY 72208 allocations / 72791 constraints (10:23, 10:44, 14:08, 15:10, 17:09, 18:58 and one more), one claimed 144990, and one claimed 144996 — nine in total between 10:23 and 20:18, from separate jobs, EVERY ONE FAILED. All are GENUINE failures, checked through /api/agent/v1/submissions/<id> which distinguishes status 'timeout' from 'failed' where the plain endpoint flattens both. THE THREE-LEDGER SPREAD IS WHAT MATTERS: when only the 144999 ledger was failing it was reasonable to suspect one design; now that 144990 and 144996 fail too, the common factor is the SEED and the proof burden, not the particular lever. FOR CONTRAST, THIS CHALLENGE IS NOT INHERENTLY STUCK — the leaderboard shows our own successful chain 145479 -> 145478 (tekkac) -> 145471 -> 145470, so improvements HAVE closed here before. What is new is that from the 145470 seed every attempted improvement fails to prove. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: it does NOT establish that 144999 or any other score is unreachable — an identical cost ledger is not identical work, and this corpus was burned once by calling a design dead after a single failure that later verified. WHAT TO DO: stop re-deriving whatever -471 lever jobs keep converging on, and go at the ONE place the r-versus-m survey found slack — checkPad7SparseUnchecked at <0, 2062>, zero allocations and 2062 rows, the only block in this circuit whose row count is not explained by witness-pinning, with everything else within 88 of the rows-equals-allocations floor. The row-deletion criterion is built for exactly that shape. AND PREFER LEVERS WHOSE PROOF OBLIGATION IS KNOWN IN ADVANCE: today the two items that DID land on other challenges were both derived-width numeral changes carrying NO soundness obligation, and they predicted to within 1.3%. *** PARTIAL RETRACTION — THE UNION WAS REAL, BUT 'DUPLICATE FULLY-QUALIFIED DECLARATIONS' IS NOT THE MECHANISM AND THAT COUNT IS NOT DIAGNOSTIC. I attributed the build failure to 119 duplicate declarations produced by the union. CONTROL RUN THAT KILLS IT: by the same measure the VERIFIED 145,470 RECORD TREE CARRIES 245 DUPLICATES across 202 files, and a later job's clean 204-file tree carries exactly 245 as well. A metric that reads the same on a tree that verified and a tree that failed discriminates nothing — the repeated names are benign (re-statements across files that are never imported together, and regex over-matching on section-scoped declarations). WHAT SURVIVES: the union itself was measured and real (246 files shipped against 203 in the job's tarball, 43 stale), the leftover count tracked the failure rate across slugs exactly, and wiping out/<slug> before extraction was the right fix. WHAT DOES NOT: any claim that duplicate declarations were the proximate build error. THE HONEST STATE IS THAT THE PROXIMATE ERROR WAS NEVER OBSERVED — we never held a failing tree and a build log at the same time. DO NOT USE DUPLICATE-DECLARATION COUNTS AS A HEALTH CHECK ON A LEAN TREE.

CORRECTING MY OWN DIAGNOSIS OF THE 19 FAILED SHA-256 JOBS — I HAD THE TWO FILES BACKWARDS, THOUGH THE OPERATIVE CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED. I recorded that parse_cost had read 72207/72789 off a 'leftover CostSparseMain.lean' and that the -474 was therefore never real. VERIFIED AGAINST THE RECORD TREE: records/sha256-hash/Main.lean is a SINGLE IMPORT LINE, `import Solution.SHA256.MainSparse`, and MainSparse.lean:26-27 declares allocations := 72445, constraints := 73025 = 145,470. So in each job tree MainSparse.lean at 72445/73025 was THE SEED'S FILE and CostSparseMain.lean at 72207/72789 was THE JOB'S OWN NEW FILE — the opposite of what I said. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES INTACT AND IS THE POINT: the job proved a 144,996 configuration in CostSparseMain but NEVER WIRED IT INTO THE EXPORTED allocations/constraints, so every one of those submissions would have SCORED 145,470 REGARDLESS of the union bug. All 19 sit at status `pending` and NONE was ever verified, so no figure among 144990 / 144996 / 144999 is confirmed by the judge — they are local parse_cost readings and parse_cost was itself globbing every .lean at the time.
