THE SIGMA LINE IS CLOSED BY AN EXACT CRITERION, AND THE REASON IS A NUMBER-THEORETIC PROPERTY OF SHA-256'S ROTATION CONSTANTS — STOP ATTACKING IT. Complete single-row taxonomy, derived from A*B + C = 0 by substituting the honest z = T(x): FORM I (a_z b_z = 0) is T*M = P*Q + L, and crucially P IS FORCED INTO span{M, 1} — THE MULTIPLIER IS ONE FACTOR OF THE PRODUCT, a constraint that pure rank arguments miss; FORM II (a_z b_z != 0) is T^2 + U*T = P*Q + L, the decoy-root form. Both reduce to exact linear algebra, and the controls reproduce every shipped gadget (Xor3 with M = x1 - x0, Maj32, Ch32, PackedCh, PackedMaj). THE CRITERION: A LAMBDA-PACKED PAIR OF GATE LANES ADMITS A ROW IFF THE TWO LANES SHARE AT LEAST TWO INPUT BITS. Verified positively — 2-shared XOR3 DOES pack, with M = x2 - x1, checked on all 16 cube points. Verified negatively and more strongly: 1-shared and 0-shared XOR3 have an EMPTY multiplier space AND an unsolvable form II, which means NO ROW CAN EVEN MENTION SUCH A z — that closes multi-row schemes too, not just the single-row ones. AND SHA-256 NEVER QUALIFIES BECAUSE ALL FOUR ROTATION TRIPLES ARE SIDON SETS: Sigma0 {2,13,22}, Sigma1 {6,11,25}, sigma0 {7,18,3} and sigma1 {17,19,10} each have pairwise-distinct differences mod 32. Machine-swept over every lane pair that actually meets on a common word — Sigma0 x Sigma0, Sigma1 x Sigma1, sigma0 x sigma0, sigma1 x sigma1, and sigma0 x sigma1 on W[j] which meet 13 steps apart — MAX SHARED IS 1, ALWAYS. (Sigma0 x sigma0 does reach 2, but those act on state words versus schedule words and never meet.) THIS IS A PROPERTY OF THE CONSTANT CHOICE, NOT A MISSING GADGET.

THE SHA-256 LEDGER IS 2 x (WITNESS COUNT) + 580, SO THE ONLY LEVER IS FEWER WITNESSES. Rows = allocations + 580 exactly, from Lean Count literals. Breakdown: XOR3 sigma/Sigma lanes at 2 units/bit and UNPACKABLE ~62,000 (43%); bit decompositions at 2 units/bit and proved optimal ~58,000 (40%); packed Ch + Maj at 1 unit/bit = 20,480 (14%); carries, flags, high-bit pairs and digest ~4,300 (3%). Key literals: sha256RoundPairCost <328,330> = 4x64 sigma + 4x64 decomposition + 64 Ch + 64 Maj + 18 adders; scheduleStepCost <91,92> = 29 sigma0 + 22 sigma1 xor3 + 7 packed xor2 + 32 W bits + 1 carry. PER ROUND THE FLOOR IS 32 Sigma0 + 32 Sigma1 (2/bit, unpackable) + 32 Ch + 32 Maj (1/bit, packed) + 64 decomposition bits (2/bit, proved optimal) + 9 adder units = 329, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT SHIPS. THE <0,2062> PADDING OUTLIER IS AN ACCOUNTING ARTIFACT, NOT SLACK: checkPad7SparseUncheckedCost's 1673 allocations are hoisted to top level and are SCHEDULE INPUT BITS (239 bytes x 7 = the sigma0 inputs of W[1..15] across 4 blocks) sitting at the proved 2/bit floor; only 119 high-bit pairs + 16 SparseW0 rows are genuinely extra. Field headroom exists but is not spendable: lambda = 2^40, lane payload bound 2^35, baseLambda_sep needs p > 2^76 against BN254's r ~ 2^253.6, so about 3x — and every scheme that would spend it is refuted below.

ELEVEN SHA-256 IDEAS PRICED AND REFUTED WITH EXACT LINEAR ALGEBRA — DO NOT RE-PROPOSE ANY OF THEM. (a) SIGMA AS MAJORITY (Sigma0 = X + Y + Z - 2*maj, then pack maj 2:1), which would have been worth 19,840 (13.6%) — THE MOST expensive refutation here: a maj-pair with one shared input HAS a multiplier, M = 1 - 2*x2, but quad(T*M) is NOT in the pencil m_i q_j + m_j q_i; the 0-shared case has no multiplier at all. (b) Ch-pair plus lambda^2 * Maj-pair in one 8-variable witness, 9,920: no affine multiplier drops the degree. (c) 3-deep Ch chain, 3,413: form I's multiplier fails the pencil test and form II is unsolvable. (d) 3-deep Maj chain, 3,413: same, and additionally 4 piecewise-affine cells cannot be covered by 2 rows — an x_0-coefficient contradiction arises in all three pairings. (e) xor3 + lambda*xor2, xor3 + lambda*ch, xor3 + lambda*maj, ch + lambda*maj, ~2,600 each: multiplier space empty. THE ONE GENUINELY OPEN SPACE IN SHA-256, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE LEFT — ROWS WHOSE COEFFICIENTS DRAW ON OTHER ALLOCATED WITNESSES. Every analysis so far, mine and the tree's own audit sections, restricts A, B and C to be affine in the INPUT BITS. The cost model forbids no such thing: it forbids two products, and a row may legally be affine in ANY ALLOCATED WITNESS — other sigma lanes, Ch/Maj outputs, carry bits. That is a strictly larger space and NOTHING IN THE TREE CLOSES IT. The tree already exploits a weak form of it exactly once, and it was the single biggest win in the file: PackedMaj.Spec IS ONLY THE ROW, with FusedAAdder recovering the exact value downstream via PackedMajOne.packed_exact, taking Maj from <32,64> to <32,32> — worth 4,960. FORMULATION TO DECIDE: T*M = P*Q + L with M, Q, L in V = span{1, bits, PRIOR WITNESSES} and P in span{M, 1}. PRIZE: a sigma-lane pair at 1 allocation + 2 rows is about 15,000 (10%); at 1 allocation + 1 row it is about 30,000. Confidence low, but it is the only unexplored space and the existing decision-procedure tooling extends to it directly. THE GENERAL LESSON IS WORTH MORE THAN THE SPECIFIC PRIZE: WHEN A SEARCH COMES BACK EMPTY, CHECK WHETHER THE SEARCH SPACE WAS THE MODEL'S OR AN ASSUMPTION YOU IMPORTED. 'Affine in the input bits' was never a rule of this cost model.

A LEVER FROM THE GF(2) SISTER CHALLENGE THAT APPLIES VERBATIM HERE, AND THE TARGET SHAPE IS ALREADY IN THIS TREE. Cost.lean:50-53 declares sigmaCost = <32,32>, lowerSigma0Cost = <32,32> and lowerSigma1Cost = <32,32>, each being 32 XOR3 lanes at <1,1> (Cost.lean:170 proves CostIs (subcircuit Xor3.circuit b) sigmaCost). THE IDENTITY, VERIFIED OVER 20,000 RANDOM WORDS FOR ALL FOUR MAPS: Sigma0(a) = rotr2 + rotr13 + rotr22 - 2*SUM_{j=0}^{30} 2^j maj(a_{j+2}, a_{j+13}, a_{j+22}) (mod 2^32). The exact-over-Z version needs j up to 31, but the j=31 term of the CARRY word enters with a factor of 2, so its weight is 2^32 AND IT VANISHES MOD 2^32. Exactly one lane is droppable — the j=30 term has weight 2^31 and is live. MAJ3 is single-row native with implied booleanity ((2s-3)(4o-s) = s), so every surviving lane is still <1,1>: 32 lanes become 31, i.e. sigmaCost <32,32> -> <31,31>, -2 SCORE PER SIGMA INSTANCE. THIS IS SOUND HERE BECAUSE EVERY CONSUMER TAKES THE WORD, NOT THE BITS — ComputablePairB1.lean:113 reads (newE + sigma + Maj a b c + (2^32-1-d) + 1), a mod-2^32 sum — and because a's bits are already decomposed for Ch and Maj, so the rotations are free affine reads either way. SITE COUNT: roundCost (Cost.lean:63) charges 2 * sigmaCost per round and the schedule charges 2 lower sigmas per step, so on a 64-round 48-step block that is 224 instances = -448 per compression block; COUNT THE ACTUAL INSTANCES RATHER THAN TRUSTING THAT ARITHMETIC. THE ONE CHECK THAT COULD HALVE IT, TEN MINUTES, DO IT BEFORE WRITING ANYTHING: the addend handed to each reduction becomes Sigma0 + 2^32*maj_31 in [0, 2^33), so every fused reduction's carry range grows by one — T1 has <=5 addends (carry [0,4] -> [0,5]) and the a' adder has 3 (carry [0,2] -> [0,3]). Both SHOULD stay inside their existing carry-bit widths, but if any carry sits exactly on a power-of-two boundary in Cost.lean, one extra witness there cancels a round's saving. NOTE THIS IS NOT THE REFUTED IDEA: sigma-as-majority followed by 2:1 maj packing is dead; this is truncation, a different use of the same identity, and nothing refutes it.

CALIBRATION AGAINST EVERY PUBLIC PLAIN-R1CS KECCAK — WE ARE ALREADY 1.6x BETTER THAN THE BEST OF THEM. circom keccak-circom/keccak256-circom: about 150848 constraints, because circomlib's XOR3 costs 2 constraints per bit (mid <== b*c; out <== a*(1-2b-2c+4mid)+b+c-2mid) and its chi costs 3. bkomuves/hash-circuits: about 146000 constraints for the permutation. The widely quoted naive breakdown is 7744/round = 185856. Our record is 92160 constraints, and the entire gap is the 1-row XOR3 and 1-row chi gadgets. Anything reported faster than this is out of scope: Keccacheck (eprint 2025/1764) quotes '<4k constraints per instance' but that is the amortised cost of a Groth16 wrapper around a sum-check/GKR proof with random challenges and MLE commitments, not an R1CS encoding; Polyhedra's binary GKR is GKR+sum-check; Binius makes XOR free only by moving to binary tower fields with a different commitment scheme; zkEVM Keccak circuits (Scroll/Polygon/halo2 spread tables) are entirely lookup-based.

ALTERNATIVE STATE REPRESENTATIONS — ALL MEASURED, ALL WORSE (do not spend a slot re-deriving these). (a) PACKED BASE-8 DIGITS, the lookup-free analogue of the 'spread' trick: packing a lane as sum_i 8^i * A[i] is free, and summing 5 lanes gives digit values in [0,5] with no carries — but extracting each parity bit needs C and a quotient q in {0,1,2}, costing 128 allocations + 193 constraints per column-lane = score 321 against the current 256. Worse, because the 1-row XOR3 already handles its carry implicitly and there is no lookup-free way to range-check the digits more cheaply. (b) +/-1 FOURIER BASIS (b -> (-1)^b, XOR becomes multiplication): 3-input parity costs 2 rows instead of 1, 5-input 4 instead of 2 — uniformly about 2x worse, because the boolean encoding is exactly what lets L1/L2/M exploit booleanity. (c) AND-FIRST restructuring (materialise the 1600 chi ANDs and keep everything else GF(2)-linear): 6400 rows/round, because next-state bits become 33-term XORs.

CHI IS AT A PROVEN FLOOR, NOT JUST AN OBSERVED ONE: MC(chi5) = 5 is SAT-PROVED MINIMAL (Ko Stoffelen, 'Optimizing S-box Implementations for Several Criteria using SAT Solvers', FSE 2016, Table 1 — a proven minimum, not an upper bound; same table gives Ascon 5, ICEPOLE 6). Our chi costs 1600 rows/round = 5 rows per 5-bit S-box = exactly that floor, so NO better S-box decomposition exists. Caveat kept honest: a row is strictly more powerful than a GF(2) AND gate (XOR3 is 1 row and 0 ANDs), so MC is a heuristic floor for rows rather than a theorem — but here it is tight. By contrast MC(theta) = 0: every one of theta's 2240 rows/round is pure overhead from GF(2)-linearity not being F_p-linear.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER ARGUMENT OF MINE — 'R1CS ROWS ARE FACTORABLE QUADRICS SO ONE EQUATION CANNOT PIN TWO VARIABLES' IS TRUE PER ROW BUT FALSE ACROSS ROWS. The SPAN of two rows' quadratic parts need not split. Explicit counterexample, verified for p = 5,7,11,13,17,19,23,29,31,101,127: row 1 (z1+z2)(z1-z2) = z3 gives z1^2 - z2^2 = z3; row 2 ((d-1)*z2)*z2 = z3 gives (d-1)z2^2 = z3; together z1^2 = d*z2^2 with d a NON-RESIDUE forces z1 = z2 = z3 = 0 uniquely. So TWO rank-1 rows DO pin THREE unknowns. BN254 GOTCHA: p = 1 mod 4, so -1 IS a quadratic residue and x^2 + y^2 = 0 has nontrivial solutions — the least non-residue is 5, so use d in {5,7,10,11,14,15,17,19}. WHY IT STILL DOES NOT HELP, which is the useful part: Chevalley-Warning bounds the prize — r degree-2 rows in m unknowns with sum of degrees < m cannot have exactly one solution, so r >= ceil(m/2) and AT MOST A FACTOR 2 is ever available. And empirically it is not even that: over 1,140,029 sampled affine 3-cubes with uniquely-solvable fibers, two rows never pinned more than ONE affinely-independent function. Structurally, uniqueness with r < m forces the solution to be a singular point, the elimination gives a norm equation whose constant must vanish, and that forces the pinned values to be AFFINE in the inputs — i.e. values that were free anyway. CONCLUSION UNCHANGED, REASONING FIXED: stop looking for sub-one-row-per-non-affine-witness.

*** SUPERSEDED — the fusion question below is now CLOSED BY PROOF via the single-witness row criterion; read that entry first, and note it CORRECTS the claim that partial b0-fusion 'survives the lemma but is useless' (it does not exist at all). *** FUSING THETA INTO CHI IS IMPOSSIBLE — the open question from an earlier pass is now CLOSED, by a RESTRICTION LEMMA. Lemma: if L1 - (z + L2)*M = 0 encodes f on the boolean cube with L1,L2,M affine and M non-vanishing, then fixing any subset of the inputs to constants gives affine restrictions L1',L2',M' with M' still non-vanishing, encoding f on the subcube. So SINGLE-ROW ENCODABILITY IS CLOSED UNDER SUBCUBE RESTRICTION. Application: the attractive fusion is to skip materialising the 1600 theta outputs and feed chi its pre-XOR inputs, z = chi(a0+d0, a1+d1, a2+d2) = b0 + b2 + b1*b2, which would cost 2560 rows/round (122880 total). Restrict a1 = d1 = 0: then b1 = 0 and f becomes a0 + d0 + a2 + d2, a 4-INPUT XOR of four free variables — which we proved by SMT has no single-row encoding. Contradiction, so the fused gate does not exist. GENERALISATION WORTH REMEMBERING: any single-row gadget whose function restricts on some subcube to a XOR of 4 or more free variables is impossible. Partial fusion (absorbing one D bit into chi's b0 slot only) survives the lemma but is useless, because every theta output bit is consumed in all three chi roles across the five S-boxes of its row and must be materialised anyway.

PROVED WITH SMT — THE SINGLE-ROW XOR STOPS AT 3 INPUTS (cvc5 QF_FF over the circom prime, harness validated against the known 3-input row before trusting the negative results). Question asked: does an n-input XOR admit ONE rank-1 row that pins z uniquely, i.e. L1 - (z + L2)*M = 0 with L1, L2, M affine in the boolean inputs and M non-vanishing on the cube? (This is the fully general single-row shape: a row quadratic in z has two roots and cannot pin z, so z must appear linearly, giving z*M = N with M affine non-vanishing.) RESULTS: n=2 SAT, n=3 SAT, n=4 UNSAT, n=5 UNSAT. CONSEQUENCES FOR KECCAK: Xor5Lane = 2 x Xor3Lane at 128/128 is OPTIMAL — there is no single-row 5-input parity to find, so ThetaC's 640 per round cannot be shaved this way; and ThetaXor (1600) and ChiLane (1600) are already at 1 row per bit, the single-row minimum. The whole 3840-per-round record is therefore a LOCAL OPTIMUM of the 'materialize every state bit with single-row gadgets' strategy. Beating 184320 needs a STRUCTURAL change, not a better gadget. The concrete open question: theta+chi together currently cost 2 rows per output bit (ThetaXor 1600 + Chi 1600 for 1600 outputs) — is there a FUSED gadget computing chi(A'_i, A'_i+1, A'_i+2), where each A' is itself a 3-input XOR of materialized bits, in FEWER than 2 rows per output bit? That is 9 boolean inputs; given 4-input parity is already impossible in one row, a 1-row fusion is out, so the target is a 2-row-for-two-outputs (or similar amortized) encoding.

COST DIAGNOSIS (derived — verify before trusting): the record 184320 = 1600 bits x 24 rounds x 4.8. The sibling GF(2) challenge does the SAME permutation shape at 2.0 per bit-round (1 allocation + 1 constraint = just chi's product). The whole 2.8/bit gap is XOR OVERHEAD: over the circom prime a XOR b = a + b - 2ab costs a MULTIPLICATION, whereas over GF(2) it is free addition. So the entire remaining win on this challenge is in how XOR is encoded — not in chi, whose multiplicative complexity is already minimal (5 per 5-bit row, SAT-proven).

SUM-THEN-EXTRACT-PARITY for wide XORs (the main lever): to XOR k bits over a large prime field, do NOT chain k-1 pairwise a+b-2ab products. Instead form S = b_1 + ... + b_k as a FREE affine combination (zero constraints), then extract S mod 2 by decomposing S into ceil(log2(k+1)) bits with one linear equation S = 2q + r; the parity bit r IS the XOR. Cost ~log2(k) allocations + booleanity instead of (k-1) multiplications. theta XORs 5 lane bits plus a rotated column parity (k~5-11), where log2 beats linear decisively — this is how theta becomes near-free in a NON-binary field.

FOLD BOOLEANITY INTO THE PRODUCT: if c = a*b with a,b already known boolean, c is automatically boolean — do NOT emit a separate c(c-1)=0 row. Likewise the parity bit from a sum-decomposition is forced boolean by the range argument. Every redundant booleanity row is a pure loss at 1 constraint each, and at 38400 chi outputs that is 38400 constraints if repeated.

DO-NOT-TRY, AND IT IS A TEMPTING ONE: XOR-GATE / SHORTEST-LINEAR-PROGRAM MINIMIZATION BUYS EXACTLY ZERO HERE. There is a large and still-active literature on minimizing the number of 2-input XOR gates needed to evaluate an F2-LINEAR MAP — the Shortest Linear Program problem: Boyar-Peralta, Tan-Peyrin (TCHES'20) adding randomization and 3-input XOR gates, the 'Superior Boyar-Peralta' (SBP) depth-aware heuristic, 'Improved Heuristics for Low-Latency Implementations of Linear Layers', and eprint 2025/1493 which revisits BP and cuts the AES linear layer from 91 to 89 g-XOR. Keccak's theta (and rho/pi, and SHA-256's Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1) are exactly such linear maps, so this looks like the obvious attack on the biggest remaining slack. IT IS NOT, BECAUSE AN XOR GATE COSTS NOTHING IN EITHER OF OUR COST MODELS. In native R1CS an affine combination lives inside the A/B/C vectors of a row and is free. In the GF(2) challenges the harness restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A and B AFFINE, so an arbitrary XOR-combination is free inside a multiplicand. Halving the XOR count of theta changes the score by ZERO. WHAT THETA'S 2240 ROWS PER ROUND ACTUALLY PAY FOR IS *MATERIALIZATION*, NOT XOR COUNT: a value costs an allocation exactly when it must appear as a BARE WITNESS VARIABLE — because it is a circuit output, or because its consumer needs a variable rather than an affine form. THEREFORE THE ONLY QUESTION WORTH ASKING IS: for each currently-materialized intermediate, WHO CONSUMES IT, and can that consumer take an affine form instead? CONJUGATE-CIPHER CROSS-ROUND AMORTISATION: THE LINEAR CASE IS CLOSED, ONLY A NONLINEAR CONJUGATOR REMAINS OPEN. For the conjugated round C.F.C^-1 to still cost 1600 for chi, C must NORMALISE the chi layer (320 disjoint chi_5). The linear maps that do are generated by cyclic shifts within each 5-row and permutations of the rows — ALL PERMUTATION MATRICES — and conjugating the linear layer by a permutation is pure relabelling, leaving the row count identical. Any C not preserving the S-box structure turns chi into a generic 1600-output quadratic map and destroys the 1-row-per-bit gadget. Conjugating by L or by chi themselves merely rotates the round word cyclically and is cost-invariant. So the mechanism needs a genuinely NONLINEAR C whose own cost is paid twice over 1600 bits. Verified linear-algebra facts about L = rhoPi o theta, computed locally: rank(L) = 1600, rank(L - I) = 1598, rank(theta - I) = 319, L fixes the all-ones vector, dim ker(L^d - I) = 2d for d = 2,4,8,16 (a two-cycle permutation signature) — tempting but not exploitable for the reason above.

LAMBDA-PACKING AND THE TWO-ROOT DECOY DO NOT TRANSFER TO KECCAK, BECAUSE THIS CIRCUIT HAS NO BOUNDED-ARITHMETIC CONSUMER ANYWHERE. Both SHA-256 record tricks depend on the packed word being consumed ADDITIVELY by a modular adder, which splits the lambda slots for free and rejects the decoy at zero cost. In Keccak every consumer is a boolean gadget whose soundness needs each input as an IsBool value: from z = f_A + lambda*f_B neither half is an affine form, so a packed witness cannot feed a downstream Xor3Lane or ChiLane row (whose R1CS certificate requires AffineW inputs and whose soundness requires IsBool inputs). Any packing must be undone at cost, and a decoy root would simply satisfy the next row at a different value — UNSOUND rather than merely expensive. This does not formally close packing (a redesigned consumer reading the packed form directly is conceivable) but it is the precondition every packing proposal must answer first.

THE SINGLE-WITNESS ROW CRITERION — A CLOSED-FORM TEST THAT DECIDES, FOR ANY BOOLEAN FUNCTION AND ANY NUMBER OF ROWS, WHETHER ONE FRESH WITNESS SUFFICES. USE IT BEFORE PROPOSING ANY NEW GADGET ON ANY R1CS CHALLENGE — it is one linear-algebra solve and it is exact. DERIVATION (proved): a row is Q + A*B with Q,A,B affine in (inputs x, z). Put gamma(x) = R(x,0) and g(x) = R(x,1) - R(x,0) = q_z + a_z*b(x) + b_z*a(x) + a_z*b_z. Then (i) g is AFFINE IN x (+-1-Fourier degree <= 1) — the load-bearing constraint, which the earlier SMT formulation never exploited; (ii) completeness forces gamma = -f*g with deg gamma <= 2, hence deg(F*g) <= 2 where F = 1-2f; (iii) uniqueness at x needs some row's g(x) != 0, because R_i(x, 1-f(x)) = g_i(x)*F(x). THEREFORE z IS PINNABLE BY ANY NUMBER OF ROWS WITH ONE FRESH WITNESS IFF THE LINEAR SPACE G_f = {g affine : deg(F*g) <= 2} HAS NO COMMON ZERO ON THE CUBE. VALIDATED: exhaustive n=3 gives 192/256, reproducing the cvc5 QF_FF census in _common EXACTLY by an independent method, and both record gadgets land in the space (ChiLane's multiplier 4a+b+c-3 is exactly -g). RESULTS, exact rational arithmetic: XOR_n has dim G = 0 for ALL n >= 4 (general proof: F = u_1...u_n and deg g <= 1 give deg(F*g) >= n-1 > 2), so an n-input parity with n >= 4 CANNOT be pinned by one witness AT ANY ROW COUNT, not merely by one row. THE FULL THETA+CHI FUSION chi(b0,b1,b2) with each b_j a 3-XOR (9 inputs) has dim G = 0, because F's degree-9 Fourier term can only pair with |S| <= 1 and forces g = 0 — IMPOSSIBLE AT ANY ROW COUNT, strictly stronger than the restriction-lemma argument. PARTIAL FUSION IS ALSO IMPOSSIBLE, NOT MERELY USELESS: absorbing a single 2-XOR into chi's b0 slot gives dim G = 0; into b1 or b2 gives dim G != 0 but G has common zeros so z is not pinned; any 3-XOR into any slot, and the output-side form z = chi(a,b,c) XOR e, all give dim G = 0. NEW CENSUS AT n=4: 950/65536 functions certifiable, 264 essentially 4-ary — a genuine 4-input native gate library EXISTS — but every one has +-1-Fourier degree of F at most 3, while every keccak-relevant 4-input function (4-XOR, chi-plus-one-XOR) has degree >= 4. So no wider gate helps.

THE ONE CONCRETE SAVING THAT EXISTED HERE IS PROVED IMPOSSIBLE, AND Xor5Lane IS NOW PROVED OPTIMAL. THE LEVER, worth stating because it is the natural thing to try: score is allocations + constraints and a plain-R1CS row may have NO fresh witness, so a 5-input parity witnessing ONLY C and adding TWO assertion rows would cost 1 alloc + 2 constr = 3 per bit against Xor5Lane's 2 + 2 = 4 per bit — 320 C bits per round, -320/round, -7680 total, 184320 -> 176640 AND A LEADERBOARD. IT DOES NOT EXIST: by the single-witness row criterion XOR_n for n >= 4 has dim G = 0, so a 5-input parity cannot be pinned with one materialised witness at any row count. Two witnesses then force >= 2 rows by rank, so Xor5Lane's 128/128 (t = XOR3(a,b,c) then C = XOR3(t,d,e), Xor5Lane.lean.txt:21-23) IS THE EXACT OPTIMUM for an isolated 5-XOR. The 320 C bits of a round are parities of PAIRWISE-DISJOINT variable sets (column x, slice z), each needing ceil(4/2) = 2 three-input-XOR gates with no cross-column sharing possible, and each C is reused by exactly 2 D's — so ThetaC's 640/round is tight as a GF(2) 3-XOR addition chain (MODELLED for the no-cross-sharing step, a standard SLP direct-sum argument rather than a theorem).

MATERIALISATION CENSUS OF THE 184320 RECORD, AND THE PREMISE THAT KEEPS GETTING RE-PROPOSED AND IS FALSE. Per round the record materialises exactly four families and EVERY ONE IS READ: (a) 320 Xor5Lane intermediates t, read once each by the second Xor3Lane row of the same Xor5Lane (Xor5Lane.lean.txt:22-23); (b) 320 column parities C, read TEN times each by ThetaXor's Xor3Lane rows (ThetaXor.lean.txt:76 — lanes with x = x'+1 and x = x'-1, five lanes each); (c) 1600 theta outputs A', read THREE times each by ChiLane rows in the a/b/c roles (Chi.lean.txt:182-184, chiSource1/chiSource2 at BitwiseOps.lean.txt:61-66); (d) 1600 chi outputs, read by the next round's ThetaC and ThetaXor, or in round 23 exported through the free affine iotaWire. THERE IS NOT ONE VALUE MATERIALISED ONLY SO AN EQUATION CAN BE CHECKED AGAINST IT, so the secp 'assertion, not value' mechanism has NO SITE HERE: every materialised value is a boolean MULTIPLICAND SLOT of at least one downstream row, and that slot syntactically demands an affine form whose VALUE is a bit. NOW THE FALSE PREMISE, WHICH I PROPOSED MYSELF AND WHICH IS WORTH INOCULATING AGAINST: 'the theta output is A + C[x-1] + rot C[x+1], which is AFFINE in the state and the parities, so delete the 1600 theta materialisations.' IT IS GF(2)-AFFINE, NOT F_p-AFFINE, AND THE COST MODEL IS F_p. With bits encoded as field elements 0/1, A + Cl + Cr is a syntactically Affine EXPRESSION whose VALUE is the integer sum in {0,1,2,3}, not the XOR. The 1600 ThetaXor rows exist PRECISELY to convert the free affine sum into the non-affine XOR value; same for the 640 parities, a 5-XOR being a sum mod 2 of degree 5. WHENEVER A PROPOSAL SAYS 'XOR IS AFFINE SO IT IS FREE', CHECK WHICH FIELD IT IS AFFINE OVER — that confusion is the whole content of this challenge's 2.4x gap to the dimension floor. RESIDUAL OPEN GAP, STATED HONESTLY: the criterion covers systems with EXACTLY ONE fresh witness; a multi-witness multi-output gadget beating 2.4 materialisations per output bit is not excluded by anything above. But chi alone is at the SAT-proved MC(chi5) = 5 floor, theta's outputs are each read multiplicatively three times, and every single-witness fusion is dead — so there is no mechanism left to build one on. Allocate no slots.

THE 184320 RECORD IS RECONSTRUCTED TO THE UNIT AND IS AT THE r = m FLOOR — THE REMAINING SLACK IS 8.3% AND IS PROVED UNREMOVABLE. Per round: 320 XOR5 (theta C) at 2 rows + 2 allocs = 4 each -> 1280; 1600 XOR3 (theta out) at 1+1 -> 3200; 1600 chi at 1+1 -> 3200; total 7680 x 24 rounds = 184320 EXACTLY. So the record already runs one-row XOR3 and one-row chi. Allocations per round are 640 + 1600 + 1600 = 3840 and rows are 3840 — r = m EXACTLY, i.e. at the structural floor where every row introduces exactly one witness. THE ONLY FAT IS THE 320 XOR5 INTERMEDIATES PER ROUND (640 score, 15360 total, 8.3%), AND IT IS UNREMOVABLE: parity of n >= 4 bits is provably not one-row — dim{A affine : deg(A * parity_n) <= 2} = 0 for n = 4,5,6,7 computed EXACTLY OVER Q, so it holds over every field, and the two-row/one-witness case-split variant dies too (Q1 = (s - z1)*par(s) on {0..5} forces a degree-2 polynomial to have three roots). XOR5 = XOR3 composed with XOR3 at 2 rows + 2 allocs is OPTIMAL. NEWLY REJECTED, DO NOT RETRY ANY OF THESE: (a) fusing theta into chi to skip allocating theta-out — dim = 0 with all three theta-XORs inlined and dim = 0 inlined on the `a` position; inlining on `b` or `c` has dim 2 but every theta-out bit occupies `a` for one chi, `b` for another and `c` for a third, so the allocation never goes away; (b) packing 2-3 theta-out bits sharing both C operands into one witness — exhaustive search over weights {1,2},{1,3},{1,4} and coefficients -3..3 finds none, and chi groups over x while theta-out groups over y with rho/pi scrambling between, so unpacking would cost more anyway; (c) materialising D (3840 vs 3200 per round, worse — confirms the existing fold); (d) allocating t = NOT b AND c and pushing chi's XOR into theta's linear layer (12800 vs 7680, much worse); (e) absorbing the column-parity recurrence C' = C xor C[x-1] xor ROT(C[x+1],1) — genuinely one gate instead of two, but rho/pi/chi intervene before the next theta so the identity never applies. TAKEN TOGETHER THIS IS A STRONG CASE THAT THE CHALLENGE IS CLOSED at 184320 up to 8.3% that is itself proved unreachable.

RECONCILING TWO 'OPTIMALITY' CLAIMS THAT LOOK CONTRADICTORY, BECAUSE GETTING THIS WRONG WOULD BLOCK REAL WORK. Claim A: Keccak's chi has MULTIPLICATIVE COMPLEXITY EXACTLY 5 over GF(2), proven by SAT-UNSAT, and the naive implementation already uses 5 AND gates — so per-S-box chi is provably optimal. Claim B: chi is realisable in ONE R1CS ROW PER OUTPUT BIT with the output's booleanity free. BOTH ARE TRUE AND THEY ARE NOT ABOUT THE SAME OBJECT. Claim A counts AND GATES IN GF(2) for the 5-bit-in/5-bit-out row map; claim B counts RANK-1 ROWS OVER F_p for ONE OUTPUT BIT, and an F_p row is not an AND gate — it is a product of two affine forms over a large field, which is strictly more expressive. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: the GF(2) multiplicative-complexity literature is the right guide for the gf2-* challenges and the WRONG guide here, and in particular DO NOT conclude from 'MC(chi) = 5' that 5 rows per chi row-map is a floor. The genuine remaining question the GF(2) analysis raises is SHARING ACROSS THE 320 PARALLEL S-BOXES OR ACROSS ROUNDS, which nothing in the literature attempts — but note our own census already showed no chi output is an F_p-affine function of the inputs and the other four outputs (rank 11 versus 10), so the within-row-map version of that sharing is closed.

OUR SEEDED TREE ALREADY BEATS THE ONLY OTHER PUBLIC IMPLEMENTATION, AND THE PER-ROUND COST IS A FLOOR FOR SINGLE-ROW ENCODINGS. Decomposition, both trees, allocations = constraints, 24 identical rounds, with rho and pi pure rewiring and iota an affine xorConst, both free: theta column parities C are 5 x 64 x 2 = 640; theta's A' = A xor ... is 25 x 64 x 1 = 1,600; chi is 25 x 64 x 1 = 1,600. Round = 3,840, x24 x2 = 184,320. thryec pays 320 more per round because it MATERIALISES D = C[x-1] xor rot(C[x+1]) before a 2-input XOR, where the leader feeds a SINGLE Xor3Lane per lane with (state[i], c[(x+4)%5], rotl 1 c[(x+1)%5]) — and since a 3-input XOR costs the same ONE ROW as a 2-input one, materialising D is pure waste, worth 24 x 320 x 2 = 15,360. Both trees carry the identical single-row 3-input XOR identity (Verified-zkEVM/clean#395): (6a + 6b - 24c) - (z + 2a + 2b + 7c)(a + b - 4c + 1) = 0, whose multiplier lies in {+-1, +-2, +-3} and never vanishes, verified over all 8 boolean assignments.

PROVED: NO SINGLE R1CS ROW CAN PIN THE XOR OF FOUR OR MORE BOOLEAN INPUTS — SO 3,840 PER ROUND IS A FLOOR FOR ANY ONE-ROW-PER-OUTPUT ENCODING. The argument, done symbolically: for a general row (A)(B) = C with A, B, C affine in the inputs and the output z, z appearing in BOTH factors gives a quadratic whose unique-root condition forces z to be AFFINE in the inputs, impossible for parity; so z sits in one factor only and z = (N - A*M)/D with D = beta*A - gamma affine. Substituting parity t = (1 - PROD u_i)/2 in +-1 coordinates u_i = 1 - 2 x_i and reducing mod u_i^2 = 1, the degree-4 monomial coefficient of t*D + A*M - N is -d_0/2 and the four degree-3 coefficients are -d_1/2 through -d_4/2, and NOTHING ELSE IN THE EXPRESSION REACHES DEGREE 3 — so all five force D = 0 identically. CONSEQUENCES: xor5Lane at 2 rows per bit is OPTIMAL and theta's C at 640 per round is a floor; xor3Lane at 1 row per bit is optimal, and n = 3 is exactly where the degree-2 terms can still be absorbed by A*M, which is why that gadget exists at all; AND THE OBVIOUS FUSION IS DEAD — folding chi and the following theta-XOR into one row gives out = (b xor (NOT c AND d)) xor C_1 xor C_2 at u-degree 5, and t*D cannot be pushed below degree 4 unless D = 0. Same for feeding an unmaterialised 3-XOR into chi's b slot. THE ONE UNCLOSED DOOR: this assumes each output bit is pinned by a single dedicated row whose only new witness is that bit. A MULTI-ROW AMORTISED ENCODING PINNING SEVERAL WITNESSES JOINTLY IS NOT COVERED and is the only place left to look.

THETA'S COST IS EXACTLY A SHORTEST-LINEAR-PROGRAM COUNT IN THE 3-INPUT-XOR BASIS, AND THIS CORPUS TOLD JOBS NOT TO LOOK. THE REFRAMING, WHICH IS THE WHOLE FINDING: a value costs a row exactly when it must be a bare bit-valued witness, and Xor3Lane pins z = a XOR b XOR c in ONE row. A gate input must be a bit-valued affine form — an already-materialised bit or a constant — so 'a+b' is NOT a legal input. Therefore theta's cost = THE MINIMUM NUMBER OF GATES IN A STRAIGHT-LINE PROGRAM OVER THE BASIS {XOR of <=3 previously-materialised bits} computing the 1600 theta outputs from the 1600 state bits, and score = 2 x gates. That is the g-XOR SLP problem of Boyar-Peralta, Tan-Peyrin TCHES'20, SBP, eprint 2025/1493. THE COST LAW: round score = 48 x (3200 + h) where h is the helper-gate count. THE RECORD DECOMPOSES EXACTLY: theta = 2,240 gates/round = 320 column-slices x (1 intermediate t + 1 parity C) + 1,600 outputs, so h = 640; round = 2,240 + 1,600 (chi) = 3,840; 48 x 3,840 = 184,320. EXTERNAL CALIBRATION, FETCHED AND READ: the Keccak team's own implementation overview 3.2 §1.3 gives '1824 XORs, 600 ANDs and 600 NOTs', i.e. 76 lane-XORs/round = theta 50 + chi 25 + iota 1, and theta's 50 lane-XORs are 3,200 two-input bit-XORs per round. THE RECORD IS THAT TEXTBOOK CIRCUIT RE-BASIS'D INTO 3-INPUT GATES, NOT AN SLP OPTIMUM. Also confirmed from the same document: §2.3's redundant state representation (materialising D) costs 640 + 320 + 1,600 = 2,560 gates/round = 199,680, bit-for-bit what thryec scores, so it is worse BY THE DESIGNERS' OWN NUMBERS; and §2.4.1 'early parity' is pure scheduling worth ZERO, since C is computed 24 times either way.

THE 'PROVED UNREMOVABLE 8.3%' CLAIM IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND SAT BEATS THE CONSTRUCTION ON THE FAITHFUL ANALOGUE. The corpus argues the 320 XOR5 intermediates per round (15,360 score) are unremovable because a 5-XOR is not one-row. THAT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT AN ISOLATED GADGET and says nothing about a global SLP re-wiring. WHAT IS ACTUALLY PROVED, exhaustively on the real w=64 index structure: a theta output is a 3-XOR of other theta outputs and raw state bits in EXACTLY 4 WAYS (the same-column siblings T[x][y][z] = T[x][y'][z] XOR A[x][y'][z] XOR A[x][y][z]); 'target = 2 targets + <=1 input' has ZERO solutions; 'target = 3 targets' has ZERO solutions. So helpers carrying column-parity content are unavoidable and each column-slice needs at least one first-partial helper — targets only ever have column-restriction weight 0, 1 or 5, so a weight-2-to-4 gate is never a target. FLOOR: theta >= 1,600 + 320 = 1,920 gates/round, SCORE >= 168,960. THE RECORD SITS 15,360 ABOVE THAT FLOOR. SAT RESULT ON THE REDUCED INSTANCE, WITH FAITHFULNESS CHECKED FIRST (for both NX=3 and NX=5 the target-to-target relation census is IDENTICAL to the real w=64 one — 4 same-column siblings, 0 others): NX=3 with 15 inputs and 15 outputs, the 2-helpers-per-column construction gives 21 gates and SAT FINDS 20 (5 helpers = 1.67 per column), model extracted and independently re-verified; the seeds-only sub-problem goes 9 -> 8. NX=5 at G=35/34/33 and seeds-only at G=15..12 were INCONCLUSIVE (still running past an hour). THE MECHANISM THE SOLVER FOUND, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: NEVER MATERIALISE A CLEAN COLUMN PARITY. Carry a RIDER bit through the helper chain so it lands as the seed target's own A-bit, and assemble the last column's parity INSIDE a target gate from a shared partial plus an already-computed target — concretely g1 = A[1][1] XOR A[1][3] XOR A[2][3] with the rider A[2][3] coming from a foreign column, through to g6 = C[0] XOR C[1] XOR A[2][3] WHICH IS ITSELF the target A'[2][3]. HONEST CAVEAT, STATED BECAUSE IT MATTERS: the 20-gate win is on the 3-column analogue, NOT on Keccak's theta. It proves the 2-helpers-per-column FAMILY is not optimal for theta-shaped maps; it does NOT prove 2,240 is beatable, and the saving may be O(1) rather than proportional.

THREE KECCAK DIRECTIONS PRICED AT ZERO, ONE OF WHICH CLOSES gf2-k12 ENTIRELY. (a) CONJUGATE CIPHER (eprint 2026/1365) — the paper body could not be read (Cloudflare 403 through five routes; only the abstract is confirmed: a generic conjugacy framework applied to SKINNY ONLY, gaining 5.5%/3%, Keccak not mentioned). BUT THE REFUTATION DOES NOT NEED THE PAPER. Write chi = A o B; then (L o A o B)^r = L o A o (B o L o A)^(r-1) o B, so the total is MC(A) + MC(B) + (r-1) MC(M) with M = B o L o A, and a gain needs MC(M) < 1600. L = pi o rho o theta is INVERTIBLE OVER GF(2) (rank 1600), hence span{L(A(x))_j} = span{A(x)_i}, which contains EVERY ONE of A's product bits individually — so all MC(A) products are still needed; B's own products carry degree-4 classes independent of A's degree-2 classes. Therefore dim span of M's output classes mod affine = 1600, MC(M) >= 1600 = MC(chi), total >= 19,200 and score >= 38,400. ZERO GAIN, FOR EVERY SPLIT, INCLUDING AFFINE CONJUGATORS (which preserve class dimension). WHY SKINNY GAINS AND KECCAK STRUCTURALLY CANNOT: the gain needs an AND before the linear layer to meet an AND after it on the same variables, and SKINNY's MixColumns has an IDENTITY ROW so bits pass through untouched, whereas theta has NO PURE COPIES — every output bit is a XOR of 11 input bits. (The SKINNY matrix claim is from memory and unverified; the refutation does not rest on it.) MARK gf2-k12 CLOSED. (b) CHI'S ALGEBRAIC GROUP STRUCTURE (Kriepke-Kyureghyan; iterates span the gamma_{2^k} and form a group isomorphic to (F_2[X]/X^((n+1)/2))*) IS REAL — verified by brute force rather than trusted, and one fetched summary was WRONG: ord(chi_5) = 4, not 8; chi_5^2(x)_i = x_i XOR x_{i+4}(1 XOR x_{i+3})(1 XOR x_{i+1}) confirmed on all 32 points; chi_5^{-1} = chi_5^3 confirmed. PRICE ZERO: MC(chi^2) = 10 (the five pentagram pair-products {1,3},{2,4},{0,3}, {1,4},{0,2} plus five finals) = 2 MC(chi), so merging two chi layers saves nothing EVEN IF L VANISHED, and over F_p chi^2 needs 2 rows per bit against chi's 1. (c) REDUNDANT AND PACKED REPRESENTATIONS, ALL WORSE: the +-1 encoding LOOKS free — given a materialised bit a, 1-2a = (-1)^a is a free affine expression, so a 2-XOR is w = (1-2a)(1-2b) with a XOR b = (1-w)/2 free, exactly XorLane's price — BUT CHAINING GIVES A 4-XOR IN 3 GATES AGAINST XOR3'S 2, so it is uniformly >= XOR3 and never <. Base-8 digit packing needs q in [0,2] range-checked (t = q(q-1), t(q-2) = 0, plus the parity bit) = 5 score per digit = 320 per column-lane against Xor5Lane's 256. AND PACKING CAN NEVER HELP CHI: the componentwise product of two 64-bit lanes is a RANK-64 BILINEAR MAP, so >= 64 rows per lane, and the record is exactly at that rank floor.

THE THETA-AS-SLP LEAD HAS A MATURE ALGORITHM LITERATURE AND WE WERE ATTACKING IT THE EXPENSIVE WAY — SWITCH FROM EXACT SAT TO RANDOMISED-RESTART GREEDY. Web pass, August 2026. Our own analysis established that theta's cost IS a shortest-linear-program count in the 3-input-XOR (g-XOR) basis, then tried to settle it with an exact SAT encoding, which resolved the 3-column analogue (21 -> 20 gates) and STALLED past an hour on the 5-column one. That is the wrong tool: the g-XOR SLP has been attacked heuristically for years and the algorithms are published, implemented and still improving. THE CONCRETE ALGORITHM (Algorithm 3, PickNewBaseElementXOR3, in 'Optimizing implementations of linear layers using two and higher input XOR gates', PMC10807753; the original 3-input extension is eprint 2021/1400, Springer DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-92518-5_7): extend Boyar-Peralta by enumerating, at every step, ALL TRIPLES i<j<k as candidate new base elements alongside all pairs i<j; score each candidate by the resulting distance-to-target vector; and WHEN CANDIDATES TIE, BREAK RANDOMLY AND RESTART THE WHOLE SEARCH MANY TIMES (the RNBP randomised variant). The tie-breaking randomisation plus restarts is where the gains come from, not the greedy step. ONE ADAPTATION IN OUR FAVOUR: that literature prunes hard on a DEPTH bound because it targets low-latency hardware. WE HAVE NO DEPTH CONSTRAINT — only gate count — so drop the depth pruning entirely and the search gets strictly more freedom than the published runs had. WHY TO BELIEVE IT MOVES: in that literature multi-input gates routinely beat hand constructions by large margins (AES MixColumns 55 -> 44 gates; a 4x4 involutory MDS matrix 45 -> 19), and eprint 2025/1493 took the AES linear layer to 89 g-XOR from a previous best of 91 as recently as November 2025 — the ground is still moving. DO NOT PORT THOSE NUMBERS: they are 2-input-XOR baselines being beaten by multi-input gates, whereas our record ALREADY uses XOR3. The transferable claim is narrower and is the one that matters — OUR THETA IS A HAND CONSTRUCTION (the textbook circuit re-based into 3-input gates, confirmed against the Keccak team's own implementation overview), and randomised-restart greedy search routinely beats hand constructions in exactly this problem. EXISTING CODE TO START FROM rather than writing it: Boyar and Peralta's own C++ at imada.sdu.dk/~joan/xor/Improved2.cc, and the SBP repository (github demirmehmet0/SBP). Recall the pricing: round score = 153,600 + 48h with h = 640 today and a proved floor of h = 320, and h = 639 is already a record because a tie does not leaderboard.

*** A CLAIMED PROOF THAT 184,320 IS OPTIMAL — AND WHY IT IS REFUTED, AT EXACTLY THE STEP ITS OWN AUTHOR FLAGGED AS UNPROVEN. READ THIS BEFORE DE-FUNDING KECCAK. *** A structural pass derived a floor of 2,240 theta gates per round (= 4,480 score), which with chi's 3,200 gives 7,680/round = 184,320 exactly, i.e. the standing record sits ON the claimed bound. The argument has three steps: (1) THE 1,600 THETA OUTPUTS EACH NEED THEIR OWN GATE — verified computationally, the 1,600 support sets are PAIRWISE DISTINCT 11-ELEMENT SETS (1600 distinct, 0 duplicates), so their top multilinear monomials differ and the functionals are independent modulo affine; THIS STEP IS SOLID and the A'-layer at 3,200 is genuinely optimal. (2) each column needs a low-support helper first (the t intermediate), 320 forced. (3) the full column parity C must ALSO be pinned, 320 more, because with only t available the seed has arity >= 5 over pinned values. *** STEP 3 IS FALSE ON THE FAITHFUL REDUCED INSTANCE, AND THIS CORPUS ALREADY HAS THE COUNTEREXAMPLE. *** The corpus's own SAT result on NX=3 — faithfulness checked first, target-to-target relation census IDENTICAL to the real w=64 structure — found 20 gates where the 2-helpers-per-column construction gives 21, model extracted and independently re-verified: 5 helpers for 3 columns, i.e. 1.67 per column, not 2. THE MECHANISM IS PRECISELY WHAT STEP 3 ASSUMES AWAY: never materialise a clean column parity; carry a RIDER bit through the helper chain so it lands as the seed target's own A-bit, and assemble the last column's parity INSIDE a target gate from a shared partial plus AN ALREADY-COMPUTED TARGET. Step 3's case analysis considers only helpers and raw bits as gate inputs; the SAT model uses other theta OUTPUTS as inputs. The author flagged this exact hole ('a careful case analysis over the fan-in-3 gate library, not a machine-checked SLP minimisation; an exhaustive fan-in-3 SLP search could in principle find a cleverer global program') and the search has already been run and already won. *** SO KECCAK IS NOT CLOSED, THE THETA RE-WIRING LEAD SURVIVES INTACT, AND h = 639 (ONE HELPER SAVED PER ROUND) IS STILL A RECORD AT 184,272. *** Note the convergence worth having: the pass independently recommends a Boyar-Peralta-style greedy adapted to fan-in-3 XOR run on the real 1600->1600 theta matrix as the highest-value next step, which is ALREADY this corpus's standing recommendation (switch from exact SAT to randomised-restart greedy, RNBP, no depth pruning). Two independent routes now point at the same computation. RUN IT.

WHAT THE OPTIMALITY PASS ESTABLISHED THAT DOES STAND — FOUR RESULTS AND ONE NEW PRIMITIVE, ALL FROM EXACT RATIONAL LINEAR ALGEBRA WITH POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE CONTROLS, INDEPENDENT OF THE REFUTED STEP 3. *** (1) THE C-LAYER CANNOT BE SKIPPED BY A RATIONAL HELPER, AND THIS IS A CONCLUSIVE NEGATIVE. *** The prize was making the seed directly pinnable from one helper per column, skipping C entirely: 1,920 gates/round -> 168,960, an 8.3 percent win. Tested as a RELAXATION that DROPS THE RANK-1 REQUIREMENT (allowing A*R to be any element of V*V), so a negative is conclusive for R1CS a fortiori. Target e XOR parity(S_a) XOR parity(S_b) from basis {1, a_i, h_a, b_i, h_b, e}: dim(projection onto R) = 0 in EVERY case — symmetric helpers 1/(S+delta) over a grid of ~105 delta values, distinct delta per column, and random non-symmetric 1/(rho.a + rho_0) at k=4 and k=5. Positive controls fired in the same harness (XOR3 -> dim 1, chi -> dim 3, parity-3 from raw bits -> dim 3); negative controls behaved (XOR5 from {1,S} -> 0, parity-4 from raw bits -> 0). NOTE THIS IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE SLP RE-WIRING and does not bear on it: it closes the RATIONAL-HELPER route to skipping C, not the WIRING route to needing fewer helpers. *** (2) NEW PRIMITIVE, NOT PREVIOUSLY IN THIS CORPUS: THE INVERSE OF AN AFFINE FORM COSTS 1 ALLOCATION + 1 ROW. *** h = 1/L is pinned by the single row (h)(L) = 1, sound whenever L is a unit on the reachable set. That is a legitimate NON-BOOLEAN helper and it is worth carrying to every challenge, not just this one. It genuinely works on parity-5: with S = sum_y A[x,y] (free affine, in [0,5]) and h = 1/(S+delta), explicit solutions make parity(S) single-row pinnable at delta = -7/2, -10/3, -5/3 — so C[x] costs 1+1 for h then 1+1 for C = 4, EXACTLY TYING the t-then-C chain by a structurally different route. No win here, but the primitive is new and the tie is informative. *** (3) THE COMPLETE ONE-ROW BIT-EXTRACTION CRITERION, AND IT IS GENERAL. *** A single row pins c = f iff f = O/R - A with A, R, O affine over already-pinned values and R a unit — equivalently iff f*R HAS DEGREE <= 2. Computing the kernel of R -> (high-degree part of parity_k * R) exactly over Q gives dim 3 at k=3 and *** DIM 0 AT k = 4, 5, 6, 7 ***. And the vanishing ideal: for k >= 4 the ONLY quadratics vanishing on graph(parity_k) are the booleanity relations x_i^2 - x_i (dim 5 at k=4 in 5 variables, dim 6 at k=5 in 6 variables, and dim 12 for TWO DISJOINT parity-5s in 12 variables — so mixing instances does not help). Booleanity says nothing linking output to inputs, so parity_k for k >= 4 cannot be pinned by ANY number of rows over (inputs, output) alone; it needs an auxiliary allocation, hence >= 2 allocations and >= 2 rows. cost(XOR5) >= 4 and 4 is achieved: XOR5 IS OPTIMAL, now by a second independent route. THE CLEAN GENERAL STATEMENT: *** ONE ROW PLUS ONE ALLOCATION EXTRACTS ONE BIT FROM A FREE-AFFINE FIELD ELEMENT IF AND ONLY IF ITS RANGE IS A SET OF AT MOST 4 VALUES. *** The reason is a degrees-of-freedom count — a Moebius map has 3 d.o.f. plus 2 for the additive affine part = 5, matching a 2-valued non-affine pattern on n points is n conditions, so n=4 is exactly break-even and n>=5 is inconsistent. Verified: parity and top-bit of V in {0..3} yes (R = 2V-3); parity of V in {0..4}, parity of V in {0..5}, bit-2 of V in {0..5}, top bit of V in {0..7} all no. USE THIS AS THE FIRST TEST ON ANY PROPOSED ONE-ROW GADGET ON ANY CHALLENGE. *** (4) FOUR MORE KECCAK DIRECTIONS CLOSED WITH ARITHMETIC. *** PARITY VIA INTEGER SUM costs exactly 2t-1 with t = ceil(log2(k+1)): k=3 is 3 vs 2 and loses, k=5 is 5 vs 4 and loses, k=6,7 is 5 vs 6 and WINS — the crossover is real but theta never exposes an unshared parity of arity >= 6 (the 11-way A'[x,y] costs 7 standalone against 2.8 amortised; D at 10-way costs 7 against 4), so sharing beats the log every time here. FUSING THETA INTO CHI dies by DEGREE, a second independent proof beyond the existing restriction-lemma one: (a0 XOR d0) XOR (NOT(a1 XOR d1) AND (a2 XOR d2)) has multilinear degree 6 (the coefficient of a0.d0.a1.d1.a2.d2 is -16), and with the output allocated linearly r rows reach degree <= 2^r, so r >= 3, worse than the amortised 4. PACKED/CARRY-SAVE STATE is off by exactly one: (sum_y 2^y a_y).d = sum_y 2^y p_y is 1 row + 5 allocations, but unpacking needs 5 booleanity rows, 11 against 10. PLUS-MINUS-1 (MULTIPLICATIVE) ENCODING is strictly worse — XOR becomes a product so a 3-way XOR costs 2 rows instead of 1; the {0,1} ratio-gadget is exactly what makes XOR3 cheap. CROSS-ROUND AMORTISATION has no term to share: the bound is a sum over rounds of forced functionals, since chi materialises the state every round, so the order or minimal polynomial of the theta matrix is irrelevant.

LITERATURE SWEEP RESULT — THE STRONGEST EXTERNAL CALIBRATION WE HAVE, ONE ACTIONABLE TOOL, AND THREE NEGATIVES THAT CONFIRM OUR GADGETS ARE UNPUBLISHED RATHER THAN WRONG. *** (1) THE ONLY PUBLISHED PLAIN-R1CS KECCAK PERMUTATION COUNT ON BN254 IS gnark's 191,898 CONSTRAINTS, AND WE BEAT IT. *** Consensys/gnark issue #1391, compiler log quoted in the issue body: nbPublic=200 nbSecret=200, nbConstraints=191898 for ONE Keccak-f[1600] (25 u64 in, 25 u64 out), Groth16/BN254. Compare our record's 184,320 SCORE — and score counts allocations AND constraints, so we are far below it on the comparable axis. The circom figures (vocdoni/keccak256-circom 150,848; ePrint 2023/681 Table 3 reports 151,357 using that same code) are a WHOLE HASH of a 32-byte input, not a bare permutation, so do not compare them to our number directly. *** (2) AND THE CIRCOM ARITHMETISATION IS EXACTLY OUR SEED, TO THE UNIT — WHICH SETTLES WHAT THE SEED IS. *** Derived from the circom sources (XOR = 1 constraint/bit via out = a+b-2ab, AND = 1/bit, Xor3 = 2/bit, Xor5 = 4/bit, shifts and constant XORs free after folding): theta 3,200 + chi 3,200 = 6,400 constraints/round, x24 = 153,600, which brackets the published 150,848 with the difference consistent with round-1 constant folding. *** DOUBLE IT FOR ALLOCATIONS AND YOU GET 307,200 — BIT-FOR-BIT THE projs/ SEED SCORE. *** So the seed IS the textbook fully-bit-blasted circom circuit, and the 184,320 record is precisely that circuit re-based into 3-input gates, confirming the corpus's reading from an independent direction. Useful ratio from the same derivation: of circom's 6,400 constraints/round, 4,800 (75 percent) are F2-LINEAR and only 1,600 (25 percent) are the genuinely nonlinear AND in chi. NO PUBLISHED PER-STEP theta/chi CONSTRAINT SPLIT EXISTS for any BN254 R1CS implementation — this derivation is the only one. *** (3) ACTIONABLE: THE FAN-IN-3 SLP TOOL IS OPEN SOURCE, SO DO NOT REIMPLEMENT IT. *** Baksi-Dasu-Karmakar-Chattopadhyay-Isobe, 'Three Input Exclusive-OR Gate Support For Boyar-Peralta's Algorithm', ePrint 2021/1400, states in its own abstract that it is 'the first open-source work to support higher input XOR gates' and that it extends the RANDOMISED Tan-Peyrin variant (TCHES'20, RNBP) with 'native support for XOR3, XOR4 etc. gates, while taking care of the individual costs for each gate'. The heuristic is named BDKCI downstream (PeerJ CS 2024, DOI 10.7717/peerj-cs.1820). Lineage: Banik et al. IWSEC'19 first supported XOR3 but its source is NOT public; Maximov ePrint'19 supplies the extra tie-breaker. FETCH AND RUN 2021/1400's CODE ON THE REAL 1600->1600 THETA MATRIX rather than writing a greedy from scratch. Their cost metrics are gate count plus four ASIC libraries; WE WANT GATE COUNT ONLY AND HAVE NO DEPTH CONSTRAINT, so drop every depth term and the search gets strictly more freedom than the published runs. *** (4) THE ONE-ROW XOR3 IS GENUINELY UNPUBLISHED, AND circomlib USES TWO CONSTRAINTS. *** circomlib/circuits/sha256/xor3.circom computes mid = b*c then out = a*(1-2b-2c+4mid) + b + c - 2mid, i.e. TWO R1CS constraints per bit; every downstream copy found via code search is byte-identical, including the optimistically-named XOR3_v3. Clean has no one-row XOR3 either and does its Keccak XOR by eight ByteXorTable LOOKUPS per 64-bit word. Searches for a one-constraint 3-input XOR returned zero matches in papers, circomlib, Clean, Aztec/barretenberg, plonky2 and halo2. OUR GADGET IS REAL — it is in a verified record tree and has now been re-derived twice independently via the non-vanishing multiplier R = 2S-3 on S = a+b+c — so the negative CONFIRMS NOVELTY rather than refuting the gadget. *** AND IT NAMES THE TRAP: the naive two-root shape (a+b+c-o)(a+b+c-o-2) = 0 IS one rank-1 row but is UNSOUND ON ITS OWN, because it admits o = -2 at s = 0. That is very likely why nobody publishes a one-row XOR3. Do not let a job ship that shape. ***
rsa-pkcs1v15-sha256-4096-65537: HEAD-TO-HEAD MODMUL COUNTS ACROSS FOUR CODEBASES, ALL COMPILED AND MEASURED IN OUR MODEL (no lookups, no challenges), for one 256-bit a*b mod p over BN254: jsnark/xJsnark with a CONSTANT modulus and lazy range = 623 constraints at 32-bit chunks; jsnark with a variable modulus = 637 at 26-bit; arkworks r1cs-std emulated_fp = 680 (66 for mul_without_reduce + 614 for reduce) at 17 limbs x 15 bits; gnark v0.8.1 = 724 at 26x10 and 888 at its shipped 64x4. LIMB WIDTH 26-32 IS OPTIMAL AND 64 IS 18-22% WORSE — measured independently in two different codebases, and it reproduces xJsnark's own Figure 5 parameter sweep (b about 32 near-optimal, b = 120 about 40% worse). WE USE 4 LIMBS OF 64 BITS, i.e. the worst end of that curve; this is the same conclusion the pseudo-Mersenne analysis reached from a different direction, so treat 32-bit limbs as strongly corroborated. STRUCTURE OF THE COST, which is why: product limbs hinted and verified at 2n-1 FIXED points costs 2n-1 rows (15 at w=32) and is essentially free; q*p is FREE when p is a compile-time constant since constant scalings are linear; grouped carry propagation is 60-110; and ABOUT 80% OF THE WHOLE THING is bit-decomposition range checks on the quotient and remainder. LAZY REDUCTION IS WORTH ABOUT 600 CONSTRAINTS PER AVOIDED REDUCE (arkworks measures mul_without_reduce at 66 against reduce at 614, and additions cost literally zero), so a*b + c*d with one shared reduction is about 746 against 1360. FINALLY, WHY GNARK'S HEADLINE 99 CONSTRAINTS PER EMULATED MUL IS NOT AVAILABLE: modern gnark's mulMod emits ZERO constraints and defers to a Schwartz-Zippel check at a commitment-derived challenge (std/math/emulated/field_mul.go), and std/multicommit panics outright if the frontend is not a Committer — so it cannot even compile on a plain Groth16 frontend. Strip the challenge and the lookups and gnark's own pre-v0.10 code lands at 724.

PARAMETER TUNING — THREE OF THE FIVE CLOSURES NEEDED CORRECTING, AND ONE REVERSED. Karatsuba/Toom remains subsumed by evaluation at 2m-1 fixed points (Theta(m), below Karatsuba's m^1.58, interpolation free) — that one stands. The others: (a) SQUARING IS CHEAPER THAN MULTIPLICATION AFTER ALL, BUT NOT VIA tri(m). It is true that a(c)*a(c) costs the same one row per point as a(c)*b(c) IF every coefficient must be materialised. THE ESCAPE IS NOT TO MATERIALISE THEM: a grouped carry check only ever reads the 2K GROUP SUMS S_w = sum_{e<g} coeff(gw+e)*2^(Be), so it suffices to verify a GENERATING IDENTITY S(c) = beta(c)^2 + (c - t^9)*Hi(c) at 2K fixed points. For a SQUARE the high part Hi = sum_{i+j>=gw} h_i h_j is a SYMMETRIC staircase form of rank gw-1, so ceil((gw-1)/2) products suffice — 4 at gw = 9, realised in Lean as 2h8(A1-A4) + 2h7(A2-A4) + 2h6(A3-A4) + A5(2A4-A5) with A_k = sum_{j>=k} h_j. Cost 2m(1 + 1/gw) ~ 2m against 4m-3 for coefficient materialisation. MEASURED SAVING 294 per squaring, 4408 total — this IS the 326297 -> 321889 move. THE LIMIT OF THE TRICK IS EXACT: for a GENERAL product the staircase is BILINEAR of rank gw-1, needing gw-1 products, so the windowed cost is (2m/gw)*2*gw = 4m against 4m-3 — three units WORSE. It applies to the 15 chain squarings and provably cannot extend to q*n or to the final block's a^2*b. Tensor rank is the whole story: symmetry halves it, bilinearity does not. (b) MERGING SQUARINGS FAILS ON CARRY WIDTH, NOT ON WITNESS BITS. On bits alone merging is nearly neutral — a block covering k squarings needs 4096*(2^k - 1) quotient bits plus one 4096-bit residue = 4096*2^k for k squarings, so k=1 and k=2 TIE at 8192 per squaring and only k >= 3 is bit-worse. (My earlier '26302 against 18782' was wrong, and so is the record's own doc claiming exact cost-neutrality.) THE REAL OBSTRUCTION IS THE CARRY-WIDTH LAW w ~ (d-1)*B + log2(g*d*m), where d is the DEGREE of the verified product — VERIFIED AGAINST MEASUREMENT: d=2, B=24, g=9, m=171 gives model 35.6 against measured max 33 (the balanced representation buys ~2.6); d=3, B=16, g=13, m=256 gives model 45.3 against measured max 47. Merging two squarings takes d from 2 to 4, so w jumps by a whole B, the group budget w + B*g <= 253 collapses from g=9 to g=7, and the carry cost per squaring goes 2267 -> 8121 at B=24 (4243 even at B=12). COROLLARY THAT EXPLAINS A DESIGN CHOICE: the final block runs at B=16 rather than the chain's B=24 precisely because it verifies a DEGREE-3 product, where halving B removes about B bits of carry width. (c) THE LIMB WIDTH IS A FLAT OPTIMUM — RETIRE THE 'b=17 BEATS b=24 BY 0.9%' CLAIM. Contradicted three ways. The record's own measured pre-window sweep has B=24 as a SHARP local minimum (20:20120, 22:20124, 23:20260, 24:20006, 25:20283, 26:20248, 28:20140). A post-window model calibrated on the measured B=24 point (3361 modelled against 3328 measured, 1% high) is flat across 16..24: 16:3363, 17:3351, 18:3359, 20:3318, 22:3374, 24:3361, 26:3588, 32:4052 — best case about 43 per squaring, ~645 total, inside the model error. And B MUST BE A MULTIPLE OF 8 or the free byte-to-limb packing breaks. Fully built-out but ABANDONED Params32.lean (B=32, 129 limbs) and Params24Final.lean show the sweep was done empirically. DO NOT RE-OPEN THE LIMB WIDTH.

WHERE THE COST ACTUALLY IS, AND WHY IT IS HARD TO MOVE: about 82% of each modmul is TWO 4096-bit range checks — the quotient q and the remainder r, roughly 8037 rows each at b=24 — with grouped carries about 2627 and the evaluation rows about 1364. THE OBVIOUS ATTACK FAILS FOR TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS. Dropping the quotient range check (letting the carry bounds force q small) is INCOMPATIBLE WITH GROUPED CARRIES: grouping bounds only the group sums, not the individual coefficients, so you would need one carry per coefficient — 12276 bits per op instead of 1368, a net loss of about 21800 against the 8037 saved. It is also UNSOUND for adversarial n: if every limb of n is even, take q0 = 1/2 mod p and every (q*n)_i is a 23-bit value, the carry chain passes, and the circuit accepts a*b - r = n/2. RNS/CRT is likewise dead in plain R1CS — reducing modulo an auxiliary prime needs a witnessed quotient of full bit length, costing at least what it saves; RNS only pays when range checks are lookups. Barrett vs Montgomery is irrelevant because the quotient is nondeterministic advice, so there is no division to optimise. AND THE RANGE CHECK ITSELF IS OPTIMAL: a k-bit check costs 2k-1 (k rows + k-1 allocations) and that is a lower bound — r rank-1 rows cut a variety whose projection has degree at most 2^r by Bezout, so at most 2^r values can be accepted. The top-bit-fold already attains it; base-4 or base-8 digit decompositions tie at best.

RETRACTION — THE BYTE-WISE RANGE-CHECK LEVER DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE ARRAYS IT TARGETED ALREADY COST ZERO. Two independent errors in my earlier note. (1) THE MODULUS AND SIGNATURE RANGE CHECKS ARE ALREADY FREE: `costIs_sub_bytes24ToBigInt` is `Count.zero`, because the limbs are affine in the input bytes and the byte bounds come from the challenge Assumptions (IsOctetString). There is nothing there to save. PadDigest24 is likewise Count.zero, and the REASON is worth knowing: B = 24 is BYTE-ALIGNED (3 bytes per limb), so packing is affine — the legacy PadDigest at limbBits = 121 has to witness 14 split bits plus 16 booleanity rows, while PadDigest24 witnesses nothing. (2) The 512 x (2*8 - 1) = 7680 arithmetic is wrong for a FRESH witness. The 2k-1 form (k-1 allocations + k rows via the top-bit fold) is available only when there is an already-allocated or affine expression to fold the top bit against. For a fresh k-bit witness Bezout gives BOTH bounds — r quadrics in A^a have at most 2^a isolated solutions so a >= k, and the projection has degree at most 2^r so r >= k — hence 2k exactly, and splitting into 512 independently-checked chunks cannot beat it because each chunk then needs its own allocation. MEASURED: the record's quotient check is 4095 allocations + 4095 rows = 8190 = 2*4095, and its remainder check is 8192 = 2*4096. Both are AT the floor, not at 8037. Total slack across all 31 range checks in the circuit: 31 units.

CORRECTION — THERE IS NO SHA-256 IN THIS CIRCUIT. Verified against the challenge interface: `digest : Vector F digestBytesLen` is an INPUT ('SHA-256 digest of the message being verified'), and the seed solution contains zero hash/compression files — every module is bigint machinery (SqMulModBal, ModExpSq, GroupedEq*, EqViaCarries, MixedRadix, Bytes*). The published '66% SHA-2 / 14% bigint' split for RS256 circuits does NOT apply here because those circuits hash the message and this one does not. ALL ~326k of the cost is non-native bigint arithmetic: the 16 squarings + 1 multiply mod a 4096-bit N, plus byte<->limb conversion and the padding comparison. Optimise the modmul and the limb/carry machinery; do not go looking for a hash to shrink.
Exponent 65537 = 2^16 + 1: exactly 16 squarings + 1 multiply; every step is a fixed-modulus modmul — share reduction machinery across all 17.
Fixed modulus: precompute q'[0] (Montgomery -N^{-1} mod 2^w), R^2 mod N, and all modulus limbs as circuit CONSTANTS — no in-circuit inverse or per-op setup.
CIOS/Montgomery with carry elimination: when the top modulus word is bounded ((D-1)/2-1), the t[N]/t[N+1] carries are provably zero, dropping ~5N+2 additions per multiply (gnark result).
Limb count sweet spot N<=12 wide limbs; minimize the number of carries that need range checks — each naive range check costs ~1/2 constraint per bit, so wider limbs with fewer carries win.
CRT / RNS residue representation to split the 4096-bit reduce into independent smaller-modulus channels; recombine once at the end.
Only range-check the modular residual, the quotient coefficient, and carries — not every intermediate; use top-bit-fold range checks.

LAZY REDUCTION with static limb-bound tracking (xJsnark long-integer arithmetic): carry a compile-time upper bound per limb and let partial products accumulate in wider limbs; emit a carry-normalization + range check ONLY when a limb's tracked bound would exceed field capacity, instead of normalizing after every op. Across the 16 squarings + 1 multiply this removes whole normalization passes, not just individual carries.

DEFERRAL BUDGET, concretely (circom-ecdsa): with n-bit limbs and k of them, unreduced accumulation is safe while 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < (native field bits). Use this inequality to place carry/reduce passes at the LAST legal moment instead of guessing; multiples of the fixed modulus used to reduce are compile-time constants.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce): keep products unreduced in wide limbs and reduce once per accumulated expression, not per multiply. CAUTION: bellman-bignat [OWWB20] and similar bigint libraries are tuned for constraint DENSITY, not constraint COUNT — do not copy their limb layout without re-costing it against allocations+constraints.

mulmod as ONE polynomial-identity check at a single constant point (gnark/eprint 2025/933): hint quotient q and error/carry limbs e out of circuit, then enforce a(X)b(X) = c(X) + alpha(X)q(X) + (2^B - X)e(X) evaluated at ONE fixed X=2^B — collapses the full limb-by-limb equality into a single rank-1 product plus range checks on q,c,e, instead of one constraint per limb coefficient. Evaluate-at-a-point beats coefficient-matching in this R1CS metric; reuse the same hinted-then-checked shape for all 17 squarings/multiplies.

PKCS1v15 padding is almost entirely CONSTANT: the 0x00 01 FF...FF 00 prefix and the DigestInfo DER header are fixed bytes. Comparing the recovered padded block against them costs only affine equality checks against constants — allocate nothing for the padding bytes themselves, and never range-check a byte whose value is fixed by the spec.

CORRECTION + PROOF — THE RANGE CHECK IS EXACTLY AT ITS FLOOR, AND THE FLOOR ARGUMENT IN OUR CORPUS WAS ONLY HALF AN ARGUMENT. MEASURED FROM Solution/.../CostBal.lean squareModBalGTCount at m=171,B=24,tq=15,tw=16,G=39: one middle/first squaring is 9836 alloc + 9874 constr = 19710, split as q-certification 8190, r-certification 8192, grouped carries 2267, window 380, evaluation 681. THE TWO CERTIFICATION FIGURES ARE EXACTLY 2x THE BIT-LENGTH: q is 170*24+15 = 4095 bits and costs 8190; r is 170*24+16 = 4096 bits and costs 8192. Zero slack, not 'roughly 8037'. (Also correct in that entry: grouped carries are 2267 not 2627, and the evaluation block is 681 = (2m-2) alloc + (2m-1) constr, not 1364.) THE CORPUS JUSTIFICATION ('r rank-1 rows cut a variety whose projection has degree at most 2^r by Bezout') BOUNDS ROWS ONLY AND THEREFORE PROVES ONLY HALF OF 2k-1. THE MISSING HALF IS A DIMENSION ARGUMENT: by Heintz's Bezout inequality, r quadrics in A^N have sum-of-component-degrees at most 2^min(r,N), so a gadget whose accepted set for a designated affine form is finite of size 2^k needs BOTH r >= k rows AND N >= k coordinates. With the value itself already allocated the marginal cost is (k-1) allocations + k rows = 2k-1, and that is exactly what RangeCheck.mainBits emits. SUPERSETS DO NOT HELP AND SLACK STRICTLY COSTS: an accepted set of size 2^(k+s) costs >= 2(k+s), and completeness forces size >= 2^k, so 2k is the floor for any finite acceptor regardless of how loose it is. BASE-4/BASE-8 DIGITS TIE EXACTLY (not 'at best'): the degree-2^k root set built by composing quadratics, w1 = z^2+az, w2 = w1^2+..., final w_{k-1}(w_{k-1}-c) = 0, is k-1 allocations + k rows = 2k-1, identical to booleanity. THE F_p-SPECIFIC ESCAPE HATCH (the 'true per row, false across rows' failure mode) WAS CHECKED AND CLOSES: restricting a field element to a multiplicative coset of index d via y^d = z costs about 2*log2(d) — again exactly 2 per bit — and yields a coset, not an interval, so it cannot certify integer smallness. HONEST SCOPE: this is a bound on a GADGET that pins a value to a finite set. It is NOT a lower bound on the modmul or on the circuit; see the global-floor entry.

THE QUOTIENT RANGE CHECK IS NECESSARY FOR EVERY MODULUS, NOT ONLY FOR EVEN-LIMB ONES — CORRECTING OUR OWN ATTACK WRITE-UP. Our corpus says dropping it 'is also UNSOUND for adversarial n: if every limb of n is even, take q0 = 1/2 mod p'. That understates it by a lot. VERIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION at toy scale (p = 2^61-1, B=4, m=8 limbs, carry groups of 4): with the quotient limbs left as unconstrained field elements, the map q -> (grouped carry sums of (q*n)) is F_p-LINEAR from F_p^m to F_p^(m/gw), i.e. 8 unknowns against 4 equations, so it is surjective for essentially every n and the adversary simply SOLVES for q. 200 out of 200 random trials with ODD, top-bit-set n produced a full forgery: an arbitrary chosen r != a^2 mod n accepted, with all carries set to zero. At our real parameters it is 171 free field unknowns against 37 group equations — even more underdetermined. So the even-limb story is a cute special case, not the reason; the real reason is a dimension count, and it means NO relaxation of the quotient certification survives as long as the carry chain is grouped. Corollary: an F_p convolution coefficient (q*n)_j only has an integer meaning if q_j is certified below 2^B, and that is the whole of why the check exists.

THE RANGE-BIT CONSERVATION LAW — THE SINGLE MOST DECISION-RELEVANT FACT ABOUT THIS CHALLENGE, AND IT KILLS BATCHING, LAZY REDUCTION AND MERGED SQUARINGS IN ONE LINE. For any reduction node certified by a witnessed integer identity P = q*n + r, the certification cost is 2*(bits(q) + bits(r)) = 2*bits(P), because bits(q) = bits(P) - bits(n) and bits(r) = bits(n). SO THE COST OF A REDUCTION IS EXACTLY TWICE THE BIT-LENGTH OF THE PRODUCT IT REDUCES, and nothing about how the reduction is organised changes it. CONSEQUENCES, all checked numerically. (1) A node fusing M reduced 4096-bit residues under one quotient costs exactly 8192*M, so the whole exponentiation's certification cost is 8192*(sum of arities), independent of the shape of the DAG. (2) MERGING TWO SQUARINGS IS EXACTLY COST-NEUTRAL on certification, not a loss — x^4 = q*n + r has bits(q)+bits(r) = 12288+4096 = 16384, identical to two separate squarings at 8192 each. Our corpus entry blames 'the quotient grows to 12288 bits'; that is the wrong reason. The real reason merging loses is the EVALUATION block, which grows like (M-1)^2 (measured: 4m-3 cells at M=2, 16m-9 at M=3). Merging three or more IS a certification loss: 4096*2^k against 8192*k. (3) LAZY / DEFERRED REDUCTION IS WORTH ZERO HERE, and this is why the secp figures do not transfer. Sharing one reduction across M products pays off only for a SUM of products (sum_i a_i b_i has a quotient of just 4096 + log2 M bits), and affine EC formulas are sums of products. A modular exponentiation chain contains no additions at all — every step is a single product — so there is nothing to share. Do not port the '424 rows at M=1, 457 at M=2' curve from the secp entries to this challenge. (4) MEASURED TOTAL: 15 squarings at 16382 certification each plus the fused final node at 16382 = 262112, which is 80.3% of our 326297 and 81.4% of the 321889 record. Everything else in the circuit — all carries, all evaluation rows, all byte packing — is the remaining 19%.

THE MULTI-ARITY REDUCTION DAG IS THE RIGHT COST METRIC, NOT 'NUMBER OF MODMULS', AND OUR CURRENT SHAPE IS PROVABLY OPTIMAL UNDER IT. Our corpus says '17 MULTIPLICATIONS IS PROVABLY OPTIMAL' from l(65537) >= 17. That is true and irrelevant: our own record does 16 reduction nodes, not 17, because the last square and the last multiply are FUSED into one arity-3 certificate a*a*b = q*n + em (SqMulModBalTo, measured 12955+13018 = 25973 at m=256,B=16, with the residue FREE because em is an affine form of the digest). The correct objective is sum-of-arities. FORMALLY: a reduction node of arity M sums M previously-computed exponents at cost C(M), so the reachable exponent after nodes M_1..M_k is at most prod M_i, and 65537 needs prod M_i >= 65537. Calibrated cost model (fitted exactly to the two real gadgets in the tree: C(2) = 8192*2 + 4m + carry = 19147 at the best limb width, C(3) = 34511, C(3) with free residue = 26319 against the measured 25973): rate C(M)/ln M is 27625 at M=2, 31414 at M=3, 39839 at M=4 — arity 2 has the best rate, so arity 3 only pays where it saves a whole node. EXHAUSTIVE RESULT: of all arity multisets with product >= 65537, EXACTLY ONE is cheaper than our current shape — thirteen arity-2 nodes plus two arity-3 nodes, 309741 against 313524, a 1.2% gap — and a complete DFS over every chain of at most 15 nodes with arities in {2,3} proves NO such chain reaches 65537 exactly. (Product 2^13*9 = 73728 clears the bound but the exponent is not attainable.) Everything involving an arity-4 or arity-5 node is strictly worse. CONCLUSION: 15 squarings + one fused arity-3 tail is optimal, and there is ZERO headroom in the exponentiation structure. Stop looking at addition chains, windowing and merged squarings; they are all closed.

THE MODULUS IS AN INPUT — READ FROM Challenge/Instances/.../Interface.lean, NOT INFERRED. `structure Input (F) where modulus : Vector F 512; digest : Vector F 32; signature : Vector F 512`. All three are public inputs; the modulus is fully adversarial. THE ONLY THINGS Assumptions GIVES US (Specs/RSASSAPKCS1v15.lean): IsOctetString on modulus, digest and signature, and HasBitSize (os2ip n) 4096, i.e. 2^4095 <= N < 2^4096. THERE IS NO ODDNESS, NO PRIMALITY, NO gcd CONDITION, NO CO-PRIMALITY WITH e. An all-even-byte modulus such as N = 2^4095 satisfies Assumptions exactly. SO THE FOLLOWING ARE ALL DEAD: precomputed multiples of N as compile-time constants, constant-folded reductions, modulus-shape-specific folds, pseudo-Mersenne tricks, Orup-style modulus rescaling to N~ = -1 mod 2^k, casting-out-primes with a free native leg. WHAT SURVIVES AND IS ALREADY USED: N's limbs are inputs, so ANY affine function of them (3N, N shifted, a balanced-representative offset proportional to N) is a free linear combination and costs nothing — the balanced-residue window already exploits 2^4095 <= N to buy one bit off the middle quotient (tq = 15, not 16). SECOND CONSEQUENCE, WORTH MORE THAN IT LOOKS: because IsOctetString is ASSUMED and not checked, the modulus, signature and digest bytes need NO range check at all — Bytes24ToBigInt.circuit and PadDigest24.circuit are both literally Count.zero. Our corpus entry proposing to 'range-check the BYTES rather than the limbs of the modulus and signature, saving about 357 each' is chasing a check that does not exist; the 8037/8190 figures are the QUOTIENT and RESIDUE certifications inside each squaring, not input checks. Nothing to save there.

WEB PASS, FOUR TOPICS, ALMOST ENTIRELY DRY — RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-SEARCHES. (1) BATCHED / AMORTIZED RANGE PROOFS WITHOUT LOOKUPS OR CHALLENGES: none exist. Bulletproofs/BP+/BP++ aggregation shrinks PROOF SIZE only, never the multiplication-gate count, and needs Pedersen commitments plus challenges. Sharp (CCS'22), CKLR21 bounded integer commitments, Daza-Rafols-Zacharakis updateable IPA, lattice amortized shortness — all need challenges, vector commitments or hidden-order groups. ZNARKs (SNARKs over the integers) do give the dream 4-constraint range check but need an integer commitment, a random prime challenge AND an unknown-order group. (2) SUM-OF-SQUARES RANGE PROOFS (Boudot, Lipmaa, Groth 4x+1 = a^2+b^2+c^2, Couteau-Peters-Pointcheval) ARE CHALLENGE-FREE AND ALGEBRAIC — and VACUOUS over F_p, because every element of a finite field is a sum of TWO squares, so the R1CS is satisfiable for every x. The only repair is to range-check each w_i, which costs 1.5x to 3x more than checking x directly. This is the most tempting-looking dead end in the space; it is definitively dead. (3) PROOF-OF-EXPONENTIATION (Wesolowski, Pietrzak, BBF PoE/PoKE, Block et al., Gerbicz-Li, all batch PoEs) DIES TWICE: every one needs a verifier-chosen prime or challenge, AND every one has verifier cost Omega(lambda) group operations, i.e. 128+ modmuls against our 17. Wesolowski literally DEGENERATES at e = 65537: for any lambda >= 17 the challenge prime exceeds the exponent, so q = 0, pi = 1, and the verifier's check IS the original exponentiation. Schul-Ganz and Segev (TCC 2020) prove a matching generic-group LOWER BOUND that non-trivial non-interactive batch verification is impossible, which is as close to an impossibility theorem for this direction as exists. Delegation/outsourcing of modular exponentiation (Hohenberger-Lysyanskaya, Chen et al.) is probabilistic (1/2, 2/3 checkability) AND needs client-held secret randomness — structurally impossible inside a circuit. (4) HARDWARE MODMUL LITERATURE, READ ALGEBRAICALLY: Orup quotient pipelining looks like a huge win ('the quotient digit is literally the low limb of the accumulator') and IS NOT — determining the quotient was never our cost, the quotient is free advice; CERTIFYING it is the cost, and Orup does not change bits(q)+bits(r). Adopting it would force us to materialise n intermediate accumulators, i.e. n^2 limb certifications. Walter's no-final-subtraction invariant and o1js 'almost reduced' top-limb bounds are both already the balanced-residue design we run. Negre-Plantard-Robert's n(n+1)/2 squaring saves LIMB PRODUCTS, which are free for us at 2m-1 evaluation points. Bipartite/tripartite modular multiplication is parallelism-only. CONFIRMED: no published R1CS constraint count for RSA-4096 exists anywhere (checked zk-email, circom-rsa-verify, halo2-rsa, noir_rsa, noir-bignum, zkPassport, gnark, xJsnark, Cinderella). Best real comparables: Ozdemir et al. USENIX'20 7563 constraints per 2048-bit modmul with a CONSTANT modulus; xJsnark 88949 for the whole RSA-2048 e=65537 modexp with a hardcoded modulus; circom-rsa-verify 536212 for RSA-2048 including SHA-256. Our 321889 for RSA-4096 with a VARIABLE modulus almost certainly remains the best number in existence.

THE HONEST GAP, STATED PRECISELY, BECAUSE IT IS THE ONLY PLACE A BIG WIN CAN STILL LIVE. Everything above proves that our GADGETS are at their floors and that the CHAIN SHAPE is optimal. None of it is a lower bound on the CIRCUIT. The accepted set of public inputs is {(n, h, s) : 2^4095 <= N < 2^4096, s < n, s^65537 = EM(h) mod n}, of size about 2^(4095+256) = 2^4351, since for almost every (n,h) there is at most one s. Applying the same Heintz/Bezout counting to the whole circuit gives rows >= 4351 and (public inputs + witnesses) >= 4351, so with 1056 public field elements the floor is about 3295 + 4351 = 7646 in score. WE PAY 321889 — FORTY-TWO TIMES THE FLOOR. Nothing information-theoretic forbids a vastly cheaper circuit. What forbids it, concretely, is one thing and only one thing: the F_p convolution coefficient (q*n)_j has an integer meaning only if q_j is certified below 2^B, and the only known certifications of integer smallness in a prime field cost 2 per bit. Every technique that beats that rate — lookups, log-derivative/logup, Schwartz-Zippel at a challenge point, casting out primes with a free native leg, integer commitments, hidden-order groups — is excluded by this challenge's model, and we verified externally that the literature contains nothing else. THE OPEN QUESTION, STATED SO IT CAN BE ATTACKED: is there a JOINT certificate over the 31 quotient/residue vectors of the whole chain whose accepted set is NOT finite coordinate-wise but is still sound? The Bezout floor for the joint object is only about 2*8192 = 16384, since the entire witness is determined by (s, n), so nothing in our lower-bound machinery rules it out. Neither a construction nor an impossibility proof was found, in our work or in the literature. That is the one live question; everything else in this file is closed.
