CHECK WHETHER WE ALREADY DO xJsnark-STYLE LAZY REFRESH ACROSS THE 16 SQUARINGS — IT IS THE ONE EXTERNAL RESULT STATED IN OUR EXACT COST MODEL. xJsnark (IEEE S&P 2018, https://akosba.github.io/papers/xjsnark.pdf, repo https://github.com/akosba/xjsnark) is a Groth16/jsnark-era system with NO lookups and NO in-circuit randomness, so unlike every modern source its long-integer technique prices exactly as ours does. It represents long integers as groups of b-bit words with DEFERRED ALIGNMENT AND CARRY PROPAGATION: multiply repeatedly in a 'Muled' unnormalised form and only 'refresh' back to fresh 64-bit limbs when the overflow bound actually forces it, optimising globally across the whole integer dataflow instead of per operation. Reports 1.2x-2x+ smaller circuits than prior art on SHA-256, RSA and AES, and ships a FIXED-MODULUS FIXED-EXPONENT modexp example — our exact shape. THE QUESTION TO ANSWER FIRST, since this challenge is on NO_DISPATCH and only merits a slot if the answer is no: does our chain refresh after EVERY squaring, or does it carry unnormalised limbs as far as the bound allows? Note the related lead that is NOT worth pursuing: gnark PR #1700 adds 4-bit windowing to in-circuit ModExp, which cannot beat 16 squarings + 1 multiply for e=65537 — do not re-derive that.

WHERE THE COST ACTUALLY IS IN AN RSA MODEXP CIRCUIT, MEASURED BY THE ONE SYSTEM THAT PRICES LIKE US. xJsnark's RSA-2048 modexp is 88,949 constraints, of which ABOUT 70,000 ARE RANGE CHECKS ON PROVER WITNESS VALUES — the multiplication check itself is 2k-1 = 127 constraints, i.e. 0.14% of the circuit (xJsnark Sec VII-A and Table III, https://akosba.github.io/papers/xjsnark.pdf; their own comparison baseline Cinderella is 144,933 for the same relation). xJsnark is Groth16-era jsnark with NO lookups and NO in-circuit randomness, so unlike gnark or kimchi its accounting is directly comparable to ours. THE LESSON FOR OUR 321,769: do not go looking for a cheaper multiply — that is already 2k-1 via interpolatedMul and is noise in the total. THE ONLY THING WORTH AUDITING IS THE RANGE-CHECK AND CARRY LEDGER, and specifically xJsnark's grouped equality assertion (Sec IV-B-4): rather than forcing limbBits bits to zero per word pair, MERGE as many word pairs as the native prime allows into one grouped difference, force the grouped prefix to zero, and propagate the remainder — jsnark's rule is to keep merging while the accumulated bound stays under 2^(log2(p) - 2), with the witnessed carry range-checked to only its true width. Related and already ours in spirit: Ozdemir-Wahby-Whitehat-Boneh (USENIX Sec 20, https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/1494) tighten the QUOTIENT width to ceil(log2(floor(x_max/d_min))) rather than the width of x — the same 'size it to the call site' law we already apply. This challenge is on NO_DISPATCH and none of this changes that unless the carry grouping turns out to be genuinely unexploited.

THE FULL REJECTION TABLE FOR THIS CHALLENGE, ALL WITH REASONS — THIS IS WHY IT STAYS ON NO_DISPATCH. (1) MONTGOMERY FORM IN-CIRCUIT LOSES ON EVERY AXIS: division is a HINT costing zero rows, so the thing Montgomery exists to avoid is already free, and it adds a full extra non-native multiply for m = (ab mod R)N' mod R plus two conversion multiplies, while m < R is the SAME WIDTH as q so there is no range-check saving. Measured externally: circom-rsa-verify (Montgomery CIOS) is 536,212 constraints for RSA-2048 against zk-email's 178,976 — 2.9x WORSE. (2) BARRETT loses for the same reason: precomputed mu = floor(2^2B/N) times a witness is a real product with its own carry chain and range checks, to compute what a hint gives free. (3) LAZY REDUCTION ACROSS MULTIPLICATIONS LOSES ~1.9x FOR A SQUARING CHAIN, quantified: carry and range cost scale with PRODUCT SIZE, which doubles each skipped reduction, while reducing costs only ~1x the product size — reduce-every-step ~32.8k range bits against ~61k for skip-one. NOTE THE DISTINCTION that makes the arkworks result look contradictory: accumulating a SUM OF PRODUCTS before one reduction DOES win (~4.5x); a SQUARING CHAIN does not. Our exponentiation is a squaring chain. (4) RNS/residue representation: multiplication becomes componentwise but every comparison, carry and range check needs conversion back to positional form, each conversion needing a witnessed reduction with its own ~W-bit range-checked quotient — conversion exceeds the multiplication saving, and multiplication was under 10% to begin with. (5) CRT check mod native P and mod 2^t is worth ~253 bits, about 50% of carries at W=256 (which is why Mina and Aztec use it) but ~3% at W=4096. (6) EXPONENT-CHAIN GOLF HAS ZERO HEADROOM: l(65537) = 17 is optimal since l(n) >= ceil(log2 n) and the binary chain meets it, and squaring is NOT cheaper than multiplying in this model — the product step is well under 1% of rows. (7) FUSING THE LAST TWO EXPONENTIATION STEPS (y^2 * x = qN + m) is dead on arrival: a degree-3 limb product has ~3n + log k = 369-bit coefficients and does not fit 254 bits. (8) MAKING RSA PSEUDO-MERSENNE VIA A SPARSE MULTIPLE OF N IS IMPOSSIBLE: multiples of N are spaced N apart, so the closest multiple below 2^t leaves a remainder below N ~ 2^4096, never small; and CRT mod p,q is off the table since the factorisation is secret.

WINOGRAD ON RSA: THE RESIDUE-MULTIPLY TRICK IS ALREADY TAKEN WHERE IT WINS AND PROVABLY LOSES WHERE IT IS NOT — WITH THE REASON, WHICH IS A FACTOR OF TWO FROM SYMMETRY. WindowSquare.lean's own docstring states the structural fact: the balanced squaring battery only ever consumes the GROUP SUMS of the coefficient vector of a*a, so the grouped carry chain reads only 38 group sums of the 341 convolution coefficients — A RANK-38 LINEAR PROJECTION. That is exactly the 'consumer reads only a residue' condition and the tree exploits it: 372 instead of 681, via S(c) = beta(c)^2 + (c - t^9)*Hi(c) checked at 38 compile-time points. Per point the cost is ceil(rank/2) rows, and the ranks over the BN254 scalar field are EXACTLY: square window 9 -> 5 rows -> 10 per point -> 380 (live 372 after TailSquare5); q*n window 18 -> 9 rows -> 18 per point -> 684 AGAINST THE CURRENT 681, LOSING 3; fused difference certificate 27 -> 14 rows -> 28 per point -> 1,064 against 1,053, LOSING 11. THE MECHANISM: the 9x9 anti-triangular staircase M[i][j] = [i+j >= 9] has rank exactly 8 (verified gw = 4..15, always gw-1); the SQUARE gets ceil(8/2) = 4 products from the symmetric discount while a genuine BILINEAR q*n gets 8. THAT FACTOR OF TWO IS THE WHOLE STORY, and the gap has WIDENED from 3 to 11 on the fused variant since TailSquare5 landed. WINOGRAD CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE (Math. Systems Theory 10 (1977) 169-180, DOI 10.1007/BF01683270): 2N - k products are necessary with k the number of DISTINCT irreducible factors (P need not be squarefree), tight when |F| >= 2*max deg(P_i^e_i) - 2; generalised by Alder-Strassen (TCS 15(2):201-211, 1981) to R(A) >= 2 dim A - t(A). BN254 clears the field condition by about 2^246.

GLV DESIGN SPACE — CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT ARGUMENT (a subagent compiled real gnark circuits for secp256k1 emulated over BN254, PATCHING OUT gnark's lookup-based range checker so the numbers are in OUR model). Loop totals, plain R1CS: naive 256-bit ladder 958486; classic 2-dim GLV 452744; fake-GLV without endomorphism 452398; 4-dim GLV+fake-GLV at 66 bits 288019. THE 4-DIM CONSTRUCTION IS THE RIGHT ONE and the extra two lattice dimensions come from NON-DETERMINISTIC ADVICE, not from the curve: hint Q = [s]P and verify a relation, which makes the kernel lattice rank 4 with determinant n and all four coefficients about n^(1/4). GENERAL LAW, matching gnark-crypto's own documented bounds to within half a bit: allowing t points in the verified relation gives rank 2t, determinant n^(t-1), coefficients Theta(n^((t-1)/(2t))) — 1.15*sqrt(r) at t=1, 1.25*r^(1/4) at t=2, 1.28*r^(1/3) at t=3. CRUCIALLY THAT EXPONENT INCREASES WITH t, so beyond 4 dimensions the loop gets LONGER: measured 6-dim costs 370251 against 4-dim's 256287, plus about 80k more precomputation — a 70% loss. Per-iteration cost is nearly FLAT in dimension (3727/3810/4104 rows per iteration at 2/4/6 dims), so in-circuit cost is essentially iterations x constant and iterations = bit length. This is why the software result of eprint 2025/1151 (three scalars of a third the size, ~20% faster verification) DOES NOT TRANSFER to circuits, and why gnark ships the 6-dim variant only for NATIVE twisted Edwards with LogUp, never for emulated curves. Window size confirmed too: at 4 dims w=1 is the global optimum (256287) and w=2 loses badly (331953).

CORRECTION — A SIGN SELECT ON AN EMULATED POINT IS 4 ALLOCATIONS + 4 CONSTRAINTS, NOT ~599. I earlier costed the fake-GLV sign handling at about 599 rows for one emulated Select. In this cost model a mux over a 4-limb Emu value is literally 4 rows (one per limb), so the record's four sign selects total 16 allocations + 16 constraints. THE DESIGN RULE THAT MATTERS: mux only the SIGN-DEPENDENT part. Negating a point changes y and nothing else, so muxing a whole 9-cell FlaggedPoint wastes rows on x and isInf. The underlying advice — handle signs by negating the POINTS, never the scalars, and keep the loop free of sign work — stands and is what the record does.

MEASURED TARGET FOR THE MODMUL: 845 SCORE, AGAINST OUR 1463 (mulModSub2Cost = 728 alloc + 735 constr). These numbers come from actually compiling circuits with circom 2.2.3 and reading row counts out of the .r1cs with snarkjs, then witness-testing on 508 vectors including the worst case (p-1)^2 — not from a paper. Reference points, as rows + allocations: circom-ecdsa BigMultModP(64,4) = 7707; circom-pairing FpMultiply(43,6) at secp256k1 = 2509; fold with tightened carry parameters at n=32,k=8 = 1527; FOLD + CRT at n=32,k=8 = 845 (424 rows + 421 allocs). THREE INGREDIENTS, IN ORDER OF IMPORTANCE. (1) THE PRODUCT IS ALREADY FREE — the full 256x256 limb product is 2k-1 rows by asserting the limb-polynomial identity at 2k-1 evaluation points (circom-ecdsa's BigMultNoCarry is 7 rows), so 99.8% of a naive BigMultModP is carries and range checks and NO effort should go into the multiplication. (2) THE FOLD IS FREE FOR EVERY MODULUS — reducing the 2k-1 product limbs back to k via precomputed constants 2^(n(k+i)) mod p is a LINEAR COMBINATION, zero rows. What p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977 buys is that the fold coefficients are TINY (literally 977 and 1 when n = 32, because c = 2^32 + 977 is limb-aligned there), which cascades: folded limb width 77 bits instead of 101, quotient bound 36 bits instead of 68, CRT limbs 2 instead of 3, carry width 46 instead of 70 — worth about 27% (424 vs 578 rows for a generic 256-bit prime, both compiled). USE n = 32 PRECISELY BECAUSE c IS LIMB-ALIGNED THERE. (3) THE BIG ONE — CHECK THE IDENTITY BY CRT, NOT BY A CARRY CHAIN (Lubarov and Baylina, 'Casting out Primes', eprint 2022/1470): verify under a FIXED set of moduli M = {r_BN254, 2^(nT)} and conclude the identity holds mod lcm(M), which suffices when |f| < lcm(M). NOTE THIS NEEDS NO RANDOM CHALLENGE — the moduli are fixed constants, so it maps to plain R1CS. Mod r_BN254 the check R - p*X - out = 0 is ONE PURELY LINEAR ROW because the modulus is a CONSTANT; mod 2^(nT) only T = 2 carries at 46 bits are needed instead of a full chain of 8. Soundness margin measured at 25 bits (|D|max = 2^293 < r*2^64 = 2^318) and brute-forced on scaled-down analogues. CAVEAT FOR RSA: there the modulus is an INPUT, so p*X is a genuine product and the native leg is NOT free — this transfers to the secp challenges much better than to RSA.

SPARSE-PRIME CANONICITY IS 8 ALLOCATIONS + 11 CONSTRAINTS GIVEN THE BITS — MY EARLIER '37 ROWS' WAS 2x TOO HIGH. Comparing an already-decomposed 256-bit value against p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977 needs neither a subtraction nor a generic lexicographic comparator, because p's binary expansion has ONLY SIX ZERO BITS (positions 32, 9, 8, 7, 6, 4) and everything else is 1. So x < p iff some all-one run of p contains a zero of x, checked as a short prefix chain: (1) topEq <- IsZeroField(sum of deficit bits over positions 255..33), then one row topEq*b[32] = 0; (2) midEq <- IsZeroField(deficit over 31..10), throughMid <== topEq*midEq; (3) ONE row throughMid*(b[9]+b[8]+b[7]+b[6]) = 0 — four boolean bits sum below the native modulus, so one row enforces all four; (4) through5 <== throughMid*b[5]; (5) lowEq <- IsZeroField(deficit over 3..0), one row through5*(b[4] + lowEq) = 0. TOTAL 8 allocations / 11 constraints ON TOP of the decomposition = 19 score, against 260/265 for Normalize + LessThan. THE METHOD IS GENERIC: count the ZERO bits of the modulus, summarise each all-one run with one IsZeroField, chain the prefix-equality state with one product per run boundary — rows scale with the number of ZERO BITS of p, not with 256.

THE PSEUDO-MERSENNE QUOTIENT FOLD IS NOW IMPLEMENTED AND IT WAS THE WHOLE 36% CUT — MY EARLIER ESTIMATE UNDERSTATED IT. p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977, so 2^256 = cFold = 2^32 + 977, and the 7 product cells fold onto 4 by d_k = c_k + cFold*c_{k+4} — a FREE linear recombination because cFold is a compile-time constant. THE POINT IS WHAT THAT DOES TO THE QUOTIENT: instead of witnessing q as a 4-limb BigInt and paying a 252-row Normalize on it, q becomes ONE FIELD ELEMENT WITH A 71-BIT RANGE CHECK, and the carry chain collapses from 3 carries at 68 bits to ONE carry at 107 bits (grouped schedule L=6, groups [2,1,3], G=3). MEASURED: the target certificate goes 464/468 -> 184/186, so a multiply-subtract goes 728/735 -> 448/453 — 562 score per certificate, not the 316 I predicted. Across 350 live certificates that is 196,700, which is essentially the entire 559597 -> 355748 improvement. I also predicted GroupedEqXV would be 'a wash'; it is better than a wash. IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE: FoldParams / FoldTheorems.lhsVec+rhsVec / FoldTarget / MulModFold.

THE Y-FREE (x, lambda) LOOP IS 4 CERTIFICATES NOT 5 AND IS WORTH ~55k — BUT IT IS BLOCKED BY THE IDENTITY TABLE ENTRY, SO DO NOT ATTEMPT IT BEFORE RECODING. This replaces my earlier note that simply called it the biggest lever; the algebra is better than I said and the obstruction is one I had not seen. THE ALGEBRA WORKS, AND THE SAVING COMES FROM REUSING AN EXISTING CONSTRAINT. Our Slope2 already computes the halo2 quantity: its Spec asserts w*(xSe - rx) = 2*ry, i.e. 2y = w*(x_S - x). Stop treating that as the equation that DETERMINES w and treat it as the DEFINITION of y, and y/y' stop being witnesses. Four witnesses (lam1, x_S, w, x') and four constraints: (1) lam1*(t_x - x) = t_y - w*(x_S - x)/2; (2) x_S = lam1^2 - x - t_x; (3) x' = A^2 - x_S - x with A = lam1 + w free affine; (4) HANDOFF w'*(x_S' - x') + w*(x_S - x) = 2*A*(x' - x), which is the old y' = A(x'-x) - y with BOTH y's substituted — step i's from its own (w, x_S), step i+1's from ITS own (w', x_S'). Constraint (4) needs ZERO extra convolutions: its own is A*(x'-x), w*(x_S-x) is reused free from (1), and w'*(x_S'-x') free from step i+1. THE T-FORM PORT OF THE FIXED-BASE SIBLING IS THE WRONG DESIGN AND IS NEARLY WORTHLESS: anchoring the implied y to the last table point (y = lam*(u-x) - v) needs a FIFTH witness lam' — the chord slope of 2R and T — with its own certificate, giving 5 FRESH + 5 CERT + 2 convolutions = 2214/2239, a saving of only 84 per step.

x-ONLY ARITHMETIC: MY EARLIER COSTING WAS 2.5x TOO PESSIMISTIC, BUT THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES. I previously wrote that a Brier-Joye x-only ladder is '~10 field muls per bit ~ 2560 modmuls ~ 1.9M rows'. THE CORRECT FORMULAS ARE ONE DEGREE-4 CONGRUENCE PER GROUP OPERATION, both VERIFIED 200/200 on secp256k1: xADD is x+ * x- * (x1 - x2)^2 = (x1*x2)^2 - 28*(x1 + x2), and xDBL is 4*x'*(x^3 + 7) = x^4 - 56*x. These are Vieta applied to Semaev's third summation polynomial, which for b = 7 symmetrises to the 9-monomial e2^2 - 4*e1*e3 - 28*e1 = 0 (also verified 200/200). At 8x32 a D=4 certificate is 1004, so an x-only group operation is 512 + 1004 = 1516 against 2 x 745 = 1490 for a y-free affine one — A WASH PER OPERATION. IT STILL LOSES BY ABOUT 4x OVERALL, and the reason is STRUCTURAL, NOT ARITHMETIC: x-only forces a LADDER (the difference must be pinned), which forbids windowing and forbids the 4-dimensional fake-GLV, so it costs ~512 operations against our 62 steps. Real total about 775k, not 1.9M. ALSO STATE THE DO-NOT-TRY CORRECTLY: secp256k1 having prime order rules out the MONTGOMERY MODEL, not x-only differential arithmetic, which exists on every short Weierstrass curve. S_4 (191 monomials, degree 12, ~11 units) and S_5 (degree 32) are dead; division polynomials psi_n are degree n^2; elliptic nets / EDS are 8 independent degree-4 congruences per bit, about 19x worse than our 1.25.
GLV: decompose k = k1 + k2*lambda (mod n) into two ~128-bit halves; the endomorphism psi(x,y)=(beta*x mod p, y) costs ~6 constraints; then k*P = k1*P + k2*psi(P) halves the number of doublings.

GLV-3 / higher-dimensional decomposition (eprint 2025/1151, 2025/933): split k into THREE ~85-bit sub-scalars using the endomorphism twice (k = k0 + k1*lambda + k2*lambda^2 mod n); ~85 doublings instead of ~128, run as a joint 3-MSM sharing every doubling. Fewer doublings = fewer non-native Fp ops.

Find SHORTEST decomposition vectors via integer lattice reduction or a half-extended Euclidean algorithm in the endomorphism ring (eprint 2025/933); secp256k1's small CM discriminant (D=-3, j=0) admits extra reductions (reported 22-53% proving-time drop vs prior SOTA).
Run the decomposed halves/thirds as a width-w windowed joint-MSM (double-then-add) sharing doublings — reference figure ~2176 constraints for the 2-MSM core.
Per scalar bit the naive cost is ~4 (point selects) + ~4 (adds) + ~2 (double); wNAF / signed-digit windows cut the number of ADDITIONS via longer zero runs.

PRIME-REDUCE for a FIXED prime (circom-ecdsa): do limb mul/add WITHOUT carries into a wide form (k=4 x 64-bit registers for 256-bit; a product spans ~10 registers), then collapse 10 registers back to 4 in ONE reduction (~1000 constraints) by subtracting PRECOMPUTED multiples of p — compile-time constants because p is fixed. DEFERRAL BUDGET: keep 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < 254 (native field bits); that inequality tells you exactly how many unreduced products you may accumulate before a carry/reduce pass is actually required — defer right up to it, not further.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce, ~2x fewer reductions): accumulate a*b +/- c*d in WIDE UNREDUCED limbs and reduce ONCE at the end. Affine EC formulas are exactly this shape — lambda = (y2-y1)*inv(x2-x1), x3 = lambda^2 - x1 - x2, y3 = lambda*(x1-x3) - y1 — so reduce once PER OUTPUT COORDINATE, never per intermediate product.

DEFINITIVE CLOSURE OF THE COORDINATE-SYSTEM QUESTION, WITH THE RIGHT REASON — MY EARLIER REASON WAS WRONG. I wrote that 'an inversion costs ~1 allocation + 1 constraint'. THAT IS FALSE HERE: in the emulated setting a hinted inverse must be certified by x*inv = 1 mod p, which is a FULL certificate at ~901. What is actually true is that an affine DIVISION lam = num/den is ONE certificate (den*lam = num), i.e. exactly one modular multiplication — so I = M = S = 1 reduction, and every result in the ECC literature since 1985 optimises the ratio I/M in [8, 100] and therefore RUNS BACKWARDS here. Re-costed by MATERIALISATIONS PER GROUP OPERATION, which is what the master cost law charges for: affine (x,y) add 3 / double 3 (the 3x^2 folds into the slope certificate); affine (x, lambda) 2; affine (x, lambda) with the degree-3 merge 1.5; Jacobian 7-9; projective-complete 9-10; Meloni co-Z >= 10. JACOBIAN IS 3.5x WORSE, and no amount of free raw products rescues it, because a Jacobian doubling is degree 4 in (X, Y, Z) and degree 4 already costs more than two materialisations. EFD shortw/jacobian-0 confirms: DBL 2M+5S = 7 reductions against affine 3, ADD 11M+5S = 16 against 3. ALSO CLOSED: Montgomery's simultaneous-inversion trick is 3m-2 reductions against m for m hinted inversions — STRICTLY WORSE FOR EVERY m >= 2, do not batch inversions.
Use INCOMPLETE / affine addition formulas (cheaper than complete-addition) where exceptional cases are ruled out by the decomposition, guarded by a soundness argument.

Precomputed-points-as-HINTS (eprint 2025/933): compute the scalar-mul result and per-step accumulator points OUTSIDE the circuit and pass them as witnesses; the circuit only CHECKS each group-law relation, which is cheaper than deriving points in-circuit. The prior R1CS baseline was ~9 constraints per scalar bit — beat that per bit.

AUDIT FOR OVER-ALLOCATION in the incomplete-add ladder (circom-ecdsa finding): only the first ~3 steps actually need the complete-addition guard, so accumulator/point arrays sized [bits] can be cut to [bits-3] and [3]. Allocations are HALF the cost metric here — sweep every witness array for entries that are never constrained or never read.

Non-native Fp: minimal-limb schoolbook mul + reduce with carry-save accumulation and top-bit-fold limb range checks; the flexible-limb EqViaCarries family (see reference/) may pack the equality check tighter.

THE EISENTRAEGER-LAUTER-MONTGOMERY RECASTING: COMPUTE [2]P + Q AS (P+Q)+P AND NEVER FORM y_R — 5 ROWS PER DOUBLE-AND-ADD STEP INSTEAD OF 7. Source: zcash/zcash issue #3924 ('Faster variable-base scalar multiplication in zk-SNARK circuits'), which claims 6 constraints/bit against a prior best of 8.5 with recoded scalars. WARNING, AND THIS IS WHY IT CANNOT BE COPIED VERBATIM: the equations in that issue are for a MONTGOMERY curve B*y^2 = x^3 + A*x^2 + x, and secp256k1 has PRIME ORDER so it has no Montgomery form at all (see the Montgomery-ladder do-not-try note). Only the RECASTING transfers. DERIVED AND VERIFIED HERE for short Weierstrass with a = 0: the point is that y_R of the intermediate R = P+Q is never needed, because lam2 = (y_R - y_P)/(x_R - x_P) simplifies to lam1 + lam2 = -2*y_P/(x_R - x_P). FIVE ROWS, five allocations: (1) (x_Q - x_P)*lam1 = y_Q - y_P; (2) lam1*lam1 = x_R + x_P + x_Q; (3) (x_R - x_P)*(lam1 + lam2) = -2*y_P; (4) lam2*lam2 = x_S + x_P + x_R; (5) (x_P - x_S)*lam2 = y_S + y_P. Against the naive route — double (x*x = xsq; (2y)*lam = 3*xsq + a; lam*lam = x2 + 2x; (x - x2)*lam = y2 + y, 4 rows) then add (3 rows) = 7 — that is 2 rows AND 2 allocations saved, i.e. 4 SCORE PER SCALAR BIT. VERIFIED: 39991/39991 exact matches against reference (P+Q)+P over a small curve with a = 0, every output on the curve. THE EXCEPTIONAL CASES ARE COMPLETELY CHARACTERIZED, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE GUARD CHEAP: exactly two rows can degenerate — row 1 when x_Q = x_P (i.e. Q = +-P), and row 3 when x_R = x_P, which happens IF AND ONLY IF Q = -2P (verified: every sampled degeneracy was exactly that). Nothing else can fail, so an exception guard needs those two tests and no more. HONEST RANKING AGAINST WHAT WE ALREADY HAVE: the halo2 'never witness y in the loop' note above is the STRONGER form — it carries (x_A, lam) and drops row 5 as well, so ELM is strictly an intermediate. Use ELM where a y-coordinate genuinely has to exist at that step (window boundaries, the final point), and halo2's ladder everywhere else.

SLOPE-ONLY TERMINAL ASSERTION — PROVING 2*A + T = O COSTS ONE SLOPE GADGET AND FOUR ROWS, NOT A DOUBLE-AND-ADD. When the last step of a scalar-mul or MSM only has to ASSERT that the accumulator chain closes to infinity, do not compute 2A+T and test the flag. Write S = A + T for the chord sum: the chord formula gives y_S = lambda*(x_A - x_S) - y_A, which collapses to -y_A exactly when x_S = x_A. So 2A + T = O <=> S = -A <=> x_S = x_A. A slope gadget already produces lambda and x_S = lambda^2 - x_A - x_T, so the whole assertion is ONE row A.isInf - T.isInf = 0 plus FOUR rows (1 - A.isInf)*(x_S[k] - x_A[k]) = 0. MEASURED (secp256k1 over BN254, 4 limbs x 64 bits): 1070 allocations / 1085 constraints, against 1792/1809 for double-then-cancel and 1783/1802 for assert-negated-sum — 722 allocations and 724 constraints saved, and being a pure assertion it materialises no output point. THE ONE SOUNDNESS OBLIGATION: the degenerate branch where x_T = x_A makes the slope gadget return the TANGENT, and you must show that branch cannot satisfy the assertion. For a = 0, b = 7 it forces lambda^2 = 3x together with 2*y*lambda = 3x^2, hence x^3 = -28 and y^2 = -21; -21 is a quadratic NON-RESIDUE mod p, proved by one kernel `decide` on a binary modPow at ZERO circuit rows. Re-derive the analogous non-residue before using this on another curve.

DO NOT ASSUME COMPLETE ADDITION IS EXPENSIVE — WITH LIMB-LEVEL MUXES IT IS 1.3% OF A STEP, AND THIS OVERTURNS THE USUAL ADVICE. The received wisdom (and my own earlier notes) says to use incomplete affine addition and discharge the exceptions by a soundness argument. MEASURED, THAT IS THE WRONG TRADE IN THIS COST MODEL: a FULLY COMPLETE fused double-add step is 2346 allocations / 2371 constraints, of which the entire exception apparatus is about 30 allocations — the other 97.9% is the five non-native certificates. The apparatus is two 9-cell point muxes (9/9 each) for A = O and T = -A, two 256-bit equality tests at 5/5, and one 2/2 opposite-y detector. THREE TRICKS MAKE IT THIS CHEAP. (1) 256-BIT EQUALITY IN 5 ROWS: pack limbs 0,1 into one native element and limbs 2,3 into another (each under 128 bits, safely below the native modulus), run two IsZeroField at 2/2, AND them with one row. DO NOT COMPARE LIMBWISE. (2) T = -A IN 2 ROWS USING ONE LIMB: witness inv of y_A[0] - y_T[0], set oppY <== yDiff*inv, assert yDiff*(sameX - oppY) = 0. Only the LOW LIMB is needed, because two finite points with equal x are equal or opposite and p is odd, so y != -y already differs in limb 0. (3) A BOOLEAN OR THAT COSTS ZERO: if one input IMPLIES the other (here T = O re-routes the intermediate x so sameX is forced to 1), the OR EQUALS the implied flag, and a downstream flag - other is a free affine expression instead of a witness plus a row. SO: reach for incomplete formulas only where a cheaper SPECIALISED gadget results — e.g. adding P to phi(P), where x_{phiP} != x_P is free from beta != 1 and x != 0, worth 63 allocations — and not to avoid completeness per se.

DEFERRED SUM-OF-EIGHT MOD-n CONGRUENCE IN 38 ALLOCATIONS / 44 CONSTRAINTS. The GLV scalar-side relation u1 + lambda*u2 + s*(v1 + lambda*v2) = 0 (mod n) decomposes into four mod-n products; DO NOT REDUCE THEIR SUM. Split each term by its sign into a positive and a negative bucket, bias the positive side by a constant 4n (free — n is a compile-time constant so 4n is a constant limb vector), witness a SINGLE quotient q, range-check it to THREE BITS (2 allocations / 3 constraints), and assert sum(positives) + 4n = sum(negatives) + q*n with ONE grouped-carry limb equality (35/41). TOTAL 38/44. Against reducing each partial sum mod n that is roughly a 4x saving on the tail of the decomposition proof, and it is why the whole scalar relation is 2932/2954 = 1.65% of a 355748-score circuit. THE BIAS CONSTANT IS THE DESIGN PARAMETER: choose it so every limb of the positive side stays non-negative and the quotient bound stays tiny — four signed terms each below n need 4n and give q < 8.

THE RECORD'S TOP-LEVEL SHAPE, FOR ORIENTATION (355748 = 176973 allocations + 178775 constraints, read from its own cost proofs). 4-dimensional FAKE GLV with the result WITNESSED, never computed: witness Q (9 cells, 0 constraints), validate it on-curve and canonical (1864/1895 — which ALSO emits the output bytes for free), witness four signed 64-bit coefficients (260 allocations) with booleanity (260 constraints), assert the mod-n scalar relation (2932/2954), build a 16-entry table of all subset sums of {+-P, +-phiP, +-Q, +-phiQ} (16881/17074), then run a 64-position 4-way interleaved MSM that ENDS IN AN ASSERTION that u1*P + u2*phiP + v1*Q + v2*phiQ = O (155027/156592). NO RECODING AT ALL — no NAF, no wNAF, no signed digits; plain binary magnitude with one sign bit per coefficient, and signs applied to the TABLE POINTS. Window width 1 per coefficient, interleaved 4-wide, so each position consumes a 4-bit nibble indexing the 16-entry table. THE LOOP IS 87.6% OF THE CIRCUIT and one step is 2481/2506 = VarLookup 135/135 (a 4-level mux tree of 15 9-cell point muxes) plus FusedStep 2346/2371. The coefficient bound 2^64 = n^(1/4) comes from a PIGEONHOLE argument, not a lattice algorithm: (2^64)^4 > n forces a collision, and the short-coefficient property is used in exactly one place — ruling out the u = v = 0 forgery.

WHY THE Y-FREE LOOP IS CURRENTLY UNSATISFIABLE, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS A DIFFERENT PROJECT. The invariant 2y = w*(x_S - x) defines y only when x_S != x. Slope2.main FORCES x_S = x whenever T = O — `let xSe <- Mux { selector := tIsInf, ifTrue := rx, ifFalse := xS }` — deliberately, to reach the tangent branch. AND T = O IS GENERIC, NOT ADVERSARIAL: GLVBuildTable.lean:124 proves `subsetPoint B 0 = .infinity`, i.e. TABLE ENTRY 0 IS THE POINT AT INFINITY, because the table is SUBSET sums with no recoding. Nibble 0000 selects it with probability 1/16 per position; over 62 interior steps the expected count is 3.9 and P(never) = (15/16)^62 = 1.8%. So on essentially every honest input the y-free system asserts 0 = 2y and THE CIRCUIT IS UNSATISFIABLE — a completeness failure, not a corner case. DROPPING THE CONSTRAINT INSTEAD IS A TOTAL SOUNDNESS BREAK: w unconstrained => A = lam1 + w unconstrained => x' unconstrained => the accumulator is steerable => the terminal `= O` assertion is free, and because fake-GLV WITNESSES Q the prover can engineer the collision at will. Halo2 is safe only because its base is fixed and public and its exclusion argument (Halo paper Thm 3 plus an integer index-shadow loop) runs over Z with one bounded scalar; our rank-4 lattice with witnessed Q and phiQ = lambda*Q admits no such argument. FOUR ESCAPES CHECKED, ALL CLOSED: (i) tangent from the implied y is w*w*(x_S-x) = 3x^2, DEGREE 3 — our interpolatedMul is a degree-2 convolution at 7 points with a 71-bit folded quotient, and a triple product needs 10 points and a ~512-bit quotient, dearer than the 531 saved; (ii) the T-form is non-degenerate at x_S = x but its tangent is still cubic in mu*lam*(u-x), and reducing it needs a witnessed pi = w*lam at 440/445 — exactly what was saved; (iii) a reciprocal state iota = 1/(2y) makes the tangent degree 2 but the CHORD cubic; (iv) an offset/blinding point making the table O-free needs Delta != -T_j for 16 adversarial T_j. THE PREREQUISITE IS THE ALL-ODD SIGNED-DIGIT RECODE (see the fixed-base sibling's free-recode entry, 0/0 cost) so that no nibble can select the identity. Sequence it that way — the recode is independently valuable and also unblocks incomplete addition in the table build. EVEN AFTER THE RECODE, S = +-R (i.e. T = -2R) still has to be excluded by an index argument that could not be constructed for adversarial Q. TREAT THAT, NOT THE ALGEBRA, AS THE REAL OPEN QUESTION.

THE MASTER COST LAW, DERIVED FROM THE RECORD'S OWN GADGETS AND CALIBRATED TO 1.6%: score ~= 2 * M * (256 + Wq + Wc), where M is THE NUMBER OF MATERIALISED EMULATED FIELD ELEMENTS. The multiply-subtract decomposes EXACTLY as 512 + 19 + 370: 512 = 4 limbs x (63 alloc + 64 constr) of ToBitsAffine plus 4 witness allocs = materialising ONE element; 19 = the sparse x

= 256 rows; the record's 252 allocations + 256 constraints is EXACTLY that floor. DEGREE-3 CERTIFICATES: PUT A POLYNOMIAL IN A *FACTOR*, NOT ONLY IN THE TARGET, AND DELETE A WHOLE MATERIALISATION. The corpus already keeps a raw convolution as a certificate TARGET (free). The new move is to keep one as a FACTOR, which costs one extra fold level and is affordable ONLY once f is small. MEASURED IN THE MODEL: CERT(D=3) is 1597 at 4x64 — the folded position exceeds 2^253, INFEASIBLE, the group check cannot pack even one position — but 454 at 8x32. Since a materialisation is 531, the merge gain is -700 (A LOSS) at 4x64 and +290 at 8x32. THE CONCRETE MERGE, VERIFIED 200/200 AGAINST REAL secp256k1 POINTS: ELM rows (2) and (3) fuse into ONE degree-3 certificate that never materialises x_R — (lam1^2 - 2*xP - xQ)*(lam1 + lam2) + 2*yP = 0 (mod p), materialising lam2 only — and row (4) becomes x_S = lam2 (x) lam2 - lam1 (x) lam1 + xQ, a degree-2 certificate with TWO convolutions under one quotient, which also never touches x_R. A y-free ELM step therefore goes from 4 materialisations to 3. Modelled at -29,200 over 62 steps. THE DEGREE CEILING, for the record: at 8x32, D=2 costs 214, D=3 454, D=4 1004, D=5 dead (fold overflow); D=4 also needs 7 <= k <= 9 or the 2m-1-point interpolation itself overflows the native field. GENERAL RULE: a value consumed ONLY ADDITIVELY can be carried as a polynomial for free at any depth; a value consumed MULTIPLICATIVELY must either be materialised (531) or raise the certificate degree (+240 for D=2->3, +550 for D=3->4). Compare those two numbers before witnessing anything.

PORT THE FIXED-BASE ALL-ODD RECODE INTO THE VARIABLE-BASE LOOP — IT HALVES THE TABLE, HALVES THE LOOKUP, AND DELETES THE EXCEPTION APPARATUS. Recode each 64-bit fake-GLV coefficient with digits d_i = 2*b_i - 1 in {+-1} (a pure wire permutation, 0/0), so sum d_i 2^i = 2m - 2^64 + 1 and EVERY DIGIT IS NONZERO. Then no position can select the identity and no two consecutive sites can collide, so the whole loop uses INCOMPLETE addition guarded by a Lean hypothesis: -100 per step of exception apparatus. The table becomes 8 entries (+- pairs) instead of 16, so VarLookup goes from 15 muxes of 9 cells to 7 muxes of 8 cells plus a k-row conditional y-negation: 135 -> 60 rows at k=4, 255 -> 120 at k=8. THE PARITY OBLIGATION AND ITS HONEST PRICE: the fake-GLV kernel lattice has determinant n, which is ODD, so it surjects onto (Z/2)^4 and an all-odd representative ALWAYS exists — but the pigeonhole bound then needs |u| < 2^65..2^66, i.e. ONE OR TWO EXTRA LOOP STEPS (+3k to +6k) against ~22k saved. CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE IF THAT IS UNPALATABLE: offset every table entry by a fixed constant point C; the accumulated (2^64 - 1)*C is a compile-time constant, so the terminal assertion becomes sum = (2^64 - 1)*C at ZERO cost — though that only kills the identity case, not consecutive collisions. NOTE THIS IS ALSO THE PREREQUISITE FOR THE Y-FREE LOOP, which is blocked precisely because table entry 0 is the point at infinity.

THE j=0 CM IDENTITY P + phi(P) = (beta^2 * x, -y) COSTS ZERO ROWS — CORRECTING MY OWN 'j-INVARIANT 0 BUYS NOTHING' NOTE. Because 1 + lambda + lambda^2 = 0 in the endomorphism ring, P, phi(P) and phi^2(P) are COLLINEAR (they are the three intersections of the horizontal line y = y_P with y^2 = x^3 + 7), so P + phi(P) = -phi^2(P) = (beta^2 * x_P, -y_P) — a pure constant scaling and a negation, BOTH FREE. VERIFIED 200/200 on real secp256k1 points. The 16-entry fake-GLV table needs 11 non-trivial subset sums of {P, phiP, Q, phiQ}; two of them (P + phiP and Q + phiQ) are now free, so the build drops from about 12.6 additions to 9, worth roughly -5,400. In the 8-entry +- table of the all-odd recode the same identity gives A = P + phiP and C = Q + phiQ free, leaving 10 additions. MY EARLIER NOTE SAID 'j-invariant 0 / a = 0 buys exactly zero rows' — that is true of the ENDOMORPHISM EVALUATION (a field addition is free), but the COLLINEARITY relation is a genuine free group addition and the corpus was not using it.

FAKE GLV CANNOT GO PAST DIMENSION 4, AND THE REASON IS SOUNDNESS, NOT COST. I previously recorded only that 6-dim measured 70% worse. The sharper fact: adding a THIRD witnessed point R with a prover-chosen multiple makes the kernel lattice rank 6 with coefficients ~n^(1/6) ~ 2^43, but the relation u1*P + u2*phiP + v1*Q + v2*phiQ + w1*R + w2*phiR = O is SATISFIABLE FOR ANY Q by choosing R appropriately — the verifier can only check the mod-n scalar congruence for the KNOWN scalars, so R is unconstrained and soundness collapses outright. Genuine 8-dimensional GLV needs a GLS curve over F_p^2. 64 POSITIONS IS THE FLOOR FOR THIS FAMILY; stop sweeping the dimension. RELATEDLY, DETERMINISTIC BATCHING OF THE PER-STEP CONGRUENCES IS CLOSED BOTH WAYS: asserting sum_i 2^(s*i) * D_i = 0 over the integers IS sound (radix uniqueness pins each D_i = 0 given |D_i| < 2^(s-1)) — but it SAVES NOTHING, because the grouped-carry cost is linear in the number of limb POSITIONS and stacking three certificates triples the positions. Schul-Ganz & Segev, 'Accumulators in (and Beyond) Generic Groups: Non-Trivial Batch Verification Requires Interaction', TCC 2020 / eprint 2020/1106, prove the general statement. THE ONE TECHNIQUE THAT DOES BEAT RECOMPUTATION for Q = [k]P is Eagen's ECIP (eprint 2022/596, ~100x fewer multiplications via principal divisors and Weil reciprocity) and it buys that saving PRECISELY by evaluating at a random point — so it is the single escape hatch if the no-challenge constraint ever relaxes, and nothing else in the ECDLP, index-calculus, EDS or VDF literature is deterministic.

DROP CANONICITY ON WITNESSED SLOPES — THE RIVAL DOES THIS AND WE DO NOT, AND IT IS WORTH ~2584. Measured against RajeshRk18's 561573 tree: ValidP is 260/267 in BOTH trees, but the rival adds NormalizeFe at 252/256 and uses it where we use ValidP. Delta 8 allocations + 11 constraints = 19 SCORE PER USE. MECHANISM: NormalizeFe is just the four ToBitsAffine 63 limb decompositions proving BigInt.Normalized (value < 2^256); it OMITS ValidP's sparse-prime tail (3 IsZeroField + 2 prefix products + 3 quadratic assertions). A slope lambda is a DIVISION WITNESS THAT ONLY EVER FEEDS MULTIPLICATION CERTIFICATES, so it never needs to be the canonical representative — canonicity is uniqueness, and nothing downstream needs uniqueness. THE PORT IS EASIER FOR US THAN FOR THEM. Their version needs widened-quotient scaffolding (Fe.ValidW2 widened to 2^(64*4+1)-1, the hab_lt hypothesis dropped, quotient bound q < 6*2^(Bm) instead of q < 6n) because their certificates carry a value bound on a. OURS DO NOT: MulModFold.Assumptions and MulModFoldT.Assumptions are PURELY LIMBWISE — (all i, a[i].val < Ca) and (all i, b[i].val < Cb) and (all i, target[i].val < Nt) — with NO value bound on a at all, and in MulModSub2W2 the ha_valid.2 component is never used. So we only need to (i) swap ValidP.circuit lam for a NormalizeFe-style assertion in DivOrZeroF3 and DivUncheckedD3, (ii) weaken three Assumptions, (iii) re-prove the two hlam_valid.2 uses in the den = 0 branch via divisibility — take hdvd : p divides value(lam) and conclude decodeFe lam = 0 by ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff, which is all any consumer needs. INSTANCE COUNT: 62 glvStep x 2 (slopeXS + slope2) + 1 glvStepLastSlope + 9 completeAdd in the table = 134 divOrZeroF3, plus 2 divUncheckedD3 in phiPairAdd = 136 x 19 = 2584.

EVERYTHING ABOUT THE INPUT POINT IS ASSUMED — RE-AUDIT ANY ROW THAT VALIDATES P. The Interface gives for free: IsBits input.bits (all 256 scalar bits, NO booleanity rows), IsBytes px AND IsBytes py (64 byte range checks), coordVal px < p AND coordVal py < p (TWO FULL CANONICALITY CHECKS), and OnCurve of the decoded base point (A WHOLE MODULAR CERTIFICATE). Because coordBytes are BYTE-ALIGNED, the 4 x 64-bit limbs of px and py are affine recombinations of the input bytes, so materialising the base point costs 0/0. THE ASYMMETRY TO KEEP STRAIGHT: the OUTPUT gets nothing — Spec includes OutputValid, which demands IsBytes on x and y, IsBool isInf, coordVal < p on both, and zero-masking when isInf = 1, all of which the circuit must ENFORCE. Input validation is free; output validation is mandatory. Any row spent proving something about px or py that appears verbatim in Assumptions is pure waste.

TWO MECHANISMS, BOTH REUSABLE. (1) SqEqGated — A GATED CONGRUENCE WITH NO MATERIALISED REMAINDER. It asserts lam*lam = ax + ax + ex (mod p) WHEN THE GATE sel IS ZERO, handing the three-summand target straight to one folded certificate; both the factor and the target are muxed against zero by sel, so on the gated branch the certificate degenerates to 0 = 0 and is satisfied for free. (2) denSafeVec — A ZERO-GUARD THAT IS PURE AFFINE RECOMBINATION. The guarded denominator den + z*e_0 adds the zero-flag z into limb 0 only: when z is set every limb of den vanishes so the vector is the constant 1, otherwise it is den itself. Being affine it costs NO witness and NO row, where a Mux there would have charged 4/4. GENERAL RULE: a guard that must turn a vector into a CONSTANT can often be an affine addend on one limb instead of a multiplexer — look for it wherever a Mux exists only to avoid division by zero.

CORRECTED AND RE-PRICED AGAINST OUR TREE — THE HORIZONTAL-LINE REGROUPING IS REAL ALGEBRA BUT IS NOT A TABLE OPTIMISATION, AND ITS 'FREE' ENTRIES ARE NOT FREE. The identity is sound: for R=(x,y) with x != 0 the chord to (beta*x, y) has slope exactly 0, so x3 = -(1+beta)x = beta^2 x and y3 = -y; the Lean proof is half a page, since beta^3 = 1 and beta != 1 (both by decide) give beta^2 + beta + 1 = 0. BUT 'BOTH COORDINATES ARE FREE AFFINE' IS FALSE IN OUR REPRESENTATION: secp is NON-NATIVE, so beta^2 * x mod p is not an affine combination of x's limbs — it is a modular reduction needing a fresh canonical witness, which is exactly MulModBeta32 at 733, of which 512 is the irreducible 256-bit range check on the output. A 'FREE' ENTRY COSTS 733-1310, NOT 0. ONE REAL SHARPENING OVER THE LEAD AS STATED: store the representative phi^2(R) = (beta^2 x_R, +y_R) rather than -phi^2(R), so the y wire is SHARED with R at zero cost and the entry is 733 instead of 1310; under a +-1 table the two differ only by the stored sign. RE-PRICED IN OUR ATOMS the migration yields about -7,300 IN THE TABLE, not the ~10,550 I recorded, and the lead's '39 general + 2 constant' baseline is wrong — we run 33 general + 2 constant (11 adds x 3 certificates). AND IT IS NOT A TABLE REWRITE AT ALL: our Subset builds SIXTEEN entries over 0/1 coefficients consumed by a 4-bit VarLookup, whereas the lead assumes a SIGNED-DIGIT +-1 EIGHT-entry table — so adopting it is a SCALAR-RECODING MIGRATION porting into GLVMSM, GLVStep, VarLookup, GLVScalarRelation and FakeGLVSound. ITS REAL PAYLOAD IS IN THE LOOP, NOT THE TABLE: an 8-entry table halves VarLookup from 15 muxes to 7 (270 -> 126 across 63 lookups = -9,072), netting about -8,568 IF FusedStep can be widened to accept an UNREDUCED table y; if it cannot, the per-step negation costs SubMod 577 x 62 = +35,774 and the idea dies outright. IT ALSO OWES ~+2,719 BACK: a +-1 digit set represents exactly the ODD integers, the fake-GLV lattice does not deliver odd |u_i|, so a parity correction costs one extra VarLookup (135) plus one CompleteAdd (2584). NET ABOUT -13,200, at the cost of re-proving five modules. SOUNDNESS TRAP THE LEAD GOT WRONG: 'R_eps != O' IS NOT PROVABLE — in soundness Q is only assumed Valid and may be O (k = -+1 gives R_+- = O), so the build must be O-TOLERANT rather than assume non-degeneracy. That happens to work out, because beta^2 * 0 = 0 and noXZero_secp gives x = 0 iff infinity, so the free entries need no canon-x mux.

TWO SOUNDNESS AUDITS RAISED AGAINST THE STANDARD CONSTRUCTION — WE PASS BOTH, AND THE REASONS ARE WORTH KEEPING. (1) THE Acc = B_i DEGENERACY. In the incomplete doubleAndAdd(Acc, B_i) = (Acc+B_i)+Acc, the case Acc = +B_i makes the first row read 0*lambda1 = 0, leaving lambda1 COMPLETELY FREE, after which the accumulator is a 1-parameter family and the final equality is one equation in one unknown. gnark defends this by adding a generator G to Acc with the note that Acc = G would mean G = -Phi^2([s+1]P) — A DISCRETE-LOG ARGUMENT, NOT A PROOF — and in fake-GLV the adversary CHOOSES Q as a hint output, so Acc = B_i iff [du]P + [dv]Q = O, satisfiable by setting Q = [-du/dv]([du]P + [2^L]G) with no dlog needed. WE DO NOT HAVE THIS EXPOSURE: our tree contains no GeneratorMultiples and no generator addition; FusedStep.lean:52-62 handles the degeneracy STRUCTURALLY, with SlopeXS computing sameX1 and oppY1 as constrained booleans and `cancel := s1.oppY1` selecting the correct branch, so the slope is never left free. Do not 'simplify' toward the generator-offset design — it would trade a proof for an assumption. (2) THE ITERATION COUNT. The relation lattice {(u1,u2,v1,v2) : (v1 + lambda v2)s + (u1 + lambda u2) = 0 mod n} has DETERMINANT n ~ 2^256 in Z^4, so Minkowski on the L-infinity ball guarantees a nonzero vector with sup-norm <= det^(1/4) = 2^64 AND NO BETTER (the lattice is generic; LLL over 60 random s gave max coefficient in [2^63, 2^64) every time). SO 64 MAGNITUDE BITS IS THE PROVABLE FLOOR, and our coeffBits = 64 with 62 steps is at it. This CORROBORATES, by an independent route, the earlier conclusion that the tightened gnark bound offers us no slack. ADJACENT FREE WIN STILL WORTH TAKING: all four coefficients are <= 64 bits, so every SCALAR-SIDE mod-n multiplication should be arranged to have a 64-bit operand, making its quotient need 64 range-check bits instead of 256 — restructure s(v1 + lambda v2) + u1 + lambda u2 as (s*lambda)*v2 + s*v1 + lambda*u2 + u1 with s*lambda computed once, giving 1 full mulmod plus 3 short-operand ones instead of 3 full. About 1,100.

REJECTED FOR VARIABLE-BASE, WITH THE ARITHMETIC — DO NOT SPEND SLOTS HERE. (a) x-ONLY / MONTGOMERY LADDER / KUMMER: Brier-Joye on short Weierstrass is 15 products per bit, the a=0 specialisation 14, Hamburg's record ladder 11, against affine ELM at 5 and windowed+GLV at ~1.25 mulmods per scalar bit — 3-5x worse. No Montgomery or twisted Edwards model exists because all need rational 2-torsion and #E(secp256k1) is prime (Costello-Smith: a Montgomery curve can never have prime order, always 4 | #E). And a differential ladder CANNOT USE GLV AT ALL, forfeiting the 4x that is the whole point. (b) PROJECTIVE / JACOBIAN: the classical wisdom fully INVERTS — affine ELM is 5 mulmods per step, Jacobian 18, complete Renes-Costello-Batina about 26 — because lambda is ONE ROW here (the reciprocal is witnessed and fused into the multiply, so I ~ M rather than I ~ 80M) and every Z-coordinate is pure overhead. (c) MONTGOMERY'S BATCH INVERSION TRICK IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL: two independent divisions are 2 rows, batching them is 4 — strictly 2x worse at any batch size. (d) TAU-ADIC / ENDOMORPHISM-AS-RADIX: tau = 1-omega costs 4 mulmods per 1.585 norm-bits = 2.52, tau = 2-omega gives 2.85, against doubling at 4 per 2 bits = 2.00 — radix 2 wins outright, and the digit-set closure that makes Koblitz tau-NAF work fails because phi is not free here. (e) LARGER WINDOWS: total mulmods (256/4w)(4(w-1)+5) + 3*2^(4w-1) gives 344 at w=1 and 672 at w=2 — the current 8-entry signed-16 table is exactly optimal. (f) TWO-PASS / HALF-SPLITTING THE SCALARS: [u_lo]P + [u_hi][2^33]P needs 33 doublings for each of [2^33]P and [2^33]Q (264 mulmods) to save 32 steps (160). (g) HIGHER DIMENSION THAN 4 IS STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: End(E) = Z[omega] has Z-RANK 2 and fake-GLV adds exactly one witnessed point, so the relation module has Z-rank 4; any 5th-8th basis point is a Z-combination of the first four and the lattice acquires DEGENERATE short vectors carrying no information about s. The 8-dim variant prices out at 1,044 mulmods against 364, killed by the 128 doublings needed to certify [2^128]P. (h) EAGEN's ECIP / WEIL-RECIPROCITY DIVISOR ARGUMENT — the natural verify-don't-compute candidate — is EXCLUDED because the divisor witness is checked by evaluating a logarithmic derivative at a RANDOM CHALLENGE POINT; with a fixed public challenge a cheating prover crafts the function to pass at that one point. (i) COMBINING TWO MULMOD CERTIFICATES UNDER ONE QUOTIENT is UNSOUND for any fixed K — it constrains only the combination and leaves the prover a degree of freedom; only a random K would work. (j) DERIVING y_T FROM x_T instead of muxing it needs a square root, 3 mulmods per step against 56 for the tree mux — 40x worse.

TABLE-BUILD REJECTIONS, ALL WITH ARITHMETIC — DO NOT RE-PROPOSE. (a) DELETING THE EXCEPTION APPARATUS ON THE NINE CROSS-ADDS (worth 918): impossible, because Q is the CLAIMED RESULT and only assumed Valid — Assumptions explicitly allow Q.isInf = 1, and k=1 gives Q=P while k=n-1 gives Q=-P, so x_B0 = x_B2 is reachable and PhiPairAdd.FiniteAssumptions cannot be discharged at the call site. The two places it IS dischargeable, P/phiP and Q/phiQ via beta != 1 and noXZero_secp, ALREADY use PhiPairAdd. (b) MAKING t3/t12 FREE BY THE HORIZONTAL-LINE TRICK (worth 4,964): t3 = sigma0*P + sigma1*phi(P) equals -phi^2(P)*sigma0 ONLY WHEN sigma0 = sigma1, and the four signs are independent outputs of the lattice reduction; computing both branches and muxing costs more than it saves. (c) NORMALISING THE RELATIVE SIGN by rewriting the decomposition: multiplying the relation by lambda maps (u1,u2) -> (-u2, u1-u2) and (v1,v2) -> (-v2, v1-v2) SIMULTANEOUSLY, so it cannot fix the two relative signs independently, and |u1-u2| costs a magnitude bit that breaks the 64-bit coeffBits budget. (d) FREE WIRE PERMUTATIONS VIA phi ACROSS ENTRIES: every image is sign-dependent, so no entry is a compile-time permutation of another. (e) FEWER THAN ELEVEN ADDITIONS: 11 entries have popcount >= 2, and the only sub-2584 maps available are phi (733) and negation (577), neither of which sends any table entry to another — 11 IS THE FLOOR. (f) PUSHING THE TWO 176/178 FOLDS DOWN TO 101/103 (worth 3,300): mulModFold32 needs BOTH operands in base 2^32, and it already applies wherever that holds; the div certificate multiplies lambda by a 64-bit-limb difference, and converting an operand costs Split32 at 508 against 150 saved, while storing table coordinates in base 2^32 inflates VarLookup from 9 to 17 cells per entry = +15,120. THE TREE'S MIXED REPRESENTATION IS ALREADY OPTIMAL. (g) A LAMBDA-FREE AFFINE ADDITION FORMULA: needs 5 certificates against 3, and one-product-per-row forbids folding them.

TWO NEW CANDIDATES FROM THE SWEEP, BOTH IN THE HOT LOOP. (1) VarLookup's isInf LANE COSTS 15 PRODUCTS PER STEP BUT SHOULD COST 3, worth 1,536. The lane is expensive only because tinf is treated as a 16-vector of variables; but tinf[0] = 1 is a CONSTANT (RawTable.mk infConst ...) and entries 1-15 are subset sums of four bases of prime order, so IF they are provably never infinity the lane collapses to out_isInf = e_0 = (1-b0)(1-b1)(1-b2)(1-b3) — 3 products instead of 15, i.e. -12 allocations and -12 rows across 64 lookups. THE OBLIGATION IS ONE LEMMA: tinf[i] = 0 for i >= 1, from GLVBuildTable.Subset.Spec plus P != O. THE SAME LEMMA ALSO RELEASES the 12 x-canonicalisation muxes in GLVBuildTable.lean:620-644, another 96. (2) THE lambda CERTIFICATE IN GLVScalarRelation.lean:100-103 IS THE LAST LIVE CERTIFICATE-INVERSION SITE, worth 1,072. THE REFRAME THAT MATTERS MORE THAN ANY SINGLE LEVER: THE LOOP'S COST IS SET BY THE EXCEPTION DETECTORS, NOT BY THE GROUP LAW. Of the five materialised elements per step, only lambda1 and w are materialised because the ARITHMETIC needs them — they are multiplicands. xS, x4 and y4 are materialised ONLY BECAUSE THREE CHEAP LIMB-LEVEL EXCEPTION DETECTORS NEED CANONICAL REPRESENTATIVES: sameX1 = EqFe(tx,rx) at SlopeXS.lean:79 needs rx, which is the previous x4; oppY1 via ry[0]-ty[0] at SlopeXS.lean:81-84 needs ry, the previous y4; and sameX2 = EqFe(xSe,rx) at Slope2.lean:76 needs xS. THAT IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and every 'eliminate an intermediate' lever in this corpus dies on it unless it also replaces the corresponding detector. IN PARTICULAR THE EARLIER -29,200 xS-MERGE ESTIMATE IS OVER-STATED because it silently ignores sameX2. THE ENABLING TOOL IS ALREADY IN THE TREE: interpolatedMul (InterpMul.lean:20-31) ALREADY witnesses the 15 convolution coefficients z_k and asserts 15 evaluation identities, so any value of the form (one convolution) plus (affine in materialised values) IS ALREADY SITTING IN THE WITNESS as a 15-cell vector. Carrying it that way instead of as a canonical 8-limb value costs ZERO allocations. Additive consumption is free (it only widens subtrahend caps — the ParamsD3 'triply-unreduced multiplicand' family is exactly this mechanism, already Lean-proved, just at 8 positions and cap 3*2^64 instead of 15 positions and cap ~2^73); multiplicative consumption costs one certificate degree (22 positions instead of 15); and LIMB-LEVEL TESTS BECOME IMPOSSIBLE, which is precisely why the detectors bind. DEPTH IS FREE — y_j telescopes to a sum of convolutions plus y_0 but is STILL 15 CELLS, with only the coefficient magnitude growing about 6 bits over 62 steps, which is why carrying a value across many steps needs no anchoring.

IDEA A — A PROVER-SELECTED TABLE BASIS MAKES THE SIGNED TABLE PROVABLY IDENTITY-FREE, AND THE OBLIGATION IS A FINITE `decide`. This supersedes the entry claiming the all-odd signed table is not identity-free; that entry is right about the default basis and wrong that it cannot be fixed. A table entry vanishes iff (e1 + e2*lambda) + s*(e3 + e4*lambda) = 0 mod n. Enumerating all 16 sign patterns over the basis {P, phiP, Q, phiQ} gives EXACTLY SIX BAD s, and they include s = 1 and s = n-1. Now build the table from the basis {P, phiP, Q+P, phi(Q+P)} — a UNIMODULAR change, so the rank-4 relation lattice and its 2^64 Minkowski bound are unchanged and the scalar-side congruence absorbs it as free affine. Its bad set has FIVE elements AND IS DISJOINT FROM THE FIRST. So ONE WITNESSED BIT selecting the basis makes the table identity-free FOR EVERY s. Assert once that all 8 entries are non-infinite (they are outputs of additions, so assert the chord denominators are nonzero — 8 sites, one-off), after which tIsInf is identically 0 and LEAVES THE LOOP ENTIRELY. PRICE: one-off build of Q+P (3 certificates, ~2,500) plus an 8-limb basis mux (32); per step DELETE the xSe mux (8), the num2 mux (8), the bMul mux (8) and the sel1 OR, i.e. about -70 per step = -4,340. THE WHOLE SOUNDNESS OBLIGATION IS THAT THE TWO BAD SETS ARE DISJOINT — a finite check on 11 explicit constants mod n, decidable by decide or norm_num. Soundness imports no assumption because the non-infinite assertions are checked IN-CIRCUIT. WHY IT IS NOT STANDARD: everyone runs subset-sum tables with an explicit identity entry and pays the infinity apparatus; nobody treats the identity entry as a CHOICE OF LATTICE BASIS.

IDEA B — DELETE THE ACCUMULATOR'S y FROM THE WITNESS SET ENTIRELY, ~-500 PER STEP = -31,000. THIS IS NOT THE DEAD y-FREE LOOP AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT. ry is consumed ADDITIVELY everywhere (dyU = ty - ry, num2 = 2ry, y4 = A*b - ry) except at two tangent denominators and oppY1, so fix those three. (1) STAGE-1 TANGENT DENOMINATOR 2ry -> 2ty: when sameX1 = 1 we have ty = +-ry != 0 since n is prime so there is no 2-torsion, and substituting keeps lambda1 = +-mu with xS = lambda1^2 - 2rx = x(2R) in BOTH signs (verified 200/200); ty is a MATERIALISED TABLE COORDINATE so the lambda1 certificate stays degree 2. THIS REQUIRES IDEA A, because T = O has ty = 0. (2) STAGE-2 TANGENT DENOMINATOR -> THE CONSTANT 1: den2 = mux(sameX2, 1, xSe - rx) with num2 = 2ry additive; on the sameX2 branch the result is flagged O by zOut, so w = 2ry is harmless garbage and the row stays satisfiable — this removes the second ry-product AND the 8-limb mux. (3) oppY1 -> CANCEL-PINNING: witness a boolean cancel, assert cancel*(1 - sameX1) = 0 (one row) and sameX1*(ty - ry - 2*cancel*ty) = 0 mod p; if sameX1 = 1 this forces ty = ry when cancel = 0 and ty = -ry when cancel = 1, and IS UNSATISFIABLE FOR THE WRONG BIT, so cancel is uniquely pinned with NO IsZero and NO non-native inverse (verified 400/400). Then y4 is never allocated: only the 15 coefficients of A (x) bMul are witnessed and y4 is that minus ry as a FREE AFFINE 15-cell vector. PRICE: delete MulModSub2W2 (~-885), pay num2 mux widened 8 -> 15 cells (+14), the cancel certificate (~+310, with no big-by-big product — only boolean-by-value terms over a folded 15-cell target, quotient ~74 bits) and wider subtrahend caps at 3 sites (+30). WHY THIS IS NOT THE EARLIER FORGERY: that construction replaced y by an expression containing a NEW FREE WITNESS w, underdetermined when x_S = x. HERE NOTHING NEW IS WITNESSED — y_{j+1} occurs LINEARLY WITH UNIT COEFFICIENT in exactly one equation, which DEFINES it, and we eliminate that variable and that equation, so the two solution sets are IN BIJECTION BY PROJECTION, a one-line Lean argument. The residual obligations are arithmetic only: coefficient cap 62*2^67 < 2^73, folded U < 2^330, CRT window 2^t * r / 2 > U with t >= 77.

IDEA C — MERGE xS AWAY AND REPAIR THE sameX2 DETECTOR, ~-285 PER STEP = -17,700. Two identities, verified 300/300 on real secp256k1 points: w * (lambda1 (x) lambda1 - 2*rx - tx) = 2*ry, a degree-3 relation replacing BOTH the xS certificate and the w division; and x4 = w (x) (2*lambda1 + w) + tx, which is SHARPER than the earlier form x4 = lambda2 (x) lambda2 - lambda1 (x) lambda1 + tx because it uses ONE convolution instead of two, saving ~30 per step and avoiding a widened operand. THE MISSING PIECE IN THE EARLIER VERSION WAS sameX2, and here is the repair: replace it with a witnessed boolean zOut pinned by zOut * (lambda1 (x) lambda1 - 2rx - tx) = 0 mod p. Note zOut * lambda1 is boolean-by-8-limb (16 cells), so this is an ORDINARY DEGREE-2 'assertion, not value' certificate with no fresh result. The converse — xS = rx implies zOut = 1 — is FREE, because with zOut = 0 the chord row becomes w * 0 = 2ry, unsatisfiable since ry != 0. PRICE: delete MulModSub2F32 (-733), pay the w-certificate widened to 22 positions (~+200), x4's subtrahend unreduced (~+40) and the zOut certificate (~+234), less the deleted EqFe and mux (-26). PRICED AND REJECTED — THE RANDOMNESS-FREE SUBSTITUTE FOR EAGEN'S DIVISOR ARGUMENT. Plane-curve incidence is the natural way to avoid the random challenge point: 3d points on a degree-d curve sum to O by Abel's theorem, so assert incidence directly with no challenge. PRICED HONESTLY IT LOSES ON COST, NOT ON RANDOMNESS: a line certifies 3 points for 959 score (320 per point) — AND THAT IS EXACTLY THE CURRENT SLOPE FORM — while a conic, normalising c3 = 1, needs 5 materialised coefficients plus 6 degree-3 incidence certificates, about 6,700 (1,117 per point). Degree-d curves carry roughly one unknown coefficient per point against a line's one per three, and force D = 3. LINES ARE OPTIMAL. Separately, soundness would need the 3d points to be pairwise distinct AS A MULTISET, or a tangency condition is missing, and that is O(d^2) non-native inverses.

THE STATE-OF-THE-ART PAPER ON THIS EXACT PROBLEM IS BY ONE OF OUR LEADERBOARD RIVALS, AND IT CONFIRMS OUR ARCHITECTURE WHILE NAMING ONE THING IT LEAVES UNDONE. Eagen, El Housni, Masson, Piellard, 'Fast elliptic curve scalar multiplications in SN(T)ARK circuits', Latincrypt 2025, eprint 2025/933 — El Housni is `yelhousni` on this leaderboard. Read from the Latincrypt slides (eprint PDFs are Cloudflare-blocked from here; the slide deck is open at ciencias.medellin.unal.edu.co). WHAT IT CONFIRMS: their headline single-scalar construction is 'GLV with hints' — witness the output Q and verify a lattice relation [x]P + [y]psi(P) - [z]Q - [t]psi(Q) = 0 — reduced to a QUADRUPLE 64-BIT SCALAR MULTIPLICATION. THAT IS EXACTLY OUR ARCHITECTURE (4-dimensional, coeffBound = 2^64, coeffBits = 64), so there is NO ARCHITECTURAL GAIN SITTING IN THIS PAPER and nobody should spend a slot looking for one. Their double-scalar variant is a SEXTUPLE 86-BIT decomposition, which solves k1 P1 + k2 P2 and is not our problem. THE ONE ACTIONABLE THING IS THE AUTHORS' OWN STATED LIMITATION, verbatim from the final slide: 'The scalar decomposition is not optimal yet (xgcd vs lll)'. They decompose with extended-gcd; LLL on the same lattice gives shorter vectors. FOR US THAT IS A COEFFICIENT-BOUND QUESTION AND THEREFORE AN ITERATION-COUNT QUESTION: our loop runs 64 iterations because the four coefficients are bounded by 2^64, and 64 = 256/4 is the information-theoretic floor for a 4-dimensional decomposition, so LLL CANNOT BEAT IT ASYMPTOTICALLY — but the CONSTANT is what decides whether the bound is 2^64 or a shade under, and one iteration is a whole glvStep = 4,349. CHECK BEFORE FUNDING: compute the actual LLL-reduced basis of our decomposition lattice and see whether every coefficient lands strictly below 2^63; if it does not, the lead is worth zero and should be closed. CRITICAL CALIBRATION SO NOBODY PANICS AT THEIR NUMBERS: the paper reports secp256k1 at 78,940 -> 60,089 R1CS CONSTRAINTS against our ~153,000, and THAT COMPARISON IS MEANINGLESS HERE. gnark's emulated-field range checks are LOOKUP/commitment-based, which is exactly the primitive this challenge bars — the corpus already records the same finding for the RSA state of the art, where fits_in_bits is a table lookup. Their 60k and our 153k are not the same cost model and no part of that ratio is available to us.
secp256k1-fixed-base-scalar-mul: HEAD-TO-HEAD MODMUL COUNTS ACROSS FOUR CODEBASES, ALL COMPILED AND MEASURED IN OUR MODEL (no lookups, no challenges), for one 256-bit a*b mod p over BN254: jsnark/xJsnark with a CONSTANT modulus and lazy range = 623 constraints at 32-bit chunks; jsnark with a variable modulus = 637 at 26-bit; arkworks r1cs-std emulated_fp = 680 (66 for mul_without_reduce + 614 for reduce) at 17 limbs x 15 bits; gnark v0.8.1 = 724 at 26x10 and 888 at its shipped 64x4. LIMB WIDTH 26-32 IS OPTIMAL AND 64 IS 18-22% WORSE — measured independently in two different codebases, and it reproduces xJsnark's own Figure 5 parameter sweep (b about 32 near-optimal, b = 120 about 40% worse). WE USE 4 LIMBS OF 64 BITS, i.e. the worst end of that curve; this is the same conclusion the pseudo-Mersenne analysis reached from a different direction, so treat 32-bit limbs as strongly corroborated. STRUCTURE OF THE COST, which is why: product limbs hinted and verified at 2n-1 FIXED points costs 2n-1 rows (15 at w=32) and is essentially free; q*p is FREE when p is a compile-time constant since constant scalings are linear; grouped carry propagation is 60-110; and ABOUT 80% OF THE WHOLE THING is bit-decomposition range checks on the quotient and remainder. LAZY REDUCTION IS WORTH ABOUT 600 CONSTRAINTS PER AVOIDED REDUCE (arkworks measures mul_without_reduce at 66 against reduce at 614, and additions cost literally zero), so a*b + c*d with one shared reduction is about 746 against 1360. FINALLY, WHY GNARK'S HEADLINE 99 CONSTRAINTS PER EMULATED MUL IS NOT AVAILABLE: modern gnark's mulMod emits ZERO constraints and defers to a Schwartz-Zippel check at a commitment-derived challenge (std/math/emulated/field_mul.go), and std/multicommit panics outright if the frontend is not a Committer — so it cannot even compile on a plain Groth16 frontend. Strip the challenge and the lookups and gnark's own pre-v0.10 code lands at 724.

MEASURED TARGET FOR THE MODMUL: 845 SCORE, AGAINST OUR 1463 (mulModSub2Cost = 728 alloc + 735 constr). These numbers come from actually compiling circuits with circom 2.2.3 and reading row counts out of the .r1cs with snarkjs, then witness-testing on 508 vectors including the worst case (p-1)^2 — not from a paper. Reference points, as rows + allocations: circom-ecdsa BigMultModP(64,4) = 7707; circom-pairing FpMultiply(43,6) at secp256k1 = 2509; fold with tightened carry parameters at n=32,k=8 = 1527; FOLD + CRT at n=32,k=8 = 845 (424 rows + 421 allocs). THREE INGREDIENTS, IN ORDER OF IMPORTANCE. (1) THE PRODUCT IS ALREADY FREE — the full 256x256 limb product is 2k-1 rows by asserting the limb-polynomial identity at 2k-1 evaluation points (circom-ecdsa's BigMultNoCarry is 7 rows), so 99.8% of a naive BigMultModP is carries and range checks and NO effort should go into the multiplication. (2) THE FOLD IS FREE FOR EVERY MODULUS — reducing the 2k-1 product limbs back to k via precomputed constants 2^(n(k+i)) mod p is a LINEAR COMBINATION, zero rows. What p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977 buys is that the fold coefficients are TINY (literally 977 and 1 when n = 32, because c = 2^32 + 977 is limb-aligned there), which cascades: folded limb width 77 bits instead of 101, quotient bound 36 bits instead of 68, CRT limbs 2 instead of 3, carry width 46 instead of 70 — worth about 27% (424 vs 578 rows for a generic 256-bit prime, both compiled). USE n = 32 PRECISELY BECAUSE c IS LIMB-ALIGNED THERE. (3) THE BIG ONE — CHECK THE IDENTITY BY CRT, NOT BY A CARRY CHAIN (Lubarov and Baylina, 'Casting out Primes', eprint 2022/1470): verify under a FIXED set of moduli M = {r_BN254, 2^(nT)} and conclude the identity holds mod lcm(M), which suffices when |f| < lcm(M). NOTE THIS NEEDS NO RANDOM CHALLENGE — the moduli are fixed constants, so it maps to plain R1CS. Mod r_BN254 the check R - p*X - out = 0 is ONE PURELY LINEAR ROW because the modulus is a CONSTANT; mod 2^(nT) only T = 2 carries at 46 bits are needed instead of a full chain of 8. Soundness margin measured at 25 bits (|D|max = 2^293 < r*2^64 = 2^318) and brute-forced on scaled-down analogues. CAVEAT FOR RSA: there the modulus is an INPUT, so p*X is a genuine product and the native leg is NOT free — this transfers to the secp challenges much better than to RSA.

LAZY REDUCTION IS WORTH FAR MORE THAN IT LOOKS, BECAUSE LIMB PRODUCTS ADD FOR FREE. Measured, same compiled setup: sharing ONE reduction across M products costs 424 rows at M=1, 457 at M=2, 490 at M=4, 553 at M=8 — i.e. 424, 228, 123 and 69 rows PER MULTIPLICATION. Each extra product adds only about 15 rows (the 2k-1 convolution) plus roughly one bit to the carry widths, verified correct including at M*(p-1)^2. Affine EC formulas ARE sums of products. CORRECTION TO THE CANONICALITY FIGURE IN THIS ENTRY: I claimed the pseudo-Mersenne shape gives x < p in 37 rows against 333 for a generic comparison. Either my 37 was a different unit or about 28 rows x 2 invocations are still available. CONTRAST with the VARIABLE-BASE record, which gets canonicality in 8/11 GIVEN AN EXISTING BIT DECOMPOSITION by walking the zero bits of p; if the bits are already there for another reason, prefer that form.

My earlier estimate of 316 per multiplication was 1.85x too low, and my prediction that GroupedEqXV would be 'a wash' was wrong — it more than halves. THE SELECTOR IS 20.5% OF THE CIRCUIT, NOT ~2% — MY EARLIER NOTE HAD BOTH THE GADGET AND ITS MULTIPLICITY WRONG. It costed SelectX.mainX at 342 and said 'x2'. SelectX.lean IS DEAD CODE (a NEUTRALIZED build-fix stub); the live gadget is Select12.main at 336/336, and it is invoked TWENTY-ONE times — twice explicitly and once per iteration of the 19-step fold. That is 14112 score, 20.5% of a 68797 circuit, against the ~1368 my note implied. THE ONE-HOT BOUND (minimum 2^w - w - 1 multiplications to build a full one-hot from w bits, split-invariant) IS NOT CONTRADICTED — the record never builds a 2^11 one-hot at all, it factors it (see the factored-one-hot entry). WHERE THE BOUND NOW BINDS, AND A FREE 420 SCORE: the outer 4-bit one-hot HITS the bound at 2 + 9 = 11 = 2^4 - 4 - 1 exactly. The inner 7-bit half misses it by exactly 10 — the record pays blk 3 + inner4 15 + inner6 48 + inner7 64 = 130 against the optimum 3 + 9 + 45 + 63 = 120 = 2^7 - 7 - 1. The fix is mechanical and the construction is ALREADY PRESENT in the same file (hot4o's 'drop the last row AND the last column' identity): inner4 should witness 9 not 15 (cell(i,3) = a_i - sum_j h[i+3j], cell(3,j) = c_j - sum_i h[3j+i], cell(3,3) from the two); inner6 should be 45 not 48 (drop the last row too, recoverable from sum_a hot6(a,c) = pair2(c)); inner7 should be 63 not 64 (sum_a hot7(a,1) = xExpr(6)). 10 allocations + 10 constraints per window x 21 windows = 420 score. THE OTHER LEVER IS STILL OPEN: selecting a one-wire borrow instead of a whole 4-limb p-y array drops the output-wire count from 12 to 9, which by the factored formula gives 120 + 11 + 135 + 15 = 281 per window.

CALIBRATION — OUR NUMBERS APPEAR TO BE THE ONLY PLAIN-R1CS ONES IN EXISTENCE. circom-ecdsa ECDSAVerifyNoPubkeyCheck(64,4) is 1508136 constraints and its fixed-base ECDSAPrivToPub is 95444 (stride 8, 32 windows, 256-entry tables); subtracting gives roughly 1.39-1.40M for its variable-base scalar multiplication. Against that our 559597 and 80147 are about 2.5x and 1.2x better. Everything smaller in the literature is out of scope: gnark's 100914 for [s]P uses logUp range checks plus a multicommit challenge; spartan-ecdsa's 3039 proves over secq256k1 where the field is NATIVE; halo2-ecc is PLONKish and lookup-driven. The one transferable idea from spartan-ecdsa is the efficient-ECDSA transform (two scalar multiplications down to one), which is R1CS-neutral and orthogonal to this challenge.

VERIFICATION TIME IS A HARD CONSTRAINT, NOT JUST COST (observed, twice). A solution scoring 80191 — beating the 80195 record, no sorry/admit, all required declarations present, cost parsed clean — was submitted and came back status=timeout from the zk.golf verifier. It was re-downloaded from the job and submitted a SECOND time and timed out identically, so this is a property of the solution, not a transient. It differs from the verified 80195 in 20 files (Chain, PairAdd, AffineChainAdd, CheapIncompleteAdd, FinalAdd), i.e. a real structural rework, at the same file count (148) and the same maxHeartbeats profile. LESSON: a lower-cost solution that cannot be CHECKED inside the verifier's budget scores nothing. Keep elaboration cheap as you golf — prefer many small lemmas over one huge `decide`/`simp` blowup, avoid raising maxHeartbeats to paper over a slow proof, and if a rewrite makes the build dramatically slower, treat that as a cost regression even though it does not show up in allocations+constraints.
