Base G is FIXED: every window multiple j*(2^{w*i})*G is a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT — bake the whole comb table into the circuit as constants (zero constraints to build it), unlike the variable-base case.
Comb method: k = sum b_{i} 2^{i}; group bits into d combs of width w so each step is ONE table select + ONE add; fewer adds than plain windowed double-and-add.
Width-w NAF / signed-digit recoding of the scalar so table entries cover +/- multiples, halving table size and generating more zero (skip) positions.

Signed-digit tables cost almost nothing to apply: -P = (x, -y), so the sign bit drives ONE modular negation of y (an affine op), NOT a second multiplexer. So a width-w signed table needs only 2^{w-1} constant entries selected, plus a conditional y-negation — half the select cost of an unsigned width-w table for the same window count.
Constant-table point selection as a multiplexer over field constants: select cost is linear in window size but touches only additions/booleans, no non-native mul.

PRIME-REDUCE for a FIXED prime (circom-ecdsa): do limb mul/add WITHOUT carries into a wide form (k=4 x 64-bit registers for 256-bit; a product spans ~10 registers), then collapse 10 registers back to 4 in ONE reduction (~1000 constraints) by subtracting PRECOMPUTED multiples of p — compile-time constants because p is fixed. DEFERRAL BUDGET: keep 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < 254 (native field bits); that inequality tells you exactly how many unreduced products you may accumulate before a carry/reduce pass is actually required — defer right up to it, not further.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce, ~2x fewer reductions): accumulate a*b +/- c*d in WIDE UNREDUCED limbs and reduce ONCE at the end. Affine EC formulas are exactly this shape — lambda = (y2-y1)*inv(x2-x1), x3 = lambda^2 - x1 - x2, y3 = lambda*(x1-x3) - y1 — so reduce once PER OUTPUT COORDINATE, never per intermediate product.

COORDINATE-SYSTEM TRAP: in R1CS an inversion costs ~1 allocation + 1 constraint (hint inv as a witness, enforce x*inv = 1), so division is nearly FREE here — the opposite of the software cost model. Jacobian/projective/co-Z formulas (incl. Meloni co-Z ladders at ~11M+5S+23A per scalar bit) exist ONLY to avoid inversion, and pay for it with extra MULTIPLICATIONS — which are the expensive non-native op in-circuit. Prefer plain AFFINE add/double with hinted inverses; do NOT port inversion-free coordinate systems from the ECC literature.

Combine comb sub-scalars as a joint accumulation sharing point doublings/additions (multi-comb), analogous to the joint-MSM trick, so the fixed precompute is amortized across all windows in one add-chain.

Port secp256k1-scalar-mul's GroupedEqXV / MulModTarget non-native machinery (see reference/) if it lowers the per-add Fp mul-mod cost below the current Flex path; competitor csko pushed this challenge to 90041, a large structural gap — a comb-table + incomplete-add rewrite is likely needed, not incremental tweaks.

GLV BUYS NOTHING ON A FIXED-BASE COMB — MY EARLIER ENTRY CLAIMING IT IS 'STRICTLY BETTER AND MISSING FROM THIS PLAYBOOK' IS WRONG, DO NOT SPEND A SLOT ON IT. GLV halves the number of DOUBLINGS. A comb has NO in-circuit doublings at all — the doubling ladder is a table of compile-time constants — so the in-circuit work is exactly ONE table select plus ONE addition PER WINDOW, and the window count is (scalar bits)/w regardless of how the scalar is split. Concretely: today 21 windows of 12 bits covers 252 bits; with k = k1 + k2*lambda you get 2 x ceil(128/12) = 22 windows, i.e. MORE additions, plus a mod-n decomposition check (~3000 by analogy with the variable-base ScalarRelation at 2932/2954). The same argument kills GLV-3 and 4-dimensional splitting here, and it is why mLSB-set comb + GLV is a SOFTWARE win (it shrinks the precomputed table, which is FREE for us) and not a circuit win. THE ONLY LEVERS THAT ACTUALLY MOVE A COMB ARE: fewer windows (wider w, bounded by the chord-slope table's elaboration cost), a cheaper selector, and a cheaper per-addition certificate.

Push the same idea further: with all tables being compile-time constants there is no table-size penalty for HIGHER-DIMENSIONAL decomposition (GLV-3 via lambda^2, or 4-dimensional GLV). Each extra dimension shortens the sub-scalars (256 -> ~128 -> ~85 -> ~64 bits) and shortens the shared doubling chain proportionally, at the cost only of more CONSTANT tables (free) and a slightly bigger decomposition check. Sweep the dimension and pick the minimum of (doublings + selects + decomposition check).

mLSB-set comb is the standard pairing of comb methods with GLV curves (see the fixed-base comb / GLV-GLS literature) — combine mLSB-set recoding with the two (or more) constant tables rather than treating comb and GLV as alternatives.

SLOPE-ONLY TERMINAL ASSERTION — PROVING 2*A + T = O COSTS ONE SLOPE GADGET AND FOUR ROWS, NOT A DOUBLE-AND-ADD. When the last step of a scalar-mul or MSM only has to ASSERT that the accumulator chain closes to infinity, do not compute 2A+T and test the flag. Write S = A + T for the chord sum: the chord formula gives y_S = lambda*(x_A - x_S) - y_A, which collapses to -y_A exactly when x_S = x_A. So 2A + T = O <=> S = -A <=> x_S = x_A. A slope gadget already produces lambda and x_S = lambda^2 - x_A - x_T, so the whole assertion is ONE row A.isInf - T.isInf = 0 plus FOUR rows (1 - A.isInf)*(x_S[k] - x_A[k]) = 0. MEASURED (secp256k1 over BN254, 4 limbs x 64 bits): 1070 allocations / 1085 constraints, against 1792/1809 for double-then-cancel and 1783/1802 for assert-negated-sum — 722 allocations and 724 constraints saved, and being a pure assertion it materialises no output point. THE ONE SOUNDNESS OBLIGATION: the degenerate branch where x_T = x_A makes the slope gadget return the TANGENT, and you must show that branch cannot satisfy the assertion. For a = 0, b = 7 it forces lambda^2 = 3x together with 2*y*lambda = 3x^2, hence x^3 = -28 and y^2 = -21; -21 is a quadratic NON-RESIDUE mod p, proved by one kernel `decide` on a binary modPow at ZERO circuit rows. Re-derive the analogous non-residue before using this on another curve.

DO NOT ASSUME COMPLETE ADDITION IS EXPENSIVE — WITH LIMB-LEVEL MUXES IT IS 1.3% OF A STEP, AND THIS OVERTURNS THE USUAL ADVICE. The received wisdom (and my own earlier notes) says to use incomplete affine addition and discharge the exceptions by a soundness argument. MEASURED, THAT IS THE WRONG TRADE IN THIS COST MODEL: a FULLY COMPLETE fused double-add step is 2346 allocations / 2371 constraints, of which the entire exception apparatus is about 30 allocations — the other 97.9% is the five non-native certificates. The apparatus is two 9-cell point muxes (9/9 each) for A = O and T = -A, two 256-bit equality tests at 5/5, and one 2/2 opposite-y detector. THREE TRICKS MAKE IT THIS CHEAP. (1) 256-BIT EQUALITY IN 5 ROWS: pack limbs 0,1 into one native element and limbs 2,3 into another (each under 128 bits, safely below the native modulus), run two IsZeroField at 2/2, AND them with one row. DO NOT COMPARE LIMBWISE. (2) T = -A IN 2 ROWS USING ONE LIMB: witness inv of y_A[0] - y_T[0], set oppY <== yDiff*inv, assert yDiff*(sameX - oppY) = 0. Only the LOW LIMB is needed, because two finite points with equal x are equal or opposite and p is odd, so y != -y already differs in limb 0. (3) A BOOLEAN OR THAT COSTS ZERO: if one input IMPLIES the other (here T = O re-routes the intermediate x so sameX is forced to 1), the OR EQUALS the implied flag, and a downstream flag - other is a free affine expression instead of a witness plus a row. SO: reach for incomplete formulas only where a cheaper SPECIALISED gadget results — e.g. adding P to phi(P), where x_{phiP} != x_P is free from beta != 1 and x != 0, worth 63 allocations — and not to avoid completeness per se.

THE ALL-ODD SIGNED-DIGIT RECODE COSTS EXACTLY ZERO ROWS, AND THE SCALAR'S PARITY IS ABSORBED BY THE TOP WINDOW'S CONSTANT TABLE. Do not build a recoder. With MSB-first input bits, define db[c] := bits[254 - c] for c < 255 and db[255] := 1 — a pure WIRE PERMUTATION with one hard-coded 1, cost 0/0. Grouping db into W windows of w bits gives digits d_i = 2*v_i + 1 - 2^w, all ODD and in +-{1, 3, ..., 2^w - 1}, and the identity sum_i d_i * 2^(w*i) = k + 1 - bits[255] holds. THE PARITY FIX IS FREE: the comb computes k*G when the scalar is odd and (k+1)*G when even, and the -+G correction is folded into the TOP window's table by making the scalar's LSB an extra INDEX BIT of that table — a 16-entry 4-bit top table costs 11 rows whether or not the parity bit is in the index, so the fix costs NOTHING. WHAT THIS BUYS, AND IT IS THE WHOLE EXCEPTION STORY: every digit is odd hence nonzero, so no window can ever select the identity, and no two consecutive sites can collide — which is what lets the entire ladder use incomplete addition with no runtime guard except the 44-score final screen. SECOND BENEFIT: the magnitude index of a NEGATIVE digit is the bitwise COMPLEMENT of the magnitude bits, obtained as XNOR(sign, b_i) at ONE multiplication per bit (11 for w = 12), so the sign costs 11 rows and no separate table.

KEEP THE ACCUMULATOR AS (x, lambda) AND MATERIALISE y EXACTLY ONCE FOR THE WHOLE SCALAR MULTIPLICATION — THIS RECORD ALREADY DOES IT, DO NOT REGRESS IT. State is {x : Emu, lam : Emu, T : AffPoint}; the real accumulator is (x, impliedY) with impliedY = lambda*(T.x - x) - T.y, where T is the LAST table point added. One chain step is stageC1 (the new slope computed directly from x, lambda, T_prev, T_new — two non-native products under one shared reduction) followed by stageX (x' = lambda'^2 - x - T.x, one product). MEASURED: ChainExtFold 1170/1177 per window against ChainFinish 730/735 for the single y-materialisation at the end — deferring y saves roughly 730/1465 per step and is paid ONCE instead of 20 times. THE SECOND y-MATERIALISATION IS STILL THERE AND IS WORTH 2016: FinalAdd's chord is CheapIncompleteAdd = ChainStartQ6Zero 1445/1453 + ChainFinish 730/735, so the circuit materialises y TWICE. Fold the top window in as a 20th lambda-form extension step and reuse the ONE existing ChainFinish: 1005 allocations + 1011 constraints saved.

A 43000-ENTRY CONSTANT POINT TABLE IS PROVABLE IN LEAN ONLY VIA CHORD-SLOPE CHAINS — BUDGET THIS BEFORE WIDENING THE WINDOW. If you widen the window the blocker is not circuit cost but ELABORATION: proving T[win][j] = (2j+1)*2^(w*win)*G for 21 x 2048 entries by group-law evaluation will not finish. The record instead stores, PER WINDOW, a list of 2047 precomputed CHORD SLOPES (21 x 2047 = 43248 hex constants) and certifies each whole window with ONE chordChainOK application, so each entry's certificate is a cheap field identity (y_{j+1} - y_j) = s_j*(x_{j+1} - x_j) rather than a group-law computation. The doubling ladder between windows is a separate 256-entry slope table. SCALING: w = 13 needs 19 x 4095 = about 78k slope constants and w = 14 needs 18 x 8191 = about 147k. REMEMBER THE VERIFIER TIMEOUT — a table this size stresses it directly, and a timeout is reported as a FAILURE, not as a bad score.

w = 13 IS WORTH ABOUT 1554 SCORE OVER w = 12, RECOMPUTED WITH THE RECORD'S OWN POST-FOLD NUMBERS (the earlier ~2% estimate is corroborated, not superseded). At w = 12: 21 selector invocations plus 19 chain steps = 21*672 + 19*2347 = 58705. At w = 13: 19 windows of 13 bits plus a 9-bit top window, selector 454 multiplications via a 2^8 (x) 2^4 factored one-hot, giving 19*908 + 17*2347 = 57151. w = 14 is WORSE at 63112. THE CONSTRAINT THAT DECIDES IT IS NOT SCORE BUT ELABORATION — see the chord-slope table entry: w = 13 needs about 78k slope constants against the current 43k. Sequence the work so the fold is finished on all four modmul sites FIRST (worth 9-11k), since that is both larger and cheaper to prove than a table widening.

WIDE-FOLD BOUND DERIVATION, DONE AND GREEN ON ALL FOUR SITES — THE LEVER IS UNBLOCKED. The fold's carry width is set by exactly ONE clause of GVXHyps: (a) OFF_R(k) + OFF_L(k) < 2^(W k), and OFF_L(0) = cFold*C/2^64 = C/2^32 where C is the max convolution coefficient at a position. Everything else — the field-capacity clauses (d) and the final-group clause — has 2^23 or more of headroom at every site and NEVER BINDS. GroupedFlex cost = (sum_{k<G-2}(W_k - 1), sum_{k<G-2} W_k + 1); the fold's L=5, gf=2, G=3 layout is FORCED (gf=3 pushes Sigma_L to 2^290 > r), so there is no schedule search to do. PER SITE, with C traced through the biased-subtraction representation (dtil_k < 3*2^64 from twoPBorrowDigit in [2^64, 2^65); xd1/xd2_k < 2^65 from the 2^64-1 offset, whose 2^256-1 = p + c976 identity is what puts the c976*lam cross term on the RHS): stageX and stageO2 have C = 4*2^128 -> W0 = 99; stageA has C = 12*2^128 (val_conv_lam_dtil_le) -> OFF_L(0) = 3*2^98 -> W0 = 100; stageY has C = 8*2^128 (val_convLX_lt) -> W0 = 100; stageC1 has C = 20*2^128 (12 + 8, both already proved in-tree at PairAddTheorems 1283 and 2454) -> OFF_L(0) = 5*2^98 = 1.25*2^100 -> W0 = 101. NO SITE FAILS AND NO SITE NEEDS A PRE-REDUCTION OR A DIFFERENT BIAS CONSTANT. stageC1 cannot reach W0 = 100 — that would need C < 16*2^128, i.e. a canonical xd1, costing a 252/256 NormalizeImplicit to save 2 score, so don't.

THE FOLDED QUOTIENT IS 34 BITS SMALLER THAN THE SHIPPED RANGE CHECK — A 2-LINE, 1292-SCORE FIX ON CODE ALREADY IN THE TREE. Writing A*B = hi*2^256 + lo = hi*p + (cFold*hi + lo), the folded quotient is q = (cFold*hi + lo + bias - rem) div p, hence q <= cFold*H/p + 1 + bias_mult. For ChainFold.stageX (H = 2^256, bias 4p) that is EXACTLY c + 5 = 2^32 + 982, i.e. 33 BITS — against the shipped RangeCheck 67. Since q < 2^33 implies q < 2^67, FoldQuad and hgvFold are UNTOUCHED: change `RangeCheck.circuit 67` to `33` and prove the new completeness bound. 34 allocations + 34 constraints per site x 19 sites = 1292 score. SEPARATELY, stating nfFoldL exactly (4*2^160 + 3908*2^128 + 2^64) instead of rounding up to 2^163 drops OFF_L(0) from 2^99 to 2^98 and wfFold from 100 to 99 — another 2 per site. Folded quotient widths for the other sites: stageA 34, stageY 36, stageC1 36.

PER-SITE FOLD COSTS AND THE PREDICTED TOTAL (component table reconstructed from source and verified to reproduce the record's 34317/34480 exactly). A folded stage is: witness + NormalizeImplicit 252/256 + one q wire + RangeCheck(Wq) + interpolatedMul(s) + GroupedFlex with ONE carry at W0. stageC1 741/746 -> 406/408 (saves 673) x19 = 12787; ChainFold.stageX 429/431 -> 394/396 (saves 70) x19 = 1330; stageA 725/729 -> 396/398 (saves 660) x2 = 1320; PairAddQ6Zero.stageO2 720/724 -> 394/396 (saves 654) x2 = 1308; Chain.stageY 730/735 -> 398/400 (saves 667) x2 = 1334; one-hot fix 20 x21 = 420. TOTAL PREDICTED 50298 without the final-add reorder, 49536 with it, from 68797. START WITH stageO2 — ITS BOUND WORK IS ALREADY DONE: its circuit body uses only xA, xT1, lam1 and its lhs/rhs are CHARACTER-IDENTICAL to ChainFold.stageX, so PairAddQ6Zero.stageO2 xA yA xT1 yT1 lam1 IS ChainFold.stageX xA xT1 lam1 modulo one lemma x3Val = x2W. Zero new bound work, 1308 score. THE RESIDUAL RISK IS PROOF VOLUME, NOT SOUNDNESS: stageA (fat multiplicand), stageY (2-wide xd2 plus the c976 cross term) and stageC1 (TWO products summed — define the coefficient vector as convLD2 + convLX1 and the same split7 identity goes through) each need a FoldQuad variant. GENERALISE FoldQuad over (C, bias, remainder bound) rather than copy-pasting it four times; it runs nlinarith on 300-bit naturals and large `decide`s, and the verifier timeout is a hard constraint.

THE 420-SCORE ONE-HOT FIX, CELLS WRITTEN OUT. sum_v pairExpr(x,y,xy,v) = 1 is a POLYNOMIAL identity (P0 = 1-x-y+xy, P1 = x-xy, P2 = y-xy, P3 = xy) — it needs no booleanity, so every dropped cell is free and unconditionally sound, and the drop CASCADES because the 16 reconstructed inner4 cells also sum to 1 identically. inner4 15 -> 9: witness h4[a+3c] = P^0_a * P^1_c for a,c < 3; cell(a<3, c=3) = P^0_a - h4[a] - h4[a+3] - h4[a+6]; cell(a=3, c<3) = P^1_c - h4[3c] - h4[3c+1] - h4[3c+2]; cell(3,3) = blk[1] - sum_{a<3}(P^0_a - h4[a] - h4[a+3] - h4[a+6]). This is hot4o retargeted from pairs 3,4 to pairs 0,1. inner6 48 -> 45: witness h6[15c+a] = H4(a) * P^2_c for a<15, c<3; cell(a<15, 3) = H4(a) - h6[a] - h6[15+a] - h6[30+a]; cell(15, c<3) = P^2_c - sum_{a<15} h6[15c+a]; cell(15,3) = blk[2] - sum_{a<15} H4(a) + sum_{j<45} h6[j]. inner7 64 -> 63: witness h7[a] = H6(a) * x6 for a < 63; cell(t=1, a=63) = xExpr(6) - sum_{a<63} h7[a]; cell(t=0, a) = H6(a) - cell(t=1, a). Result 3 + 9 + 45 + 63 = 120 = 2^7 - 7 - 1, hitting the proved minimum, and Select12 goes 336 -> 326. CAUTION: the a=15 and a=63 row-drop cells expand into sums of 15 and 63 derived sub-expressions — define them as named defs with `attribute [local irreducible]` plus one Affine lemma each (as hot4o, xSelExpr and mismatchCount already do) or the simp-based localLength proofs blow up.

THE FINAL-ADD REORDER IS PERMITTED BY THE SCREENING, BUT THE GUARD WIDENS FROM 22/22 TO 30/30. Both mismatchCount predicates depend only on input.scalarBits, and TTop' only on db, so the screen can sit between the 19-step chain and a 20th ChainExt exactly as it sits before FinalAdd today; the x_A != x_T fact it establishes is about st27.x vs TTop'.x — THE SAME WIRES in either arrangement — so the exceptional-scalar analysis transfers verbatim, and isInf := zCancel and the special-point output mux are untouched. THE CORRECTION TO THE EARLIER 2016 ESTIMATE: Mux costs (size M, size M), and in chain form the routed object is a ChainState (x 4 + lam 4 + TP 8 = 16 wires), not an AffPoint (8), because ChainExt.Assumptions needs OnCurve <x, impliedY x lam TP> and impliedY = lam*(TP.x - x) - TP.y is not constant unless TP is muxed too. So the lever is 2000, not 2016, if taken BEFORE the folds — and only 762 if taken after them, since the ChainStart + ChainFinish it deletes are by then already folded. The final total is 49536 either way. UPSIDE VARIANT: inline stageC1/stageX instead of calling the FormalCircuit wrapper and split soundness on `exceptional`, and only x needs routing (4/4) — the sole completeness obligation is x != x_T, dischargeable by picking x_safe outside the 16 compile-time top-window x-coordinates at zero rows. That recovers 24 more score for a bespoke proof.

THE MASTER COST LAW, DERIVED FROM THE RECORD'S OWN GADGETS AND CALIBRATED TO 1.6%: score ~= 2 * M * (256 + Wq + Wc), where M is THE NUMBER OF MATERIALISED EMULATED FIELD ELEMENTS. The multiply-subtract decomposes EXACTLY as 512 + 19 + 370: 512 = 4 limbs x (63 alloc + 64 constr) of ToBitsAffine plus 4 witness allocs = materialising ONE element; 19 = the sparse x

= 256 rows; the record's 252 allocations + 256 constraints is EXACTLY that floor. CONSEQUENCE THAT REFRAMES THE WHOLE PROBLEM: no encoding trick makes a 256-bit range check cheaper, so the ONLY lever on the 86% of the circuit that is range-check bits is REDUCING M. 'Carry values unreduced for several steps' is NOT the answer; 'never let the intermediate exist' is.

THE FOLD CONSTANT'S LIMB ALIGNMENT IS WORTH 22 BITS OF CARRY, AND IT IS THE GATE ON EVERYTHING ELSE. c = 2^32 + 977 is ONE 33-bit limb in base 2^64 (f = 32) but the two TINY limbs (977, 1) in base 2^32 (f ~ 10) — and f enters the carry width LINEARLY. Re-costing the certificate post-fold with the master law: 4x64 CERT = 365, 8x32 CERT = 214, 9x29 = 218, 10x26 = 213, 16x16 = 186. The gain splits as -64 bits from n and -44 from f, against +16 for the extra cells. THE PENALTY IS THE MUX, NOT THE CERTIFICATE: VarLookup is 15 FlaggedPoint muxes of 2k+1 cells, so 135 rows at k=4 and 255 at k=8 (+240 per step, +14,880 over the loop) — WHICH IS EXACTLY CANCELLED by porting the fixed-base all-odd recode (an 8-entry +- table is 7 nodes x 2k cells + k negate rows = 120 rows at k=8). SHIP THE TWO TOGETHER OR NEITHER. Modelled effect of 8x32 alone: -26,600 over 62 steps plus about -6,000 on the ~40 non-loop certificates. THIS CORROBORATES THE OLD 26-32-BIT CROSS-CODEBASE FINDING FROM A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT DIRECTION, POST-FOLD: 901 -> ~745 per multiply-subtract is 17%, against the 18-22% the pre-fold comparison predicted. NON-UNIFORM LIMBS DO NOT HELP: cell magnitude is driven by the MAXIMUM limb width, so [32,64,64,64,32] still gives 2^130 cells and buys nothing; the RSA MixedRadix gadget does not transfer, and no constraint system in existence uses non-uniform limbs.

PORT THE FIXED-BASE ALL-ODD RECODE INTO THE VARIABLE-BASE LOOP — IT HALVES THE TABLE, HALVES THE LOOKUP, AND DELETES THE EXCEPTION APPARATUS. Recode each 64-bit fake-GLV coefficient with digits d_i = 2*b_i - 1 in {+-1} (a pure wire permutation, 0/0), so sum d_i 2^i = 2m - 2^64 + 1 and EVERY DIGIT IS NONZERO. Then no position can select the identity and no two consecutive sites can collide, so the whole loop uses INCOMPLETE addition guarded by a Lean hypothesis: -100 per step of exception apparatus. The table becomes 8 entries (+- pairs) instead of 16, so VarLookup goes from 15 muxes of 9 cells to 7 muxes of 8 cells plus a k-row conditional y-negation: 135 -> 60 rows at k=4, 255 -> 120 at k=8. THE PARITY OBLIGATION AND ITS HONEST PRICE: the fake-GLV kernel lattice has determinant n, which is ODD, so it surjects onto (Z/2)^4 and an all-odd representative ALWAYS exists — but the pigeonhole bound then needs |u| < 2^65..2^66, i.e. ONE OR TWO EXTRA LOOP STEPS (+3k to +6k) against ~22k saved. CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE IF THAT IS UNPALATABLE: offset every table entry by a fixed constant point C; the accumulated (2^64 - 1)*C is a compile-time constant, so the terminal assertion becomes sum = (2^64 - 1)*C at ZERO cost — though that only kills the identity case, not consecutive collisions. NOTE THIS IS ALSO THE PREREQUISITE FOR THE Y-FREE LOOP, which is blocked precisely because table entry 0 is the point at infinity.

THE j=0 CM IDENTITY P + phi(P) = (beta^2 * x, -y) COSTS ZERO ROWS — CORRECTING MY OWN 'j-INVARIANT 0 BUYS NOTHING' NOTE. Because 1 + lambda + lambda^2 = 0 in the endomorphism ring, P, phi(P) and phi^2(P) are COLLINEAR (they are the three intersections of the horizontal line y = y_P with y^2 = x^3 + 7), so P + phi(P) = -phi^2(P) = (beta^2 * x_P, -y_P) — a pure constant scaling and a negation, BOTH FREE. VERIFIED 200/200 on real secp256k1 points. The 16-entry fake-GLV table needs 11 non-trivial subset sums of {P, phiP, Q, phiQ}; two of them (P + phiP and Q + phiQ) are now free, so the build drops from about 12.6 additions to 9, worth roughly -5,400. In the 8-entry +- table of the all-odd recode the same identity gives A = P + phiP and C = Q + phiQ free, leaving 10 additions. MY EARLIER NOTE SAID 'j-invariant 0 / a = 0 buys exactly zero rows' — that is true of the ENDOMORPHISM EVALUATION (a field addition is free), but the COLLINEARITY relation is a genuine free group addition and the corpus was not using it.

DROP CANONICITY ON WITNESSED SLOPES — THE RIVAL DOES THIS AND WE DO NOT, AND IT IS WORTH ~2584. Measured against RajeshRk18's 561573 tree: ValidP is 260/267 in BOTH trees, but the rival adds NormalizeFe at 252/256 and uses it where we use ValidP. Delta 8 allocations + 11 constraints = 19 SCORE PER USE. MECHANISM: NormalizeFe is just the four ToBitsAffine 63 limb decompositions proving BigInt.Normalized (value < 2^256); it OMITS ValidP's sparse-prime tail (3 IsZeroField + 2 prefix products + 3 quadratic assertions). A slope lambda is a DIVISION WITNESS THAT ONLY EVER FEEDS MULTIPLICATION CERTIFICATES, so it never needs to be the canonical representative — canonicity is uniqueness, and nothing downstream needs uniqueness. THE PORT IS EASIER FOR US THAN FOR THEM. Their version needs widened-quotient scaffolding (Fe.ValidW2 widened to 2^(64*4+1)-1, the hab_lt hypothesis dropped, quotient bound q < 6*2^(Bm) instead of q < 6n) because their certificates carry a value bound on a. OURS DO NOT: MulModFold.Assumptions and MulModFoldT.Assumptions are PURELY LIMBWISE — (all i, a[i].val < Ca) and (all i, b[i].val < Cb) and (all i, target[i].val < Nt) — with NO value bound on a at all, and in MulModSub2W2 the ha_valid.2 component is never used. So we only need to (i) swap ValidP.circuit lam for a NormalizeFe-style assertion in DivOrZeroF3 and DivUncheckedD3, (ii) weaken three Assumptions, (iii) re-prove the two hlam_valid.2 uses in the den = 0 branch via divisibility — take hdvd : p divides value(lam) and conclude decodeFe lam = 0 by ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff, which is all any consumer needs. INSTANCE COUNT: 62 glvStep x 2 (slopeXS + slope2) + 1 glvStepLastSlope + 9 completeAdd in the table = 134 divOrZeroF3, plus 2 divUncheckedD3 in phiPairAdd = 136 x 19 = 2584.

HEADROOM VERDICT: RANK THREE OF SEVEN, ~4700 AT STAKE, ALL MECHANICAL. THE BORROW-PACKED y-NEGATION SELECT — CORRECTING THE ENTRY THAT SAYS THE SIGN BIT COSTS NOTHING. That entry claims '-P = (x,-y) so the sign bit drives ONE modular negation of y (an affine op), NOT a second multiplexer'. LIMBWISE p - y IS NOT AFFINE — it needs three borrows — and the naive fix IS a second multiplexer: the pre-fold tree witnessed yDeltaProd : fields 60 (60 alloc + 60 rows), one full 4-limb selection of the sign delta. THE CHEAP FORM, SHIPPED AT SelectCost.lean:216-224 AND 303-318: pack the three borrow bits of p - yTable[j] into ONE small scalar per table entry (packedTable = Borrow.packedNat), select that scalar over the SAME outer one-hot with a 15-cell product array, witness bits : fields 3 with 3 booleanity rows, and pin them with ONE row selectedE = b0 + 2*b1 + 4*b2. Then every limb of the delta is affine: P256_limb - 2*negLimb + b_limb*2^64 - b_{limb-1}. COST 15 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 22 cells against 60+60 = 120, i.e. -42 alloc / -41 rows, MEASURED as part of Select12 342/342 -> 298/299. GENERAL RULE: when a signed table needs a modular negation of a selected multi-limb value, select the BORROW PATTERN (a few bits) rather than the negated limbs, and let the limbs fall out affinely.

GLV ON A FIXED-BASE COMB IS A PURE REPARAMETRIZATION, NOT A LEVER — THIS SUPERSEDES THE 'SWEEP THE GLV DIMENSION' AND 'COMBINE mLSB-SET COMB WITH GLV' ENTRIES, WHICH ARE STALE AND MUST NOT BE ACTED ON. There are exactly two ways to build a GLV comb and BOTH LAND ON A CONFIGURATION A PLAIN COMB ALREADY REACHES. (a) TWO SEPARATE CHAINS: split k = k1 + k2*lambda and run two 128-bit combs at width w. Windows = 2*(128/w) = 256/w, IDENTICAL to a plain comb at width w — same select, same addition, same count. The shared table (one table serves both halves because phi is a free constant scaling) is the entire prize, and the prize is worth ZERO because the table is compile-time constant. (b) ONE COMBINED LOOKUP indexed by the pair (d1,d2), T[d1][d2] = d1*2^(wi)*G + d2*2^(wi)*lambda*G: that is 2^(2w) constant points per window and 128/w windows, which is EXACTLY A PLAIN COMB AT WIDTH 2w — same window count, same table size per window, same one-select-plus-one-addition. In both variants GLV then ADDITIONALLY pays the mod-n decomposition check (the variable-base 4-dim GLVScalarRelation is 2932/2954; a 2-dim one is a fraction of that but not free), so it is STRICTLY DOMINATED. THE ARGUMENT FOR (b) IS INDEPENDENT OF HOW THE SELECTOR SCALES, which is why it is the one to quote: both configurations hand the selector an IDENTICAL problem — pick one of 2^(2w) constant points — so no model of Select12's factored one-hot is needed. IT ALSO DOES NOT RELIEVE THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, which is not circuit cost but the VERIFIER TIMEOUT from elaborating the chord-slope certification table: variant (b) needs the same 2^(2w) constants as a plain width-2w comb. ARITHMETIC CORRECTION to the earlier 'GLV buys nothing' entry: it compares GLV at width 12 PER HALF (2*ceil(128/12) = 22 windows) against a plain width-12 comb (21) and reads the difference as a structural loss; that is a CEILING ARTIFACT. The correct comparison is GLV w=6 per half against plain w=12, which ties exactly. The conclusion is unchanged and now rests on an isomorphism rather than on a window count. THE GENERAL RULE: GLV's win is that it shrinks the PRECOMPUTED TABLE needed per scalar bit covered. In this cost model a fixed-base table is free, so GLV optimises the one resource nothing is charged for. Reach for it on VARIABLE-base work, where the table must be built in-circuit, and never on a comb. THE ONLY LEVERS THAT MOVE A COMB REMAIN: fewer windows (wider w, bounded by the table's elaboration cost, not by circuit cost), a cheaper selector, and a cheaper per-addition certificate.

THE GENERAL LAW BEHIND THE FIFTH LOST-GROUND CASE — AN AFFINE EXPRESSION IS ALREADY A VALUE; NEVER MATERIALISE A COPY OF ONE TO SATISFY A TYPE. Any gadget returning `fields n` can return n AFFINE EXPRESSIONS over wires it has already allocated. Witnessing a fresh vector and linking it with `forEach ... assertZero (copy - expr)` type-checks, looks like ordinary plumbing, and costs exactly n allocations + n constraints for zero information — the copy is determined by the original in one direction and constrains nothing in the other. THIS IS THE SAME LEDGER ERROR AS 'assertion, not value' SEEN FROM THE OTHER SIDE: there the deleted cell was the TARGET of a certificate that already pinned it; here the deleted cell is a DUPLICATE of an expression the surrounding rows already pin. AUDIT RULE, RUNNABLE ACROSS THE WHOLE TREE: grep for `assertZero (p.1 - p.2)`, `assertZero (a - b)` and any `Vector.zip`/`forEach` whose body is a bare difference of two wires. Each hit is n free score unless one of the two sides is genuinely unconstrained. Read the ALLOCATION column to spot it — a linking loop shows up as equal alloc and constr deltas of exactly the vector length.

THE STRONGEST EXTERNAL LEAD FOR THIS CHALLENGE: gnark's SIGNED-DIGIT FIXED-BASE COMB, PR #1797 (opened 2026-07-24), https://github.com/Consensys/gnark/pull/1797. The recipe for a compile-time-constant base: recode the scalar into ODD SIGNED DIGITS, group into constant windows, precompute the table (free for us — the entries are numerals), run the ENTIRE addition chain with INCOMPLETE additions carrying Y IMPLICITLY, and do exactly ONE complete addition in the tail, with deferred zero-assertions plus a subgroup check preserving soundness. Reported in R1CS at emulated G1 ScalarMulBase 106674 -> 10984 (-89.7%) and BN254 G2 constant-base 215732 -> 19648 (-90.9%). WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW FOR US, since we already run odd signed digits and constant tables: (i) ALL additions incomplete with the exception apparatus DEFERRED to a single tail assertion rather than discharged per step, and (ii) carrying Y IMPLICITLY through the chain so intermediate y-coordinates are never materialised — which is the same shape as our own two-wire-y item but pushed to its limit, and it composes with it. MEASURE our current per-window addition against an implicit-Y incomplete add before committing. READ THE CAVEAT BEFORE TRUSTING ANY GNARK NUMBER: gnark's headline emulated-arithmetic counts are NOT reachable in our model, because its Field.MulMod/Eval deferred check uses a Fiat-Shamir challenge from a prover commitment (in-circuit randomness) and its range checks are LogUp (lookups). What transfers is the CIRCUIT STRUCTURE, and only that. Treat every percentage below as evidence a lever exists, never as our predicted saving.

SELECTION IS A SOLVED PROBLEM AND THE ANSWER IS A HYBRID, NOT A ONE-HOT — THIS SUPERSEDES THE 'Select12 MISSES THE 2^w-w-1 MINIMUM' FRAMING. Split each window's w bits as w = a + b. BOTTOM (b bits): allocate every nonlinear monomial over those b bits, each as one product m_S = m_{S minus i} * b_i, costing 2^b - b - 1 products; every entry of the 2^b one-hot is then a FREE AFFINE combination. MIDDLE (free): for each of the 2^a top branches and each output column c, the leaf value u_{c,i} = sum_beta eB_beta * T[i,beta].c is a FREE AFFINE combination — this is where the constant table finally pays nothing. TOP (a bits): a binary MUX tree over the 2^a leaves, t = u0 + b_j(u1 - u0), costing exactly 2^a - 1 products PER OUTPUT COLUMN. So P(w,C) = min_a [(2^(w-a) - (w-a) - 1) + C(2^a - 1)], minimised at a* ~ ceil((w - log2 C)/2) with minimum ~2*sqrt(C * 2^w). MEASURED AT w=10, C=11: per-column MUX tree 11,253 products; full shared monomial one-hot 1,013; HYBRID at a=3,b=7 just 197 — 5.1x better than the best pure method and 57x better than per-column. DO NOT build the one-hot with shared monomials at the top; that costs an extra 2^a - a - 1 and the MUX tree needs no monomials at all. TWO LOWER BOUNDS CLOSE THIS DIRECTION: (i) materialising a FULL one-hot costs exactly 2^w - w - 1 products, proved by a span-dimension argument — wires are functions on {0,1}^w, the initial span {1, b_1..b_w} has dimension w+1, each product row raises the span by at most 1, and the 2^w one-hot entries span everything — SO NEVER MATERIALISE A ONE-HOT FOR w ABOVE ABOUT 9; (ii) the hybrid is optimal up to a factor 2 by Paterson-Stockmeyer preconditioning. ALSO NOTE: selected values need NO range check, because z = sum e_j T_j with an exact one-hot IS identically a table entry, so its limb bounds come free — only the accumulator and lambda pay.

RE-OPTIMISE THE WINDOW WIDTH AFTER EVERY ADDITION-COST WIN — THE OPTIMUM MOVES DOWN, AND HOLDING w FIXED LEAVES THOUSANDS ON THE TABLE. Selection grows like 2^(w/2)/w while the addition count only falls like 1/w, so the stationarity condition is 4*sqrt(C)*2^(w/2)*(w*ln2/2 - 1) = S_add. MODELLED CURVE at S_add = 1476, C = 11: w=9 -> 49,612; w=10 -> 47,656; w=11 -> 48,140; w=12 -> 49,636; w=13 -> 53,116 — flat between 10 and 11, rising fast past 12. At S_add ~ 1800 the optimum is w ~ 11-12, which is consistent with our current ~21 windows. THE ACTIONABLE PART: if S_add were halved to 800 the optimum moves to w ~ 9-10 and the modelled total drops to about 29,600. So any reduction win must be followed by a window re-sweep in the SAME job, or most of it is given back.

MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED: X^8 - X - 977 FACTORS OVER THE BN254 SCALAR FIELD AS LINEAR x QUADRATIC x QUADRATIC x CUBIC, SO t = 4 AND THE WINOGRAD SAVING IS EXACTLY 3 PRODUCTS PER MULTIPLY. Context: with L=32 and k=8, folding the product is EXACTLY reduction modulo f(X) = X^8 - X - 977, since X = 2^32 and X^8 = 2^256 = 2^32 + 977 mod p. The standard route (evaluate at 15 points, multiply pointwise, interpolate) computes all 15 coefficients of the UNREDUCED product and then folds, but you only ever need the 8 folded ones. By Winograd the bilinear complexity of multiplication in F_n[X]/f is 2k - t = 16 - t, achieved by CRT: evaluate at the roots and quotients (free affine), multiply pointwise, interpolate back (free affine). I ran the distinct-degree factorisation directly over n = 21888242871839275222246405745257275088548364400416034343698204186575808495617 and got the degree pattern (1 factor of degree 1, 2 of degree 2, 1 of degree 3), total degree 8, t = 4. SO THE MULTIPLY IS 12 PRODUCTS INSTEAD OF 15, saving t-1 = 3 products = 6 score per non-native multiply, and at 3 multiplies x 25 additions that is 450 SCORE. Real but fourth-order — the agent's guess had been 250-1050 and the true value is at the low end, so queue it only after the reduction and selection work. If a future job changes the limb width, RE-RUN THE FACTORISATION: k=9 (f = X*(X^8 - X - 977)) automatically has t >= 2, and L=16 gives f = X^16 - X^2 - 977.

REJECTED FOR FIXED-BASE, WITH ARITHMETIC. (a) DIVISOR / L(nO) BATCH ADDITION CERTIFICATES: the mechanism is sound and needs no randomness if you check vanishing directly at each point, but n=3 IS ALREADY THE LAMBDA FORM — L(3O) = span{1,x,y}, and f = y + c1 x + c0 vanishing at P1,P2,-P3 IS collinearity, with Vieta giving exactly the standard constraints and lambda = -c1, so the incumbent is already the optimal divisor certificate. For n >= 4 the raw addition arithmetic marginally wins (n=7: 6,834 vs 7,370) BUT every table point must then supply x^2, x^3, x^4, xy, x^2 y as SELECTED COLUMNS, taking C from 11 to ~32-56; since selection scales as sqrt(C) that is 10,244 -> ~28,600 at w=10, a NET LOSS OF AT LEAST 12,000. The constant table being free does not save this: it is free to BUILD, not free to SELECT FROM. (b) LAMBDA-FREE FORMULATIONS (line + cubic): deletes lambda's 512-score range check but puts y3 INSIDE a product, destroying the carry-y-unreduced trick (+512) and adding a degree-3 identity needing 22 evaluation points — 1,922 vs 1,476 per addition, a 30% loss. (c) FEWER/WIDER LIMBS FOR THE TABLE POINT to shrink C: selecting x as 2 limbs of 128 bits takes C from 11 to 5 and saves 1,560, but blows the product coefficient bound from 2^67 to 2^163 so the reduction goes 189 -> 1,410 — NET LOSS ~29,000. The carry cost is far more sensitive to limb width than selection is. (d) MERGING THE TWO REDUCTIONS PER ADDITION INTO ONE is UNSOUND (E1 and E2 are only known to be multiples of p, not sign/magnitude separated), and packing their carry witnesses into one range-checked value is exactly cost-neutral since range-check score is linear in bits. (e) SIGNED-DIGIT / NAF / wNAF RECODINGS: the table is free so halving it buys nothing, and the only real content — making every digit nonzero to delete identity handling — costs one extra window and touches neither dominant term. About zero. (f) BINARY ADDITION TREE instead of a sequential chain: same N-1 additions and same N-1 range-checked outputs; the only effect is the unreduced-y bound growing as log N instead of N, worth about 2 carry bits.

AND ITS STATED LESSON — 'the quotient is dominated by an unreduced low half, so the same move buys nothing' — HAS THE IMPLICATION REVERSED: low-half domination is PRECISELY WHY W_q ~ n + log2(k), hence linear in n, hence exactly the thing narrow limbs shrink. RANK-2 PAIRING IN THE SELECT'S TOP MUX — NEW, -1,974 ALONE AND -2,730 STACKED WITH PACKED-y, AND IT IS THE FIRST SELECT-SIDE WIN FOUND IN MANY PASSES. CALIBRATION FIRST, so the numbers are checkable: Select12's 257 allocations decompose, from the witness blocks in the isR1CS_sub_select proof at Comb.lean:224-300, as w 11 + blk 5 + i4 9 + i6 45 + i7 63 + xa 48 + xb 12 + ya 48 + yb 12 + yo 4 = 257, matching select_sub_localLength = 257 at Comb.lean:79. Structurally: XNOR/sign 11, low-block one-hot on 7 bits 122 (= 5+9+45+63, which yields all 128 entries as FREE affine combinations), top MUX over 2^4 leaves at 15 products x 8 columns = 120, y-sign mux 4. THE MECHANISM: the top stage computes f_c = SUM_{i<16} u_i * leaf_{c,i} with u the one-hot on the top 4 bits and leaf_{c,i} = SUM_j T_c[i,j] e_j a FREE affine combination of the low one-hot. The tree spends ONE PRODUCT PER RANK-1 TERM. But AN R1CS ROW CAN CARRY RANK 2. With u and e one-hot (u_i u_{i'} = 0, e_j e_{j'} = delta e_j), set A = u_i + SUM_j T_c[i',j] e_j and B = u_{i'} + SUM_j T_c[i,j] e_j; then A*B = u_i*leaf_{c,i} + u_{i'}*leaf_{c,i'} + SUM_j T_c[i,j]T_c[i',j]*e_j, where the cross term u_i u_{i'} VANISHES IDENTICALLY on the boolean cube and the (gamma.e)(delta.e) term COLLAPSES TO A LINEAR combination of the e_j — a free affine correction with compile-time coefficients. ONE ROW DELIVERS TWO OF THE SIXTEEN RANK-1 TERMS, so a column costs 8 products instead of 15. EXACT COST: the 4x4 top tensor costs +9 (blk already holds the two pair-products), columns 8x15 = 120 -> 8x8 = 64, net -47 units per select = -94 score x 21 selects = -1,974. STATES: live 122 + 120 + 4 = 257; packed-y 122 + 90 + 2 = 225 (-1,344, which this model reproduces to the unit, and is why I trust it); pairing 122 + 9 + 64 + 4 = 210 (-1,974); BOTH 122 + 9 + 48 + 2 = 192 (-2,730).

THE RANK-2 PAIRING'S SOUNDNESS OBLIGATION AND ITS ONE REAL RISK. WHAT BREAKS IF (i) IS DROPPED: the prover makes e a NON-one-hot vector, the correction term SUM_j T_c[i,j]T_c[i',j] e_j stops matching (gamma.e)(delta.e), and f_c can take a value OFF THE TABLE. The one-hot property is already load-bearing for the current gadget, so this is not a new assumption — but the QUADRATIC orthogonality is now used where only the linear sum was used before, and that is the lemma to write first. A PARAMETER-COUNTING BOUND ON ANY SELECT GADGET, AND THE FACTOR-2.2 GAP IT EXPOSES — RESEARCH ITEM, NOT A QUEUED EDIT. With m product rows on k = 11 bits and C generic 64-bit output columns, the circuit has m^2 + (23+C)m + 12C free coefficients against C*2^11 = 12,288 generic table constants, giving m >= about 83 at C=6. The rank-2 pairing lands at 122 + 9 + 48 = 179. THE GAP IS A FACTOR OF ABOUT 2.2 AND IT IS REAL HEADROOM, NOT SLACK IN THE ACCOUNTING: the 122 spent building the low one-hot is nearly pure overhead under the counting argument, since only 96 specific functions of 7 bits are needed, spanning 96 dimensions, floor 88. CLOSING IT MEANS FINDING AN EXPLICIT RANK-2 DECOMPOSITION OF THE SPECIFIC 6 x 16 x 128 TABLE TENSOR — a computational search, once per window and there are 21, where each solution is a pile of compile-time constants that Lean checks by ring or decide. THE ONE-MATERIALISATION-PER-POINT LAW, AND WHY EVERY ALTERNATIVE REPRESENTATION LOSES — THIS CLOSES A WHOLE FAMILY OF IDEAS AT ONCE. EVERY scheme examined obeys: ONE MATERIALISED 256-BIT FIELD ELEMENT PLUS ONE CONGRUENCE CERTIFICATE PER ABSORBED TABLE POINT. The chord/lambda form HITS it, the divisor family TIES it, every projective form MISSES by 2-4x, and the ladder misses by 25x. (a) COORDINATE SYSTEMS ARE A TRAP AND THE RECEIVED FRAMING IS BACKWARDS: in this cost model THE WITNESSED SLOPE IS THE CHEAP THING — lambda is one materialisation at 512 and buys a degree-2 identity. Projective/Jacobian/Edwards exist to eliminate divisions in models where divisions cost; here they eliminate the witness and pay in ALGEBRAIC DEGREE, and degree is exactly what forces materialisation, since an unreduced expression may be a multiplicand only up to degree 2 at B=64 and degree 3 at B=32. Counting monomial degree in materialised values: affine + implicit y + telescoped x + witnessed lambda reaches degree 3 with ONE materialisation per addition (~1,141); mixed JACOBIAN reaches X3 degree 9 and Y3 degree 13, forcing >= 4 materialisations (>= 3,400); PROJECTIVE reaches degree 7-8, >= 3 (>= 2,600); EXTENDED TWISTED EDWARDS is bidegree (2,2) with X3 = E*F at degree 4, forcing 4 (>= 3,500); CO-Z is degree 2 with 2 (>= 2,300). EDWARDS IS DOUBLY DEAD: secp256k1 has PRIME group order n, so every F_p-isogenous curve has the same odd order and NO CURVE IN THE ISOGENY CLASS HAS RATIONAL 2-TORSION — hence no Montgomery or Edwards model exists over F_p at all. (The order-parity argument was verified; the isogeny class was not enumerated.) X-ONLY / MONTGOMERY LADDER, for completeness: differential addition needs x(P-Q) known, which for a comb means one materialisation per step AND 256 steps rather than 20, about 512 materialisations — dead by 25x independently of the sign-freedom unsoundness already recorded. THE CURRENT REPRESENTATION IS ALREADY THE DEGREE-OPTIMAL ONE. DO NOT SPEND A SLOT HERE.

THE DIVISOR / L(nO) CERTIFICATE FAMILY IS CLOSED AT EVERY n BY A DIMENSION COUNT — this generalises the earlier n=2 refutation to the whole family including n=4, which was never priced. To absorb k table points you need f vanishing at k table points, the accumulator-in, and minus the accumulator-out: k+2 zeros, so f lies in L((k+2)O), which has DIMENSION k+2, i.e. k+1 projective coefficients, one of which is fixed affinely by f(A) = 0. SO k COEFFICIENTS MUST BE MATERIALISED FOR k POINTS — RATIO EXACTLY 1, FOR EVERY k. Certificates are likewise k, one per f(T_i) = 0, and the accumulator-out is free by Vieta (SUM x_roots = c_2^2 - 2 c_1 at k=2, the same telescope mechanism). So the divisor family TIES the chord form on the chain and then LOSES ON THE SELECTS, because evaluating f(T_i) needs x_T^j and y_T x_T^j as SELECTED COLUMNS: k=1 (the current chord) needs C=6 at 236 per select and 9,912 across 21 windows; k=2 with f = x^2 + c_2 y + c_1 x + c_0 needs C=12 at 326 per select and 13,692 (+3,780); k=20 with f in L(22O) needs C=84 at about 830 per select and about 34,860 (+24,000). AND AT k >= 2 THE f(A) = 0 CONDITION CONTAINS c_1 * x_A (degree 3) AND x_A^2 (degree 4) against a telescoped accumulator, and DEGREE 4 IS DEAD EVEN AT B=32, so the accumulator must be materialised and the ratio rises to 1.5 per point.

BATCHING THE CONGRUENCE CERTIFICATES IS WORTH ABOUT 90, NOT THOUSANDS, AND THAT 90 IS ALREADY QUEUED. Two mechanisms, both priced negative. (a) A CONSTANT-COEFFICIENT LINEAR COMBINATION IS UNSOUND AND MAGNITUDE SEPARATION CANNOT RESCUE IT: SUM c_j E_j = 0 mod p does not imply each E_j = 0, and writing E_j = e_j p + r_j the check only gives SUM 2^(Bj) r_j = 0 mod p, easily satisfied with every r_j nonzero, BECAUSE THE E_j ARE NOT BOUNDED BY p — and making them bounded IS materialisation. THE REDUCTION IS THE COST; YOU CANNOT BATCH WHAT YOU HAVE NOT REDUCED. (b) A PACKED INTEGER IDENTITY with per-site quotients, SUM 2^(Bj)(L_j - R_j - q_j p) = 0 over Z, DOES work, but each q_j still needs its own ~110-bit range check and the carry chain's total width is the sum of the per-site widths; range checking is linear in bits and proved optimal at 2 per bit, so the only saving is the per-site FIXED overhead — which is exactly the +90 allocations-versus-rows gap already identified as certificate inversion plus the vacuous GroupedFlex native row. ONE GLOBAL QUOTIENT IS STRICTLY WORSE: it grows to about 6,500 bits. ALSO CONFIRMED NEGATIVE: GLV / endomorphism / scalar recoding on a FIXED-BASE comb. phi is genuinely free (x -> beta x is a constant multiply, hence affine), but 2- or 3-dimensional GLV writes s = a + b*lambda + c*lambda^2 with a+b+c still 256 bits of digits, hence THE SAME WINDOW COUNT AND THE SAME TABLE SIZES — a joint digit triple is just a wider window. FREE-TO-BUILD IS NOT FREE-TO-SELECT. Double-base and non-uniform widths re-swept and confirmed inside +-120.

THE MODULUS CLAIMS ARE VERIFIED, AND THE UNIQUENESS BOUND IS EXACTLY 2^31 — ONE BIT MORE AND IT FAILS. Two monic degree-8 moduli vanishing at 2^32 mod p differ by SUM d_i 2^(32i) = 0 mod p with degree <= 7; with |d_i| <= 2^31 the maximum |SUM| is 2^31 (2^256 - 1)/(2^32 - 1) < p, forcing SUM = 0, and successive division by 2^32 forces d = 0. AT BOUND 2^32 THE ARGUMENT FAILS, because p's own base-2^32 digits are (0xfffffc2f, 0xfffffffe, 0xffffffff x 6), ALL BELOW 2^32. So X^8 - X - 977 is unique iff the bound is 2^31. ITS FACTORISATION (1)(2)(2)(3) WAS RECOMPUTED INDEPENDENTLY by distinct-degree plus Cantor-Zassenhaus over r, squarefree with recomposition checked, giving k = 4 and Winograd rank 2N - k = 12, i.e. <12,12> per product. OTHER MODULI CHECKED AND REJECTED: X^16 - X^2 - 977 factors (2,4,4,6) for rank 28; X^2 - cF factors (1,1) for rank 2 but its coefficients exceed r and it is unusable. HIGHER-DEGREE MODULI ARE FORCED TO BE MULTIPLES OF THE UNIQUE ONE, so every extra factor arrives with an extra position and is never profitable.

THE TELESCOPE IS CONFIRMED NOT DEAD — NO IN-LOOP CONSUMER REQUIRES A NORMALIZED ACCUMULATOR x, AND THE FREENESS CLAIM IS VERIFIED FROM SOURCE. MulMod.interpolatedMul (InterpMul.lean:15-27) allocates 2m-1 fresh witnesses and pins them with 2m-1 rows; its OUTPUT is Vector.mapRange (2m-1) fun i => var {index := off+i} (interpolatedMul_output, :29) and affineW_interpolatedMul_output (:170) proves AffineW. Affine closure under +, - and CONSTANT scaling is Affine.add / Affine.sub / Affine.fconst_mul, used exactly this way in FoldQuot.affine_foldLhs (FoldQuot.lean:92). So summing 21 convolutions with alternating signs and constant multipliers is ZERO allocations and ZERO rows. R1CS legality also holds: rows come from isR1CSRow_mul_sub (affine)(affine)(affine) at InterpMul.lean:198, which admits arbitrarily WIDE affine operands — one product per row, syntactically. THE NORMALIZATION AUDIT, which is what could have killed it: Chain.ChainExt.Assumptions (Chain.lean:295) does require BigInt.Normalized 64 input.x, BUT that is the CURRENT gadget's own spec, which the telescope replaces, and its semantic use is only decodeFe input.x and decodeFe x != decodeFe T.x, both CONGRUENCE-ONLY. FoldQuot.val_foldRhs's Normalized 64 is the bound lemma for the existing rhs shape; a telescope rhs gets its own. GroupedFlex.Assumptions (:376) needs only lhs[k].val < Nf_L k, which is parametrised and bound-agnostic. interpolatedMul soundness needs only 2m-1 < p. THE ONLY HARD REQUIREMENTS ARE TERMINAL — Chain.ChainFinish.Assumptions (:347) and FinalAdd.ImplicitAssumptions — and one materialisation discharges both.

A FREE 30 PER WINDOW THAT THE ORIGINAL PROPOSAL MISSED — MERGE THE TWO lambda*x PRODUCTS. The slope identity is lambda_j * xT_j + lambda_{j-1} * xT_{j-1} - (lambda_j + lambda_{j-1}) * x_{j-1} = yT_j + yT_{j-1}. Since lambda_j + lambda_{j-1} is an AFFINE 8-vector with limbs below 2^33, THE TWO lambda * x PRODUCTS MERGE INTO ONE: 30 instead of 60, at a cost of one bit. The proposal's 118 products per window should be 88 (lambda^2 30 + merged 30 + mixed-radix 28). THE GENERAL FORM: whenever two products share a multiplicand and their OTHER operands are both affine, factor the shared operand out — the sum of the other two is affine and free, so two convolutions become one. Grep any chain for A*C + B*C with A, B affine.

So materialise x_20 as a normalized 4x64 Emu immediately BEFORE FinalAdd and FinalAdd IS UNCHANGED. That materialisation carries NO NEW PRODUCTS — it is just telescope(x_20) = q * P256 + x_20 mod p: witness plus NormalizeImplicit 512, quotient witness 1, RangeCheck 40 bits -> 79 at B=32 or 37 bits -> 73 at B=16, GroupedFlex gf=[5,1,2] G=3 W=70 -> 140 at B=32 or gf=[10,1,5] G=3 W=56 -> 110 at B=16. TOTAL 732 AT B=32, 696 AT B=16. lambda needs NO re-materialisation: lam64[i] = SUM_t lam_narrow[k*i+t] * 2^(B*t) is a free affine recombination and is Normalized 64 BY CONSTRUCTION from the narrow range checks — 'witness narrow, view wide' holds at the FinalAdd interface too. NOTE FinalAdd's Mux (M := Chain.ChainState) at <16,16> grows if lam widens to 8 or 16 limbs (+8 or +24); rounding error, not included above.

FAKE GLV IS A CATEGORY ERROR FOR FIXED-BASE — DO NOT PORT THE VARIABLE-BASE TREE'S CENTRAL TRICK OVER HERE. This is the obvious question (the sibling tree's best idea, why not use it?) and the answer is decisive. FAKE GLV BUYS A SHORTER SCALAR AT THE PRICE OF MAKING THE BASE VARIABLE: you witness Q = [s]G and assert a relation such as u1*G + u2*phiG + v1*Q + v2*phiQ = O with 64-bit coefficients over 64 interleaved positions, halving or quartering the scalar length. FOR VARIABLE-BASE THAT PRICE IS ZERO, because the base was already variable — which is exactly why it is the right technique there. FOR FIXED-BASE IT IS CATASTROPHIC, BECAUSE THE ENTIRE ADVANTAGE OF FIXED-BASE IS THAT THE BASE IS CONSTANT AND THE 21 TABLES ARE THEREFORE COMPILE-TIME CONSTANTS, COSTING NOTHING TO BUILD. Under Fake GLV, G and phiG stay constant but Q and phiQ are WITNESSED, so every subset sum involving them must be COMPUTED IN CIRCUIT: the variable-base tree pays <16881,17074> = 33,955 for precisely that 16-entry table, and its 64-position interleaved MSM is another ~311,000. Even halving the table for the two constant generators leaves you needing the whole MSM under about 33,000 to beat the current comb, a tenfold improvement on the measured variable-base figure. NOT PLAUSIBLE. THE RATIO TELLS THE STORY DIRECTLY: fixed-base sits at 49,196 and variable-base at 313,980, a factor of 6.4, and that gap IS the free-table advantage. THE GENERALISABLE FORM, WORTH CARRYING TO ANY CHALLENGE PAIR: before porting a technique between two circuits for the same primitive, ask WHAT THE TECHNIQUE SPENDS, not just what it saves. A trick that is free in one setting because a resource is already spent there can be ruinous in a setting where that resource is still intact.

*** THE SELECTOR IS BEATABLE BY SQRT(2) AND THE CONSTRUCTION IS VERIFIED OVER THE BN254 SCALAR PRIME — THIS SUPERSEDES 'SELECTION IS A SOLVED PROBLEM' AND 'HYBRID SELECTION IS ALREADY DONE AND PROVABLY OPTIMAL'. *** Those entries are right that Select12 attains the PEEL optimum R(w,m) = min_j [m(2^j - 1) + 2^(w-j) - (w-j) - 1] ~ 2*sqrt(m*2^w); they are wrong that peel is the floor. IT IS NOT, AND BEATING IT NEEDS NO SOLVER — pure rank decomposition over F_p. *** THE IDENTITY. *** Split the 11 window bits into a high block A of t bits and a low block B of j bits and BUILD BOTH ONE-HOT VECTORS, cost B(t) + B(j) with B(t) = 2^t - t - 1. Every affine form over the witness is then exactly alpha_a + gamma_c. For two of them, (alpha_a + gamma_c)(beta_a + delta_c) = alpha_a*beta_a + gamma_c*delta_c + (alpha (x) delta + beta (x) gamma). The first term depends on a ALONE so it is a free affine combination of the A one-hot; the second depends on c ALONE so it is free over the C one-hot. *** ONE PRODUCT ROW THEREFORE BUYS A WHOLE RANK-2 MATRIX, NOT A RANK-1 ONE, and each target viewed as a 2^t x 2^j matrix costs ceil(rank/2) rows instead of peel's 2^j - 1. *** *** THE NUMBERS AND THE ONE DISCREPANCY TO RESOLVE LOCALLY. *** Closed form at t=4, j=7: 11 + 120 + 8m, i.e. 179 at m=6 and 187 at m=7. A DP folding this together with peel reports LOWER at m=6 — 170 — while agreeing at m=7. WE RUN m=6, so budget the CONSERVATIVE 179: 210 - 179 = 31 rows per select x 21 selects = 651 rows = *** -1,302 SCORE ***, or -1,680 if the DP's 170 is right. Re-derive the m=6 optimum by hand before committing; the construction is small. Full DP table (peel / new / counting bound): m=1 88/69/35, m=2 119/99/53, m=3 150/118/67, m=4 180/136/78, m=5 195/153/88, m=6 210/170/97, m=7 225/187/106. *** VERIFICATION IS UNUSUALLY STRONG: *** every row checked over the ACTUAL BN254 scalar prime, not a toy prime — each product's two factors verified affine over the current witness, each output verified affine, against random target tables. *** ON 'IT BEATS THE PUBLISHED STATE OF THE ART' — STATE THIS CAREFULLY, IT IS A CROSS-MODEL COMPARISON. *** Boyar & Find, TCS 2018, Thm 7 (arXiv:1407.6169) gives 2(1+o(1))*sqrt(m*2^n) with a Thm 6 lower bound of sqrt(m*2^n) - 2n - m/2, but that whole line is MULTIPLICATIVE COMPLEXITY OVER GF(2), basis (AND, XOR, 1). We are over F_p, where a row is STRICTLY MORE POWERFUL than a GF(2) AND gate — XOR3 is 1 row and 0 ANDs — so coming in under a GF(2) bound is EXPECTED, not remarkable. It is the same GF(2)-does-not-transfer trap recorded elsewhere in this file, for once running in the flattering direction. THE SQRT(2) GAIN OVER PEEL IS REAL AND BANKABLE; THE 'BELOW THE BEST CONSTANT IN PRINT' CLAIM IS NOT ESTABLISHED. *** NEXT RUNG ~155, WELL-FOUNDED. *** Share the rank-2 pieces ACROSS outputs rather than per-output. The shared architecture's Jacobian was computed exactly over F_p and is DOMINANT AT THE COUNTING BOUND at every size tested (8x8 m=2 R=4 -> 128/128; 8x16 m=2 R=7 -> 256/256; 16x16 m=2 R=8 -> 512/512; 16x16 m=3 R=12 -> 768/768), rank rising by exactly 2(n1+n2)+m-8 per product; extrapolating to t=5/j=6 gives 83 + 72 = 155. The object is a 7 x 32 x 64 paired-rank-2 tensor decomposition. NOTE this LIFTS the old 'tensor rank is the wrong invariant' objection — that objection was that the naive contraction exploits sum(e_a) = 1, and this formulation uses that relation explicitly, which is precisely why the alpha*beta and gamma*delta terms are free. But ALS/JENNRICH CANNOT SOLVE IT over F_p: no single block has enough freedom for a linear solve (largest block 9,344 unknowns against 14,336 equations), so alternating methods have no valid step. *** THE ~106 COUNTING BOUND IS CONFIRMED REAL AS A DIMENSION STATEMENT. *** Minimal M for full Jacobian rank over F_p: (6,1) 4/5, (7,1) 6/7, (8,1) 10/11, (9,1) 15/16, (7,2) 10/11, (8,2) 15/16, (7,3) 12/14 — the bound is achieved to within 1-2 rows everywhere tested. So the map IS dominant at M ~ 107-109 and generic targets ARE reachable; the obstruction is purely CONSTRUCTIVE. Treat 155 -> 106 as an open constant in complexity theory, the same sqrt(2) unclosed for univariate polynomials since Paterson-Stockmeyer 1973 — DO NOT FUND IT. *** AND CHECK THE PACKING QUESTION ONCE, THEN CLOSE IT. *** If the m outputs packed into ONE field element the cost collapses to 69 rows. FULL PACKING IS DEAD ON WIDTH: 4 x_T limbs + 2 y_T limbs at 64 bits = 384 > 254. PARTIAL (3+3, m=6 -> m=2 at 99 rows) is open but almost certainly loses on the unpack, since a generic range check is 2 score per bit and 192 bits is 384 score per select against ~71 rows saved. The only rescue is if a SELECTED value's range rides on the selection identity instead of a generic check.

PARTIAL REOPENING OF THE VERDICT — ONE PUBLISHED MECHANISM TARGETS EXACTLY THE GAP THE DIMENSION PROOF LEFT OPEN. The proof above gives T >= 1600 per round for any circuit that MATERIALISES the intermediate round state as an affine form in (x, w); it explicitly does NOT cover cross-round amortisation. There is now a paper doing precisely that: Akpaki & David (Thales Six GTS France), 'Reducing Multiplicative Complexity via Conjugate Cipher', IACR eprint 2026/1365, received 2026-07-02. Abstract verbatim: 'We introduce a generic framework based on conjugacy to reduce the multiplicative complexity of block ciphers. Our approach exploits the ITERATIVE STRUCTURE of the block cipher to build alternative implementation based on conjugate round operations with overall smaller multiplicative complexity.' MECHANISM: replace F by a conjugate round F' = C o F o C^-1, so that F^12 = C^-1 o (F')^12 o C and the conjugation is paid TWICE rather than per round. If C is affine the dimension bound still applies and nothing changes; the content is in a NONLINEAR C, where the trade is 2*MC(C) + 12*MC(F') against 12*MC(F). REPORTED GAINS: 5.5% on Skinny64, 3% on Skinny128 — against best-known implementations, NOT against a proven per-round MC. IF A COMPARABLE GAIN EXISTED FOR KECCAK-p[1600,12] IT WOULD BE 600-1000 ANDs, i.e. score 1200-2000 BELOW 38400, WHICH WOULD TAKE THE RECORD (any strict improvement does, since a tie does not leaderboard). CAVEATS, AND THEY ARE SERIOUS: the paper does not mention Keccak; Skinny's round structure (4 multiplications per S-box, 16 S-boxes per round) is very different from chi's 5-per-S-box with 320 disjoint S-boxes; the full PDF is Cloudflare-403 from this environment and is NOT in the Wayback Machine, so only the abstract and one indexed snippet were verified. PROVED: ONE KECCAK ROUND COSTS EXACTLY 1600 ROWS -- THE 'JOINT MC OF 320 PARALLEL CHI' QUESTION IS SETTLED AND THE ANSWER IS 'ADDITIVE'. The argument is three lines and needs NO SAT solver and NO appeal to Stoffelen. Let a solution have rows/witnesses w_1..w_T; on the prover's assignment each w_t is some function W_t of the circuit input x (ComputableWitnesses forces exactly this: each witness generator may only read variables below its own index). Every output bit is an AFFINE expression in {1, x, w} (AffineOutput is part of isR1CS_Cidentity). Pass to the quotient V = {functions GF(2)^n -> GF(2)} / {affine functions}. Then [y_i] lies in span{[W_1],...,[W_T]}, so T >= dim span{[y_i]}. For ONE round the outputs are y_i = u_i + (1+u_{i+1}) u_{i+2} + rc, so [y_i] = [u_{i+1} u_{i+2}], and those are 1600 DISTINCT degree-2 monomials in the u-basis, hence linearly independent, hence dim = 1600, hence T >= 1600. Matched by the trivial upper bound 1600. COROLLARIES: (a) MC(chi_5) >= 5 falls out of the same argument (5 independent quadratic parts) -- we do not need the SAT literature for it; (b) multiplicative complexity IS additive over the 320 parallel chi instances of a round, because the lower bound is a DIMENSION count and dimension is additive over disjoint variable sets; (c) the bound survives full nondeterminism -- witnesses may be arbitrary functions and constraint expressions may even reference later variables -- because it only uses 'outputs are affine in (x,w)'; (d) no intra-round trick of any kind exists: not sharing products between adjacent 5-bit rows, not a change of basis, not one row serving two chi outputs, not leaving an output affine. Every one of those would have to lower dim span{[y_i]}, which is a fixed number.

HARNESS COST MODEL RE-VERIFIED FROM SOURCE (do not re-derive): field is ZMod 2; isCidentityRowAt k e := exists affine A B, e = var k - A*B, and flatOperationsIsCid advances the pin counter by one PER ASSERT (witnesses do not advance it), starting at n = size Input = 1600. flatOperationCount charges .witness m -> m allocations, .assert -> 1 constraint; circuitCost is an EQUALITY (CostIs := forall n, operationCount = K) so nothing can be under-declared. lookup and interact are outright rejected (False), so no lookup escape hatch. ALLOCATIONS >= CONSTRAINTS IS FORCED, so score = 2 x rows is a floor, not a convention: if row t pins var n+t with n+t outside the circuit's own witness range, then GeneralFormalCircuit.Completeness quantifies over ALL prover environments satisfying UsesLocalWitnessesCompleteness, which pins only LOCALLY ALLOCATED witnesses -- so that variable is universally quantified and the row must hold for every value of it. The only rows that survive are degenerate (var k = var k * 1), which carry no information while still costing a constraint. Conclusion: you cannot buy a row without buying an allocation, and score = 2 x AND-count exactly.

CROSS-ROUND PRODUCT REUSE IS IMPOSSIBLE IN ANY STATE-MATERIALIZING CIRCUIT -- DEGREE SEPARATES THE ROUNDS. Verified computationally: L = rhoPi o theta has rank 1600 over GF(2) (full script: build theta as bit_i + colParity(x+4,z) + colParity(x+1,z+63) and rhoPi from the RFC 9861 offsets, then Gaussian-eliminate), so each round's pre-chi state is an INVERTIBLE affine image of the previous state; also verified that chi's multiplicand pairs are 1600 DISTINCT unordered pairs per round (5 per 5-bit row, the 5 edges of a 5-cycle -- the other 5 pairs of each row are never used). Consequently a round-r product has degree 2^r in the circuit input while a round-(r+1) product has degree 2^(r+1); a needed round-(r+1) product can therefore never equal an affine combination of already-computed values. Angle closed: expect and look for nothing here.

WHY NO PROOF THAT 19200 IS OPTIMAL WILL EVER BE FOUND, AND WHY THAT DOES NOT MAKE IT WORTH ATTACKING. The unconditional bound from the dimension argument applied to the FULL 12-round map is only T >= 1600 (score 3200), because the final map has only 1600 output bits. The natural strengthening -- filter by algebraic degree and count dimensions at each level -- caps out at about 1680 rows: 1600 functions at the top level, then only ~58 needed one level down (C(58,2) > 1600), then ~12, ~6, ~4. So every counting/dimension/degree technique available tops out around 1680 while we would need 19200, a factor of 11.4. Proving MC(Keccak-p[1600,12]) >= 12n for an explicit function is a superlinear multiplicative-complexity lower bound, which is open complexity theory. THE HONEST STATEMENT IS THEREFORE: 'optimality of 19200 is unprovable with current mathematics, but no mechanism to beat it is known and the search space is unreachable by any automated method (SAT-based MC minimization tops out near 5-bit S-boxes / ~20 variables, not 1600).' The per-round bound is a THEOREM; only cross-round amortization is open, and exploiting it would require making a round's output NOT affine in (x,w) while still forming the next round's AND multiplicands as affine forms -- which is self-contradictory for any construction anyone has ever written down.

DO-NOT-TRY LIST FOR THIS SLUG (all closed by the dimension bound or by the harness): (1) a 4-multiplication chi row -- impossible, dim = 5; (2) sharing products between chi rows or between lanes within a round -- impossible, the 1600 quadratic parts are independent; (3) leaving a final-round output affine or letting outputs BE the product witnesses -- the count is dim-limited, not materialization-limited, and the existing solution already allocates exactly one witness per product with zero extra materialization; (4) first-round constant folding -- despite the slug saying 'compress', Input is 1600 FREE bits and Assumptions = True, so there is no zero capacity to exploit (baseline in instances.yml is literally allocations 19200 / constraints 19200); (5) XOR/shortest-linear-program minimization of theta -- XOR is free; (6) rows that pin an unallocated variable to get constraints without allocations -- killed by Completeness quantifying over all environments; (7) folding two ANDs into one row by letting A or B reference the pinned variable -- solving var k = (var k + P)Q over GF(2) yields only the degenerate conditionals 'Q=1 => P=0' and 'Q=0 => var k = 0', never a second product; (8) lookups -- rejected by flatOperationsIsCid.

STRATEGIC: a submission that merely TIES the baseline does not make the leaderboard (our 38400 from 2026-07-28 is verified with is_record true on the submission object, yet the challenge leaderboard is empty and best_score is None, and baseline_score is exactly 38400). To take this challenge we would need 19199 ANDs or fewer -- i.e. to beat, by at least one gate, the AND count that the entire MPC / garbled-circuit / FHE / masking / Picnic literature has quoted for Keccak for fifteen years (1600 ANDs per round, 5 per chi S-box). RECOMMENDATION: move the job slots to challenges with real headroom. There is no partial credit here: 1599 saved gates and 1 saved gate are worth the same (a record), and 0 saved gates is worth nothing, but the probability of saving even 1 by search is effectively zero.

HARNESS-VERIFIED COST IDENTITY (same as the gf2-sha256 challenge): SCORE = 2 x (MULTIPLICATIVE COMPLEXITY OVER GF(2)), EXACTLY. The field is literally ZMod 2 and isCidentityRowAt restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A, B affine, so allocations == constraints == AND count and booleanity costs nothing. DO-NOT-TRY that follows: the single-row non-vanishing-multiplier trick (clean#395) CANNOT transfer to this variant — C must be a bare variable, so the output cannot be hidden inside a multiplicand, and affine*affine never reaches degree 3 over GF(2). Baseline 38400 = 2 x 12 x 1600 confirms the identity. This variant is purely an AND-count problem.

GF(2) CHANGES THE COST MODEL: every element IS a bit, so booleanity constraints vanish entirely — the ONLY cost is chi's multiplication. theta/rho/pi/iota are all F2-LINEAR (XOR = addition, rotation = index permutation, round constant = affine offset) and must cost ZERO.
Baseline 38400 = 12 rounds x 1600 bits x (1 alloc + 1 constraint) — exactly ONE multiplication per state bit. Beating it means beating the MULTIPLICATIVE COMPLEXITY of chi, not shaving overhead.

chi over GF(2): chi_i = a_i + a_{i+2} + a_{i+1}*a_{i+2} (since NOT b = 1+b is affine). Per 5-bit row the products are a1a2,a2a3,a3a4,a4a0,a0a1 — 5 products for 5 outputs, each seemingly used once. LOOK FOR: an algebraic identity computing all 5 row outputs with FEWER than 5 multiplications, products shared between adjacent rows/slices, or a change of basis making chi cheaper.
Only 12 rounds (KangarooTwelve), not 24 — half the rounds of keccak-f1600, so per-round savings are worth proportionally more of the total.

FINAL-ROUND TRIM: the last round's chi feeds only the output. Check whether any intermediate there can be left unmaterialized, or whether the output bits can BE the product witnesses rather than separate allocations — allocations are half the score.

An allocation is only needed for a value that a rank-1 product must reference. Any bit expressible as an affine combination of existing witnesses needs NO allocation — over GF(2) that covers all of theta/rho/pi/iota, so the allocation count should equal the MULTIPLICATION count exactly, never more.

MULTIPLICATIVE-COMPLEXITY FLOOR (SAT-solver literature, FSE 2016 'Optimizing S-Box Implementations ... Using SAT Solvers' and eprint 2023/1721 revisit): the Keccak 5-bit chi S-box has a PROVABLY MINIMAL nonlinear-gate count of 5 — implementations with 5 AND/NCT gates are known and SAT-proven optimal. So 5 muls per 5-bit row x 320 rows = 1600 multiplications per round is a HARD FLOOR for the constraint side; do NOT burn effort hunting a 4-multiplication chi row, it does not exist.

THEREFORE the remaining lever is the ALLOCATION side, not the constraint side. Constraints are pinned at 19200 (12 x 1600 products). The score is allocations+constraints = 38400, so any win must come from allocating FEWER than 19200 witnesses. chi_i = a_i + a_{i+2} + a_{i+1}*a_{i+2} is AFFINE in the product, so only the PRODUCT needs a witness — never allocate the chi output itself. Audit for: outputs materialized separately from their product witness, the final round's 1600 outputs (can they BE product witnesses?), and any witness the mechanical dead-variable pass would delete.

Cross-round product reuse is the only other opening: the linear layer (theta/rho/pi) between rounds mixes lanes, so a product from round r is generally NOT reusable in round r+1 — verify this rather than assume it, but expect no win there.

CONCRETE MC TABLES FOR EVERY SYMMETRIC BOOLEAN FUNCTION UP TO 25 VARIABLES — the missing tool for the multi-operand-adder lever. Brandao, Calik, Sonmez Turan & Peralta, 'Upper Bounds on the Multiplicative Complexity of Symmetric Boolean Functions', eprint 2019/708. WHY IT IS THE RIGHT TOOL: in a multi-operand column-compression adder, each column's outputs are SYMMETRIC functions of that column's input bits (elementary symmetric Sigma^n_k and counting functions E^n_k), so this paper's tables are a direct lookup for the exact per-column cost, replacing the full-adder-tree assumption. WHAT IS NEW BEYOND Boyar-Peralta 2008: (a) ARITY-BASED HW-ENCODINGS that use full adders (H_FA) in place of the standard Hamming-weight method, cutting AND gates in phase 1; (b) DEGREE-BASED ENCODINGS that skip work for functions of degree < n; (c) FREE TRUTH-TABLE ENTRIES exploited by concatenation in phase 2. CONCRETE, AND THESE ANSWER TWO OPEN 2008 QUESTIONS: MC(Sigma^8_4) = MC(E^8_4) = 6 — strictly below the 8 - hw(8) = 7 that the Hamming-weight method charges for the full weight. Generally every symmetric function on n <= 25 variables has MC <= n - 1 (n = 22 is the lone exception at <= 22). HOW TO USE IT: the standing bound MC(Hamming weight of n bits) = n - hw(n) is for the FULL weight vector; when the adder only needs SOME output bits of a column, look the individual function up in these tables instead — Sigma^8_4 at 6 vs 7 is exactly that gap. This is the concrete handle on the one piece of unclaimed ground (joint MC of multi-operand modular addition): build the column compressor from per-column table lookups, not from a generic full-adder tree.

DO-NOT-TRY, AND IT IS A TEMPTING ONE: XOR-GATE / SHORTEST-LINEAR-PROGRAM MINIMIZATION BUYS EXACTLY ZERO HERE. There is a large and still-active literature on minimizing the number of 2-input XOR gates needed to evaluate an F2-LINEAR MAP — the Shortest Linear Program problem: Boyar-Peralta, Tan-Peyrin (TCHES'20) adding randomization and 3-input XOR gates, the 'Superior Boyar-Peralta' (SBP) depth-aware heuristic, 'Improved Heuristics for Low-Latency Implementations of Linear Layers', and eprint 2025/1493 which revisits BP and cuts the AES linear layer from 91 to 89 g-XOR. Keccak's theta (and rho/pi, and SHA-256's Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1) are exactly such linear maps, so this looks like the obvious attack on the biggest remaining slack. IT IS NOT, BECAUSE AN XOR GATE COSTS NOTHING IN EITHER OF OUR COST MODELS. In native R1CS an affine combination lives inside the A/B/C vectors of a row and is free. In the GF(2) challenges the harness restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A and B AFFINE, so an arbitrary XOR-combination is free inside a multiplicand. Halving the XOR count of theta changes the score by ZERO. WHAT THETA'S 2240 ROWS PER ROUND ACTUALLY PAY FOR IS *MATERIALIZATION*, NOT XOR COUNT: a value costs an allocation exactly when it must appear as a BARE WITNESS VARIABLE — because it is a circuit output, or because its consumer needs a variable rather than an affine form. THEREFORE THE ONLY QUESTION WORTH ASKING IS: for each currently-materialized intermediate, WHO CONSUMES IT, and can that consumer take an affine form instead? Every row saved comes from deleting a materialization, never from restructuring the XOR tree that feeds it.

LITERATURE VERIFICATION OF THE FLOOR (primary sources, fetched and quoted, not summarised from search results). (1) MC(chi_5) = 5 IS PROVED, NOT MERELY ACHIEVED. Stoffelen, 'Optimizing S-box Implementations for Several Criteria using SAT Solvers', FSE 2016 (eprint 2016/198), Table 1 row 'Keccak/Ketje/Keyak 5x5 5'. Methodology, verbatim: 'When a SAT solver successfully finds a circuit for some value k but outputs UNSAT for k-1, it is proven that k is the minimum value', and 'For all S-boxes except the one used by the PRIMATEs we are able to prove the multiplicative complexity'. The paper's own internal control confirms the reading: PRIMATEs is listed as an INTERVAL {6,7} precisely because its k=6 UNSAT instance never terminated, so a bare integer means SAT at k and UNSAT at k-1 — i.e. UNSAT at k=4 was established for chi. Corroborated (upper bound only) by Bozilov-Bilgin-Sahin ToSC 2017(1), which places chi in affine-equivalence class 68 with MC 5, and by Bolzer-Duval-Minier (arXiv:2601.08368, IEEE TCAS-I 2026) giving chi_5 -> 5, chi_6 -> 6, ..., chi_9 -> 9. (2) NOBODY HAS PUBLISHED A SUB-1600-AND KECCAK ROUND. Bristol Fashion's reference Keccak-f is 38,400 AND gates = 24 x 320 x 5; Agrawal et al. (CCS 2021) quote it verbatim as '38400 AND gates i.e. 24 AND gates per input bit'. Searched across MPC, garbled circuits, FHE, masking, threshold implementations, MPC-in-the-head/Picnic, VOLE-in-the-head and ZK, plus circuit-simplification tooling. NOT COUNTEREXAMPLES: eprint 2025/386 improves chi from 23.33 GE to 17 GE, which is silicon AREA not AND count; quantum work quotes 3200 Toffoli/round, which is 2x WORSE due to uncompute. (3) The 12-round figure 19200 appears in NO published source — it is arithmetic, not a citation.

CORRECTION TO OUR OWN HEADLINE CLAIM — 19200 IS NOT PROVED OPTIMAL; ONLY THE PER-ROUND BOUND IS A THEOREM, AND THE WHOLE-CIRCUIT GAP IS 12x, THE SAME ORDER AS RSA'S. The dimension argument applied to the FULL 12-round map gives dim Q = 1600, i.e. T >= 1600 and score >= 3200 against the 38400 baseline — an 11.9x gap. The 19200 figure is the same theorem applied to M = 'the twelve materialised round states', and THAT SET IS A PROPERTY OF THE CONSTRUCTION, NOT OF THE FUNCTION. Entry #5 states this correctly; entry #0's 'PROVED, not assumed' phrasing and any external summary saying '38400 is proved optimal' overstate it. SECOND CORRECTION, TO ENTRY #5's REFINEMENT: 'filter by algebraic degree and count dimensions at each level, caps out at ~1680' assumes both factors of a top-degree product must be high-degree. One factor may be AFFINE and there are 1601 free affine generators, so C(1601,2) swamps the 1600 needed and the recursion never bites. Degree filtration adds O(log2 deg) = about 12, not O(sqrt m): corrected ceiling 1612 rows / 3224 score. BOTH CORRECTIONS MAKE THE BOUND WEAKER AND THE STRATEGIC CONCLUSION STRONGER — no counting, dimension or degree technique will ever reach 19200, and the recommendation to stop spending job slots stands unchanged.

gf2-sha256-compress-canonical: HARNESS-VERIFIED COST IDENTITY FOR THIS CHALLENGE: SCORE = 2 x (MULTIPLICATIVE COMPLEXITY OVER GF(2)), EXACTLY — and the consequence is a DO-NOT-TRY.
