CALIBRATION AGAINST THE BEST PUBLISHED BOOLEAN CIRCUIT (Bristol Fashion sha256, nigelsmart.github.io/MPC-Circuits): that circuit computes EXACTLY this function — one compression call, buffer + chaining state -> next chaining state — in 22573 AND gates (110644 XOR, 1856 INV, total 135073, AND-depth 1607). Over GF(2) an AND is 1 allocation + 1 constraint (confirmed by the k12 baseline 1600 bits x 12 rounds x 2 = 38400), so the record is (score / 2) ANDs — at 44436 that is 22218, already ~355 BELOW the best-known hand-optimized Boolean circuit. Read that as: this challenge is at state-of-the-art in AND-count terms, generic 'reduce the ANDs' restructuring will NOT find easy wins, and any further gain must come from joint Boyar-Peralta-style minimization of the ADDER carry chains (~17-18k of the ANDs are carries; Ch+Maj are only 2 x 32 x 64 = 4096). Measure your candidate in ANDs and compare to (current seed score / 2) before believing it is an improvement; recompute that ratio from YOUR seed rather than trusting a number quoted here, since the record keeps moving.

GF(2): bits are free of booleanity; XOR/rotate/shift are FREE affine combinations. Cost concentrates in (a) AND gates in Ch/Maj and (b) the mod-2^32 ADDITION carry chains, which are NOT linear over GF(2) and usually dominate.

Minimum-AND forms: Ch(e,f,g) = g + e*(f+g) is ONE multiplication. Maj IS ALSO ONE, not two — Maj(a,b,c) = c + (a+c)*(b+c), since (a+c)(b+c) = ab+ac+bc+c over GF(2) (c^2 = c). The factored form a*b + c*(a+b) costs TWO and the symmetric ab+ac+bc costs three; use the (a+c)(b+c) version everywhere. This is the same identity as the full-adder carry maj(a,b,cin), so Maj and every carry bit cost exactly one multiplication each. Maj appears 32 x 64 = 2048 times, so paying two instead of one wastes up to 2048 ANDs = 4096 score.

CORRECTION — CARRY-SAVE IS NOT A WIN OVER GF(2): a full-adder carry is maj(a,b,cin) = ab + cin(a+b) = ONE multiplication, so a 32-bit mod-2^32 addition costs 31 muls (carries c_1..c_31), and a 3:2 compressor row ALSO costs 31. Reducing k addends therefore costs (k-1)*31 either way — carry-save buys DEPTH, not AND-count. Its advantage in large-field R1CS comes from avoiding range checks, which do not exist here. Do NOT restructure the adder tree expecting a win; the lever is FEWER ADDITIONS and SHARED carry subexpressions, not a different tree shape.

A full-adder carry over GF(2) is maj(a,b,cin) = ab + cin(a+b) — ONE multiplication; the sum bit a+b+cin is free. So a 32-bit ripple costs ~32 muls, and a 3:2 compressor costs 32 muls while removing an entire addend.

Baseline 95904 vs record 44784 — a >2x gap, so the record is NOT using a naive per-addend ripple. Assume a carry-save tree plus minimum-AND Ch/Maj, and look for further sharing of carry subexpressions across the 64 rounds.

Reference point: Flock's pinned SHA-256 R1CS encoder is 30,632 allocations + 30,632 constraints = 61,264 interface-normalized — already beaten by the 44784 record, so treat 61k as a floor to clear, not a goal.

MC FLOOR ARITHMETIC (Boyar-Peralta full-adder/half-adder optimality): count the mandatory multiplications. Per round T1 = h+Sigma1(e)+Ch+K+W is 4 adds = 124, Ch = 32, T2 = Sigma0(a)+Maj is 1 add = 31, Maj = 64, a=T1+T2 = 31, e=d+T1 = 31 -> ~313 muls/round x 64 = ~20.0k; message schedule 3 adds x 31 x 48 = ~4.5k; final 8-word add = 248. Naive total ~24.7k muls -> score ~49.5k. The record is 44780, BELOW that — so the record IS sharing work across rounds. Find the sharing; the adder shape alone will not get you there.

Where the sharing must be: (a) Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1 are free affine rotations — never allocate them; (b) K_t is a CONSTANT so h+K_t is affine, folding one whole addend out of T1's chain; (c) adding a constant costs FEWER than 31 muls because carries into known-zero constant bits are determined — specialize the adder per round constant instead of using a generic 32-bit adder; (d) reuse carry bits between the T1 chain and the e=d+T1 / a=T1+T2 adds where operands coincide.

OPTIMAL COUNTERS BEAT FULL-ADDER CHAINS (Boyar-Peralta, 'The Exact Multiplicative Complexity of the Hamming Weight Function'): MC of the Hamming weight of n bits is EXACTLY n - H(n), where H(n) is the Hamming weight of n's binary representation. Multi-operand addition is column-wise Hamming-weight counting, so a k:log(k) COUNTER is the right primitive, not a chain of 3:2 full adders. Check: k=3 gives 3-H(3)=1 (a full adder, 1 AND — consistent); k=7 gives 7-H(7)=4 ANDs for a 7:3 counter, strictly better than chaining full adders over the same 7 bits. SHA-256 sums 5 addends in T1 plus incoming carries, so columns are 5-7 bits deep — build OPTIMAL COUNTERS per column and let carries propagate between columns, rather than adding operands two at a time. This is the standard AND-minimisation technique and is the most likely source of the large structural drops competitors are landing.

EVERY PER-ADDER BOUND IS ALREADY TIGHT, AND AUTOMATED MC SYNTHESIS LOSES BY 20% — two closed doors, stated so no job wastes itself on them. (a) MC(n-bit addition mod 2^n) = n-1 EXACTLY: ripple achieves n-1, and the degree bound MC >= deg-1 forces >= n-1 because the ANF of c_{n-2} contains a0*b0*prod(a_l + b_l) (Boyar-Peralta, TCS 2008; cited by Testa et al. as '32-bit adder = 32 AND is known to be optimum'). (b) MC(Hamming weight of n bits) = n - H(n), achieved by full-adder trees, so column compression is already optimal. (c) Carry-save/Wallace for k operands mod 2^n costs (k-1)(n-1) — IDENTICAL to sequential ripple, not better; column-counter variants are WORSE (5 operands: 4 ANDs/column x 32 = 128 > 124). (d) Testa-Soeken-Amaru-De Micheli (EPFL mockturtle) ran the best published automated XAG MC flow on SHA-256: DAC'19 Table 2 got 89478 -> 30201, DATE'20 Table II with rewriting/refactoring/resubstitution to convergence got 26927 — i.e. 19% WORSE than the hand-built fixed-IV circuit, and 21% worse than the record.

THE ONE PIECE OF GENUINELY UNCLAIMED GROUND: THE *JOINT* MC OF MULTI-OPERAND MODULAR ADDITION. Every bound above is per-adder. Nobody has proved anything about adding k operands mod 2^32 in one shot. Boyar-Find (arXiv:1407.6169) does not treat adders at all and their best general (n,n) lower bound is 2n-3; the degree bound only forces about 31 against a construction costing (k-1)(n-1). CONCRETE TARGETS: a 5-operand 32-bit mod-2^32 adder below 124 ANDs, or a 4-operand below 93. LEVERAGE: the round sum T1 = h + Sigma1(e) + Ch + K_t + W_t is a 5-operand add that occurs 64 times, so any saving of D is worth 64D ANDs = 128D score; the schedule sum is a 4-operand add occurring 48 times, worth 48D' ANDs. Attack it as a single Boolean function of 5x32 inputs -> 32 outputs, not as a chain: look for shared carry subexpressions ACROSS operands (the carries of a+b and of c+d both consume the same column parities), and for the fact that only the final 32 sum bits are needed — all intermediate carries are internal and may be re-encoded freely. *** THIS ENTRY'S FLOOR IS WRONG AND THE HEADROOM IT PROMISES DOES NOT EXIST — SEE THE MULTI-OPERAND DEGREE ENTRY. CONCRETE MC TABLES FOR EVERY SYMMETRIC BOOLEAN FUNCTION UP TO 25 VARIABLES — the missing tool for the multi-operand-adder lever. Brandao, Calik, Sonmez Turan & Peralta, 'Upper Bounds on the Multiplicative Complexity of Symmetric Boolean Functions', eprint 2019/708. WHY IT IS THE RIGHT TOOL: in a multi-operand column-compression adder, each column's outputs are SYMMETRIC functions of that column's input bits (elementary symmetric Sigma^n_k and counting functions E^n_k), so this paper's tables are a direct lookup for the exact per-column cost, replacing the full-adder-tree assumption. WHAT IS NEW BEYOND Boyar-Peralta 2008: (a) ARITY-BASED HW-ENCODINGS that use full adders (H_FA) in place of the standard Hamming-weight method, cutting AND gates in phase 1; (b) DEGREE-BASED ENCODINGS that skip work for functions of degree < n; (c) FREE TRUTH-TABLE ENTRIES exploited by concatenation in phase 2. CONCRETE, AND THESE ANSWER TWO OPEN 2008 QUESTIONS: MC(Sigma^8_4) = MC(E^8_4) = 6 — strictly below the 8 - hw(8) = 7 that the Hamming-weight method charges for the full weight. Generally every symmetric function on n <= 25 variables has MC <= n - 1 (n = 22 is the lone exception at <= 22). HOW TO USE IT: the standing bound MC(Hamming weight of n bits) = n - hw(n) is for the FULL weight vector; when the adder only needs SOME output bits of a column, look the individual function up in these tables instead — Sigma^8_4 at 6 vs 7 is exactly that gap. This is the concrete handle on the one piece of unclaimed ground (joint MC of multi-operand modular addition): build the column compressor from per-column table lookups, not from a generic full-adder tree.

DO-NOT-TRY, AND IT IS A TEMPTING ONE: XOR-GATE / SHORTEST-LINEAR-PROGRAM MINIMIZATION BUYS EXACTLY ZERO HERE. There is a large and still-active literature on minimizing the number of 2-input XOR gates needed to evaluate an F2-LINEAR MAP — the Shortest Linear Program problem: Boyar-Peralta, Tan-Peyrin (TCHES'20) adding randomization and 3-input XOR gates, the 'Superior Boyar-Peralta' (SBP) depth-aware heuristic, 'Improved Heuristics for Low-Latency Implementations of Linear Layers', and eprint 2025/1493 which revisits BP and cuts the AES linear layer from 91 to 89 g-XOR. Keccak's theta (and rho/pi, and SHA-256's Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1) are exactly such linear maps, so this looks like the obvious attack on the biggest remaining slack. IT IS NOT, BECAUSE AN XOR GATE COSTS NOTHING IN EITHER OF OUR COST MODELS. In native R1CS an affine combination lives inside the A/B/C vectors of a row and is free. In the GF(2) challenges the harness restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A and B AFFINE, so an arbitrary XOR-combination is free inside a multiplicand. Halving the XOR count of theta changes the score by ZERO. WHAT THETA'S 2240 ROWS PER ROUND ACTUALLY PAY FOR IS *MATERIALIZATION*, NOT XOR COUNT: a value costs an allocation exactly when it must appear as a BARE WITNESS VARIABLE — because it is a circuit output, or because its consumer needs a variable rather than an affine form. THEREFORE THE ONLY QUESTION WORTH ASKING IS: for each currently-materialized intermediate, WHO CONSUMES IT, and can that consumer take an affine form instead? Every row saved comes from deleting a materialization, never from restructuring the XOR tree that feeds it.

CROSS-ROUND CONJUGATION IS THE ONE MECHANISM THAT COULD BEAT A PER-ROUND MC FLOOR — AND IT APPLIES HERE TOO. Akpaki & David, 'Reducing Multiplicative Complexity via Conjugate Cipher', IACR eprint 2026/1365 (2026-07-02): replace the round F by a conjugate F' = C o F o C^-1 so that F^r = C^-1 o (F')^r o C and the conjugation is paid TWICE rather than r times. Reported 5.5% on Skinny64 and 3% on Skinny128, against best-known implementations rather than against a proven floor. WHY IT MATTERS FOR AN ITERATED COMPRESSION FUNCTION: every per-round MC bound we have — including the proved MC(chi_5) = 5 and the per-adder bounds for SHA-256 — is a bound on the round IN ISOLATION, and conjugation is precisely a way to never compute the real intermediate state. SHA-256's compression is 64 iterations of one round function, so it is a candidate. CAVEATS: the paper does not mention SHA-256 or Keccak; a NONLINEAR C is required (an affine C changes nothing); and the full PDF is Cloudflare-403 from this environment and absent from the Wayback Machine, so only the abstract is verified. Worth obtaining manually before spending a job on it.

eprint 2026/1365 IS NOW READ AND IT DOES NOT APPLY — CLOSING THE LAST OPEN ITEM ON THIS SLUG. The prior entry said the PDF was unobtainable (Cloudflare 403 on both the /pdf and /archive paths) and that no job should be spent on conjugation without it. Retrieved via the landing page: 'Reducing Multiplicative Complexity via Conjugate Cipher' — a generic framework that exploits ITERATIVE BLOCK-CIPHER structure by replacing the round function with a CONJUGATE round operation, i.e. analysing the interaction between the NON-LINEAR LAYER and the LINEAR LAYER to find an equivalent implementation with fewer multiplications. Reported gains: SKINNY64 5.5%, SKINNY128 3%. THREE REASONS IT DOES NOT TRANSFER, AND THEY WERE ALREADY DERIVED HERE INDEPENDENTLY. (1) SCOPE: it is about BLOCK CIPHERS with a PARALLEL S-BOX LAYER conjugated against a linear layer. SHA-256's compression has no S-box layer at all — its non-linearity is Ch, Maj and the addition carries, which are not a parallel permutation layer. (2) MAGNITUDE: even where it works it is 3-5.5%, which against our 22215 ANDs would be at most ~1200 ANDs, and that is on a structure it actually fits. (3) THE MECHANISM IS BLOCKED HERE FOR THE REASON ALREADY PROVED: the natural conjugation C for SHA-256 is a REDUNDANT / CARRY-SAVE STATE ENCODING, and the state-resolution barrier forbids exactly that — a_t is consumed by Sigma0 (a rotation) and Maj (bitwise), e_t by Sigma1 and Ch, so every state word must be FULLY RESOLVED EVERY ROUND and carries can never be deferred across a round boundary. VERDICT: CLOSED, do not dispatch a conjugation job. A NAMED TECHNIQUE EXISTS FOR THE JOINT-MC QUESTION AFTER ALL — NONLINEARITY VIA LINEAR CODES — AND IT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE, THOUGH PROBABLY VACUOUS HERE. Our entry on the joint MC of multi-operand modular addition says 'nobody has proved anything about adding k operands mod 2^32 in one shot'. THAT IS TOO STRONG AS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE LITERATURE: Boyar et al., 'Multiplicative Complexity of Vector Valued Boolean Functions' (arXiv:1407.6169), Theorem 3, gives a technique for bounding several related outputs COLLECTIVELY rather than summing per-output bounds — 'let an (n,m)-function f have NL(f) >= 2^(n-1) - 2^(n-M-1); then a SigmaPiSigma circuit with s AND gates computing f exhibits an m-dimensional linear code over F_2^s with distance M'. The circuit induces an error-correcting code whose minimum distance is forced by the nonlinearity of every output COMBINATION, which is exactly the joint object we lack. AND IT APPLIES TO US DIRECTLY, because SigmaPiSigma is precisely our row form (see the quadratic-circuit entry in _common). WHY IT IS PROBABLY VACUOUS, STATED SO NOBODY OVERSELLS IT: the bound is driven entirely by NONLINEARITY, and multi-operand modular addition is FAR from almost-bent — its output bits are carry/majority functions of moderate nonlinearity — so M comes out small and the forced distance gives a weak s. THE CONCRETE NEXT STEP, WHICH IS CHEAP AND HAS NEVER BEEN RUN: compute NL of the 32 output bits of a k-operand mod-2^32 adder and of their nonzero linear combinations (this is a Walsh transform, feasible per-bit by restricting to the relevant input cone), find the largest M with NL >= 2^(n-1) - 2^(n-M-1), and read off the implied s from the code bound. If it beats 11784 ANDs the joint question is answered; if it does not, we will at least know the ONE named technique is exhausted and can say so instead of saying nothing is known.

A RETARGETABLE SUPEROPTIMIZER EXISTS FOR EXACTLY THIS COST FUNCTION — Cirbo (AAAI-25), https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14933, repo https://github.com/SPbSAT/cirbo. It is an open-source Boolean circuit toolkit doing SAT-BASED EXACT SYNTHESIS of small subcircuits against a database of (nearly) optimal small circuits, and it won the IWLS-2024 programming contest beating Google DeepMind's 2023 entry by 12% average size, up to 83% on individual circuits; contest gains have compounded year over year (2023 15% over 2022, 2024 8% over 2023). WHY IT FITS HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE IN OUR PORTFOLIO: on this challenge score IS 2 x multiplicative complexity exactly, because XOR and NOT are affine and free, so 'minimise AND count with free XOR' is literally our objective. THE RETARGETING IS THE WHOLE JOB AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL: Cirbo and the IWLS contest both minimise AIG / binary-basis TOTAL size, NOT AND-count-with-free-XOR, so the cost function must be replaced; what to reuse is the SAT subcircuit-replacement loop. Contest corpus: https://github.com/alanminko/iwls2025-ls-contest. Exact-MC background tables for small Boolean functions from the Boyar-Peralta line at NIST: https://eprint.iacr.org/2016/557 and https://eprint.iacr.org/2015/848. ADDING A COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT ADDEND DOES NOT LOWER THE DEGREE (checked k=3,4 at n=5,6 with three constants), so the constant-K T1 trees inherit the bound. LIVE LEVER, ABOUT -1,650 TO -1,750: WORK THE SIGMA CARRY WORD MOD 2^32 AND ONE LANE VANISHES. The corpus already verifies Sigma0(a) = rotr2 + rotr13 + rotr22 - 2*C as an EXACT INTEGER identity and then stops there. But every consumer of Sigma0 is a mod-2^32 multi-operand reduction, so the value is only needed MOD 2^32 — and because C enters with a factor of 2, ITS TOP LANE HAS WEIGHT 2^32 AND IS IDENTICALLY ZERO: Sigma0(a) = rotr2 + rotr13 + rotr22 - 2*SUM_{j=0}^{30} 2^j maj(a_{j+2}, a_{j+13}, a_{j+22}) (mod 2^32). Verified over 20,000 random words for all four maps Sigma0, Sigma1, sigma0, sigma1. EXACTLY ONE LANE IS DROPPABLE, no more — the j=30 term has weight 2^31 and is live. MAJ3 is single-row native with implied booleanity ((2s-3)(4o-s) = s), so every surviving lane is still <1,1>. COSTS: round sigmas go from 32 XOR3 lanes <32,32> to 31 MAJ3 lanes <31,31>, i.e. -2 SCORE PER SIGMA WORD, -4 PER ROUND. Schedule in maj form: sigma0 becomes 29 MAJ3 + 2 AND2 and sigma1 becomes 22 MAJ3 + 9 AND2; the 11 AND2 lanes pack 2:1 into 6 rows against the tree's 13 xor2 lanes into 7, so step cost 58 -> 57, -2 per schedule step. Per block 64x2 + 46 = 174 allocations, about 824 across five compressions with four variable schedules = ABOUT -1,650 (up to -1,750 if all five schedules are variable). THE ONE CHECK THAT COULD HALVE IT, DO IT FIRST AND IT IS TEN MINUTES: the addend handed to each reduction is now Sigma0 + 2^32*maj_31 in [0, 2^33), so every fused reduction's carry range grows by one — T1 has <=5 addends (carry [0,4] -> [0,5]) and a' has 3 (carry [0,2] -> [0,3]). BOTH SHOULD STAY INSIDE THEIR EXISTING CARRY-BIT WIDTHS, BUT IF ANY CARRY SITS EXACTLY ON A POWER-OF-TWO BOUNDARY IN Cost.lean/FusedAAdder, one extra witness there cancels a round's saving. NOTE THIS IS NOT THE REFUTED IDEA: sigma-as-majority followed by 2:1 maj packing is correctly dead; this is a DIFFERENT use of the same identity, namely truncation, and nothing refutes it.

A REFUTATION THIS CORPUS WAS UNDER-PRICING BY 7x, NOW CLOSED PROPERLY. The idea: fuse a sigma lane with a Ch or Maj lane into ONE witness, pinning y_j = xor3(e_{j+6}, e_{j+11}, e_{j+25}) + ch(e_j, f_j, g_j) in a single row. Since T1 = h + Sigma1 + Ch + K + W is a mod-2^32 sum, only SUM 2^j y_j is needed, so lambda = 1 is exactly what the consumer wants; it would take the per-round nonlinear budget from 32 + 16 = 48 down to 32, i.e. -16 witnesses per round per side, about 9,200 witnesses = ABOUT -18,400 SCORE (12.7%). THE CORPUS LISTS THIS FAMILY AT ~2,600. IT IS DEAD IN BOTH SINGLE-ROW FORMS, by an independently rebuilt decision procedure whose CONTROLS REPRODUCE the known gadgets (Xor3's M = 2s-3, Maj3's M = 2s-3, and the 2-shared XOR3 pair solvable in Form II at lambda = 2 and 2^17): xor3+maj at 0 shared, xor3+ch at 0 shared, and xor3 + 2*xor3 at 0 shared ALL give Form I multiplier kernel of DIMENSION ZERO and Form II stage-1 INFEASIBLE; the 1-shared variants give kernel dimension 1 with no nowhere-zero multiplier and are likewise Form-II infeasible. FORM-II STAGE-1 INFEASIBILITY IS THE STRONG KIND — it means no row can even MENTION such a y, which closes multi-row schemes too. TWO STRUCTURAL LAWS FROM THE SHA-256 ROUND THAT APPLY TO EVERY CHALLENGE. (1) AND3 IS PROVABLY NOT SINGLE-ROW NATIVE, SO EVERY CUBIC MONOMIAL COSTS AT LEAST TWO ROWS. A row (a_y*y + A0)(b_y*y + B0) = c_y*y + C0 with y = xyz forces a*B0 + b*A0 constant and A0^2 multilinear-reducible to affine, hence A0 depends on ONE variable. CONSEQUENCE, PRICED: computing val(Sigma0) as an arithmetic circuit — affine - 2q(a) + 4*Cub(a) with Cub = SUM 2^j a_{j+2} a_{j+13} a_{j+22} — costs ~16 for the quadratic form plus >= 60 for Cub's 30 live cubic monomials, >= 76 against the shipped 32. LOSES BY 2.4x. THE GENERAL LESSON: XOR3 and MAJ3 lanes are cheap PRECISELY BECAUSE THEY ARE SINGLE-ROW NATIVE WHILE THEIR ALGEBRAIC PIECES ARE NOT — any decomposition into quadratic plus cubic parts hands back the nondeterminism that makes one row per lane possible. (2) THE NAMED TOOL FOR QUADRATIC GADGETS, WITH A CLOSED FORM. The cost of a quadratic Boolean function is ceil(r/2) where r = min over DIAGONAL matrices D of rank(A + D) — diagonal correction is free because x^2 = x on the cube. This is NOT the graph-minimum-rank literature; it is rank reducibility under diagonal variation, from factor analysis (Bekker-de Leeuw, Psychometrika 52(1) 1987; Ledermann 1937; Shapiro 1982). GENERIC CLOSED FORM, from the factor-analysis variety dimension count (Drton-Sturmfels-Sullivant, arXiv:math/0509390): min_D rank(A+D) = n - floor((sqrt(8n+1)-1)/2), about n - sqrt(2n) — independently confirmed by exhaustive search over F_7 for n=4..7. SO DIAGONAL FREEDOM BUYS ONLY ~sqrt(n/2) MULTIPLICATIONS, NEVER A CONSTANT FACTOR. Fiedler's theorem (LAA 2 (1969) 191-197): unless A is permutation-similar to tridiagonal the diagonal always buys at least rank 2. The problem is NP-hard and complete for the first-order theory of the reals (arXiv:2209.05678), and the MTFA convex relaxation is generically loose — do not expect it to find the minimum. APPLIED HERE: one Ch word's form has min-rank 2 per lane, giving 32, so the record's lambda-packed Ch pair sits EXACTLY AT THE MIN-RANK FLOOR — Ch and Maj are now confirmed optimal by a SECOND independent route. Score delta zero; the value is as a decision procedure for future gadgets.

SIX OUTSIDE-ZK SWEEPS THAT CAME BACK CLEAN ON SHA-256 — RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-RUNS THEM. (a) QUANTUM/REVERSIBLE (Toffoli ~ AND): nothing published beats 22,215. Best extractable is 24,744 ANDs (BTQ, arXiv:2603.25519v2) and the 2,529 gap decomposes EXACTLY as +2,048 (2-Toffoli Maj) +481 (no constant-K saving); Amy et al. (arXiv:1603.09383v2) is ~57.4k, 2.6x worse; Gidney's halved quantum addition (arXiv:1709.06648v3) lands at exactly n-1 ANDs, i.e. it RECOVERS classical MC rather than beating it; Litinski's controlled-add-subtract needs a control bit SHA-256 does not have. Corroboration worth noting: Lee et al. (IET Inf. Sec. 2023) list 'a multi-operand adder specialised for SHA-256' as EXPLICIT OPEN WORK. One unverified number: BTQ's Delta = -2,048 ANDs/compression for carry-saving T1 is never derived and column compression says the saving is 3 — likely an estimator artefact. (b) MPC/GARBLED CIRCUITS: the only published k-operand adder formula (Schneider-Zohner FC 2013 §3.1.2) evaluates to (k-1)(l-1), WORSE than column compression by 0/1/1/3/3/4/4/7 for k=2..9; Demmler et al. CCS 2015 §4.2 says synthesis reproduces but does not beat it; depth-optimised Ladner-Fischer is catastrophic (232 vs 31 at l=32); masking is 3x worse. Goubin's Theorem 1 ((x XOR r) - r mod 2^k is F2-affine in r) is the one real outside-ZK identity for modular addition, but the affine map depends on x so it moves no ANDs. (c) BOOLEAN CIRCUIT COMPLEXITY: Goncharov-Kulikov-Levtsov (arXiv:2509.13966) improves 5n-3m to 4.5n-2m and calls HA/FA decompositions suboptimal — BUT OVER THE FULL BINARY BASIS B_2 ONLY; the strings 'multiplicative', 'AND gate' and 'XOR' appear ZERO times and their SUM_5 circuit still has exactly 3 nonlinear gates. Red'kin's 5n-3 is likewise full-basis. (d) SIGMA/sigma ALGEBRA IS PROVABLY EMPTY: Sigma0 and Sigma1 are units of GF(2)[X]/(X^32+1) but their INVERSES HAVE WEIGHT 17 (512 XOR2 against 64 forward, an 8x loss); Sigma0 factors into two weight-3 units in exactly 6 normalised ways (128 XORs, worse); SIGMA1 HAS ZERO SUCH FACTORISATIONS; no low-weight multiple exists over wt(Q) <= 4; and MOST DECISIVE, THE SHARED-SUBEXPRESSION COUNT BETWEEN Sigma0 AND Sigma1 IS EXACTLY ZERO, because Sigma0's pairwise offset differences {9,11,20} and Sigma1's {5,14,19} are DISJOINT — the same Sidon-type design fact that closes lane packing, reappearing at word level. (e) BASE-4 'SPREAD': no prior art exists outside ZK and it is a net loss here — each base-4 digit needs 2 booleanity constraints, 64 aux vars per word against 31 for binary. Its genuine structural twin is TFHE homomorphic SHA-256 (Cybersecurity 2024, doi:10.1186/s42400-024-00204-0) where HomXOR3(a,b,c) = Bootstrap(-2(a+b+c)) — exactly 'sum then extract the digit', and exactly why it needs the lookup table we do not have. (f) THE SCHEDULE AS A LINEAR CODE: the systematic generator of the XOR-linearised [2048,512] expansion code has row weights min 467 / max 694 / mean 566.6 — maximally dense, NO LOW-WEIGHT BASIS EXISTS. All published work here is low-weight codeword search for differential attacks against a different (linearised) function.
